Verified live: 17/20 live hosts detected on-desktop (the 3 misses are headless-spawned — correct), `keptOnDesktop 0→11`, slice-2 target list empty. ## The detector failure (fix the guard, not just the bug) [Section titled “The detector failure (fix the guard, not just the bug)”](#the-detector-failure-fix-the-guard-not-just-the-bug) “0 on-desktop/hard-exempt” was in the journal for a month. The broken shape is mechanically detectable: **open windows + live interactive hosts + zero protected owners**. The sweep routine (`idle-session-reaper-action.ts`) now runs an exemption health probe before any destructive slice and logs the three counts every sweep, warning loudly on that shape. If you see that warning, treat every kill in the same sweep as suspect. ## Traps for future work here [Section titled “Traps for future work here”](#traps-for-future-work-here) * **Never key desktop/window logic on window titles or window pids** without accounting for TUI title rewriting and single-process emulators. * **`isOwnerFocusedOnDesktop`** (the stall-waker auto-ESC focus guard) still uses the rotted launch handles and is likely a no-op for post-May-31 sessions — tracked as **WI-1588**. The ancestry signal is deliberately NOT used there: it is presence-grade, not focus-grade (any focused terminal window would match every terminal-hosted session via the shared emulator pid, suppressing auto-recovery fleet-wide). * The exemption runs in **papercup-bg-host** (`:3270`, staging tree, has `DISPLAY`) — a box/service without `DISPLAY` sees no windows and protects nothing, by design (headless fleet boxes).

# Gate dev-only UI on import.meta.env.MODE, not .DEV

> The desktop dev shell runs `vite build --mode development`, so import.meta.env.DEV is FALSE there. Gate dev-only UI on MODE !== 'production' or it never appears in the desktop. Verified by build-grep.

## What [Section titled “What”](#what) To gate a dev-only UI surface so it ships in the desktop **dev** shell but is **absent from the production build**, gate on `import.meta.env.MODE !== 'production'` — **not** `import.meta.env.DEV`. 
```tsx
// ✅ shows in the desktop dev shell, tree-shaken out of production
const DevAdminRail =
  import.meta.env.MODE !== 'production'
    ? lazy(() => import('../components/dev-admin-rail/DevAdminRail'))
    : null;


// ❌ NEVER appears in the desktop — DEV is false in a `vite build`
const DevAdminRail = import.meta.env.DEV ? lazy(...) : null;
```
 ## Why (the trap) [Section titled “Why (the trap)”](#why-the-trap) Vite ties `import.meta.env.DEV` / `.PROD` to the **command** (`vite` serve vs `vite build`), while `.MODE` follows `--mode`. The desktop’s three run modes (see [Dev modes](/internal/docs/desktop/dev-modes)) are: | Run mode | command | `MODE` | `DEV` | | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------- | ----------- | | `bin/desktop-dev` (HMR) | `vite` (serve) | `development` | `true` | | `bin/desktop-dev-nohmr` (rebuild-watch) | `vite build --watch --mode development` | `development` | **`false`** | | shipped (`tauri build`) | `vite build` | `production` | `false` | `bin/desktop-dev-nohmr` is the **default** `npm run dev` for the desktop, and it is a `vite build` — so `import.meta.env.DEV` is `false` there. A `DEV`-gated surface compiles away and **never appears in the desktop you’re testing in**, even though you’re “in dev”. `MODE` is the only flag that is `development` in **both** dev shells and `production` only in the shipped build. (Empirically confirmed on this repo’s rolldown-vite: a `DEV`-gated rail was absent from both a `--mode development` build and a production build; the `MODE`-gated rail was present in the dev build and absent in the prod build.) ## How to verify the gate (build-grep) [Section titled “How to verify the gate (build-grep)”](#how-to-verify-the-gate-build-grep) `MODE` is a static string Vite replaces at build time, so a `MODE`-gated lazy chunk is dead code in prod — Rollup drops it. Prove both directions by building to throwaway dirs and grepping for a marker unique to your surface: 
```bash
cd apps/operator-vite
npx vite build                          --outDir /tmp/p --emptyOutDir   # production
npx vite build --mode development       --outDir /tmp/d --emptyOutDir   # dev
grep -rho "<your-unique-class-or-string>" /tmp/p/   # → 0 (absent in prod)
grep -rho "<your-unique-class-or-string>" /tmp/d/   # → >0 (present in dev)
```
 Run the two builds **sequentially** to separate `--outDir`s — concurrent `vite build`s share the vite cache dir and cross-contaminate each other’s output. ## Two more gotchas this surfaced [Section titled “Two more gotchas this surfaced”](#two-more-gotchas-this-surfaced) * **CSS imported by a dead lazy module still leaks.** Vite eagerly collects a `import './x.css'` into the output stylesheet even when the importing module is a tree-shaken dynamic chunk — the JS goes, the class names stay. Carry dev-only CSS as a JS string injected via `<style>{CSS}</style>` (a JS import tree-shakes with the dead module) instead of a `.css` import. (FeaturesAdmin’s inline `<style>` pattern, for the same reason.) * **Pick a unique class prefix.** `pc-dev-*` is already heavily used by the `/dev` page (`pc-dev-rail-*`, `pc-dev-panel`, `pc-dev-row`, `pc-dev-kv`). Reusing it bleeds CSS onto that page. The dev admin rail uses `pcdar*`. ## Where this came from [Section titled “Where this came from”](#where-this-came-from) The dev admin rail (`apps/operator-vite/src/components/dev-admin-rail/`, plan `dev-admin-sidebar-2026-06-05`). Its plan named `import.meta.env.DEV`; that would have made the rail invisible in the very desktop it’s meant for. The mount in `apps/operator-vite/src/routes/__root.tsx` carries the corrected gate + rationale.

# Dispatch flags (crossWorkspace, etc.) are read off the PROJECTED def, not the source def

> A defineTool flag like crossWorkspace can be set on the def yet silently dropped in projection, so the host dispatch never honors it. Symptom appears far from cause. Diff the source def against lookupByMcpName(name).

## The trap [Section titled “The trap”](#the-trap) `defineTool` has **two** registration paths into the projected-tool registry: * **principal-gated** (the default) → `definePrincipalGatedTool` → `registerLegacyAsProjected(def, …)` * **role-gated** (`requirePrincipal: false`, or `agentRoles`) → `defineRoleGatedTool` The host dispatch (`_mcp-handler.ts`) and the scoped-superuser clamp read a tool’s dispatch-relevant flags — `crossWorkspace`, `profile`, `harness`, … — off the **PROJECTED** def via `lookupByMcpName(name)`, **not** off the source def you wrote. So a flag that is set on the source def but not threaded through *both* projection paths is **silently ignored** by the host. EI-2378 was exactly this: `crossWorkspace` was on the principal-gated `def` (with a P-062 comment intending it) but `registerLegacyAsProjected` didn’t copy it into `registerProjectedTool({…})`, while the role-gated path did. Result: `memory:*` (principal-gated, `crossWorkspace: true`) ran on a workspace-scoped tx instead of the admin handle, and failed `requires a workspace-scoped call` from an unscoped (`?workspace=*`) psu session. ## Why it’s nasty [Section titled “Why it’s nasty”](#why-its-nasty) The **symptom is far from the cause**. You set `crossWorkspace: true`, read the code, see the flag on the def, and the tool *still* behaves workspace-isolated. The drop is in a generic projection helper you’d never think to look at, one path of two. ## The heuristic [Section titled “The heuristic”](#the-heuristic) When a `defineTool` dispatch flag seems ignored, **diff the source def against the projected def**: 
```ts
import { lookupByMcpName } from '@papercusp/tooldef'; // (the registry this file lives in)
lookupByMcpName('memory:search')?.crossWorkspace // ← what the HOST actually sees
```
 If the projected value disagrees with your source `defineTool({ … })`, the projection dropped it. Fix it in the registration path that’s missing the field (and add a parity test — see `crossWorkspace projection parity (EI-2378)` in `libs/generic/tooldef/src/positional-integration.test.ts`). ## Related: crossWorkspace + the scoped-superuser clamp [Section titled “Related: crossWorkspace + the scoped-superuser clamp”](#related-crossworkspace--the-scoped-superuser-clamp) A `crossWorkspace` tool runs on the `getOrgPg` admin (rolbypassrls) handle — it **must self-derive `workspaceId`** (`args.workspace ?? ctx.principal?.workspaceId ?? activeWorkspaceId()`) and never rely on the tx’s RLS for confinement. The scoped-superuser clamp DENIES `crossWorkspace` tools from a workspace-scoped session unless they’re on `SCOPED_SAFE_CROSSWORKSPACE` (a reviewed-in-the-gate allowlist). A surface partitioned by a non-workspace axis (e.g. `memory:*` by user-id/harness-slug) belongs on that allowlist — it crosses no workspace tenant boundary.

# Hermetic dispatch tests must seed EVERY postInvoke-seam table (tool_invocations + decision_ledger)

> A hive integration test that dispatches a governed tool through the real dispatch path runs the postInvoke seam, which writes to BOTH harness_shared.tool_invocations (recordInvocation) AND harness_shared.decision_ledger (recordDecisionLedger, migration 260). A beforeAll that hand-curates a migration subset and seeds only some of those tables reddens the WHOLE file via vitest-fail-on-console. Symptom: 'Expected test not to call console.warn()' wrapping 'relation harness_shared.X does not exist'.

## The symptom [Section titled “The symptom”](#the-symptom) A hive integration test (`packages/operator-core/lib/hive/*-e2e.integration.test.ts`, `shared-hive-loop/*.integration.test.ts`) goes red with: 
```plaintext
vitest-fail-on-console > Expected test not to call console.warn().
[decision-ledger] insert failed: relation "harness_shared.decision_ledger" does not exist
    at recordDecisionLedgerImpl (.../lib/decision-ledger/emit.ts:190)
```
 The assertion the test *wrote* passes; the file fails anyway because **any `console.warn` reddens the whole file** under `vitest-fail-on-console`. The warn comes from a side-effect you didn’t write — the dispatch postInvoke seam. This bit EI-496 + EI-497 (`declared-event-wake-e2e`, `start-hive-e2e`) on 2026-06-14. The same file already carried the identical comment one table earlier for `tool_invocations` — so this is the **second** postInvoke-seam table to draw blood. Expect a third when a new seam table lands. ## Why [Section titled “Why”](#why) These hermetic tests don’t run the migration runner — their `beforeAll` hand-curates a *subset* of `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/*.sql` (plus a couple of inline `CREATE TABLE`s). But every governed tool dispatch runs the shared endpoint **postInvoke seam**, which writes to: * `harness_shared.tool_invocations` — `recordInvocation` (projected-tool-deps), on EVERY dispatch incl. reads. * `harness_shared.decision_ledger` — `recordDecisionLedger` (`lib/decision-ledger/emit.ts`), migration **260**, on governed (non-read) non-SU actions. Miss either table and the seam `console.warn`s rather than throwing (it’s best-effort by design — the ledger must never break a real dispatch), so the test *runs* but the file goes red. ## The fix [Section titled “The fix”](#the-fix) Seed BOTH tables in `beforeAll`. `260-decision-ledger.sql` is self-contained (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` depending only on the `harness_shared` schema + the `harness_app`/`harness_zero` roles, both created earlier in these hooks), so just apply it like the other migrations: 
```ts
await rootSql.unsafe(readMigration('260-decision-ledger.sql')).simple();
```
 `tool_invocations` is created inline in these files (see the existing block). When you add a new hermetic dispatch test, copy a *current* sibling’s `beforeAll` rather than an old one — the seam’s table set only grows. ## Rule of thumb [Section titled “Rule of thumb”](#rule-of-thumb) If a test dispatches a governed tool through the real path, its `beforeAll` must provide every table the postInvoke seam touches — not just the tables your assertions read. When a new seam side-effect adds a table, every hand-curated hermetic dispatch test inherits the gap at once; the watchdog will file it as a “test failing repeatedly” EI per file.

# Distributed test gate: shard hermeticity (DG-6)

> What a machine needs to run a test shard from (stagingSha, shard), which coverage self-narrows off the dev box, and what the gate does NOT cover.


**Source of truth:** `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hive-git/gate/hermeticity.ts` (the machine-readable registry + classifier; this page is the narrative). Audit: 2026-07-02, plan `cross-machine-coord-parity-and-trust-2026-07-01` P-049. ## The model [Section titled “The model”](#the-model) A gate **shard** is one `(workspace, unit|integration)` pair (`gate/shards.ts`, DG-2). Verdicts are keyed by `(shardId, inputsHash)` — so a shard must produce the **same verdict from `(stagingSha, shard)` on any capable machine**. That is hermeticity, and it is the property the whole distributed gate rests on. ## What a machine must offer (`shardCapabilities`) [Section titled “What a machine must offer (shardCapabilities)”](#what-a-machine-must-offer-shardcapabilities) * **unit shard** → `node` (a runtime + an `npm ci`’d checkout at the sha). * **integration shard** → `node` + `docker` (testcontainers Postgres/redis/ typesense; images pullable or pre-pulled). All four integration workspaces (`apps/operator`, `packages/operator-core`, `libs/papercusp/libs/db`, `libs/test-config`) ride `@papercusp/test-config` — throwaway per-run DBs, never a host Postgres. ## Why the suites are hermetic by design [Section titled “Why the suites are hermetic by design”](#why-the-suites-are-hermetic-by-design) * `test-config/src/setup-hermetic-env.ts` scrubs spawn-env pollution (workspace pins, git-config injection, release-gate roots, PGBOUNCER class-defaults) and redirects state-dir seams (`PAPERCUSP_*_DIR`) off the real `~/.papercusp`. * Live-operator suites **probe and self-skip** (`it.skipIf(!live)`, reachability → `describe.skip`, or an explicit env opt-in). Their verdict stays valid everywhere; only live coverage narrows. The audited list lives in `KNOWN_COVERAGE_COUPLINGS` — add rows only with the guard line in hand. * The admin test-runs reporter’s dev-DSN fallback is fail-soft (1s timeout → null): on a foreign machine it reports nothing and fails nothing. The gate’s own verdict facts (DG-1 `gate/verdicts.ts`) are the cross-machine record. ## The class that was fixed (don’t reintroduce it) [Section titled “The class that was fixed (don’t reintroduce it)”](#the-class-that-was-fixed-dont-reintroduce-it) Five suites read migration DDL through hand-rolled `../../..` candidate lists with a **hardcoded dev-box absolute path** as last resort (one pointed at a path that existed on no machine at all). Fixed 2026-07-02 with `readRepoFile(__dirname, 'libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/…')` from `@papercusp/test-config` — a walk-up resolver that is depth-, dist- and machine-proof and **throws loudly** instead of falling back. Use it for ANY repo-relative file a test reads. Never write an absolute checkout path in a test. ## What the gate does NOT cover (loud boundary) [Section titled “What the gate does NOT cover (loud boundary)”](#what-the-gate-does-not-cover-loud-boundary) `GATE_COVERAGE_BOUNDARY`: Playwright e2e, Cargo tests, LLM scenarios — they run on their own rails. `green(S)` means *all npm-workspace shards passed*, not *all testing passed*.

# How the papercusp-workspace + papercup-self-registration boot path works

> Two fire-and-forget bootstrap helpers run on every operator boot to make Papercusp dogfood itself — sentinel workspace ensure + papercup repo auto-register. Idempotent + non-disruptive to existing installs.

## What [Section titled “What”](#what) Two helpers make Papercusp dogfood itself: 1. **`ensurePapercuspWorkspace()`** — guarantees a workspace called `papercusp-workspace` (literal name) exists in the workspace registry. Idempotent. 2. **`registerPapercupHarness()`** — if running from the papercup source repo, auto-registers it as a harness named `papercup` inside that sentinel workspace, `state: private`. Idempotent * no-op for packaged installs. Together: Papercusp dogfoods itself. The user finds `papercup` in their harness dropdown when they switch to `papercusp-workspace` — no manual `harness create` step. Files (current boot location): * `packages/operator-core/lib/harness/papercusp-workspace.ts` * `packages/operator-core/lib/harness/register-papercusp.ts` (renamed from `register-papercup.ts`; still exports `registerPapercupHarness` + `detectPapercupRoot` — the fn names deliberately keep the legacy `Papercup` spelling) * `packages/operator-core/lib/harness/ensure-papercusp-hive.ts` — the **third** helper (see the B-merge note above) * `apps/operator/scripts/run-dogfood-bootstrap.ts` (one-shot manual driver) Caution **Update (2026-06):** The original boot wiring was the Next.js instrumentation hook (apps/operator/instrumentation-node.ts), which is **retired** along with the Next standalone operator. The two helper modules moved from apps/operator/lib/harness/ to `packages/operator-core/lib/harness/`. As of this audit there is **no live boot-time caller** of `ensurePapercuspWorkspace()` / `registerPapercupHarness()` in the operator source — they are exercised only by the one-shot driver `apps/operator/scripts/run-dogfood-bootstrap.ts` (npm `verify:dogfood-bootstrap`) and their unit tests. Run the driver manually to flip dogfooding on; the rest of this page (sentinel name, the scoped-write trick, `detectPapercupRoot`) is still accurate. **Update (2026-06, papercup→papercusp B-merge):** `register-papercup.ts` is now **`register-papercusp.ts`** (the exported fns `registerPapercupHarness` / `detectPapercupRoot` keep the legacy `Papercup` spelling on purpose). The driver now runs a **third** helper, `ensurePapercuspHive()` (`packages/operator-core/lib/harness/ensure-papercusp-hive.ts`), shipping Papercusp as a shared **hive** (slug `papercusp`). Because `papercusp` is that MERGED operator-home hive, `registerPapercupHarness` keeps `LEGACY_STANDALONE_HARNESS_SLUG = 'papercup'` (the pre-merge standalone slug, deliberately distinct from the hive) but **skips re-creating a separate `papercup` harness** once the merged `papercusp` hive exists — so a post-merge boot no longer dumps a duplicate `papercup` into the dropdown. The “two helpers” framing below is therefore now **three**. ## Why two helpers, not one [Section titled “Why two helpers, not one”](#why-two-helpers-not-one) They do different things: * **`ensurePapercuspWorkspace`** writes to `~/.papercusp-workspaces/registry.json` (file-backed) — the user’s list of workspaces. * **`registerPapercupHarness`** writes to PG (`harness_shared.harness_registry`) **scoped to** the sentinel workspace (not the active workspace) — the harness list within that workspace. Splitting them keeps each helper testable in isolation. The bootstrap calls them in order: sentinel ensure → register papercup as harness. ## The “scoped to the sentinel workspace, not active” trick [Section titled “The “scoped to the sentinel workspace, not active” trick”](#the-scoped-to-the-sentinel-workspace-not-active-trick) When you have multiple workspaces, the harness registry is per- workspace: each workspace has its own list of harnesses. The operator’s existing `saveHarnessRegistry()` defaulted to writing to the **active** workspace. If P-024 wrote to the active workspace, it would silently dump `papercup` into whichever workspace the user happened to be looking at — usually `default`. Bad: pollutes the user’s workspace. The fix (commit `b53185ee`): add an optional `workspaceId` param to `saveHarnessRegistry()` (additive, 100% back-compat across 52 call sites). The dogfood bootstrap passes `PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE_ID` explicitly so the write lands in the sentinel workspace regardless of which one is active. A symmetric `wsOverride?` was already on `readOperatorState`; this just closes the API asymmetry at the underlying `writeOperatorState` helper. ## How the papercup-root auto-detector works [Section titled “How the papercup-root auto-detector works”](#how-the-papercup-root-auto-detector-works) `detectPapercupRoot(start)` in `register-papercusp.ts` walks UP from the given directory looking for both markers: 
```ts
existsSync(join(dir, 'apps', 'operator', 'package.json'))
  && existsSync(join(dir, 'libs', 'papercusp', 'package.json'))
```
 Two markers because either alone could be coincidental in unrelated projects. Both together pin the directory to “this is the papercup repo.” Bounded to 8 levels up so it can’t unbounded-walk a weird filesystem. Returns `null` for packaged desktop installs where neither marker exists — the bootstrap silently skips with a `state: 'skipped'` result. ## When you touch this code [Section titled “When you touch this code”](#when-you-touch-this-code) * **Renaming the sentinel** (`papercusp-workspace` → anything else)? Bad idea: many future surfaces (Cupboard, plan dogfood docs, multi-machine reconciliation) hardcode the name as a stable reference. The constant is in `papercusp-workspace.ts` for the one place that needs it; don’t make it a per-install variable. * **Changing the markers** in `detectPapercupRoot`? Be conservative — the two-marker rule was chosen specifically to avoid false positives. Adding a 3rd marker is fine; removing one is risky. * **Adding a 3rd bootstrap helper** (e.g. auto-register sub-harnesses for papercup’s submodules)? Add it to the one-shot driver (`run-dogfood-bootstrap.ts`), alongside the existing two. Keep each helper idempotent. ## Verifying it works without restarting the operator [Section titled “Verifying it works without restarting the operator”](#verifying-it-works-without-restarting-the-operator) There’s a one-shot driver at `apps/operator/scripts/run-dogfood-bootstrap.ts`: 
```bash
cd apps/operator && npx tsx scripts/run-dogfood-bootstrap.ts
```
 Runs the same code paths the boot path runs. Prints the registry + PG state. Useful when: * You just made a change to the bootstrap helpers and want to verify it works against the live PG. * The running operator predates your changes (memory rule: don’t restart the user’s running dev server). The script exercises your new code without touching the operator process. * You’re debugging a “papercup isn’t showing up in the dropdown” symptom and want to confirm the PG row is there. Sample output: 
```plaintext
=== STEP 1: ensurePapercuspWorkspace ===
workspace entry: id=papercusp-workspace, name=papercusp-workspace, createdAt=...
workspaces total: 6, current: default
✓ sentinel 'papercusp-workspace' present in registry
=== STEP 2: registerPapercupHarness ===
state: already-registered
path: /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercup
=== STEP 3: verify PG row ===
harness_registry@papercusp-workspace: 1 projects
  - papercup  →  /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercup
✓ papercup registered in sentinel workspace
=== PASS — dogfooding flipped on ===
```
 ## Related [Section titled “Related”](#related) * `packages/operator-core/lib/harness/classify-tree.ts` — the 5-rule classifier for nested `.git` entries; uses the same `existsSync`-on-markers pattern. See [the classifier insight](/internal/docs/agent-insights/harness-tree-classifier). * v5 plan Phase 1a P-014 (workspace bootstrap) + Phase 4 P-024 (papercup self-registration). * `packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-registry.ts` — the underlying file- backed registry helpers. * `packages/operator-core/lib/operator-state-pg.ts` — `readOperatorState` / `writeOperatorState` with optional `wsOverride` for per-workspace scoping.

# Dogfood go-live runbooks — P-026 orchestrator run + P-051b Cupboard deploy

> Step-by-step runbooks for the two remaining user-driven dogfood items. P-026 is the first end-to-end orchestrator run on a real papercup feature; P-051b is the Cupboard server deploy. Both require user creds or live UI interaction — autonomous agents cannot complete them.

Caution **Update (2026-06):** This runbook references plan files dated 2026-05-24, which predate the autoloop retirement (2026-06-05). The director-cadence loop mechanism (`director-config.json`, autoloop `setInterval`, DBOS `autoloop-workflow.ts`) is **retired** — both loops are GONE. Step 4 in P-026 (letting autoloop pick the feature) no longer applies. Drive features manually via “Start working” + deliberate dispatch, or schedule via blueprint `triggers.schedule` instead. The rest of this runbook (pre-flight, run sequence, verification checklist, Cupboard deploy) remains valid. ## When this applies [Section titled “When this applies”](#when-this-applies) You (a human) want to drive Papercusp’s dogfood plan to substantial completion. The two remaining items below need either live UI clicks or external credentials (Cloudflare, DNS, GitHub OAuth secrets) that no agent has. Everything else is shipped + tested — these are the last threads. If you’re an agent reading this: do NOT try to run either runbook end-to-end. P-026 requires GitHub merges from the user’s account. P-051b requires Cloudflare + DNS creds. Both are user steps. Prep the surrounding code + verify the substrate is healthy, then hand off to a human. ## P-026 — first end-to-end orchestrator run on papercup [Section titled “P-026 — first end-to-end orchestrator run on papercup”](#p-026--first-end-to-end-orchestrator-run-on-papercup) **Plan:** `apps/operator/docs/plans/papercusp-dogfood-phase4-single-engineer-dogfood-2026-05-24.md`. ### Pre-flight [Section titled “Pre-flight”](#pre-flight) 1. **Substrate is on**: `PAPERCUSP_DOGFOOD_SUBSTRATE_ENABLE=1` in the running hono-host env. Check via `curl -s http://localhost:3070/api/admin/dogfood-substrate-status` → `enabled: true`. 2. **Papercup harness is registered**: see `harness_papercup` schema in PG. Check via `curl -s http://localhost:3070/api/harness/projects/lite | jq '.projects[] | select(.slug=="papercup")'`. 3. **F-DOGFOOD-001/002/003 exist in queue**: check via `curl -s http://localhost:3070/api/harness/papercup/features | jq '.[] | .id'`. 4. **Director config is set**: `papercup/.papercusp/director-config.json` should have `autoLoop: true` + `autoIntervalSeconds: 60` (or shorter for the run). Caution **Update (2026-06):** The `director-config.json` + `autoLoop:true` / `autoIntervalSeconds` cadence mechanism in pre-flight step 4 and run-sequence step 4 is **retired** (`autoloop-pot-operator-rebuild-2026-06-05`, P-009/P-010 D-009). Both director-cadence loops (the legacy in-process `setInterval` ticker in `autoloop.ts` and its DBOS twin `dbos/autoloop-workflow.ts`) are GONE — they read a `director-config.json` enablement surface nothing wrote. The surviving cadence path is the **blueprint** one: a harness’s blueprint declares `triggers.schedule`, `harness:create` materializes them into `harness_shared.routines`, and the durable DBOS `routinesTick` fires them. So ignore step 4 and “let autoloop pick it” — drive the feature manually (“Start working” + a deliberate dispatch) for the first run, or schedule it via the blueprint. The per-`(workspace, harness, role)` fire-state still lives on `harness_shared.autoloop_state` (now with read `consecutive_errors` backoff). ### Run sequence [Section titled “Run sequence”](#run-sequence) 1. **Open the papercup harness in the operator** (live Tauri shell): `http://localhost:3070/harness/papercup`. 2. **Pick the feature** to run end-to-end. F-DOGFOOD-002 or 003 are safer than 001 (which is the observations-capture feature itself and should stay in the queue indefinitely). 3. **Click “Start working”** on the feature’s row in the Queue column (P-038a). This adds you to the working\_users set; the orchestrator will exclude the feature from auto-pickup. 4. **OR: let autoloop pick it.** Skip step 3 if you want the orchestrator to drive autonomously. The autoloop fires the director every `autoIntervalSeconds`. Within \~5 min the director should dispatch a worker on the feature. 5. **Watch the lanes panel** in the harness dashboard. A new worker run should appear with `role: worker` + the feature id. 6. **When the worker finishes**, review the produced diff against the papercup repo (it’s a commit on the user’s branch under `<papercup-clone>/.papercusp/user-trees/<your-github-user-id>/`). 7. **Push + open a PR manually** (Phase 7 auto-PR is wired but the path is verified per-harness; manual is fine for the first run): 
   ```bash
   cd /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercup/.papercusp/user-trees/<github_user_id>
   git push -u origin user/<github_user_id>
   gh pr create --fill
   ```
 8. **Merge on GitHub** via the normal review flow. 9. **Within 60s of merge**, the Phase 2 verifier daemon stamps `completion_ref` on the feature row + flips status to `shipped`. Verify via the operator UI (tier-B ✓ badge appears) or `curl -s http://localhost:3070/api/harness/papercup/features/F-DOGFOOD-002 | jq '.feature.completion_ref'`. ### Verification checklist (P-026a–e) [Section titled “Verification checklist (P-026a–e)”](#verification-checklist-p-026ae) * [ ] P-026a — orchestrator picked the feature within 5 min OR I manually triggered it. * [ ] P-026b — worker run completed with a real diff. * [ ] P-026c — PR opened (auto or manual). * [ ] P-026d — PR merged on GitHub by me. * [ ] P-026e — `completion_ref` populated + status flipped to shipped within 60s of merge. * [ ] P-026f — record total wall-clock time as a data point. ### Likely friction points [Section titled “Likely friction points”](#likely-friction-points) * **Orchestrator pick latency**: if no worker dispatched after 5 min, check `harness_shared.autoloop_state` and the director config. * **Worker prompt quality on a real codebase**: papercup is large + has 175+ tables. First run may produce a noisy diff. Note in F-DOGFOOD-001 observations. * **`completion_ref` not stamping**: confirm the verifier daemon is running. Check `packages/operator-core/lib/harness/completion-ref-verifier.ts` * the daemon’s logs. ### Then update Phase 4 plan [Section titled “Then update Phase 4 plan”](#then-update-phase-4-plan) After P-026 lands (or fails meaningfully), run P-027 (observe pain points → F-DOGFOOD-001 comments) + P-028 (gate verdict). Update `papercusp-dogfood-phase4-single-engineer-dogfood-2026-05-24.md`’s `## Now` accordingly. *** ## P-051b — Cupboard server deploy to Cloudflare Workers + D1 [Section titled “P-051b — Cupboard server deploy to Cloudflare Workers + D1”](#p-051b--cupboard-server-deploy-to-cloudflare-workers--d1) **Plan:** `apps/operator/docs/plans/papercusp-dogfood-phase9-cupboard-discord-sync-2026-05-24.md`. **Code:** `apps/operator-public/` (already shipped 2026-05-25 — Hono on Cloudflare Workers + D1, 18 server tests + 14 indexer tests). ### Pre-flight [Section titled “Pre-flight”](#pre-flight-1) 1. **Cloudflare account** with Workers + D1 enabled. 2. **`wrangler` CLI** authenticated: `wrangler whoami`. 3. **DNS for the hostname** you’ll bind (e.g. `cupboard.papercusp.dev`). 4. **GitHub OAuth app** with client id + secret. Used for the `gh-bearer` auth on publish / claim / report endpoints. ### Deploy sequence [Section titled “Deploy sequence”](#deploy-sequence) 
```bash
cd apps/operator-public

wrangler d1 create papercusp-cupboard
wrangler kv:namespace create papercusp-cupboard-counters

npm run d1:apply:remote


# 3. Set secrets.

# 7. Verify.

```
 ### Verification checklist (P-051b-1/2/3) [Section titled “Verification checklist (P-051b-1/2/3)”](#verification-checklist-p-051b-123) * [ ] P-051b-1 — Worker live at chosen hostname with TLS (`curl https://<hostname>/healthz` returns 200). * [ ] P-051b-2 — D1 backups: D1 has automatic point-in-time recovery enabled by default; verify in CF dashboard. Test by opening the ShareWizard, picking `shared-public`, and confirming the publish goes through. ### Cron + indexer [Section titled “Cron + indexer”](#cron--indexer) The hourly stats indexer runs as a Workers Cron Trigger (configured in `wrangler.toml` as `0 * * * *`). The first cron tick after deploy will refresh tier-A stats for any listed harnesses. Check via `wrangler tail` or the CF dashboard Cron logs. ### What deploys today even with zero listings [Section titled “What deploys today even with zero listings”](#what-deploys-today-even-with-zero-listings) The endpoints are live but `GET /harnesses` returns `[]` until someone publishes via the ShareWizard. That’s expected. Publish flow: desktop operator’s ShareWizard step 9 → POST `/api/harness/cupboard/publish` (operator proxy) → POST `https://<hostname>/harnesses` (Cupboard) with the user’s gh token. Browser never sees the token. ### After deploy: update Phase 9 plan [Section titled “After deploy: update Phase 9 plan”](#after-deploy-update-phase-9-plan) Flip `papercusp-dogfood-phase9-cupboard-discord-sync-2026-05-24.md` frontmatter `status: shipped` (or wait until first real publish lands successfully end-to-end). *** ## Why these are NOT autonomous agent pickups [Section titled “Why these are NOT autonomous agent pickups”](#why-these-are-not-autonomous-agent-pickups) Both items require state outside the agent’s reach: * **P-026** needs (a) a GitHub merge to happen, which only the user’s GitHub identity can authorize, and (b) judgment on whether the worker’s diff is acceptable (the user owns the gate before merging). * **P-051b** needs (a) a Cloudflare account the agent can’t auth into, (b) DNS that only the domain owner can edit, and (c) GitHub OAuth secrets that should never leave the user’s secret store. An agent CAN: verify the substrate is healthy, document the runbooks (this file), prep + commit any code changes that make the runbooks shorter. The agent CANNOT push the deploy or merge the PR.

# Driving the autonomous hive loop — health-check + schema runbook

> The 6-link health-check, exact tool names/args, force-tick + reset-circuit commands, a verified schema cheat-sheet, and the bg-host-drops-MCP→psql gotcha for any agent monitoring/improving the autonomous hive loop.

The autonomous **hive loop** is Papercusp dogfooding itself: the system generates its own work, places it, does it, and learns from it — with no human in the cycle. If you are the agent set on “monitor + improve the loop until it’s reliable,” this is your runbook. It exists because the same handful of schema-guesses and wrong tool names have burned multiple sessions **hours** of avoidable rework (audit 2026-07-01, W1–W3/W6/H5). Read it first; do **not** re-discover the schema by trial and error. > **Golden rule for a loop-monitor wake:** ONE batched, schema-correct health check → ONE decisive action → **end the turn**. The engine loop re-fires \~120s *after your turn settles*, so a long turn = a slow loop. Deep-diving every wake is the #1 way the cadence stretches to 30–60 min/cycle. Don’t block a cycle on a long subagent. ## The 6 links (what “the loop” actually is) [Section titled “The 6 links (what “the loop” actually is)”](#the-6-links-what-the-loop-actually-is) 
```plaintext
observation/completion ─► scout ─► route (plan | improvement | gym) ─► queen ─► bee ─► complete ─► observation
                                                                                         ▲
                                          overwatch (meta-monitor) watches ALL of it ────┘
                                          and emits the `hive-coordination-health` scorecard
```
 * **Feedback half** = scout: reads the corpus (observations, completions, patterns) and *routes* ideas onto one of three rails — `plan`, `improvement`, or `gym`. * **Forward half** = queen → bee: the Queen *places* ranked work onto generic bees; a bee does it and `complete`s; the completion feeds the next scout cycle. * **Overwatch** = the meta-monitor. Every wake it surveys system health and emits a 14-criterion `hive-coordination-health` scorecard, then acts on anomalies (files an observation, escalates, etc.). It is the thing that catches a *stalled Queen*. A “clean full cycle” (the reliability bar) is: an observation/completion → scout routes it → queen places it → a bee completes it → it lands as a new completion/observation, WITH overwatch emitting a real (non-synthesized) scorecard in the same window. ## The 6-link health check (schema-correct — copy these) [Section titled “The 6-link health check (schema-correct — copy these)”](#the-6-link-health-check-schema-correct--copy-these) All of these run under `dev:pg_query` (read-only SELECT, 5s timeout) or `psql` on the bg-host `DATABASE_URL`. **Every table below lives in the `harness_shared` schema.** Normalize timestamps to one TZ to avoid the UTC-vs-EDT misjudgement (audit W7): compare against `now()` inside the same query. **Link 1 — scout tick (is the feedback clock running?)** The live scout is the `@singleton` routine, NOT the dormant per-harness `scout-cycle` (see cheat-sheet): 
```sql
select id, active, trigger_config->>'cron' as cron, last_fired_at, next_fire_at,
       now() - last_fired_at as since_last
from harness_shared.routines
where id = 'rt__singleton_bp_singleton_scout_0';
-- healthy: active=true, cron '0 */30 * * * *', last_fired within ~30m, next_fire in the future.
```
 **Link 2 — scout rail mix (is it routing, and to what?)** `routed_at` is **BIGINT epoch-ms**: 
```sql
select rail, count(*),
       to_timestamp(max(routed_at)/1000) as newest
from harness_shared.scout_routed_ideas
where routed_at > (extract(epoch from now())*1000 - 24*3600*1000)
group by rail order by count(*) desc;
-- expect a mix across plan/improvement/gym over 24h; all-zero for hours = scout stalled or gated.
```
 **Link 3 — queen wake + placements (is the forward half moving?)** The Queen’s watchdog fallback is the `wake-brain` routine (`0 */30 * * * *`). Placements = work\_items a bee has taken recently (`taken_by`, `taken_at`): 
```sql
select last_fired_at, next_fire_at from harness_shared.routines where name = 'wake-brain';


-- ⚠ TERMINAL STATUS IS FAMILY-SPECIFIC (verified 2026-07-02): issue-family
-- (bug/change) resolves to 'resolved'/'closed'; feature-family to 'passed'.
-- Counting only status='done' reads a HEALTHY loop as "zero completions" —
-- an su burned a wake concluding the forward half was stalled when 9
-- completions had landed that hour. Count the whole terminal set:
select count(*) filter (where taken_by is not null) as taken,
       count(*) filter (where status in ('done','resolved','closed','passed')
             and updated_ts > extract(epoch from now())*1000 - 3600*1000) as done_1h
from harness_shared.work_items
where harness_slug = 'papercusp';
```
 **Link 4 — cursed / infra-loss placements (are bees dying?)** Prefer the typed tool — `hive:status` and `fleet:capacity` surface the cursed count and free slots directly. The per-item infra-breaker trips at `infra_loss_count = 12` (`infraBreakerThreshold`); a rising cursed count means bees are dying mid-placement (OOM / reaper-requeue), not a capacity wall. **Link 5 — overwatch freshness (is the meta-monitor really emitting?)** A synthesized floor scorecard is NOT a healthy signal — it’s the backstop firing because the real turn didn’t emit: 
```sql
select role, last_fired_at, last_status, consecutive_errors
from harness_shared.autoloop_state
where harness_slug = 'papercusp' and role = 'overwatch';
```
 Or, typed: `scorecards:freshness { rubricRef: 'hive-coordination-health', since: <overwatch last wake> }` → `fresh` (a COMPLETE real scorecard landed), `partial-only` (silent truncation), or `stale` (nothing landed). In `scorecards:list`/`:freshness`, **`synthesized:false` = a REAL agent scorecard**; `synthesized:true` = the derived floor. A `last_status` of “no complete scorecard within 180000ms launch deadline; backstop synthesized” means the overwatch turn didn’t finish in time — check the gateway (`:8788`) and the model window before assuming the fix regressed. **Link 6 — deploy position (is your fix live on :3070?)** Never idle waiting for the pipeline — `dev:pipeline_position { path }` tells you committed / on-staging / in-main / deployed in one call. Force it when a fix must be live to proceed (see the deploy runbook: `git-sync:run` → `release:checkpoint-run` → `release:deploy { op:'trigger' }`). ## Exact tool names + args (the ones people get wrong) [Section titled “Exact tool names + args (the ones people get wrong)”](#exact-tool-names--args-the-ones-people-get-wrong) * **There is no `overwatch:status`.** Read overwatch health via `autoloop:status { harnessSlug }` (role `overwatch`), `scorecards:freshness`, and `hive:status`. Control it with `overwatch:start` / `overwatch:pause` / `overwatch:declare-wake`. * **`plans:*` and `docs:*` need a concrete `harness` in a workspace-scoped session.** Pass `harness: 'papercusp'` — **`harness: 'all'` is FORBIDDEN** here (`harness_forbidden`); `'all'` only works in an unscoped (`--all-workspaces`) session. * **`docs:author` writes to the DOC surface of the `harness` you pass — which for a managed harness may be a DIFFERENT repo than the canonical engineering reference.** Papercusp engineering runbooks (this one included) belong in `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/` in the `papercusp` staging tree. If `docs:author` reports an `absPath` outside that tree (e.g. a sibling `hive-canary/docs`), the file is stranded — write the MDX directly to the canonical path instead and `cd apps/operator-docs && npm run build`. * **In `code:run`, verbs are camelCase**: `tools.dev.pgQuery`, `tools.dev.pipelinePosition`, `tools.hive.controlPolicy`, `tools.autoloop.status`, `tools.scorecards.freshness`. (The MCP wire names are colon-kebab: `dev:pg_query`, `hive:control_policy`.) * **Reset a gated error circuit:** `autoloop:control { op: 'reset-errors', role: '<scout-cycle|overwatch>', harness: '<papercusp|papercusp-workspace>' }` (zeroes `consecutive_errors` so backoff stops withholding fires). * **Force a routine fire NOW:** `git-sync:run` (git-sync) and `release:checkpoint-run` (green-checkpoint) are the sanctioned fire-now levers. For scout/overwatch there is no fire-now verb yet — set `next_fire_at = now()` via psql (below), or `hive:wake` to nudge the Queen. `routines:set` retunes cron / pauses, it does not fire. ## Force-tick + reset via psql (when the MCP is down) [Section titled “Force-tick + reset via psql (when the MCP is down)”](#force-tick--reset-via-psql-when-the-mcp-is-down) 
```sql
-- force the singleton scout to fire on the next tick (catchup=skip-old, no burst):
update harness_shared.routines set next_fire_at = now()
where id = 'rt__singleton_bp_singleton_scout_0';
```
 ## Schema cheat-sheet (VERIFIED against information\_schema 2026-07-01) [Section titled “Schema cheat-sheet (VERIFIED against information\_schema 2026-07-01)”](#schema-cheat-sheet-verified-against-information_schema-2026-07-01) | table (`harness_shared.`) | gotcha | | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `scout_routed_ideas` | `routed_at`, `outcome_checked_at` are **BIGINT epoch-ms** — there is NO `created_at`. `graded_at` is timestamptz. Columns: `rail`, `lens`, `routed_ref`, `outcome`, `cycle_id`, `source_hive`. | | `work_items` | PK is **`feature_id`** (text), not `id`. Raw SQL status column is **`status`** — but the `work_items:get` MCP returns it as **`.state`**. **Terminal statuses are FAMILY-SPECIFIC**: issue-family (bug/change) → `resolved`/`closed`, feature-family → `passed` — `'done'` alone undercounts (see Link 3). A terminal `set_state` REQUIRES a completion record — use `work_items:complete { id, state, completion:{ summary, status } }`; ⚠ `complete` WITHOUT `state` returns ok:true but writes NOTHING (EI-6502). `ts` / `created_ts` / `updated_ts` / `fed_ts` are **BIGINT epoch-ms**; claims use `taken_by` + `taken_at` (timestamptz). `source_plan_slug` / `source_plan_item_ids` (array) link back to a plan. | | `routines` | cron lives in **`trigger_config->>'cron'`** (jsonb), not a `cron` column. `last_fired_at` / `next_fire_at` are **timestamptz** (note: `last_fired_at`, not `last_fire_at`). `id`, `install_slug`, `name`, `active` (bool), `target_role`, `catchup`. | | `autoloop_state` | `harness_slug`, `role`, `last_fired_at` (timestamptz), `last_status` (text), `consecutive_errors` (int). NO `next_fire_at` here — that’s on `routines`. | * **The overwatch rubric `hive-coordination-health` is a CODE CONSTANT**, not a rubric-registry row: `COORDINATION_RUBRIC_REF` in `packages/operator-core/lib/overwatch/scorecard-backstop.ts` (14 criterion keys). Don’t look for it in `rubrics:list`. * **Two scout routines exist — don’t confuse them.** The LIVE one is install `@singleton`, id `rt__singleton_bp_singleton_scout_0`, name `bp-singleton-scout-0`, `0 */30 * * * *`, active. The per-harness `rt_papercusp_scout_cycle` (name `scout-cycle`) is **dormant** (`active:false`) — a decoy. ## The bg-host gotcha (why the MCP vanishes mid-session) [Section titled “The bg-host gotcha (why the MCP vanishes mid-session)”](#the-bg-host-gotcha-why-the-mcp-vanishes-mid-session) A **deploy restarts the bg-host**, which **drops the `papercusp-su` MCP and the loop’s psu-socket wake for minutes** (\~6-min boot). Worse, when the MCP drops mid-turn its tools may not even be *deferred* (ToolSearch finds none), so you cannot reconnect mid-turn — wait for a fresh wake, or fall back to `psql`. **`loop:arm` survives the restart and re-fires on reconnect**, so the loop itself is not lost. Get an MCP-independent DB handle with: 
```bash
export DATABASE_URL=$(tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$(systemctl --user show papercup-bg-host.service -p MainPID --value)/environ | grep '^DATABASE_URL=' | cut -d= -f2-)
```
 ## Failure-signal decoding (don’t chase the wrong ghost) [Section titled “Failure-signal decoding (don’t chase the wrong ghost)”](#failure-signal-decoding-dont-chase-the-wrong-ghost) * **“Prompt is too long” is NOT a 429 / gateway stall.** As of `autonomous-loop-hardening` F1, a prompt-length death classifies `context_overflow` (a LAUNCH-CONFIG bug — too many tokens loaded, e.g. an unscoped MCP toolset on a small-context model), recorded distinctly from `capacity_shed`/`infra_loss`. See `packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/invoke-outcome.ts`. If overwatch (or any spawn) dies this way, fix the **tool-scoping** (`OVERWATCH_MCP_TOOL_NAMES` in `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/invoke.ts`), not gateway capacity. * **A “rate limit” is usually account-routing, not real capacity.** Verify with `accounts:status` + `dev:rate_governor_status` before concluding you’re capacity-gated — other accounts usually have headroom (`agent-insights/rate-limit-is-usually-account-routing-not-capacity`). * **The recorded error is authoritative — read it first.** `autoloop_state.last_status` (and the work-item’s error) already carries the verbatim failure. Don’t go log-spelunking `.out` files (often stale / wrong-tree) before reading the recorded status (audit W3). * **A `CHRONIC autoloop failure: loop-su-…` EI is usually ALREADY self-resolved by the time you read it.** These are auto-filed by the chronic-failure escalator (`autoloop-chronic-failure.ts`) at `consecutive_errors >= 6`. The common cause is a **dead-owner loop** — the pinned warm su-session died, so every fire stuck-backstops. The WI-1399 dead-owner terminal guard (`loop-unreachable-guard.ts`) then auto-pauses the routine (`routines.active=false`, `last_status='loop-terminal-unreachable'`), but only after its \~4h window — *later* than the escalator’s \~3h fire, so the EI is filed in the pre-termination window and self-resolves. **Before touching anything, verify it’s already dead:** (1) the routine `active=false` (`SELECT active FROM harness_shared.routines WHERE name=<role> AND workspace_id=<ws>`), and (2) the owner `adv_session` actually `ended_at` and never restarted (confirms the terminal-unreachable verdict was correct, not a false kill). If both hold, the reported live-failure condition is GONE — a dead-owner loop *should* be dead. Close the hygiene with `autoloop:control reset-errors` (or a targeted single-row `consecutive_errors=0` UPDATE for a `*`-scoped brain row the tool can’t target). Once `active=false`, the (twice-hardened) watchdog already **skips** the row (skipped-paused), so it will NOT re-escalate. The **durable class fix** (stop the escalator firing for a dead-owner loop the terminal guard is about to own) touches the self-improvement watchdog + routines scheduler = protected surface — it is tracked as a `change` (EI-7016), not an auto-implement; don’t re-file per-loop dupes.

# Dropping a harness_shared column — the 4-place procedure

> A DROP COLUMN migration alone fails the fresh-migrate STRICT gate. Sync 4 places (migration, 000-baseline, generated.ts, schema.ts), unfreeze SELECT* views, grep pg_proc bodies, and boot-apply via dev:restart.

## What [Section titled “What”](#what) Dropping a `harness_shared.*` column in papercup touches **4 places**, not 1 — a plain `DROP COLUMN` migration alone fails the `fresh-migrate.integration` STRICT gate. First proven on migration **155** (drop `harness_features_consolidated.blocked_by`, plan `harness-blueprint-orchestration-2026-06-03` P-020/EI-1). ## The 4 consistency points (same change, same tick) [Section titled “The 4 consistency points (same change, same tick)”](#the-4-consistency-points-same-change-same-tick) 1. **The migration** — `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/<NNN>-*.sql`. Reserve the number via `db:next-migration` (never max-on-disk+1; it collides with peers’ reservations). 2. **`000-baseline.sql`** — the squashed dump still defines the column + its indexes. Re-applying baseline RAW on the post-drop head fails (`CREATE INDEX … (col)` → “column does not exist”; the `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op so it doesn’t re-add the column). The fresh-migrate “re-applying 000-baseline.sql RAW is a clean no-op” gate catches this. → **Surgically remove the column def + any index from baseline.** There is no baseline-regen CI compare (`verify-baseline.ts` only counts tables), so a hand-edit is safe. A full live-dump regen is the WRONG scope — it folds in every peer’s un-regenerated migration. 3. **`src/schema/generated.ts`** — the canonical drizzle mirror (runtime imports it via `schema/index.ts`). `pull-schema.mjs` regenerates it but the file is stale fleet-wide (peers don’t run it), so **surgical-edit** the column + index out; don’t full-regen. 4. **`src/schema/schema.ts`** — the raw drizzle-kit introspect intermediate (not imported, but keep it consistent). Same surgical edit. ## Two hazards that bite [Section titled “Two hazards that bite”](#two-hazards-that-bite) * **`SELECT *` views freeze their column list at CREATE.** `work_items` is `SELECT * FROM harness_features_consolidated` (migration 136) — created after the column existed, so it froze it and PG refuses the `DROP COLUMN` while the view lists it. The migration must `DROP VIEW` → `DROP COLUMN` → recreate the view. Views frozen *before* the column existed don’t list it — verify live with `information_schema.view_column_usage WHERE column_name='<col>'`. * **Function/trigger bodies aren’t in pg\_depend.** Grep `pg_proc.prosrc ILIKE '%<col>%'` live before dropping — `DROP … CASCADE` does not rewrite function bodies that name the column. ## Applying live [Section titled “Applying live”](#applying-live) The native `:5432` dev box **boot-applies pending migrations on `dev:restart`** (`papercup-dev-api.service`). Restart FIRST so new code stops reading the column before the drop lands (no error window), then check `notifications:recent { level: 'error' }`. ## Provenance [Section titled “Provenance”](#provenance) Lifted from the Claude memory archive (`project_drop_baseline_column_procedure`, 2026-06-04) during the claude-memory-projection-integration boundary split — runbooks live here, not in per-client memory.

# The dynamic tool surface — small seed + expand on demand

> How a seeded MCP session grows its tool list at runtime (tools:find → tools/list_changed → client re-fetch) instead of choosing between focus, token cost, and reachability. Plus tools:invoke, the universal reachability hatch. Retires the "static ?tools= trim strands the long tail" caveat.

## The problem — a trilemma [Section titled “The problem — a trilemma”](#the-problem--a-trilemma) The superuser MCP catalog is \~580 tools / \~140k tokens. Three costs compete, and every **static** approach can only buy two: 1. **Reachability** — a client can only *call* a tool it received in `tools/list` (OMP returns `toolNotFound`; a trimmed session’s `search_tool_bm25` returns only the received set). 2. **Token cost** — sending all \~580 schemas is \~140k tokens every turn — billed *and* attention-diluting — **even on a big-context model** (Codex). 3. **Focus** — a weak model handed \~580 choices hallucinates tool names. Static `?tools=core` bought token+focus but stranded the \~530-tool tail. The full catalog bought reachability but paid token+focus. **The dynamic surface buys all three.** ## The mechanism — a growable seed [Section titled “The mechanism — a growable seed”](#the-mechanism--a-growable-seed) `?tools=<core spine>` on the MCP URL is no longer a hard cap; it’s a **seed floor** that grows at runtime: 1. **Seed.** `role-launch-spec` / `psu-launcher` bake `?tools=<CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES>` into the session’s MCP URL. The core spine includes `tools:find` (discover) and `tools:invoke` (call-anything). 2. **Track.** On the first `tools/list`, `getSessionSurface(uiClientId, seed)` (`tool-allowlist.ts`) creates a **mutable per-session set**, keyed by the su session identity (`uiClientId` = `x-papercusp-client` header / `client=` / the transport session id). It’s the floor for that connection. 3. **Grow.** When the model calls `tools:find("<intent>")`, the handler calls `ctx.activateTools(hits)` → `activateSessionTools` adds the matched names to the session set **and** fires `notifications/tools/list_changed`. 4. **Re-fetch.** A `listChanged`-capable client re-fetches `tools/list`, `getSessionSurface` returns the grown set, and the surfaced tools are now callable — natively, no indirection. `MCP_SERVER_CAPABILITIES` declares `tools: { listChanged: true }` — the flag the client checks before it will act on the notification. ### The universal hatch — `tools:invoke` [Section titled “The universal hatch — tools:invoke”](#the-universal-hatch--toolsinvoke) `tools:invoke { name, args }` dispatches to ANY projected tool server-side, under the caller’s OWN context (via `ctx.dispatchTool` → `dispatchProjectedToolToMcp`), so it’s gated **exactly** as a direct call — a router, not a privilege bypass. It reaches the whole catalog even on a client that never grows its own tool list, so `tools:find` (get the name+schema) → `tools:invoke` (call it) works regardless of `list_changed` support. ## Per-client — heterogeneous by design [Section titled “Per-client — heterogeneous by design”](#per-client--heterogeneous-by-design) | Client | Mechanism | Notes | | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **OMP** | dynamic surface (`list_changed`) | **Verified live**: `refreshServerTools` re-fetches on the notification, rebuilds + installs the callable set. Seeds by default (its weak-model default; `psu-launcher`). | | **Codex** | seed + `tools:invoke` (+ dynamic if it re-fetches) | Seeds **by default on any tier** for the token-cost win (`role-launch-spec`, `input.agent==='codex'`). Recognizes `list_changed`; `tools:invoke` guarantees reachability regardless. `contextSize:'full'` opts back into the full catalog. | | **Claude** | native **ToolSearch** — untouched | NOT default-seeded. ToolSearch is the same defer-then-activate pattern client-side and better for Claude (no round-trip). It never gets a seed on frontier tiers, so no `list_changed` is fired at it. | The mechanism is **gated by seed-presence**: no `?tools=` ⇒ `getSessionSurface` returns `null` (full catalog, no surface tracked) ⇒ `activateSessionTools` no-ops ⇒ no notification. That’s why Claude-on-frontier is automatically untouched. ## Verified (2026-07-01, live against :3170) [Section titled “Verified (2026-07-01, live against :3170)”](#verified-2026-07-01-live-against-3170) A full round-trip over the real streamable-HTTP transport: * `capabilities.tools.listChanged === true` * seeded `tools/list` = exactly the 3-tool seed * `tools:find("set a feature flag")` → `activated:true`, surfaced `flags:set` + 4 more * **`notifications/tools/list_changed` delivered on `tools:find`’s response stream** (the #1 risk — notifications ride the per-request event-stream, same as `emit`/`progress`; SSE transport stays disabled) * re-fetched `tools/list` = 8 tools (3 seed + 5 surfaced) * a mid-session-surfaced tool dispatched server-side (reachability end-to-end) ## Gotchas [Section titled “Gotchas”](#gotchas) * **The notification rides the per-request stream**, not a persistent SSE channel (`disableSse: true` — no Redis). It’s fired via the same `sendNotification` as `emit`/`progress`, but **not** gated on a `progressToken` (it’s session-level). The surfaced tool becomes callable on the *next* turn — a 1-turn latency that matches the natural find→call flow. * **Session key = `uiClientId`**, resolved identically in `tools/list` (`spawnRes.ctx.uiClientId`) and the tool ctx (`spawn.uiClientId`). A session without a stable id falls back to static behavior (the seed can’t grow). * **The seed is an invariant floor** — every `tools/list` re-adds it, so a config change that widens the seed only widens the floor; growth is preserved. * **Per-session state is ephemeral** (an in-memory Map, the per-connection exception to the Postgres storage policy), swept on a lazy TTL + hard cap. * **`activateSessionTools` only grows an already-seeded session** — an un-seeded (full-catalog / Claude) session has no entry, so activation and the notification both no-op. This is the D-005 guarantee, enforced by construction.

# Editing an already-applied migration is INERT — change a view/DDL with a NEW migration

> A CREATE VIEW / DDL fix typed into an old sql/<NNN> file that's already in schema_migrations never reaches the live DB. The runner skips applied files by name. Add a new NNN migration with CREATE OR REPLACE; the in-place edit only helps fresh installs and silently passes fresh-DB integration tests while the live view stays stale.

## The trap (live, EI-395, 2026-06-13) [Section titled “The trap (live, EI-395, 2026-06-13)”](#the-trap-live-ei-395-2026-06-13) `fleet:assignments` flagged the `improvement-runner` routine’s parked claims as orphaned (a live lease whose holder never heartbeats), which nearly bulk-swept the paused improvement-implement lane. A prior agent “fixed” it by **editing the already-applied migration** `225-fleet-assignment-nursery-alias-liveness.sql` in place — adding `AND owner NOT IN ('improvement-runner')` to the view’s `orphaned` clause (committed 02:20). The fix looked done: the file was correct, and a fresh-DB integration test (which builds the schema from all `sql/*.sql`) would go green. But the **live DB never changed.** Migration 225 was applied days earlier and is recorded in `harness_shared.schema_migrations`; the boot-apply / deploy runner **skips files already in that ledger by filename**. Editing the body of an applied migration is a no-op on every existing DB. `pg_get_viewdef` confirmed the live view still had the un-excluded `orphaned` clause and improvement-runner’s 48 claims still read `orphaned=true`. ## The rule [Section titled “The rule”](#the-rule) To change a view (or any DDL) that a prior migration already defined: 1. **Reserve a new number** — `db:next-migration` (races-safe; never `ls | tail`). 2. **Write a new `sql/<NNN>` with `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW …`** carrying the full, current view body. The latest migration is the single owner of the view def. 3. **Revert the in-place edit** to the old migration so it stays faithful to what it applied (and so two files don’t both claim to own the view). Fresh installs then run old-then-new and converge; existing DBs get the new one only. 4. **`pull-schema`** (`libs/papercusp/libs/db/scripts/pull-schema.mjs`) to refresh `generated.ts`. A view change touches only the view’s `.as(sql\`…\`)\` block — revert any unrelated drift (e.g. an index opclass flip) pull-schema also picks up. ## Verify against the LIVE DB, not the file [Section titled “Verify against the LIVE DB, not the file”](#verify-against-the-live-db-not-the-file) The file is not the source of truth for a running system — the catalog is: 
```bash
PGPASSWORD=harness_admin_pwd psql -U harness_admin -h localhost -d papercusp -tAc \
  "SELECT pg_get_viewdef('harness_shared.fleet_assignment'::regclass);"
```
 (`postgresql://harness_admin:harness_admin_pwd@localhost:5432/papercusp` is the dev-box native fallback — `embedded-pg-discovery.ts` `NATIVE_FALLBACK`.) Grepping the migration file, or even grepping the viewdef for a string that lives in a comment, will lie to you — read the actual computed clause / a representative row. ## Applying it live [Section titled “Applying it live”](#applying-it-live) `db:migrate { confirm:true }` drains correctly but reports `applied:false` unless `PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DB_MIGRATE=1` is set in the serving operator’s env (the dev box doesn’t). See [staging-restart-does-not-boot-apply-migrations](/internal/docs/agent-insights/staging-restart-does-not-boot-apply-migrations) for the blessed direct path (`applyPendingMigrations` from `@papercusp/embedded-postgres-server` — idempotent, ledger-recording, NOT raw `psql -f`). If you do fall back to `psql -f`, INSERT the `schema_migrations` row (filename + `sha256sum` of the file + `now()`) in the **same transaction**, or the deploy re-runs it — and a re-run of un-guarded `GRANT`/`ALTER`/`POLICY` DDL can hit `lock_timeout` and roll back the whole deploy (see [migration-reapply-lock-guards](/internal/docs/agent-insights/migration-reapply-lock-guards)). A `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` body is idempotent, so a recorded re-run is harmless.

# Never hardcode PG port — read embedded-pg.json

> Embedded Postgres uses a discovered port written to ~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json on desktop boot. Hardcoding :5432 or :16534 breaks on any machine that wasn't the one you wrote the code on.

## What [Section titled “What”](#what) Papercusp ships with **embedded Postgres**, not a host-installed PG. On desktop boot, the embedded-pg process picks an available port and writes its connection info to: 
```plaintext
~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json
```
 Agents and the webapp resolve the connection via `getHarnessAdminUrl()` (from `packages/operator-core/lib/embedded-pg-discovery.ts`; the generic resolver is `resolvePgUrl` in `libs/generic/embedded-pg-discovery`), which reads this file. `getHarnessPg(slug)` (per-harness scoped) lives in `libs/papercusp/libs/db/src/connection.ts`. The port is **not** stable — it can shift between boots, machines, and Papercusp installs. ### Caching: only the `env` source is safe to pin — re-read `discovery`/`fallback` every call [Section titled “Caching: only the env source is safe to pin — re-read discovery/fallback every call”](#caching-only-the-env-source-is-safe-to-pin--re-read-discoveryfallback-every-call) `getHarnessAdminUrlWithSource()` caches its result **only** when the resolved source is `env` (`HARNESS_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL` etc. — injected once by Tauri main and stable for the process lifetime). A `discovery-file` or `fallback` result is **re-resolved on every call** — never cached. This isn’t incidental: the embedded-pg.json port genuinely *changes* across boots (the desktop’s Rust main picks a fresh free port each launch), and a caller that memoized an early `discovery`/`fallback` read (e.g. before `serve` rewrote the discovery file for *this* boot) would pin a previous launch’s stale port for the whole process lifetime. That exact bug wedged every later LISTEN/query on a dead port on Windows/WSL — the WSL distro persists the prior-boot `embedded-pg.json` across launches, so a memoized early read is guaranteed stale there (fixed 2026-07-02). `connection.ts`’s `adminUrl()` / `appUrl()` follow the identical contract: cache `env`, re-read + invalidate the cached pool on every `discovery` change, never cache the native fallback. If you write a NEW caller around `resolvePgUrl`, mirror this — memoizing a `discovery`/`fallback` result is the bug class to avoid. ## Why it matters [Section titled “Why it matters”](#why-it-matters) Code that hardcodes `:5432` (host PG default) or `:16534` (an older embedded-pg default we’ve seen) works on the developer’s laptop and **breaks silently on every other machine**. Symptoms: * “Connection refused” on a freshly cloned machine. * Tests that pass locally and fail in CI. * An agent’s `psql` invocation that returns nothing because it connected to the *wrong* PG instance — possibly the user’s unrelated host PG, leading to confusing query results. The native-PG path (`:5432`) is also being retired (memory: `project_papercusp_pg_topology` — “public release = desktop + embedded-pg only; native PG :5432 + webapp are dev crutches going away”). Don’t assume it’ll be there. ## How to apply [Section titled “How to apply”](#how-to-apply) * **Always resolve PG connections through `getHarnessAdminUrl()`** (admin role) or `getHarnessPg(slug)` (per-harness scoped). * **For shell scripts**, read the JSON directly. The discovery file holds a single resolved DSN under `.url` (the resolver reads `parsed.url`), so feed it straight to psql: 
  ```bash
  psql "$(jq -r .url ~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json)"
  ```
 * **Never write a config file** that bakes a PG port at install time. Resolve at runtime. * If embedded-pg.json doesn’t exist, the desktop hasn’t been booted yet — surface that to the user rather than falling back to `:5432`.

# Embedder cost: insufficient_quota ≠ rate-limit, and the spend backstop

> OpenAI returns HTTP 429 for BOTH a transient rate-limit AND a permanent insufficient_quota (out of billing credit) — don't conflate them. Production embedding costs cents/month; a large "embeddings" bill is the benchmark, not steady-state. The embed-admission governor now carries a hard daily token cap, embed-backfill is governed + keyed by PK (not ctid), and a 429 insufficient_quota fails fast as embed_quota_exhausted.

## The gotcha: OpenAI 429 means two unrelated things [Section titled “The gotcha: OpenAI 429 means two unrelated things”](#the-gotcha-openai-429-means-two-unrelated-things) `POST /v1/embeddings` returns **HTTP 429** for two conditions that need opposite handling: * **`rate_limit_exceeded`** — transient. Capacity exists; back off and retry and it clears. * **`insufficient_quota`** — permanent until you act. The account is out of credit or hit its monthly billing cap. It fails **identically on every request, one or a thousand, regardless of load**, until billing is fixed. Danger Lumping all 429s into one “rate-limited, retrying” bucket once sent a multi-hour investigation down the throughput/sharing path when the real fix was **“the account ran out of credit — add billing.”** The key was valid (`/v1/models` → 200) and the box was idle, yet every embed 429’d. Always read the response **body** — `insufficient_quota` is in the error `type`/`code` — before assuming a rate problem. `buildOpenAiEmbedder` (`memory/configure.ts`) now distinguishes them: a 429 whose body matches `insufficient_quota` is treated like a 401 — **fail fast** (one attempt, no retry-budget burn), **don’t** `penalize()` the shared admission bucket (there’s no reset window to wait for), and throw a distinct `openai_embed_quota_exhausted`. `embedFailureReason` (`op-deadline.ts`) maps it to reason **`embed_quota_exhausted`** so the agent narrates *“OpenAI quota exhausted — check billing”* instead of *“rate-limited, retrying.”* ## Cost reality: embedding is cents; the benchmark is the spender [Section titled “Cost reality: embedding is cents; the benchmark is the spender”](#cost-reality-embedding-is-cents-the-benchmark-is-the-spender) `text-embedding-3-small` is \~$0.02 per 1M tokens. The embeddable corpus is tiny — \~15k rows total (`memory_vec_openai` + `operator_turns` + the backfill tables) → embedding all of it **once ≈ $0.15**. Measured call rate is \~90 memory/search tool calls/day. Steady-state embedding is **cents/month.** So if you see a surprising “$N on embeddings” bill, it is **not** production recall. The dominant embed spender is the **memory/search benchmark** (`lib/memory/bench` — `run-bench` / `precision-monitor` re-embeds the whole corpus × every backend variant × repeats per run). Those runs use **ephemeral scopes** they create and drop, so they leave **no rows** in `memory_precision_bench` — untraceable from the DB, but it’s the documented org-TPM burner. It is budget-gated: `iq-battery/cadence-tick` **refuses** an unattended run without an owner-set `budgetUsd`. ## The spend backstop: a hard daily token cap [Section titled “The spend backstop: a hard daily token cap”](#the-spend-backstop-a-hard-daily-token-cap) The `embed-admission` governor historically capped only the **rate** (itpm + maxConcurrent) — a run that stays under the rate cap can still accumulate a large bill over hours. It now also carries a hard **daily cumulative token budget**: * `EMBED_DAILY_TOKEN_CAP` (env `PAPERCUSP_EMBED_DAILY_TOKEN_CAP`, default **5,000,000 tokens/day ≈ $0.10/day**; `0` disables). * Once a UTC-day’s estimated embed tokens exceed it, `acquire()` throws `EmbedBudgetExhaustedError` for **both** lanes → reason **`embed_budget_exhausted`**. * It is enforced **even when the `EMBED_ADMISSION` flag is off** — a spend ceiling must not be defeatable by the rate-governing toggle. * It logs loudly **once per day** when it binds, and `adm.usage()` exposes the running day-token count for monitoring. The default is \~300× real usage, so it never trips in normal operation but hard-stops a runaway (a bench/backfill loop) before it can drain a low-balance key. Raise the env var if a legitimate bulk re-embed needs more headroom. ## All three embed paths now go through the one governor [Section titled “All three embed paths now go through the one governor”](#all-three-embed-paths-now-go-through-the-one-governor) There are three OpenAI embed call sites. Two already used the governor; `embed-backfill.ts` was the **one ungoverned raw-fetch path** — so neither the rate cap nor the spend cap applied to it. It is now routed through the shared `embedAdmission()` (bench lane), so the single choke point covers everything: | Path | File | Lane | | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | -------- | | memory:\* (mem0) | `memory/configure.ts` `buildOpenAiEmbedder` | `memory` | | search:semantic / work\_items:search | `agent-tools/search/embedder.ts` | `bench` | | embed-backfill (5-min DBOS sweep) | `search/embed-backfill.ts` | `bench` | ## The embed-backfill ctid bug (fixed) [Section titled “The embed-backfill ctid bug (fixed)”](#the-embed-backfill-ctid-bug-fixed) `embed-backfill.ts` walks rows `WHERE embedding IS NULL` and fills them in 5-minute sweeps. It used to target the `UPDATE` by **`ctid`** for 3 of 4 tables. `ctid` is a **physical row pointer that changes on any UPDATE or (auto)VACUUM**, which caused: 1. **Re-embed loop / token burn** — if a row’s ctid drifted between the `SELECT` and the `UPDATE … WHERE ctid=$`, the update matched nothing, the embedding stayed `NULL`, and the row was re-embedded **every 5 minutes forever.** 2. **Wrong-row clobber** — a reused ctid could write one row’s embedding onto a different row. 3. **A latent hot-loop** — the inner `while(true)` re-`SELECT`s `IS NULL` rows; a row whose embed *persistently* fails (e.g. every request 429s during a quota outage) is re-selected forever, spinning the loop and re-spending each pass. Fixed by keying the `UPDATE` on the real **PRIMARY KEY** (composite where needed: `operator_turns(id)`, `harness_escalations`/`harness_brainstorm` `(harness_slug,phase)`, `harness_decisions(harness_slug,line_hash)`) + guarding `AND embedCol IS NULL`, plus a **zero-progress break** (stop the sweep when a full batch embeds nothing — the remaining NULLs are persistent failures; the next tick retries). ## Runbook [Section titled “Runbook”](#runbook) * **`memory:search`/`remember` returns `embed_quota_exhausted`** → the OpenAI account is out of credit. Add credit / raise the spend cap at platform.openai.com → Billing, **or** switch memory to the local embedder (`PAPERCUSP_MEMORY_EMBEDDER=local`). The key itself is fine. * **`embed_budget_exhausted`** → *our* daily cap tripped (a runaway, or a legitimate bulk re-embed). Check the once-per-day `[embed-admission] DAILY embed spend cap hit` log; raise `PAPERCUSP_EMBED_DAILY_TOKEN_CAP` if it’s real load. * **`embed_rate_limited`** (frequent) → a *true* transient 429. A fresh OpenAI key often starts at a **low TPM tier**; if it’s chronic, lower `PAPERCUSP_EMBED_ITPM` (default 600k) to match the key’s tier at platform.openai.com → Limits. 429s aren’t billed; search/memory degrade gracefully (BM25 / passthrough+retry). * **“Why did embeddings cost $N?”** → it’s almost certainly a benchmark run, not steady-state recall. Confirm steady-state with the memory/search tool-call rate in `tool_invocations`. * **Rotating the OpenAI key** → `POST /api/credentials` now invalidates the cached mem0 client on a key change, so it takes effect immediately (no ≤1h client-TTL wait).

# A 200 with an empty body passes res.ok but fatal-exits :3070 — wrap host-side loopback .json() in readJsonBody

> A host-side `await res.json()` on an EMPTY or truncated body rejects with a frame-less `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` (stack = `at parse (<anonymous>)` + processTicksAndRejections, ZERO user frames). On the shared :3070 host the deliberate fail-fast unhandledRejection guard then exits the WHOLE process — unattributably, so it recurs unfixably. `if (!res.ok) return` does NOT protect you: a 200 with a zero-byte body (host restarting mid-stream) passes res.ok and still throws in .json(). Fix: parse host-side loopback responses with `readJsonBody(res, ctx)` from loopback-fetch.ts, which reads text first and rethrows an error naming the URL/status/byte-length.

## The mistake this prevents [Section titled “The mistake this prevents”](#the-mistake-this-prevents) The shared `:3070` host dies with a fatal `unhandledRejection`: `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input`, and the stack is only `at parse (<anonymous>)` + `processTicksAndRejections` — **zero user frames**. You cannot grep your way to the offending line, and because the host is shared across the whole fleet, the same crash recurs every time the box is under load (EI-20: :3070 fatal-exited at 03:46:57 under the agent-briefs wave, \~20 sessions hammering it). ## What it actually is [Section titled “What it actually is”](#what-it-actually-is) An `await res.json()` somewhere is parsing an **empty or truncated body**. The host has no hot-reload, so it RESTARTS on every deploy (≤15min) and on the memory-watchdog recycle; an in-flight loopback self-fetch can get a `200` whose body is zero bytes or cut off mid-stream. `JSON.parse('')` throws the frame-less SyntaxError, it bubbles as an unhandled rejection, and the **deliberate** fail-fast guard in `apps/operator/bin/hono-host.ts` calls `process.exit(1)`. The trap: **`if (!res.ok) return` does NOT save you.** A `200` with an empty body passes the `res.ok` check and still rejects in `.json()`. Guarding on status alone is the bug. ## The fix [Section titled “The fix”](#the-fix) Parse host-side loopback responses with `readJsonBody<T>(res, context?)` from `packages/operator-core/lib/loopback-fetch.ts` instead of bare `res.json()`. It reads the body as text first, then `JSON.parse`s; on failure it rethrows an Error naming the **URL** (explicit `context` or `res.url`), **HTTP status**, and **body byte length** (plus a snippet, or `(empty body)`), preserving the original `SyntaxError` as `cause`. The frame-less crash becomes attributable to a route — and most empty-body cases become a handled error instead of a host kill. 
```ts
import { loopbackFetch, readJsonBody } from './loopback-fetch';


const r = await loopbackFetch(`${base}/api/harness/projects`);
if (!r.ok) return [];
// NOT `await r.json()` — an empty 200 during a restart would fatal-exit the host.
const data = await readJsonBody<{ projects?: { slug: string }[] }>(r);
```
 ## Scope / what NOT to change [Section titled “Scope / what NOT to change”](#scope--what-not-to-change) * This is about **host-side** (`:3070`) parses. A `.json()` in the browser webview can throw without killing the host — lower stakes. * Do **not** touch the fail-fast policy in `bin/hono-host.ts`. Exiting on a real unhandled rejection is a deliberate choice (EI-11 night-recovery); a small, explicitly-classified set of client-caused/transient-infra errors is already swallowed instead of exiting (`isBenignHostError()` in `apps/operator/bin/host-benign-errors.ts` — the `ERR_INVALID_STATE` stream-close class plus four others; see `agent-insights/mcp-handler-enqueue-after-close-crash`). A frame-less `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` is **not** one of them, so it still fatal-exits — the fix here is to stop *generating* an unattributable rejection in the first place, not to add it to that swallow-list. * Sibling sites that already do `.json().catch(() => null)` are fine. The danger is the ones guarded only by `res.ok`. Related: the EI-390 insight on bare `fetch failed` loopback retries (`describeFetchError`) — same file, same “make loopback failures self-diagnosing” philosophy.

# Porting Next route.ts files to defineRoute

> The non-obvious patterns from migrating all 243 operator endpoints off Next route handlers onto the Hono-mounted defineRoute primitive.

The R5 endpoint migration moved every `app/api/**/route.ts` in the operator onto `defineRoute` (mounted on the Hono `app` via `registerAllRoutes`). 243 routes, 24 family batches.
