Fix (gateway.ts proxy, `PINNED_FAILOVER_WAIT_MS`): a pinned request whose account’s **live** governor is paused (pre-check) or can’t admit within \~10s **fails over to `pool.active()`** (the failover-walked healthy account). The pin still holds for the bee’s later requests (re-checked each time → it returns to its per-credential cache once the account recovers). **Cache-affinity yields to liveness.** The fix is gateway-side ON PURPOSE: only the gateway has the live-pacing truth; a selection-side guard can’t see it. Edge: a bare framing-429 doesn’t pause the governor, so the pre-check won’t trip — CLI bees frame themselves (real 429s → covered); a raw-SDK pinned caller could still loop. ## How to diagnose next time [Section titled “How to diagnose next time”](#how-to-diagnose-next-time) If a subscription bucket is paused with no live pressure, or an account reads exhausted off `penaltyCount:1`: it’s a rolling-window over-pause, not a real cap. Check gateway `/healthz` `unified.rejected`/`utilization` for the **active** account — if `rejected:false` and util < 1, the pause is stale. If instead a *specific* bee hangs at $0 while the fleet is fine, read its `x-papercusp-account` header + that account’s live gateway governor — that’s the D-005 pinned-paced fault. (Both are distinct from the framing-429 storm, where a raw `/v1/messages` on a Max OAuth token 429s unless the first system block is the Claude Code identifier — see that insight.) Also operational: the gateway loads its account pool **only at boot** (no hot-reload) — after registering/removing accounts you must restart `papercup-inference-gateway.service` to re-pool, else it dead-ends on a stale subset. A standing durable improvement would be to hot-reload the pool.

# High FCP: server/eval libs leak into the eager client bundle via barrels

> The operator SPA's ~2s first-contentful-paint was server-only heavy libs (js-tiktoken, the TypeScript compiler) dragged into the eager boot graph by barrel re-exports. How to diagnose (sourcemap attribution) + fix (lazy import / barrel hygiene / route code-splitting).

## Symptom [Section titled “Symptom”](#symptom) The operator `/adv` shell’s **first-contentful-paint sat at \~2s** (reload, prod bundle) while the doc server response was \~43ms — i.e. it was **all JS parse/exec**, not network. Measured on `bin/desktop-preview-prod` (real `React.production`, the only honest FCP harness; a debug `tauri dev` build auto-opens devtools which inflates RSS and skews timing). ## Root cause (recurring — it hit twice) [Section titled “Root cause (recurring — it hit twice)”](#root-cause-recurring--it-hit-twice) The eager boot bundle was **\~14 MB raw** (entry `<script>` + the whole `modulepreload` graph, which executes before React renders). Two **server- / eval-only heavy libs** were dragged into it by **barrel re-exports of server-only code that the webview transitively imports**: * **`js-tiktoken` (5.5 MB BPE tables)** — `packages/agent-mcp/src/delta-eval-harness.ts` did `import { getEncoding } from 'js-tiktoken'` + `const enc = getEncoding('o200k_base')` at **module top-level** (an eager side-effect), for an eval-only `tokens()`. The agent-mcp barrel (`index.ts`) re-exports that module, and the webview imports the barrel (e.g. `chat/LocalCardHost`) → 5.5 MB eager. * **The TypeScript compiler (3.4 MB)** — `libs/generic/tooldef/src/code-orchestration/parse-check.ts` did `import ts from 'typescript'` for a server-side AST walk (`checkScript`, the `code:run` parse-check). Both the `tooldef` **and** `agent-mcp` barrels re-export `code-orchestration`, and the webview imports both barrels → the whole compiler eager. **162 of 163 tooldef-barrel importers never use code-orchestration** — they paid 3.4 MB for nothing. Contributing: **TanStack Router `autoCodeSplitting` was OFF**, so all \~81 route `component`s were statically imported into `routeTree.gen.ts` → the entry chunk (turning it on dropped the entry 2.5 MB → 281 KB, but the barrel leaks above dominated FCP). ## How to diagnose (don’t guess — attribute) [Section titled “How to diagnose (don’t guess — attribute)”](#how-to-diagnose-dont-guess--attribute) Grepping minified chunks for lib names is unreliable (`"plate"` matches `"template"`; app code is mangled). **Attribute via the sourcemap `sources`:** 
```sh
cd apps/operator-vite && npx vite build --sourcemap true
# then, for the biggest EAGER chunk (entry + modulepreload from dist/index.html):
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, collections
m = json.load(open('dist/assets/<biggest-src-chunk>.js.map'))
agg = collections.Counter()
for i, s in enumerate(m['sources']):
    parts = [p for p in s.replace('../','').split('/') if p not in ('','.')]
    grp = ('nm/'+parts[parts.index('node_modules')+1]) if 'node_modules' in parts else '/'.join(parts[:3])
    agg[grp] += len((m.get('sourcesContent') or [None]*len(m['sources']))[i] or '')
for g, n in agg.most_common(15): print(f'{n//1024:>7} KB  {g}')
PY
```
 Compute the **eager set** = the entry `<script src>` + every `modulepreload` `href` in `dist/index.html` (those execute before paint), then sum their file sizes. The rolldown build also prints `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` warnings — each names a module whose dynamic-import split was defeated by a competing static import (more leak candidates, e.g. `operator-core/lib/work-items.ts`). ## The fix pattern [Section titled “The fix pattern”](#the-fix-pattern) For a heavy lib reachable from the eager client graph but only used server/eval-side, **make the import lazy** so it splits into its own chunk fetched only when that path runs: * **Async consumer** → just `const { x } = await import('heavy-lib')` inside the function (see `delta-eval-harness.ts`: `tokens`/`evalSnapshotTransition` became async; their only callers were tests). * **Consumer must stay sync** (e.g. `checkScript`, exercised by a \~20-call test suite) → **lazy-warmup singleton**: a `let _lib`, an async `ensureXReady()` that does the dynamic `import()` once, and a sync accessor that throws if not warmed. Call `await ensureXReady()` at the (already-async) runtime entry points; tests warm in `beforeAll`. Keeps the sync API + avoids an async cascade through every caller. Use `import type` for the lib’s types (erased) so type annotations don’t re-pull it. (See `parse-check.ts`.) * **Routes** → set `autoCodeSplitting: true` on the `tanstackRouter` vite plugin. * **Barrel hygiene** (the deeper fix): don’t `export *` server-only subtrees (`code-orchestration`) through a barrel that clients import; deep-import in the few real server consumers instead. Caution Verify on `bin/desktop-preview-prod` (prod React) and re-attribute the eager set — the FCP number alone is load-noisy on the shared box (grade the **eager bundle bytes**, which are load-independent, plus FCP medians). Confirmed wins (2026-06-23 E2E sweep): eager bundle **13.86 MB → 2.35 MB (−83%)**, FCP **1927 → 932 ms (−52%)**.

# "Federation joiner test flakiness" root cause: silent schema drift in a hand-rolled test DDL, masked by a catch-all in the epoch-key drain

> hive-late-join-epoch-decrypt-federation.integration.test.ts (WI-894) was reported as "keeps flaking" — actual root cause was a deterministic (not racy) schema mismatch: the test's own minimal DDL for harness_plans never got the owner_author_pubkey column migration 414 added, so the real projection writer's INSERT threw a real Postgres error that drainQueuedEpochContent's best-effort catch{} silently swallowed, surfacing only as a downstream count mismatch.

## The symptom [Section titled “The symptom”](#the-symptom) Two duplicate research tasks (WI-1472/WI-1473) were filed asking to root-cause “why federation joiner tests keep flaking.” A PG scan of `harness_shared.test_runs` showed one currently-red joiner test: `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/__tests__/hive-late-join-epoch-decrypt-federation.integration.test.ts` (WI-894), with **different assertion lines failing on different historical runs** (`reconcile.distributed` count, `keyRowCount` count, `reapplied` count) — the classic signature agents read as “flaky/racy.” ## The actual root cause — NOT a race, 100% deterministic at any fixed commit [Section titled “The actual root cause — NOT a race, 100% deterministic at any fixed commit”](#the-actual-root-cause--not-a-race-100-deterministic-at-any-fixed-commit) Running the test 6× in a row at HEAD failed **6/6, always at the identical line** (`drainQueuedEpochContent` returning 1 instead of 2). It is not intermittent; it is fully deterministic — the *appearance* of flakiness across historical runs came from the code evolving underneath the test over time (this repo’s tree is edited concurrently by a large agent fleet), so the exact assertion that failed shifted as other parts of the reconcile/drain chain were fixed independently. The real defect: this test hand-rolls a **minimal, “prod-faithful” DDL** for `harness_shared.harness_plans` (`CONTENT_AND_KEY_DDL` at the top of the file) instead of running real migrations. Migration `414-harness-plans-owner-author.sql` later added an `owner_author_pubkey TEXT` column that `projections/harness-plans.ts`’s real `writeToPg` now includes in every INSERT — but the test’s hand-rolled DDL was never updated to match. So when the test’s drain step calls the **real** plans projection writer against its own throwaway PG, the INSERT throws: 
```plaintext
PostgresError: column "owner_author_pubkey" of relation "harness_plans" does not exist
```
 That exception is thrown *inside* `drainQueuedEpochContent`’s per-op loop (`hive-epoch-op-gate.ts`), which wraps every re-apply in a **deliberately silent** `catch {}` (documented as “a re-apply failure must not abort the merge pass” — correct production behavior for resilience, but it means a genuine schema bug downstream degrades to a silent no-op rather than a loud failure). The work\_item op (a different table, `engineer-issues`, whose DDL happened to still match) applies fine, so the test sees `reapplied === 1` instead of the expected `2` — a numeric mismatch with zero indication of *why*. ## How this was diagnosed [Section titled “How this was diagnosed”](#how-this-was-diagnosed) 1. `dev:pg_query` over `harness_shared.test_runs` filtered to `%federation%` / `%joiner%` / `%cross-peer%` file paths, ordered by `created_at DESC` — this is the fast way to find which joiner test is *actually* red right now vs. historical engineer\_issues noise (many past joiner incidents are already `resolved`/`closed`). 2. Ran the specific failing test 6× back-to-back — instantly showed it’s deterministic, not racy, at this commit. 3. Read `hive-epoch-op-gate.ts::drainQueuedEpochContent` and found the silent `catch {}` — the signal that whatever failed here would never surface a reason. 4. Temporarily added a `console.error` inside that catch (and on the success path), re-ran once, got the real Postgres error, then reverted the debug instrumentation. This is far faster than guessing from a static read of async crypto/reconcile code that turned out to be a total red herring (the crypto/epoch-key distribution logic is correct; the bug is a stale test fixture). ## The fix [Section titled “The fix”](#the-fix) Add the missing column to the test’s DDL (one line): 
```sql
owner_author_pubkey text,
```
 Verified 4/4 green after the fix (was 6/6 red before). ## The generalizable lesson [Section titled “The generalizable lesson”](#the-generalizable-lesson) * **A hand-rolled “minimal, prod-faithful” DDL fixture drifts silently as real migrations land** — there is no compile-time or lint-time check tying a test’s inline `CREATE TABLE` to the real migration history. `grep -rl "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS harness_shared.harness_plans" .` found **5 other test files** with the same hand-rolled `harness_plans` DDL; only the ones that actually exercise `buildHarnessPlansProjection`’s write path (this one, plus `federation-content-matrix.repro.integration.test.ts`, which currently still passes because its scenario doesn’t hit the same code path) are at risk. Worth a follow-up: a lint/test rule that diffs a hand-rolled fixture schema against `information_schema.columns` for the real table, or — better — a shared test helper that creates these tables FROM a real migration subset instead of re-declaring them. * **A best-effort `catch {}` around a re-apply/retry path is correct for production resilience but actively hides root causes in tests.** When diagnosing a “flaky” count-mismatch assertion inside code with a swallowed catch, add temporary instrumentation INSIDE the catch before spending time reasoning about the surrounding async/crypto logic — the actual defect is very often several layers away from where the crypto/business logic looks suspicious. * **“Keeps flaking” reported across widely-separated dates can mean “keeps breaking in different ways as the code around it changes,”** not a single racy root cause. Always re-run the CURRENTLY-red test fresh (`dev:pg_query` on `test_runs`, then `vitest run` several times) before trusting historical engineer\_issues prose — most of the historically-filed “joiner roster empty” issues in this area (WI-1378/1379/1380/1422/ 1460/1519/1534/1544/1585) are unrelated, already-resolved, LIVE 2-machine-rig incidents, not this hermetic unit-test’s bug.

# Decompose federation "X never crossed" reds in ONE query — group substrate_outbox by scope × drained-state

> A live differential (WI-971) separated three co-mingled causes behind identical federation-matrix reds (smoke wrong-workspace writes / receive-side backfill latency / joiner home-view drain gap) in minutes, once the LIVE pair's substrate_outbox was grouped by (workspace_id, harness_slug, table_name, drained_at IS NULL). Prior sessions burned hours theorizing from smoke stdout alone.

## What [Section titled “What”](#what) When a federation/replication test reports “content never crossed A→B” (or a whole matrix of federation smokes goes red at once), the instinct is to theorize from the smoke test’s own stdout — but the smoke output can’t distinguish three completely different root causes that all present as the same symptom. A live WI-971 differential separated all three in minutes by querying the LIVE pair’s `harness_shared.substrate_outbox` directly instead: 
```sql
SELECT workspace_id, harness_slug, table_name,
       (drained_at IS NULL) AS undrained,
       count(*)
  FROM harness_shared.substrate_outbox
 GROUP BY workspace_id, harness_slug, table_name, (drained_at IS NULL)
 ORDER BY workspace_id, harness_slug, table_name, undrained;
```
 ## Reading the result — three distinct root causes, one query [Section titled “Reading the result — three distinct root causes, one query”](#reading-the-result--three-distinct-root-causes-one-query) * **Undrained rows sit in a scope with NO booted substrate handle** → this is a **capture/scope bug on the SEND side** (writes are landing in the outbox under the wrong scope, or a scope that was never wired to a running handle). The send side is otherwise fine — the row is captured, it’s just captured under a scope nothing is draining. * **Rows show `drained_at` set (drained INSTANTLY) but are still missing on the peer** → this is a **RECEIVE-side problem**: the row left the sender’s outbox correctly, so look at backfill latency or the joiner’s home-view drain gap on the receiving end, not the sender. * **The undrained/missing pattern is per-TABLE selective** (some tables cross fine, others never do) → this is almost always a **mapping or scope bug** for the affected table specifically — never “the drain is down” globally, since a globally-down drain would affect every table uniformly. ## Where to get the LIVE pair’s DSN [Section titled “Where to get the LIVE pair’s DSN”](#where-to-get-the-live-pairs-dsn) The two-instance smoke tests leave the pair **running** after they finish — don’t tear them down to theorize, query them directly. Their connection strings live in `instances.env`: `harness_admin:harness_admin_pwd@localhost:<pg-port>/papercusp` (one DSN per instance). Point `dev:pg_query` (or a direct `psql`) at each pair member with the query above before writing a single line of theory. ## The detector this spec-shapes (WI-183-class) [Section titled “The detector this spec-shapes (WI-183-class)”](#the-detector-this-spec-shapes-wi-183-class) The “undrained rows sitting in a scope with no booted handle, forever” case above is exactly the input shape for a **replication-liveness detector**: alert when `undrained_age = now() - min(ts) WHERE drained_at IS NULL` exceeds a threshold, grouped per `(workspace_id, harness_slug, table_name)` scope. No such detector exists yet (as of this doc) — this query is effectively its manual, on-demand form. If you’re about to build that detector, the GROUP BY shape above is the query to automate. ## Consequence [Section titled “Consequence”](#consequence) Before spending more than a few minutes theorizing about a federation “never crossed” red from smoke-test output alone, run the GROUP BY query above against the live pair. It costs one query and immediately tells you WHICH of the three root-cause classes you’re in, instead of guessing from indirect symptoms.

# Federation public-release: known limitations + release-criteria gate

> The honest release calibration for cross-machine p2p shared-hive federation — what is proven LIVE vs proven IN-PROCESS ONLY, the standing known limitations (multi-device identity, coord control-plane local-only, revocation read-cut, LWW divergence, NAT, bg-host leak, 2-server cap), the forceReFold mechanism + its cost, and the explicit public-release checklist (which hardening briefs must be green to ship).

This is the **honest release calibration** for cross-machine peer-to-peer shared-hive federation: what is proven **live** (over real, separate machines on the public DHT), what is proven **in-process only**, the standing **known limitations**, the **`forceReFold` mechanism + its cost**, and the explicit **public-release checklist** — which of the federation-release-hardening briefs must be green before we can call federation shippable. It deliberately supersedes the optimistic “FULLY WORKING + RELEASE-READY” claim (memory `a02714f1`) with the calibrated view (memory `f64a176d`, the calibration correction — **read that one**). The core path is real and reproducible; it is **not yet at a defensible public-release bar**. Read this before telling anyone federation is done. > **The one rule this page exists to enforce: in-process green ≠ live green.** The A→B owner-admit race passed *every* in-process test and still failed live. So an in-process-green scenario is *necessary but not sufficient* evidence — every release-gating scenario must be **reproduced over real VMs**, not just asserted in the in-process matrix. *** ## Status snapshot [Section titled “Status snapshot”](#status-snapshot) | Capability | Status | Evidence | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Base federation (content/features + per-part plans + coord **data**), A→B **and** B→A | ✅ **Proven LIVE — no-restart blocker RESOLVED** | run33/34/35 + Briefs 4/3/7 (2026-07-01/02). The no-restart roster-empty class (blocker #9 / WI-1378) is fixed by THREE stacked fixes: the fresh home-resolve (3030bfd13), the directory self-echo guard (WI-1422), and the **deterministic join-time owner-device binding** (verified coords extracted from the member links + stamped on the registry view — no directory-timing dependence; Brief 7’s baseline federated FIRST-poll). These are real, teeth-proven tests — but **the whole point of the live-hardening effort is that the A→B race passed all of them and still failed live.** Treat in-process green as a *prerequisite*, never as the live proof. Each of these scenarios needs a live VM reproduction before it gates a release claim (Briefs 2–7, consolidated into the live-matrix runner, Brief 13). *** ## The `forceReFold` mechanism + its cost [Section titled “The forceReFold mechanism + its cost”](#the-forcerefold-mechanism--its-cost) `forceReFold` is the deterministic fix for the live A→B owner-admit timing race. **Root cause.** The joiner (B) bootstrap-admits the owner’s (A’s) log during the `home=<none>` boot window. It folds A’s `hive_members` op through the **member-slug-bound** projection, so A’s roster row is **dropped** at `projections/hive-members.ts` (`row.hive_home_slug !== member slug`) and the merge cursor marks the op done. When the rekey rebinds the projections to the **hive-home** slug, `retryPendingOnce` only re-*admits* still-pending peers — it does **not** re-apply an already-admitted-and-folded op. Result: empty roster → A’s content defers forever. **The fix** (`packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/boot.ts`): 1. A one-shot `let forceReFold = false` flag. 2. Set `forceReFold = true` in `rekey()`’s rebind block, *after* the `hive_members`/`hive_settings` projections rebind from the member slug to the hive-home slug. 3. Consumed at the top of the merge pass, under the merge gate: it resets the merge cursor (`mergeCursor = createMergeCursor()`) and clears the flag, so the next pass **re-folds every admitted log** through the now-hive-home-bound projection — A’s roster row re-applies and the deferred content drains. 4. Driven by a terminal `mergeNow()` at the end of `rekey()` (this is what makes it deterministic, rather than depending on the 5s periodic tick — the latency that `PAPERCUSP_A003_TRACE`’s stderr delay accidentally flipped green in run31 vs the red run32). Regression test: `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/__tests__/owner-roster-rebind-race.repro.integration.test.ts` (deterministic, RED-without / GREEN-with). Adversarial review verdict: **SAFE TO SHIP** — no CRITICAL/HIGH, race-freedom sound (the terminal `mergeNow()` always delivers the re-fold with the new binding), projections are LWW-guarded, revocation ordering correct, `pendingMemberContent` drain fires once (review record: memory `4d1db206`). ### The cost (and the one open follow-up) [Section titled “The cost (and the one open follow-up)”](#the-cost-and-the-one-open-follow-up) `forceReFold` re-folds **all admitted logs** on **each home-resolving rekey rebind**. It is **one-shot** — the flag is cleared immediately under the merge gate, so steady-state passes are unaffected — but the re-fold itself is `O(total ops across all admitted logs)`. At scale (many members, large logs, repeated rekeys) this is the thing to watch for a perf cliff; Brief 9 is characterizing it (in-process, since live many-member is blocked by the quota cap). No cliff/leak has been attributed to it yet. > **Snapshot interaction — the gating follow-up (Brief 11).** The `forceReFold` cursor reset is placed *before* `seedCursorFromSnapshots`. With `FLAGS.SUBSTRATE_LOG_SNAPSHOT` ON, the re-fold must still re-apply the dropped `hive_members` op (a snapshot op summarizes all current rows, so it should). An integration test covering `forceReFold` reset → `seedCursorFromSnapshots` with the snapshot flag ON **must land before the log-compaction/snapshot flag ships.** This is the only open review item. *** ## Known limitations (standing, document-honestly) [Section titled “Known limitations (standing, document-honestly)”](#known-limitations-standing-document-honestly) ### 1. Coordination control plane — BRIDGED for hive-scoped sends (updated 2026-07-01) [Section titled “1. Coordination control plane — BRIDGED for hive-scoped sends (updated 2026-07-01)”](#1-coordination-control-plane--bridged-for-hive-scoped-sends-updated-2026-07-01) The original Brief-7 finding (“a wake fired on A does not wake a live agent on B”) is **no longer the architecture** — it was the send-side gates, and `cross-machine-coord-parity-and-trust-2026-07-01` closed them (Phases 0–2): hive-scoped `coord:send` federates with the persisted wake intent and the receiving projection fires the wake fan on arrival (EI-279 + P-001 scope stamping); wake-on-reply bridges back (P-002); `events:emit {scope:'hive'}` re-fires keys into every machine’s await store (P-009); directed required-wakes get delivery receipts (`coord:receipt:<msg_id>`, P-008); remote agents are addressable via the federated session roster (P-005/P-007). Residual caveats: UN-scoped (operator-local) sends still never leave the machine — the send result’s `federated:` field is the truth; cross-machine wakes are budget-capped per author device (P-003); presence still rides the log until the `papercusp-presence-gossip` cutover flag flips; and the whole bridge’s LIVE 2-machine proof is still owed (the in-process suites are green — in-process ≠ live, this page’s own rule). **Handoffs are trust-gated, not broken (WI-1510 disposition, 2026-07-02).** The handoffs surface federates on the wire like messages/escalations, but the receiver-side P-013 comms-tier gate (`sync/hyperbee/projections/coord-message.ts` + `comms-tier-gate.ts`) requires the *author* to resolve to tier `steer` — via a **local** `comms_trust_list` grant or the owner-signed hive-policy default — before a remote handoff applies; below that it lands in `harness_shared.coord_quarantine` (reason `handoff-below-steer`): visible and grantable, never silently applied or dropped. There is deliberately **no owner special-case** (steer grants are per-user, per-machine, and never federate). Messages/escalations need only the `message` fallback tier, which is why they pass ungranted. Both legs live-proven in the matrix (`deb-hetzner-coord-controlplane.sh`: ungranted → QUARANTINE, steer-granted → FEDERATED). Tier lookups are TTL-cached \~30s (`PAPERCUSP_COMMS_TIER_CACHE_MS`) — a fresh grant takes up to that long to take effect. ### 2. Multi-device, same identity [Section titled “2. Multi-device, same identity”](#2-multi-device-same-identity) Federation identity is **per-device keypair**, not per-GitHub-account. The substrate is “Model B” — per-device single-writer logs + read-merge (`sync/hyperbee/peer-log.ts`), *not* Autobase — so sharing one hive keypair across a user’s devices is *safe* (no writer conflict), but **discovery and merge are separate gates**: the shared keypair grants topic discovery, while the actual merge is gated by membership (`classifySameHiveMember` admits a remote log only if its `device_pubkey` is in `hive_members`). So one human on two devices = two distinct device pubkeys, each needing its own membership admission. The dogfood per-owner hive solves the same-owner case (Solution C, `harness/papercusp-hive-share.ts`: a per-owner private identity gist + an owner-signed allowlist policy auto-admits the owner’s login), but the **two-device data-merge has only been single-box-smoke-verified, never witnessed live with a real second device.** The stricter “private key never leaves the creating device” remote-JOIN variant (share only the pubkey) is deliberately not built. The historical phase1b multi-device collision (contributor-file login-key overwrite) is *obsolete* — admission is now keyed by the stable numeric `github_user_id` + a device-signed announce/attestation ([phase1b-federation-limitations](/internal/docs/agent-insights/phase1b-federation-limitations)). ### 3. Revocation is WRITE + DISCOVERY-plane only (hard read cut-off rides the re-key) [Section titled “3. Revocation is WRITE + DISCOVERY-plane only (hard read cut-off rides the re-key)”](#3-revocation-is-write--discovery-plane-only-hard-read-cut-off-rides-the-re-key) A revoked/banned member stops being *aggregated* and stops *discovering* new content, but `swarm.ts`’s `store.replicate(socket)` serves cores to any topic peer, so a removed member (or anyone who got the link while the hive was public) keeps **reading** future content until the hive **re-keys** (C-001) or is **dissolved**. The in-place re-key epoch **K-cut** that closes the read plane is now **enabled by default in production** (`papercusp-hive-rekey` — no longer dark; built in `hive-epoch-boot-deps.ts` / `buildHiveRekeyBootDeps`, consumed on the in-place `rekey()` rebind, never a reboot). But its **cross-machine LIVE proof is still pending (Brief 3)** — today only the in-process `federation-revocation-kcut-sidecar` + `hive-late-join-epoch-decrypt-federation` tests cover the K-cut. This is a conscious product decision, not a silent hole. ([substrate-revocation-model](/internal/docs/agent-insights/substrate-revocation-model).) ### 4. LWW convergence under clock skew — the four ordering sources are FIXED (2026-07-02); one presence gap remains (§ 4a) [Section titled “4. LWW convergence under clock skew — the four ordering sources are FIXED (2026-07-02); one presence gap remains (§ 4a)”](#4-lww-convergence-under-clock-skew--the-four-ordering-sources-are-fixed-2026-07-02-one-presence-gap-remains--4a) The S0 class (“two honest peers silently materialize different rows for the same key”) had **four** distinct sources, all now fixed: 1. **Capture-boundary two-clock bug (mig 446):** two clock reads in the *same transaction* stamped the same op — the mig-314 BEFORE trigger stamps the row’s `fed_ts` with `clock_timestamp()` while the AFTER capture triggers stamped the outbox wire `ts` with `now()` (txn start), so author ≠ every receiver forever. Mig 446 threads the ROW’s `fed_ts` as the put-op wire ts in **both** capture functions. Live-verified (concurrent\_lww PASS, m1783013203). 2. **HLC-fold vs fed\_ts-guard order split (mig 458, EI-1698):** the merge winners-fold ordered by HLC while the PG guards ordered by wall-clock `fed_ts` (and later, non-transitively, by a mixed rule). Mig 458 introduces `harness_shared.fed_order_key(hlc, ts)` — an immutable SQL mirror of `lwwPick`’s derivation — and applies it to all 40 guard clauses (put+delete) across the 20 mutable projection writers: one ordering key of record end-to-end. ([hlc-merge-vs-fed-ts-guard-divergence](/internal/docs/agent-insights/hlc-merge-vs-fed-ts-guard-divergence).) 3. **Exact fed\_hlc ties swap winners (WI-1672, mig 459):** after any recv-ratchet episode, peers advance clocks by counter only in near-lockstep and routinely mint IDENTICAL `(ms, count)` stamps; every tie-accepting `>=` guard then accepts the incoming op on BOTH peers and two honest peers stably SWAP winners (observed live on the wi1544 3-frame rig). Fixed by a node-id total order: 3-segment HLC `<15-digit ms>:<5-digit count>:<16-hex node>` (locks-core `hlc.ts` + mig 459’s `hlc_clock.node_id` / 3-segment `hlc_now()`/`hlc_recv()`); a genuine full tie can now only be the same stamp replayed, where tie-accept is correct (idempotent). Legacy 2-segment stamps lose ties deterministically on every peer. 4. **The recv-ratchet amplifier (mig 460):** `hlc_recv`/`HlcClock.recv` blindly adopted any remote `ms`, so ONE absurd-future stamp pinned the clock — and, re-propagated, the whole hive — years ahead, permanently (self-demonstrated live on the dev DB during WI-1672 verification). Both now refuse to ratchet past `now + 600s` (2× the D-007 announce-admission window, so every legitimately-admitted peer still ratchets); the op’s DATA still applies, only the clock advance is skipped. Evidence for 3+4: the convergence-fuzz rig now models the REAL production topology (`localAuthorApply` = skipOwnOps + the unguarded trigger write path; `lockstep` = the ratcheted counter-lockstep) — node-LESS stamps split-brain across a 120-seed sweep (teeth), node-carrying stamps converge on all 120 seeds, monotone AND skew; plus the forced-tie two-device swarm + migrated-PG integration test (`federation-concurrent-writes-sidecar.repro.integration.test.ts`). ### 4a. Local-del resurrection under skipOwnOps — row-PRESENCE split-brain (WI-1684, OPEN) [Section titled “4a. Local-del resurrection under skipOwnOps — row-PRESENCE split-brain (WI-1684, OPEN)”](#4a-local-del-resurrection-under-skipownops--row-presence-split-brain-wi-1684-open) Found by the production-topology fuzz rig while verifying the WI-1672 fix, and **not** fixed by node ids: an author DELETES a row locally (trigger path — row gone, **no tombstone**) and its own del is skipOwnOps-excluded from its own fold; a CONCURRENT foreign put with a LOWER fed\_hlc then wins the author’s fold among foreign ops alone and hits the projection’s no-row insert path, which has nothing to arbitrate against → the row is RESURRECTED on the author peer only, while every other peer folds del + put together and keeps it deleted. Classic LWW-set missing-tombstone gap, specific to the local-write path bypassing the merge’s winners map. Needs genuinely concurrent cross-peer writes straddling a delete, so lower frequency than WI-1672 — but silent, permanent divergence when it hits. Pinned by a characterisation/teeth test in `convergence-fuzz.test.ts`; candidate fixes on WI-1684 (fed\_hlc-stamped tombstones in the projections, or folding own ops into the winners map for ORDERING while still skipping their APPLY). Fix or explicitly accept before public release. ### 5. NAT / firewall / geo assumptions — LIVE-PROVEN with one caveat (Brief 8, 2026-07-02) [Section titled “5. NAT / firewall / geo assumptions — LIVE-PROVEN with one caveat (Brief 8, 2026-07-02)”](#5-nat--firewall--geo-assumptions--live-proven-with-one-caveat-brief-8-2026-07-02) Brief 8 lifted this from the easy topology: 2 Hetzner frames **cross-region** (ash↔hil) with a **stateful restricted-cone NAT** (nftables masquerade + established/related-only inbound) in front of the member frame, real public DHT. Verdict: **holepunch PASS both directions; member→owner content PASS; owner→member content is LATE, not never** — ops the owner appends while the joiner is still in its owner-binding-null admit-refusal window stall indefinitely (80+ min observed, survives a cold restart of the member) until the **next owner-side append** kicks the replication/fold, after which the entire backlog folds within minutes. No data loss; the log is intact. Filed as **WI-1534** (unbounded staleness on quiescent hives — fix directions: force a remote-length refresh/initial sync after late admit, or an anti-entropy `update()` tick in the merge pass). Remaining out-of-scope rung: **symmetric NAT** (needs a real symmetric-NAT middlebox; port-dependent mapping defeats the restricted-cone emulation). Earlier rig work also proved that two VMs sharing one NAT egress IP **hairpin** and fail a public-DHT holepunch — a class of failure single-NAT topologies never surface. ### 6. Long-running node stability (bg-host leak) — RESOLVED (2026-07-02) [Section titled “6. Long-running node stability (bg-host leak) — RESOLVED (2026-07-02)”](#6-long-running-node-stability-bg-host-leak--resolved-2026-07-02) The original listener-leak class (25+ substrate boots adding `swarm.on('connection')` to the shared swarm without removal, WI-1088/1089, Brief 10) was fixed; the re-observed 30GB RSS climb (WI-1417) turned out to be a **different** driver — the claude-sessions full owner-dir fs sweep ([operator-memory-bloat-claude-sessions-fs-sweep](/internal/docs/agent-insights/operator-memory-bloat-claude-sessions-fs-sweep)), fixed with negative-resolution + roots TTL caches in `claude-sessions.ts`. Live-re-verified 2026-07-02: bg-host sits at a 5.7–5.8GB sawtooth plateau (GC keeping pace, not a monotonic climb), no dbos-reaper false-reap storm; recurrence-guarded by 3 tests in `claude-sessions-cache.test.ts`. WI-1415/WI-1416 (the git-sync symptom chain) independently resolved. No longer a release risk row. ### 7. Data-completeness is table-grain-guarded, column-grain is the residual risk [Section titled “7. Data-completeness is table-grain-guarded, column-grain is the residual risk”](#7-data-completeness-is-table-grain-guarded-column-grain-is-the-residual-risk) 18 federated tables (`harness-state/table-registry.ts`) are structurally guarded at table grain (every peer-log table has a producer + a projection, two green CI tests). **Column-grain drift** is the residual class: value-mappers hand-pick columns, so a federated-table column added without updating its mapper silently drops on peers. A new guard (`federated-column-completeness.integration.test.ts`) closes the general case; a live candidate gap remains (`harness_features_consolidated` drops `design_spec_id`/`source_plan_slug`/etc.). `trusted_authors` is local-only **by design** (federating the auto-run grant would be a security regression). ### 8. The 2-server quota cap → no true 3-machine multi-member LIVE [Section titled “8. The 2-server quota cap → no true 3-machine multi-member LIVE”](#8-the-2-server-quota-cap--no-true-3-machine-multi-member-live) *(historical)* The Hetzner quota was \~2 concurrent servers, so true 3-machine member↔member fanout (owner + 2 members, Brief 2) was **not live-coverable**; it was proven only via a 2-VM proxy + the in-process matrix, and the owner ratified that min-bar (D-006). **UPDATE 2026-07-03 (D-001, `shared-hive-p2p-release-readiness-2026-07-03`): Hetzner is gone entirely, and the un-gating path is now LOCAL** — extend the containerized rig to 3 frames (`bin/local-matrix.sh` provisions docker frames; the rig lib is already N-frame) and run the matrix + membership churn there (that plan’s P-010). “Gated on a >2-server quota” is obsolete; the residual gap is simply that the 3-frame local run has not been executed yet. ### 9. Owner→joiner federation can stay broken in the pure NO-RESTART join path (RESOLVED — both mechanisms fixed + live-verified 2026-07-02) [Section titled “9. Owner→joiner federation can stay broken in the pure NO-RESTART join path (RESOLVED — both mechanisms fixed + live-verified 2026-07-02)”](#9-ownerjoiner-federation-can-stay-broken-in-the-pure-no-restart-join-path-resolved--both-mechanisms-fixed--live-verified-2026-07-02) A live run (Brief 6 attempt-1, su-e7698: 2-frame, shared forceReFold `.deb`, real DHT) surfaced **owner(a)→joiner(b) content federation FAILING** in the plain join→write path with **no restart**: b’s `hive_members` roster stayed EMPTY for 270s+, so `decideMemberContentOp` dropped every owner op (b→a was fine). Code root-cause (su-0f0a4): `forceReFold` (`boot.ts`) fires **exactly once**, on the `rekey()`→hive-home rebind, then resets. If the owner’s `hive_members` op arrives at the joiner **after** that single re-fold (during drain), it is never re-applied — it stays dropped-in-the-home-window until a **restart or a later rekey**. This is consistent with Brief 5 (restart) PASSING (the restart re-folds) and means the earlier “proven live” runs (run33/34/35) may have included a restart/rekey rather than exercising the pure no-restart path. **Root cause (confirmed, su-2c799):** cross-process `opStateCache` staleness under `SUBSTRATE_SIDECAR`. `join-hive.ts` (MAIN process) commits the registry (`remote_hive:true` + `hive_slug`) and invalidates its OWN cache; but `rekey()` runs in the substrate SIDECAR process, whose warm `harness_registry` cache (2s TTL, kept hot by the sidecar’s constant reads) never saw that invalidation → it serves the STALE pre-join value → `joinerHiveHomeSlug` returns null → `resolveHiveHomeProjectionSlug` returns null → `next===prev(null)` → the rekey rebind block (boot.ts \~2599) SKIPS → `forceReFold` never fires → the member-slug projection binding latches → the owner’s `hive_members` rows drop forever → roster EMPTY. A restart cold-reads fresh at boot → binds correctly (why Brief 5 restart PASSED). Neither original candidate — it was a third mechanism (stale cross-process cache read at the resolve, not a re-fold-coverage or rebind-timing bug). **Status: FIX LANDED (su-2c799, WI-1378).** `resolveHiveHomeProjectionSlug` now calls `joinerHiveHomeSlug(ws, slug, { fresh: true })`, threaded through `loadHarnessRegistry({fresh})` → `readOperatorState({fresh})` to BYPASS the 2s cache on this one rare resolve path (hot-path callers keep the cache, so the seqscan perf win is preserved). A fresh PG read is guaranteed to see the committed write (join-hive awaits the `mutateRegistry` commit before the rekey RPC). **Second mechanism (WI-1544, the race bifurcation):** when the deterministic join-time binding resolved BEFORE the owner’s announce, the joiner’s hive-home projection conclusively rejected the owner core on the slug filter (origin=member-slug), membership chicken-and-egged, and A→B blacked out *permanently* (the rekey rescue was structurally unreachable — no binding transition). Fixed in `boot.ts`: `inJoinBootstrapWindow()` reclassifies a join-window `binding_invalid` as retryable/buffered instead of conclusive-reject, and the `scope_unresolved` buffer holds out-of-scope slug-filter frames while the hive-home projection slug is unresolved (WI-1544, resolved 2026-07-02; 41 dedicated tests in `boot.test.ts` + `announce-channel-multihive.test.ts`). **Live verification:** matrix run m1783013203 (2026-07-02) federated A→B on the FIRST poll across all 8 scenarios — no restart, no adaptive re-fold rescue needed. This limitation is closed. ### 10. Membership-lifecycle + residual trackers (P-011 verdicts, 2026-07-03) [Section titled “10. Membership-lifecycle + residual trackers (P-011 verdicts, 2026-07-03)”](#10-membership-lifecycle--residual-trackers-p-011-verdicts-2026-07-03) The post-min-bar backlog was given explicit verdicts under `shared-hive-p2p-release-readiness-2026-07-03` P-011 (full table: `shared-hive-release-testing/RELEASE-READINESS.md`). The standing ship-with-limitation rows, each with an accountable tracker: * **No un-revoke path (G8, WI-1855)** — revocation is one-way; un-banning a member has no sanctioned flow (workaround: re-invite as a fresh device/epoch, which must NOT retro-grant cut epochs). * **Membership teardown doesn’t federate (G24/G27, WI-1857)** — dissolve publishes no membership tombstone (peers’ rows orphan out by TTL) and a leaver’s `hive_members` row persists on peers. Pinned by `lifecycle-membership-teardown.gap.integration.test.ts`; the read-plane mitigation (epoch K-cut) is live-proven, so this is a hygiene gap, not a security hole. * **revoke() Hypercore session leak (G9, WI-1856)** — revoked members’ core sessions are not verifiably closed on the owner; unbounded only on long-lived owners with many revokes. * **Usage-events metering is machine-local (G2, WI-1858)** — the `contributor_usage_events` capture trigger is deliberately deferred to the GA migration (completeness-guard exemption until then). * **From-repo joiner incremental federation (WI-971, OPEN)** — the outbox drain is never wired for joined/created hive harnesses (WI-259 was closed as its duplicate). # Federation rig — restart / recovery runbook (wedged smokes, stale ports, leaked VMs)

> How to recover the two-instance federation rig when a run wedges or leaves debris: reap ONLY dead runs (reap-orphans.sh) or one run (cleanup-run.sh) — never a broad pkill/rm (EI-1739); clear stale Xvfb / testnet-DHT / orphaned sidecars; free or self-discover wedged ports (the WI-754 self-heal); reset/relaunch the linux-test-vm VMs (vmctl); restart the scheduled live-federation-gate; and — when a peer is up but silently local-only (announces nothing, discovers nothing) — restore its MISSING gh auth, the most common dead-link cause after a VM reset (WI-757).

The **federation rig** = the `papercusp-desktop/bin/*federation*.sh` / `bin/two-instance-*.sh` smokes, their shared assert core `papercusp-desktop/bin/lib/federation-asserts.sh`, and the `scripts/linux-test-vm/vmctl` VM driver. Each run boots one or two **isolated** desktop/sidecar instances (own `$HOME` → own `~/.papercusp`, embedded-PG, corestore, ports) and asserts they federate. When a run crashes, times out, or is killed, it can leave debris — orphaned sidecars / embedded-PG / `hyperdht/testnet` nodes, a stale `Xvfb`, a held port, or a powered-on VM. This is the recovery runbook. Never broad-pkill / broad-rm — EI-1739 The box runs **many rigs concurrently** (the fleet + the scheduled gate). A `pkill -f papercusp-desktop`, `pkill -f <rig-name>`, or `rm -rf /tmp/<rig>.*` matches **every** run and crashes a sibling’s **live** run mid-flight (this is exactly the EI-1739 collision: a glob over all runs + a name-wide pkill deleted a sibling’s `$WORK` mid-`initdb` and killed its processes). Always use the **run-scoped** reapers below — they refuse anything that isn’t a single per-run `$WORK` dir, so they can never touch a live sibling. ## 1. Reap debris (the safe, default first move) [Section titled “1. Reap debris (the safe, default first move)”](#1-reap-debris-the-safe-default-first-move) 
```sh
cd papercusp-desktop


# Reap ONLY dead runs (processes gone, older than the 5-min startup window).
# A live sibling always has referencing processes → never touched. Safe anytime,
# concurrently, by anyone.
bin/reap-orphans.sh                 # reap all dead runs
bin/reap-orphans.sh --dry-run       # show what WOULD be reaped, touch nothing


# Clean up exactly ONE known run's leftovers (you have its $WORK):
bin/cleanup-run.sh /tmp/hive-fromrepo-smoke.AbC123
```
 These wrap `fed_reap_orphans` / `fed_cleanup_run` in `federation-asserts.sh`. The rig’s `$WORK` prefixes are registered in `FED_RIG_TMP_PREFIXES` (e.g. `/tmp/hive-fromrepo-smoke.`, `/tmp/merge-smoke.`, `/tmp/vm-fed.`, `/tmp/deb-hzfed.`) — **add a new prefix there** if you add a rig, so the reapers keep seeing it. The reapers exclude the calling shell + its ancestors, so running them from inside an agent shell never false-flags or kills the caller. ## 2. Stale `Xvfb`, testnet-DHT, and orphaned sidecars [Section titled “2. Stale Xvfb, testnet-DHT, and orphaned sidecars”](#2-stale-xvfb-testnet-dht-and-orphaned-sidecars) The smokes run headless on a dedicated `Xvfb` display (never the user’s `:0` — see `fed_ensure_display` / `fed_fresh_display`) and spin a host `hyperdht/testnet` DHT (`fed_start_testnet_dht`). Both, plus the instance sidecars, are tracked in `FED_KILL_PIDS` and torn down by the run’s `EXIT` trap + `fed_cleanup_scoped`. After a hard kill (trap never fired) `reap-orphans.sh` (§1) catches the ones whose argv references the dead run’s `$WORK` (testnet nodes ride `$WORK` on argv exactly so the scoped reaper finds them). A **truly orphaned** `Xvfb` whose run dir is already gone is the one case the scoped reaper can’t attribute. Identify it by display number and kill **only that display** — never a bare `pkill -f Xvfb`: 
```sh
pgrep -af 'Xvfb :2(5[0-9]|99)'      # the smoke/gate display range (e.g. :99, :250, :252)
kill <pid>                          # the specific stale Xvfb, by pid
```
 ## 3. Wedged / mismatched ports [Section titled “3. Wedged / mismatched ports”](#3-wedged--mismatched-ports) Two port strategies are in play: * **Pre-assigned (robust):** the sidecar-bundle path + `deb-hetzner-federation.sh` pick a free port with `fed_pick_free_port`-style `ss` probing and pass it as `PAPERCUSP_HONO_PORT` / `PAPERCUSP_PG_PORT` — the instance binds exactly that. * **Dynamic + discovered:** the packaged `.deb`/Tauri path lets the instance pick its own ports; the rig **discovers** them. If a port is genuinely **held** by a dead run’s leftover, §1 frees it (killing the holder). To see what an instance is actually listening on, the rig now dumps it on failure (`fed_dump_instance_diag`: listening TCP ports + app-log tail). Manually: 
```sh
ss -tlnpH | sort -u        # all listeners + owning pid (own-user pids shown)
```
 ## 4. VMs (the `vmctl` linux-test-vm + the build VMs) [Section titled “4. VMs (the vmctl linux-test-vm + the build VMs)”](#4-vms-the-vmctl-linux-test-vm--the-build-vms) The `--vms` federation runs (`bin/vm-federation.sh`) drive disposable Ubuntu VMs via `scripts/linux-test-vm/vmctl`. A wedged VM: 
```sh
cd papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm
./vmctl status fed-a            # VM up? app up? operator port? disk?
./vmctl reset  fed-a            # recreate a pristine overlay from golden
./vmctl down   fed-a           # graceful power-off (teardown)
./vmctl up     fed-a           # boot a fresh overlay
```
 `vm-federation.sh` resets + reinstalls per VM by default (the clean-boot acceptance run); pass `--no-reset` to reuse overlays while iterating, and `--keep-up` to leave the VMs running for debugging. For a wedged **Mac** VM parked at the OpenCore picker / holding SPICE ports, recover via **QMP, never pkill** — see [mac-vm-qmp-recovery](/internal/docs/agent-insights/mac-vm-qmp-recovery). General VM inventory + disk discipline: [build-system/vms](/internal/docs/build-system/vms). ## 5. The scheduled gate (`live-federation-gate.sh`) [Section titled “5. The scheduled gate (live-federation-gate.sh)”](#5-the-scheduled-gate-live-federation-gatesh) `papercusp-desktop/bin/live-federation-gate.sh` runs the smokes on a schedule on a quiet box and files an EI on any RED (the green-rig/red-binary guard, WI-261/P-013). It: * runs a **hermetic \~2s assert-core self-test first** (WI-754: `bin/lib/federation-asserts.selftest.sh` — proves the port-discovery logic before spending minutes on smokes; a fail exits `GATE: RED` with a clear message). Set `GATE_SKIP_SELFTEST=1` to skip it. * **SKIPs (not fails)** when 1-min load exceeds `LOAD_GATE` — the smokes get killed under load and false-RED below the kill threshold. Better to skip and retry next window than false-RED or pile onto a busy box. **`LOAD_GATE` is now core-aware (2026-07-03, P-013):** `max(15, 3*nproc/8)` — an absolute `15` never fired on the 128-core fleet box (it sat well below the box’s ordinary operating load), reproducing the exact “gate never runs” class P-013 exists to kill; a first core-aware cut at `nproc/4` *still* undershot the observed fleet-era floor (35-46). If a mid-run load spike pushes the 1-min load above the new `STORM_GATE` (default `nproc*0.6`) by the time the verdict is computed, a would-be FAIL is **downgraded to `SKIPPED-STORM`** (no EI filed) instead of a false-RED — the exact failure mode a load-94 fleet storm caused before this existed. * **Fresh-exit + staleness guard (2026-07-03, P-013):** a GREEN younger than `GATE_SUCCESS_TTL_H` (default 22h) makes the NEXT window’s run a no-op exit before the self-test even runs (hourly timer, \~daily actual smoke run). If no GREEN has landed in `GATE_STALE_DAYS` (default 3) — every window either load-skipped, storm-downgraded, all-legs-skipped, or failed — the gate files a **loud staleness EI** itself: silence must never look like green. Set `GATE_FORCE=1` to ignore the freshness TTL and force a run now (still storm-downgrade-protected if the box saturates mid-run). * **EI filing now requires a superuser bearer** (2026-07-03, WI-1841 follow-up to WI-1861): `?superuser=1` on the MCP URL alone is not sufficient — the handler also needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` matching `~/.papercusp/superuser-token` (`GATE_SUPERUSER_TOKEN_PATH` overrides the path). A missing/short token degrades gracefully to log-only, same as before; it is not fatal. * **Build provenance is stamped** (2026-07-03, WI-1861): each rebuild logs the working-tree `HEAD` + dirty-file count, so a “torn-tree build” red (the shared checkout was mid-edit by a fleet peer at build time — unreproducible at the next build, byte-identical blueprints) is diagnosable instead of a mystery. * **`log()` now writes to stderr, not stdout** (2026-07-03, load-bearing P-013 fix): the verdict logic reads a smoke leg’s PASS/FAIL via `$(...)` command substitution, and with `log` on stdout the captured string became `"log-line\nPASS|FAIL"`, so `[ "$RES" = FAIL ]` could never match — a genuine content-matrix FAIL was silently masked out of every verdict until this fix. journald still captures both streams, so nothing is lost. * **The from-repo leg’s known-red is WI-971, not WI-259** — WI-259 was closed as a duplicate of WI-971 (outbox drain never wired for joined/created hive harnesses); WI-280/WI-1666 are resolved. A content-matrix FAIL whose only `✗` lines match the WI-971 backfill/incr-B→A signature is downgraded to `PASS-971` (not a clean pass — WI-971 remains open) rather than a red. * **A new `local-matrix` leg** (P-002, no-op until `bin/local-matrix.sh` exists) runs the full containerized 8-scenario matrix on a weekly cadence (`MATRIX_TTL_H`, default 144h), and only on a window whose content-matrix smoke already passed. * **All-legs-skipped is NOT recorded as green** — if load-gate/staleness logic let a window through but every leg still SKIPPED (e.g. `SKIP_MATRIX=1 SKIP_FROMREPO=1`), the gate now exits `GATE: SKIPPED (no legs ran)` rather than silently counting as a pass. Restart / re-run it manually on a quiet box: 
```sh
cd papercusp-desktop
bin/reap-orphans.sh                                   # clear any prior debris first
LOAD_GATE=48 bin/live-federation-gate.sh              # raise only for a dedicated/idle host
GATE_NO_FILE=1 SKIP_FROMREPO=1 bin/live-federation-gate.sh   # log-only, skip the WI-971-RED leg
GATE_FORCE=1 bin/live-federation-gate.sh              # ignore the freshness TTL, force a run now
```
 It’s a routine — check / re-arm it via `routines:list` / `routines:set` (it does **not** push the live `:3070`; it builds + boots isolated instances). ## 6. Peer is up but silently local-only — missing gh auth (WI-757) [Section titled “6. Peer is up but silently local-only — missing gh auth (WI-757)”](#6-peer-is-up-but-silently-local-only--missing-gh-auth-wi-757) The single most common reason the live link is dead after a `vmctl reset` / re-image (§4): the peer has **no GitHub auth**, so it never federates — yet it boots, serves its API, and looks healthy. The federation **announce binds the device identity to a GitHub user** (`local-announce-identity.ts`): with no `gh` token, `resolveLocalAnnounceIdentity` throws and `boot.ts`’s swarm-join catch treats it as **“stay local-only — don’t federate.”** The peer then **announces nothing and discovers nothing**, silently — there is no loud signal; the only tell is `reachablePeers: 0` on an explicit announce. (This masquerades as a deep substrate/admission/cursor bug — check auth FIRST.) Symptoms: * `GET /api/discovery/hives` on the peer returns `count: 0`. * `POST /api/discovery/set-hive {visibility:"public"}` and `POST /api/harness/hives/from-repo` return `announced:false, reachablePeers:0, error:"local-announce-identity: gh not authenticated"`. * Cross-machine: the peer’s hives never appear on any other peer’s directory. Check it FIRST: 
```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-linux -p <sshPort> tester@127.0.0.1 'gh auth status'
# "You are not logged into any GitHub hosts" → this IS your dead link.
```
 Restore (reversible; **no operator restart needed** — `hive-directory-boot` lazily re-wires the directory on the next browse/announce): 
```sh
# from the HOST (gh-authed); pipe the token over ssh STDIN, never argv:
printf '%s' "$(gh auth token)" | \
  ssh -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-linux -p <sshPort> tester@127.0.0.1 'gh auth login --with-token'
# then re-announce (or just browse) → announced:true, reachablePeers>0
```
 Use the identity the peer historically announced as (its `harness_shared.shared_presence.github_user_id`) — for fed-a that is `papercupai` (279242982); fed-b uses a different account. An operator-process restart **preserves** `~/.config/gh`; only a full **VM re-image** wipes it — so prefer a process restart over a reset, and re-auth after any reset. Coordinate a restart A restart to force a swarm re-peer must be coordinated with whoever owns the live federation/self-heal work (FED-2) — don’t restart a peer another agent is actively investigating. The durable fix (persist/restore auth across restart + a loud no-identity health signal) is tracked in WI-757. ### 6b. Loopback smoke gets 0 peer dials — ambient fleet DHT env leaking in (2026-07-03) [Section titled “6b. Loopback smoke gets 0 peer dials — ambient fleet DHT env leaking in (2026-07-03)”](#6b-loopback-smoke-gets-0-peer-dials--ambient-fleet-dht-env-leaking-in-2026-07-03) A different silently-local-only cause, specific to `fed_local_launch` / `fed_local_launch_sidecar` (`bin/lib/federation-asserts.sh`) launches on a **fleet shell**: fleet desktop sessions carry ambient `PAPERCUSP_DHT_HOST=<bridge-ip>` / `PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP=<bridge-ip:port>` for the tower↔VM rig, and a loopback smoke that inherits either one swarm-binds/bootstraps on the bridge instead of the loopback DHT the smoke actually spun up — so peers never dial each other (0 `peer_connected` fleet-wide, found 2026-07-03). Both launch primitives now **force-empty** `PAPERCUSP_DHT_HOST`/`PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP` before `"$@"` — a caller that *wants* either passes it explicitly in the trailing `VAR=val` args, which win over the forced-empty default. If you’re troubleshooting a hand-rolled smoke that calls these primitives directly and it can’t see its peer, check the calling shell’s environment for `PAPERCUSP_DHT_HOST`/`PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP` before suspecting the substrate. ## 7. Driving the live fed VMs — `fed.sh` (port self-discovery, WI-754) [Section titled “7. Driving the live fed VMs — fed.sh (port self-discovery, WI-754)”](#7-driving-the-live-fed-vms--fedsh-port-self-discovery-wi-754) `papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm/fed.sh` is the **versioned** driver for the 2-machine fed-a / fed-b VMs — the reliable replacement for the ad-hoc `/tmp/fed.sh` that **hardcoded the VMs’ dynamic operator/PG ports**. Those ports are picked fresh on every operator restart and old listeners linger, so a hardcoded (or even “latest `[serve]` log line”) port goes stale and silently hits the wrong / a dead listener (EI-3409 / WI-559 burned \~30 min on exactly this). The versioned script **discovers the LIVE ports on each call**: it SSHes in (stable host-forward port), gathers candidate loopback ports, and picks the operator = the one answering `GET /api/desktop/preflight` with **2xx** and PG = the one that accepts a `harness_admin` psql — so it survives app/VM restarts with no edits. 
```sh
cd papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm
./fed.sh a ports                       # show the discovered operator/PG ports
./fed.sh a sql  "select count(*) from harness_features"
./fed.sh a api  GET /api/discovery/hives
./fed.sh a mcp  hive:report '{"hive":"…"}'
./fed.sh a ssh  'gh auth status'       # raw ssh (used by §6's gh-auth restore)
./fed.sh b rediscover                  # force a fresh probe (after a restart)
```
 Ports are cached per-VM under `~/.papercusp/fed-rig-ports.<vm>` for `FED_PORT_TTL` (default 600s); `rediscover` (or deleting the cache) forces a fresh probe. SSH host-forward ports default to `2225` (a) / `2226` (b) — override with `FED_SSH_A` / `FED_SSH_B`. Cross-machine witness hives must be repo-bound For a live two-machine federation witness, do not create an arbitrary repo-less throwaway with `hive:create`. The cross-machine join path joins the owner’s per-member GitHub links (`joinHiveAsView` parses each member link and clones the member repo). A repo-less `hive:create` home has no member links for the peer to join, so the peer never subscribes to that hive’s topic and owner writes have no remote log to arrive on. Use `hive:create_from_repo` (or an existing repo-bound hive with a joined peer member) for B8/B10-style ban, dissolve, grant, and receipt witnesses. A valid witness setup is: owner box owns the hive, peer box has joined at least one repo-bound member, then drive the federation action. EI-3409 — workspace-scoped MCP writes Superuser MCP resolves `ctx.workspaceId='*'` while the HTTP routes/queue use `'default'`, so a hive created via `mcp` lands in the wrong workspace and the routes return `not_owner_swarm`. For a workspace-scoped WRITE tool (`hive:create` / `hive:takedown` / `hive:report` / `hive:moderation_*`), pass `"workspace":"default"` in the args — or set `FED_MCP_WS=default` and `fed.sh` injects it for you (opt-in; off by default because blanket injection breaks READ tools whose schema rejects an unknown `workspace` key). The durable fix (superuser ctx resolving the concrete workspace) is tracked on **EI-3409**. ## Quick reference [Section titled “Quick reference”](#quick-reference) | symptom | do | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | drive a live fed VM (stale `/tmp/fed.sh` ports) | `scripts/linux-test-vm/fed.sh <a\|b> ports\|sql\|api\|mcp` (§7, WI-754) | | crashed/timed-out run left debris | `bin/reap-orphans.sh` (§1) | | one known run’s `$WORK` to clean | `bin/cleanup-run.sh <WORK>` (§1) | | “API never came up” / wrong port | now self-heals (WI-754, §3); read the dumped diagnostic | | stale `Xvfb` on a smoke display | `pgrep -af 'Xvfb :…'` → `kill <pid>` (§2) | | wedged Linux VM | `./vmctl reset` / `down` / `up <name>` (§4) | | wedged Mac VM | QMP recovery, never pkill (§4) | | re-run the scheduled gate | `bin/reap-orphans.sh` then `bin/live-federation-gate.sh` (§5) | | peer up but discovers/announces **nothing** (count:0, reachablePeers:0) | check `gh auth status` FIRST → restore gh auth (§6, WI-757) | | loopback smoke gets 0 peer dials, only on a fleet shell | check calling shell for `PAPERCUSP_DHT_HOST`/`PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP` (§6b) | | **anything** | **never** `pkill -f <rig>` / `rm -rf /tmp/<rig>.*` (EI-1739) |

# Flag flips on PostHog-less boxes — MCP flags:set fails, the HTTP route works

> MCP `flags:set` returns `flag-backend-not-configured` on any box without PostHog (this dev box included) — that does NOT mean flags are broken. The HTTP route `POST /api/flags/set` (loopback, no auth header needed from the box) has a PG-override fallback the MCP projection lacks: it writes the flip to the PG override store, publishes the change bus event, and records the flag:set audit row. Symptoms that mean READ THIS — "flag-backend-not- configured" from flags:set, a flag flip that silently never lands, audit rows showing backend pg-override.

## The gotcha [Section titled “The gotcha”](#the-gotcha) `flags:set` over MCP (papercusp-su) calls `setFlag()` and surfaces the raw PostHog failure: 
```json
{ "ok": false, "reason": "flag-backend-not-configured" }
```
 On a box with no PostHog credential (the shared dev box), **every MCP flag flip fails this way**. The flag system is fine — the *write fallback* only exists in the HTTP route. ## The working path [Section titled “The working path”](#the-working-path) 
```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3070/api/flags/set \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"key":"papercusp-improvement-auto-implement","enabled":true}'
# → {"ok":true,"key":"…","enabled":true,"backend":"pg-override"}
```
 The route (`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/flags/set.ts`, `auth: 'loopback'`) falls back to `setFlagOverride()` (PG override store), calls `publishFlagChange()` so live readers update without a restart, and records the `flag:set` audit row with `backend: pg-override`. Verify with MCP `flags:get` (the read side resolves overrides correctly on every transport). `/admin/features` rides this same route — the UI works too. ## Notes [Section titled “Notes”](#notes) * Reads are fine everywhere; only the MCP *write* lacks the fallback. Filed as EI-407 (transport divergence — the endpoint system promises one tool per verb across HTTP/MCP/IPC). * The audit trail for ANY flag flip is `audit:list` with action `flag:set` (singular — `flags:set` as an action filter matches nothing). * Observed during the consume-edges P-013 supervised proof (2026-06-12): both the protective pause and the un-pause of `papercusp-improvement-auto-implement` rode the pg-override fallback.

# A flag default graduating OFF→ON silently breaks legacy tests that assert the OFF contract

> When a feature flag's DEFAULT flips to ON, legacy unit tests that assert the OFF/legacy behavior WITHOUT pinning the flag silently start exercising the ON path — their assertions break and red the green-checkpoint gate. Fix = pin the flag explicitly in the legacy test. Symptom + fix + check.

**Symptom signature.** The green-checkpoint gate goes RED — for *hours*, across multiple candidates — on a handful of unit tests in a package you didn’t think you touched. Each failing test asserts a *legacy* behavior contract (`expect(...).toBe(false)`, “is per (workspace, install)”, “defaults installSlug to ‘op’”) and reproduces deterministically in isolation. Re-running doesn’t fix it. On 2026-06-24 this red the gate \~8h and pulled in 3 agents before the cause was named. **Why.** A flag-gated re-key ships dark, then its **default graduates to ON** (the repo’s normal end-state — finished work never ships dark). The NEW behavior gets its own `*-workspace-scope.test.ts` sibling that drives the flag ON deterministically. But the **pre-existing** unit tests still assert the OLD (flag-OFF) contract and **never pinned the flag** — they relied on the default being OFF. The moment the default flips, those tests silently exercise the ON path and their assertions break. Nothing about the flip touches the test file, so the red looks like it came from nowhere. Concrete case (workspace-scoped-coordination, `WORKSPACE_COORDINATION`): the brain re-key (`workspace-brain-scope.ts`) collapses per-(workspace,install) state to one row per workspace when ON. `control-state.test.ts` (“is per (workspace, install)”) and `scout-cycle.test.ts` (“defaults installSlug to ‘op’”) asserted the per-hive OFF contract → broke on graduation. **The fix (per failing legacy test).** Pin the flag to its OFF value so the test deterministically exercises the legacy/kill-switch path it was written for — independent of the production default. Mock the flag-gate helper, not PostHog: 
```ts
// Pin WORKSPACE_COORDINATION OFF so these unit tests exercise the per-(ws,install)
// keying path they were written for — independent of the production default,
// which graduated to ON. The ON path is covered by *-workspace-scope.test.ts.
vi.mock('../../workspace-brain-scope.js', async (importOriginal) => {
  const actual = await importOriginal<Record<string, unknown>>();
  return { ...actual, isWorkspaceCoordinationOn: () => Promise.resolve(false) };
});
```
 This is correct, not gaming: the OFF path is the reversible kill-switch and must stay tested. The ON path lives in the sibling `*-workspace-scope.test.ts`. **Check before you graduate a flag default to ON.** Grep every test that touches the flag-gated code path; any that asserts the OFF-behavior contract WITHOUT explicitly pinning the flag will break on the flip. Pin them OFF (or move the assertion to the ON contract) in the SAME change that flips the default — don’t let the green gate discover it for you. This is the contract-break cousin of [default-on-flag-glue-vs-hermetic-unit-tests](/internal/docs/agent-insights/default-on-flag-glue-vs-hermetic-unit-tests) (that one is the live-PG-write hazard; this one is the assertion break).

# Fleet bee killed by the DBOS invoke timeout (was 600s/10 min; default now 45 min)

> A bee:spawn'd bee that fails with exit 143 (SIGTERM), an EMPTY error_message, and a duration landing exactly on PAPERCUSP_DBOS_INVOKE_TIMEOUT_MS was killed by the DBOS invoke timeout (invokeTimeoutMs(), orchestrator-runner.ts). The default was 600_000ms (10 min) when first hit — three bees died that way on 2026-06-11 mid-edit, one leaving the shared tree red — and has since been raised to 2_700_000ms (45 min). Don't re-dispatch a task that outruns the timeout into the same guillotine — do it inline or raise the env.

## Symptom [Section titled “Symptom”](#symptom) A `bee:spawn`’d agent shows `failed` in the nursery (`harness_shared.spawned_agents`) with: * `exit_code` **143** (SIGTERM) * `error_message` **empty** — nothing distinguishes it from a crash * `finished_at - started_at` = **exactly the invoke timeout** (the tell — measure it; default now **2,700 s / 45 min**, was **600 s / 10 min** when the bees below died) * `output_tail` cut off mid-sentence, mid-work * no respawn, even with `restart_strategy = one_for_one` Three bees died this way on 2026-06-11 (20:06, 20:19, 22:34). The 22:34 one was mid-way through hive-network-surface P-014: its half-landed edits left the shared tree with a tsc +1 over baseline and a 20/21-failing integration suite that other agents then tripped over for hours. ## Root cause [Section titled “Root cause”](#root-cause) The DBOS invoke path wraps every spawned run in a hard timeout: 
```ts
// packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/orchestrator-runner.ts:96-97
export const invokeTimeoutMs = (): number =>
  Number(process.env.PAPERCUSP_DBOS_INVOKE_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 2_700_000);
```
 2 700 000 ms = 45 minutes — raised from the original 600 000 ms / 10 min (the three bees below died at the old 10-minute default, which “was insufficient” per the code comment). A coding bee with a long brief can still exceed it. `operator-spawn.ts` supports a per-spawn `timeoutMs` override (threaded to the DBOS step), but **`bee:spawn` does not expose it** — so a dispatcher cannot grant a longer window. Filed as **EI-361** (with the empty-`error_message` and dead `one_for_one` legs). ## What to do [Section titled “What to do”](#what-to-do) * **Diagnose**: `SELECT status, exit_code, finished_at - started_at FROM harness_shared.spawned_agents WHERE spawn_id = '…'` — `143` + a duration landing on the invoke timeout (default `00:45:00`, or whatever `PAPERCUSP_DBOS_INVOKE_TIMEOUT_MS` is set to) ⇒ timeout kill, not a crash. Check `output_tail` for where it died. * **Don’t blind-retry**: a retry of a brief that outruns the timeout dies the same death and may leave MORE half-landed edits. Either do the work inline (an interactive session has no invoke timeout), split the brief into chunks each well under the timeout, or raise `PAPERCUSP_DBOS_INVOKE_TIMEOUT_MS` on the spawning host until EI-361 lands a per-spawn override. * **Always sweep for partial work** after such a kill: the bee’s edits are in the shared tree (git-sync swept them) — `git log` the kill window and check `lint:tsc` / the touched suites before assuming “nothing landed”.

# Session-level behavior lives in agent_activity, NOT tool_invocations — spawn_id can't group sessions

> harness_shared.tool_invocations.spawn_id is per-call or per-surface (palette, dev-page, one-shot UUIDs) for ~99% of rows, so grouping it never reconstructs an agent session; the per-CLI activity bridge (harness_shared.agent_activity, keyed owner_id+session_id) is the real session stream — native AND mcp__* calls, ~100–300 sessions/day since 2026-06-04.

## The trap [Section titled “The trap”](#the-trap) `harness_shared.tool_invocations` looks like the obvious substrate for per-session behavioral analysis — every dispatched tool call lands there, and its `spawn_id` column is documented as the session/spawn identity. It is not usable that way. Measured over 30 days (2026-06-12): * **1.41M of 1.41M+ distinct spawn\_ids had exactly ONE call** — one-shot UUIDs minted per request. * The few “busy” spawn\_ids are **fixed surface labels, not sessions**: `palette` (183k calls), `''`, `event-reaction`, `dev-page`. * `role` is `operator` for \~99% of traffic — the desktop UI’s dispatch, not agents. Group by `spawn_id` and you get either singletons or a single years-long “session” named `palette`. Per-call analyses (the negative-space miner’s zero-hit search mining, `dev:telemetry` rollups) are fine; session reconstruction is impossible. ## The substrate that works [Section titled “The substrate that works”](#the-substrate-that-works) `harness_shared.agent_activity` (migration 143 — the cross-CLI activity bridge) is the real per-session stream: one row per tool call from every worker CLI (Claude Code / Codex / OMP), **native tools (Bash, Edit, Read…) and `mcp__*` dispatches alike**, keyed by `(owner_id, session_id)` with `agent`, `tool_name`, `phase` (`pre`/`post`), `status` (`ok`/`error`/null), `detail`, `created_at`. * Use `kind = 'tool' AND phase = 'post'` for completed calls. * Scope `workspace_id IN (<ws>, '*')` — unscoped SU sessions (most real traffic) land in the `'*'` bucket. * Volume: \~100–300 sessions/day, \~10–25k events/day; populated **since 2026-06-04** (the bridge’s landing) — a “last 30 days” ask older than that has no data, by construction. * `status` is null for \~14% of post rows — exclude nulls from error-rate denominators. `lib/fleet-ekg/scan.ts#readSessionEvents` is the canonical reader (grouping + scoping done); `lib/fleet-ekg/features.ts` turns a session’s rows into a named behavioral vector. ## Rule [Section titled “Rule”](#rule) Per-CALL questions (which tool, how often, error classes) → `tool_invocations`. Per-SESSION questions (behavior, pacing, rhythm, anything grouped by agent session) → `agent_activity`. Don’t trust `spawn_id` as a session key without checking the calls-per-spawn histogram first.

# Don't infer the fleet's inference plan from credential presence — check the wire

> Agents repeatedly conclude "the fleet runs on the Claude Max subscription" from the presence of a `subscriptionType: max` OAuth in `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, without checking what the spawned `claude -p` bee actually presents on the wire. Credential presence ≠ the subscription serving the workload. Cost telemetry and 429s reinforce the wrong conclusion. Run `npm run check:fleet-auth` for the ground truth — and note the 2026-06-11 addendum: bees present `~/.papercusp/claude-token` (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN), NOT the global OAuth your probe uses; A/B both credentials before declaring auth healthy.

## The recurring mistake [Section titled “The recurring mistake”](#the-recurring-mistake) When the fleet is rate-limited and someone asks “are we on the API or the Max plan?”, agents check `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, see a `claudeAiOauth` block with `subscriptionType: max`, and conclude **“we’re on Max, this is just a transient throttle.”** This conclusion is reached over and over, and it skips the one thing that actually answers the question: **what the spawned `claude -p` process authenticates with on the wire, and whether that auth is the right one for a headless fleet.** The presence of OAuth credentials does **not** prove the subscription is usefully serving the workload. Two signals actively mislead: 1. **Cost telemetry looks like API billing.** claude-code reports a **non-zero `total_cost_usd` even on a subscription** — it’s an *equivalent-cost estimate* (tokens × list price), not a bill. `harness_shared.agent_usage_samples` stores it with `cost_source: provider`. So agents see real dollar figures and conclude “API key.” Wrong — the number is the same shape on both plans. 2. **It 429s, so it “looks like it’s working, just busy.”** A rate-limited bee is *authenticated* (429, not 401), so the auth obviously “works” — which gets read as “Max is fine, back off and retry.” But on a consumer subscription driven headless at fleet concurrency, the throttle is the **structural** symptom, not a transient blip. ## The ground truth: check the wire, not the config [Section titled “The ground truth: check the wire, not the config”](#the-ground-truth-check-the-wire-not-the-config) Run: 
```bash
npm run check:fleet-auth        # scripts/check-fleet-auth.mjs
```
 It runs one real `claude -p` call with `ANTHROPIC_LOG=debug` (the SDK’s HTTP logging — **this**, not the `--debug` flag, dumps the request) and classifies the **actual request auth**: * **`x-api-key` header present** ⇒ an **API key** (pay-per-token, proper API rate-limit tiers). * **`authorization: Bearer …` + `anthropic-beta: oauth-…`** ⇒ the **subscription OAuth**. It also greps every spawn-relevant env (`process.env`, `.env.local`, the `papercup-{dev,staging}-api` host process envs via `/proc`) for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — the only thing that flips a `claude` spawn off the OAuth path (claude precedence: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env → `apiKeyHelper` → OAuth file). ## What was verified on this box (2026-06-08) [Section titled “What was verified on this box (2026-06-08)”](#what-was-verified-on-this-box-2026-06-08) Every layer was traced, not inferred: | Layer | Finding | | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Command | `AGENT_CMD=claude` on both hosts → bees run raw `claude -p` (not omp/Meridian) | | API key | **None** anywhere — host envs, `.env.local`, shell, `~/.claude.json`, `settings.json`, no `apiKeyHelper`/`forceLoginMethod` | | Per-spawn creds | `writeSpawnClaudeConfig` (spawn-mcp.ts) **symlinks `~/.claude/.credentials.json`** (the Max OAuth) into each bee’s `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | | **Wire** | request sends `authorization: Bearer …` + `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` — **subscription OAuth, not `x-api-key`** | So the fleet **does** authenticate with the Max OAuth. But that is the trap’s other half: ## The part that matters — a consumer subscription is the wrong auth for a headless fleet [Section titled “The part that matters — a consumer subscription is the wrong auth for a headless fleet”](#the-part-that-matters--a-consumer-subscription-is-the-wrong-auth-for-a-headless-fleet) A consumer **Pro/Max** subscription is gated for **interactive, single-session** Claude Code. Driving it **headless (`claude -p`) at fleet concurrency** (a hive of opus-xhigh agents + N bees through one OAuth) gets throttled hard — `"Server is temporarily limiting requests (not your usage limit)"`. The subscription is technically the auth, but the fleet is **not getting usable Max throughput** from it. In the sense that matters, *the Max subscription is not actually serving the fleet* — which is the real thing to discover, and the thing the “creds exist → Max → fine” shortcut misses. **The fix for a production fleet is a real `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`** (or Bedrock / Vertex) with an appropriate rate-limit tier — set it in the spawning host’s env so `claude` picks it up (`x-api-key`), and lean on the API’s proper rate-limit headers instead of fighting a consumer throttle. The fleet’s AIMD concurrency back-off + the Apiary runner’s rate-limit relaunch (`bee-instance.ts`) mitigate the throttle but cannot fix an auth/workload mismatch. ## Addendum (2026-06-11) — there are TWO credentials; probe the one the workload presents [Section titled “Addendum (2026-06-11) — there are TWO credentials; probe the one the workload presents”](#addendum-2026-06-11--there-are-two-credentials-probe-the-one-the-workload-presents) The 2026-06-08 table above is one layer stale: since the fleet-token staging landed, bees no longer ride the symlinked global OAuth. `fleet-claude-token.ts` (orchestrator) reads `~/.papercusp/claude-token` (a dedicated long-lived `claude setup-token`, staged so a psu `/login` can’t rotate it away) and `invoke.ts` exports it as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` for everything the fleet spawns — and that env var **outranks the credentials file**.
