Signal is limited when no spec-driven hive is running (rate `unknown`). `model_fit` is neutral until its lane ships — do NOT flag its absence. * **Drift markers.** Queen micro-dispatching item-by-item instead of issuing/versioning specs; bees bypassing the scheduler (self-prioritizing the raw frontier, hand-claiming) instead of pulling via `get_next`; non-deterministic or floor-violating resolution; duplicate-plan-item claims (dedup floor breached); pulled claims that never make progress (zombie holds). NOT a drift: `model_fit` being neutral (descoped). Low evidence (no spec-driven hive running) is `unknown`, not `broken`. ## How to grade (the observation shape) [Section titled “How to grade (the observation shape)”](#how-to-grade-the-observation-shape) An agent grading this rubric files a structured observation (via `improvements:capture { lane: 'observation', observation: { ... } }`). The `ratings` shape follows the P-001 accept schema (`rubric-driven-observations-2026-06-20` D-003) — a map keyed by the criterion `key`, one entry per criterion assessed, evidence MANDATORY (capture rejects an empty-evidence rating): 
```jsonc
{
  "rubricRef": "hive-coordination-health",
  "ratings": {
    "end-to-end-flow":          { "rating": "degraded", "evidence": "scout 0 ideas/24h (transport-death) but bees completing WI-214 03:43; closure broken at the scout->plan hand-off" },
    "queen-workitem-selection": { "rating": "healthy",  "evidence": "held WI-263/268 (needs-design), left WI-231 (cursed), placed the 2 actionable bugs — matches what I'd pick" }
    // ... key = a rubric criterion `key`; rating = a value from that criterion's scale
  }
}
```
 Rate only what the live evidence supports; an unobservable criterion is `unknown` with the reason as evidence. Never invent a rating to fill the scorecard. ## See also [Section titled “See also”](#see-also) * `rubric-driven-observations-2026-06-20` — the plan (D-001 model, D-002 scope + owner #1, D-003 the schema contract). * `hive-coordination-test-loop-2026-06-20` D-001 — the owner’s original 13-question scorecard this rubric crystallizes. * `rubrics:get { rubric_id: 'hive-coordination-health' }` — the structured rubric (criteria keys, rating scale, drift markers).

# Hive instance prompt overrides must be ADDITIVE — never a wholesale base snapshot

> A hive's promptOverride.<role> is APPENDED after the generated blueprint persona, so it must carry only the hive-specific delta — never a full copy of the generated base. A wholesale snapshot silently duplicates content and freezes it (a stale section drifts from the generated source forever). Covers the additive-append mechanism, the papercup-hive su wholesale-snapshot incident + fix, how to put generic content in the generated base (marker + render note), the warn-only guard, and the re-seed path.

## The rule [Section titled “The rule”](#the-rule) A hive’s per-role prompt override (`hive_settings` key `promptOverride.<role>`, federated over the hive peer-log) is **APPENDED after** the generated blueprint persona — it **specializes, it never replaces** (`getHiveInstancePromptOverride` → `role-launch-spec` appends `inst`; the store’s own comment: *“the override SPECIALIZES … it does not replace the role”*). So an override must contain **only the hive-specific delta**. The default prompt is the GENERATED chain (`blueprints/<chain>/prompts/<role>.md` + the spliced sections + the client tooling overlay); a hive adds its specifics on top. **Generated by default; the override only when a user explicitly authors one — and even then, only the additive part.** ## The trap (what went wrong) [Section titled “The trap (what went wrong)”](#the-trap-what-went-wrong) It is tempting to author an override by copying the whole assembled prompt and tweaking it. That is a **wholesale snapshot**, and it is wrong two ways: 1. **It duplicates.** The override re-states sections the generated base already supplies (AUTO mode, looping, coordination, “Who you are”, wire schemas…). The assembled prompt then carries each twice. 2. **It freezes.** The snapshot is a point-in-time copy in PG. When the generated source changes (e.g. the `## AUTO mode` clause is reworded/consolidated), the override keeps the **stale** copy forever — and because it’s appended *last*, the stale version is what the agent reads. Real incident (2026-06-24): `papercusp/promptOverride.su` was a \~21.6 KB wholesale copy of `hive-instances/papercup-hive.su.md`. With `su-blueprint-persona` ON, the generated su base is the *generic* `blueprints/base/prompts/su.md` (which carried no AUTO mode), so **every** Papercusp-specific section — including a now-stale `## AUTO mode` — was riding the frozen snapshot. A fresh edit to the canonical AUTO clause never reached the live hive psu, and consolidating AUTO would have produced a *contradictory double* (fresh generated + stale appended). ## The fix pattern [Section titled “The fix pattern”](#the-fix-pattern) When you find generic content trapped in an override, **move it to the generated chain and slim the override to the delta**: 1. **Put the generic/cross-cutting content in the generated base**, authored once. The clean mechanism is a render function + a splice marker (mirrors `renderWireSchemasSection` / `renderCoordLegend`): e.g. `renderModesPolicy()` in `operating-modes-policy.ts`, spliced at `AUTO_MODE_MARKER` by `renderSuPlaybook` / `writeSplicedPlaybook`. Add the marker to the bases that should carry it (`blueprints/base/prompts/su.md`, `papercusp-su-engineer.tools.md`, `papercusp-su-power.tools.md`). An absent marker is a clean no-op (a base may opt out). 2. **Re-seed the override without the moved content.** `hive-instances/<hive>.<role>.md` is the version-controlled SOURCE; the live copy is the federated `promptOverride.<role>` in `hive_settings` (they DIVERGE — the file is not auto-synced). Re-seed via the loopback write path: `POST /api/agent-mcp/hive-override-set { hiveSlug, kind:'prompt', name:'<role>', value:<file md> }` (an empty value CLEARS it). Verify the PG row updated (`harness_shared.hive_settings`). ## The guard [Section titled “The guard”](#the-guard) `hive-override-additive-guard.ts` (`additiveOverrideWarning(md)`) detects the smell — an override that re-states a base-owned section heading or embeds a `PAPERCUSP-SU:` splice marker — and the `hive-override-set` route surfaces it as a **non-blocking warning** (overrides are the owner’s to author; we flag, we don’t gate). If you’re adding a new generic section to the base, add its heading to `BASE_OWNED_HEADINGS` so the guard keeps catching copies of it. ## Why it’s not flag- or materialization-sensitive [Section titled “Why it’s not flag- or materialization-sensitive”](#why-its-not-flag--or-materialization-sensitive) The su prompt is assembled by `renderSuPlaybook` on **both** paths — `su-blueprint-persona` OFF (base = `papercusp-su-engineer.tools.md`) and ON (base = the generic `blueprints/base/prompts/su.md`) — so the marker belongs in whichever base a path uses. Prompt files resolve from the integration/staging tree (`promptHarnessRoot` → `PAPERCUSP_PROMPT_ROOT`/`PAPERCUSP_INTEGRATION_ROOT`, else `harnessRoot()` = `libs/papercusp/packages/harness`), so editing the canonical `libs/` source goes live for new sessions without a release. The `.papercusp/.materialized/` + desktop `sidecar/harness/` copies are generated artifacts — they regenerate from `libs/` at build; don’t hand-edit them. ## See also [Section titled “See also”](#see-also) * [override-settings-backbone](/internal/docs/agent-insights/override-settings-backbone) — the broader hive override + local-blueprint settings backbone. * [engine-managed-loops](/internal/docs/agent-insights/engine-managed-loops) — `loop:arm` cadence, which the AUTO-mode clause references.

# The Hive Queen is already fresh-per-wake (--session-id), not a forever-session

> Every declared/event/watchdog Queen wake spawns a FRESH claude session via the hive launch blueprint (--session-id <new uuid>), carrying NO transcript. The only --resume path is the generic wake-executor inbox/await delivery channel. Map of the wake paths + where resume-vs-fresh is decided.

## What [Section titled “What”](#what) A common (and load-bearing) misread: “the Hive Queen RESUMES her prior session every wake (`claude --resume`), so she’s a forever-session with an unbounded growing transcript.” **This is wrong.** Verify before designing on it. The Queen’s **declared, event, watchdog, and manual wakes are ALL already fresh-per-wake** — each spawns a brand-new claude session with a fresh session id and **no carried transcript**. Historically the only path that `--resume`d the Queen was the *generic* wake-executor inbox/await delivery channel (a `coord:send` with `wake:true` to her owner id, or an `events:await` she registered — which her persona tells her not to use) — **that exception is now closed** (queen-brief-cache-assembly B-01/P-012, see Consequence below): `wake-executor.ts` detects a hive-operator session and routes even that path through the same fresh hive launch. ## The wake paths (ALL fresh — the last exception closed by P-012) [Section titled “The wake paths (ALL fresh — the last exception closed by P-012)”](#the-wake-paths-all-fresh--the-last-exception-closed-by-p-012) | Path | Trigger | Mechanism | Session | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | Time wake | `hive:declare-wake {inSeconds}` | `hive-wake` routine → DBOS routinesTick → `system:blueprint-run` → `fireLaunchBlueprint('hive')` → `POST /harness/:slug/invoke?bpkind=hive` | **FRESH** | | Event wake | `hive:declare-wake {events}` | reaction rule → `hive:wake` tool → `fireLaunchBlueprint('hive')` → same invoke route | **FRESH** | | Watchdog recovery | turn-end / boot / 30s tick (`watchdog.ts armFallbackHiveWake`) | `declareHiveTimeWake` → same routine | **FRESH** | | Manual / user | `hive:wake` | `fireLaunchBlueprint('hive')` → same invoke route | **FRESH** | | Inbox / await | `coord:send {wake:true}` to her owner id, or her own `events:await` | await pump → `wake-executor.ts executeWake` → detects the `hive ·` label → `defaultFireHiveWake` → `fireLaunchBlueprint('hive')` | **FRESH** (closed exception — was `--resume` before P-012 landed) | ### Where “fresh” is decided [Section titled “Where “fresh” is decided”](#where-fresh-is-decided) `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/harness/spawn.ts` (the `/invoke?bpkind=hive` route): mints `nativeSessionId = randomUUID()` **fresh on every fire** and passes it as `PAPERCUSP_NATIVE_SESSION_ID`. Then `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/invoke.ts` turns that into `claude --session-id <uuid>` — which **creates a new session**, never `--resume`. Because the uuid is freshly minted each fire, no transcript is ever continued. The session id is *recorded* in `adv_sessions` so the **inbox/await** path (wake-executor) *could* later `claude --resume <that id>` — but that path resumes the LAST short fresh session (one turn), never a forever-transcript. ### The easy way to get it wrong [Section titled “The easy way to get it wrong”](#the-easy-way-to-get-it-wrong) The misread conflates three true-but-unrelated facts: (a) the BEE forced session id at `operator-spawn.ts:646-656` (that’s `bee:spawn`, recorded so a bee *pane* can `--resume`); (b) the `spawn.ts` comment noting a bee’s `coord:send {wake:true}` resumes the Queen via wake-executor; (c) `resumeCommandFor` building `claude --resume`. None of those is the Queen’s scheduled-wake path. ## Consequence [Section titled “Consequence”](#consequence) * The Queen ALREADY re-derives her working state from durable world-state every scheduled wake — and it works. Her load-bearing cross-wake state lives in durable artifacts (work-item claims, `blocked_by` edges, priorities, the `hive:declare-wake` routine, presence, the decision ledger), not the transcript. * **The cutover has now landed** — the Queen is **uniformly** fresh-per-wake; the “one exception” row in the table above is closed. `wake-executor.ts executeWake` detects a hive-operator session by its `adv_sessions` label (`hive · <slug>/<role>`, `hiveInstallSlugFromLabel()`) and routes its ended-session wake through the SAME fresh hive launch (`defaultFireHiveWake` → `fireLaunchBlueprint(HIVE_BLUEPRINT_ID, ...)`, the wake text as kickoff) instead of `resumeCommandFor` — so an inbox-wake or an `events:await` firing on an ended Queen session no longer resumes a stale transcript. A wake-floor debounce (`withinWakeFloor`/`effectiveHiveWakeFloorSec`) collapses a burst of bee-wakes within the floor window to one fresh launch. On fire-failure: PARK, never resume (the always-armed time/watchdog wake re-surveys). All other (non-Queen) agents still resume as before. (queen-brief-cache-assembly B-01 / P-012, channel `hive-fresh-wake`.) ## How to verify [Section titled “How to verify”](#how-to-verify) `grep -n 'randomUUID\|--session-id' spawn.ts invoke.ts` shows the fresh mint + `--session-id` create. `resumeCommandFor` (`--resume`) is reached only from `executeWake`, which is the await/inbox pump — not the hive routine/blueprint path. Don’t trust a prose claim that “the Queen resumes” without tracing the `fireLaunchBlueprint('hive') → invoke?bpkind=hive → --session-id` chain.

# HIVE_REKEY (C-001 read-plane re-key) flip-readiness — code-complete, owner-gated on the live 2-machine cut witness

> The papercusp-hive-rekey flip is an ATTENDED security cutover, not a code task. The op-path is wired end-to-end (encrypt-on-write, decrypt-on-read, advance-on-boundary), the hermetic end-to-end content read-cut witness is green, and ~88 re-key tests pass. The ONE remaining gate is the live 2-machine K-CUT-on-content witness (WI-560, blocked on WI-559 peering). This is the exact flip surface (3 edits), the evidence, the residual risk, and the go/no-go the owner ratifies against.

## TL;DR — what the owner is deciding [Section titled “TL;DR — what the owner is deciding”](#tldr--what-the-owner-is-deciding) `papercusp-hive-rekey` (FLAGS.HIVE\_REKEY) is the master gate for the shared-hive **read-plane re-key** (C-001): hive CONTENT is AEAD-encrypted under a per-epoch group key, and a removed/excluded member loses the ability to **READ** post-boundary content (key-denial **and** ciphertext-unreadability), not just the ability to write. **This is no longer a code task.** As of 2026-06-24 the op-path is wired end-to-end, the hermetic **end-to-end content read-cut witness is green**, and \~88 re-key tests pass. WI-403’s 2026-06-22 note (“advanceEpochAndWrap + encrypt-on-write + decrypt-on-read are NOT yet in the live op path — resolveHiveEpochCrypto returns the notImplemented stub”) is **STALE** — that wiring has since landed. The flag stays dark **only** because flipping it begins encrypting **live** federated content: a crypto/op-path bug would break federation reads for a whole hive. So the dark case is an **attended security cutover** (owner-authority), gated on the **live 2-machine K-CUT-on-content witness** (WI-560) + owner ratification — exactly the carve-out the CLAUDE.md dark-flag rule reserves for a “reversible CUTOVER kill-switch needing an attended live verify the OWNER runs.” The owner performs the flip; an agent must not flip it. ## What is wired (the live op-path) [Section titled “What is wired (the live op-path)”](#what-is-wired-the-live-op-path) All flag-gated on `papercusp-hive-rekey`; **OFF ⇒ byte-identical to today** (no encryption, the `notImplementedHiveEpochCrypto` fail-closed stub). | Concern | Where | Note | | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Flag gate / crypto resolve | `hive-epoch-serving.ts` `resolveHiveEpochCrypto(enabled)` | `true` ⇒ real `createHiveEpochCrypto()` (sodium); `false` ⇒ fail-closed stub (never silent plaintext) | | Boot composition (flag FIRST) | `hive-epoch-boot-deps.ts` `buildHiveRekeyBootDeps` | one cached flag read; `null` for OFF / non-hive / no-device — cheap off-path | | Encrypt-on-write | `wire-outbox.ts` → `outbox-drain.ts` (`epochEncrypt.encryptOp`) | exclude-set: `shouldEncryptOpForRekey` encrypts all CONTENT, keeps admission/key/policy tags plaintext (`REKEY_PLAINTEXT_TAGS`), fail-closed (new tag defaults to encrypted) | | Decrypt-on-read | `boot.ts` `rekeyDeps.epochGate(enforcedApply)` | op carries its `epoch`; gate resolves epoch key → decrypt, else defers (pending-epoch buffer) | | Advance-on-boundary (revoke) | `hive-revoke-contributor.ts` → `advanceEpochOnHiveBoundary` | wraps the new epoch key to REMAINING members only; revoked device excluded forever (K-CUT). Loud `rekey_boundary_skipped` boot event if it no-ops | | Advance-on-boundary (go-private) | `hive-set-listing.ts` → `advanceEpochOnHiveBoundary` | re-keys to all current members (no cutOff) | | Deferred-content drain | `boot.ts` `epochDrainQueue` / `onEpochKeyApplied` | re-applies buffered content once a member’s key row arrives | ## No durable green idle-reconnect witness yet. * **`WI-560` (F-MEMBER-KCUT):** fed-b is a VIEW-joiner but **not yet a real crypto member** (`hive_epoch_keys` has 0 rows for it) — the member-admission path on the 2-machine rig isn’t cracked, so a true K-revoke→K-CUT on the binary hasn’t been witnessed. # Re-keying a hyperbee harness onto a new swarm topic must be IN PLACE, never via reboot

> A harness that goes shared (joins or publishes a hive after boot) must switch from its gh-repo topic to the hive-pubkey topic. Doing that with rebootHarness (close + re-boot the Corestore-backed substrate) silently breaks the OWNER's corestore replication-SERVING of its own log core — the re-keyed owner admits + connects to the joiner and knows its log length, but fires ZERO upload events, so the joiner downloads zero blocks (contig=0) and the feature never crosses. Re-key IN PLACE instead with handle.rekey / rekeyHarness — leave the old topic + join the new one while keeping the store, open cores, and replication streams ALIVE. The symptom is asymmetric — the joiner serves its log to the owner fine; only the owner-to-joiner direction is dead.

When a harness “goes shared” at runtime — an owner **publishes** a hive, or a peer **joins** one — its substrate booted earlier (at host-bootstrap) on the `gh:<repo_id>` topic, before the hive identity existed. It must **re-key** onto the hive-pubkey topic so owner + joiner share a topic. The obvious primitive is `rebootHarness` (close the handle, boot fresh, re-resolve the binding). **That is wrong, and the failure is silent + asymmetric.** ## The symptom [Section titled “The symptom”](#the-symptom) The feature written on the owner (A) never lands in the joiner (B), even though every earlier step passes: same hive topic, `peer_connected` both ways, `announce_admitted` both ways with the **correct** log keys (`A.ownLog == B.admitted` and vice-versa). The packaged `two-instance-hive-from-repo-smoke.sh` shows `post-join-merge=FAIL` with everything else green. Instrument the replicas (`core.peers`, `core.contiguousLength`, and the `upload`/`download` events) and the asymmetry is stark: * **B → A works:** B’s own log fires `upload` for blocks 0..N; A’s replica of B’s log reaches `contig=N`. The joiner serves its log fine. * **A → B is dead:** B’s replica of A’s log has `peers=1` and knows the length, but `contig=0` — it downloads **nothing**. And **A fires ZERO `upload` events for its own log core.** The owner never serves. So it is not a missing session, a wrong topic, a bad key, or admission — it is that **the re-keyed OWNER does not upload its own writable log core to the joiner.** ## Why reboot breaks it [Section titled “Why reboot breaks it”](#why-reboot-breaks-it) A↔B share ONE Hyperswarm socket (Hyperswarm dedupes per peer-pair), carrying ONE Protomux muxer that the **directory** swarm creates first (gossip) and the harness `corestore.replicate(socket)` then rides (`socket.userData`). When `rebootHarness` tears the Corestore-backed substrate down and re-creates it, the owner’s writable log core is re-opened against a session whose serving side never gets re-attached to that pre-existing external muxer. The owner can still *download* (it pulls B’s log) but never *uploads* its own. `keepStore` (keeping the Corestore cached across the reboot) is **not** enough — re-creating the handle/swarm/streams still drops the serving side. ## The fix — re-key in place [Section titled “The fix — re-key in place”](#the-fix--re-key-in-place) Never reboot to re-key. Leave the old topic and join the new one on the **same live handle**, keeping the store + open cores + replication streams + merge loop untouched: * `boot.ts` exposes `handle.rekey(binding)` — closes the current `SwarmHandle` (leave old topic), then `joinForBinding(newBinding)` (join the new topic) with the SAME `store` / `ownLog` / `onAnnounce`. `swarm` is a live getter, not a boot-time snapshot. * `boot-all.ts` exposes `rekeyHarness(workspaceId, slug)` — re-resolves the binding via `defaultResolveSwarmBinding` (which calls `resolveHiveSwarmBinding` first, so a shared hive resolves the hive-pubkey topic) and calls `handle.rekey`. Falls back to `bootSingleHarness` when not yet booted. * The two “go shared” call sites use it: `join-hive.ts` step 2c (joiner) and `hive-publish-from-repo.ts` step 7 (owner). Because the streams are never torn down, the owner keeps serving its log core, and the new joiner’s block requests are answered immediately. `post-join-merge` flips to PASS (verified stable across repeated runs of the from-repo smoke). ## The general lesson [Section titled “The general lesson”](#the-general-lesson) For any Corestore/Hypercore peer multiplexed over a **shared, externally-created muxer**, a topic change must be a swarm-level leave+join — **never** a teardown * re-create of the data layer. Tearing down the store drops the serving side of replication for cores that were open before the tear-down, and a fresh store cannot re-attach to the surviving muxer. Verify with `upload`/`download` core events + `contiguousLength`, not just `peers` and `length` — a peer can be connected, know the remote length, and still download zero blocks.

# Hive-scoped federation (re-key from harness → Hive identity)

> How a shared project's substrate federates at HIVE scope, not harness scope — the Ed25519-pubkey topic re-key, per-Hive admission (revoked-pubkey union), Track A coord/presence, and Track B lock authority. Read before touching lib/hive-federation.ts, lib/authority/*, lib/sync/hyperbee/{boot,boot-all,wire-presence}.ts, or anything that resolves a swarm topic / lock authority. Includes the complete P-003 anchor inventory — every capture trigger, PEER_LOG_TAG_TO_TABLE tag, drain-routing site, and lib/authority scope-key. Plan — shared-hive-federation-2026-06-08.

## One paragraph [Section titled “One paragraph”](#one-paragraph) Federation used to key on `harness_slug` (migs 144/150 — a pre-redesign artifact). As of `shared-hive-federation-2026-06-08` the sharing boundary is the **Hive** (the project = harnesses + plans + settings, identified by a stable **Ed25519 keypair**), not the harness. A shared Hive federates its substrate over **one topic derived from the Hive pubkey**; all of the Hive’s harnesses join that one topic, and `harness_slug` demotes to the **within-Hive component demux**. This was a **re-key, not a rebuild** (D-003): the Model-B peer-log, projections, Hyperswarm transport, and admission/revocation machinery are unchanged — only the topic key + scope boundary moved. Cross-Hive (message-passing between sovereign Hives) is **BUILT and wired** (this previously said “deferred” — stale, corrected by cross-machine-coord-parity-and-trust-2026-07-01 P-024): `hive:ask` / `hive:request_work` / `hive:asks` / `hive:cross_grant` over the dedicated `papercusp/cross-hive` Protomux transport, with a durable outbox (mig 196), the ask-ledger state machine (migs 231/235), and default-deny directed grants (`packages/operator-core/lib/cross-hive-*`). ## The load-bearing invariant [Section titled “The load-bearing invariant”](#the-load-bearing-invariant) `harness_slug` is NOT the federation key anymore — it is the **component scope inside** a Hive’s single peer-log. The Hive pubkey is the key. Re-keying a trigger or a projection back to `harness_slug` as the *top* unit re-breaks this (see D-010: the migs-144/150 triggers were verified a **no-op** precisely because `harness_slug` stays the capture/demux column while the *topic* routes content to the Hive). When you add federated state, scope it to the Hive topic and keep `harness_slug` as the demux — don’t reintroduce harness-as-top-unit. ## Where the scope is resolved [Section titled “Where the scope is resolved”](#where-the-scope-is-resolved) * **`lib/hive-federation.ts`** — `resolveHiveSwarmBinding(ws, harnessSlug)` returns `{ kind:'hive', hive_pubkey }` when the harness belongs to a **shared** Hive, else `null` (caller falls back to the per-harness gh/local binding). `hiveHomeSlugForHarness(ws, harnessSlug)` answers “which Hive is this harness in” (itself if it’s a `kind:'hive'` home, else its registry `hive_slug` member pointer) — shared by the topic re-key AND the admission/presence/authority seams. * **Gate — only a *shared* Hive federates.** “Shared” = the owner published the Hive to the directory as `public`/`invite` (`getOwnedHiveMeta(...).visibility`). A `private`/un-published Hive stays local-only and never announces on the DHT, so the re-key is a **dormant, zero-risk path** for today’s local hives (no privacy regression). The federation gate reuses directory visibility rather than minting a separate `federate` flag. ## Admission is per-Hive (P-006) — a UNION, fail-open [Section titled “Admission is per-Hive (P-006) — a UNION, fail-open”](#admission-is-per-hive-p-006--a-union-fail-open) A contributor/device joins the **Hive once** and is thereby admitted to all its member harnesses, instead of joining N harness swarms (D-004). The enforcement seam is in **`lib/sync/hyperbee/boot.ts`** (`bootHarnessSubstrateInner`): the revoked-pubkey set the harness boots with is the **UNION** of * the harness-scope revocations (`loadRevokedPubkeys`, the base set), and * the Hive-scope revocations (`loadRevokedHivePubkeys(ws, hiveHome)` from `lib/hive-membership-store.ts`) when `hiveHomeSlugForHarness` resolves a home — so a contributor revoked at the **Hive grain is refused on EVERY member harness**. The read-admission decider itself is unchanged. The hive lookup is **best-effort / fail-open**: a failure leaves the harness-scope set intact (you stay no-worse-than the pre-Hive behavior). Backing store: `hive_members` (mig 185) + the `hive_members` federation projection (mig 189). Membership is also **torn down on departure**: `hive:leave` (a member removing its own row, G27 — `removeHiveMember`) and `hive:dissolve` (the owner removing *all* members, G24 — `removeAllHiveMembers`) DELETE the relevant `hive_members` rows, which fire the **same mig-189 capture trigger** → a federated `del` membership tombstone, so peers’ read-merge drops the departed member (see `shared-hive-join-leave-lifecycle`). Membership **producers** (set `ProjectEntry.hive_slug`): `addHarnessToHive` / `removeHarnessFromHive` (`agent-tools/hive/_add-member.ts`) for an existing harness, and the `harness:create { hive }` create-time path (`agent-tools/harness/create-hive-membership.ts`). Until something sets `hive_slug`, a Hive has only its home and no members. **Boot-storm robustness (2026-07-03, WI-1892/P-059).** `boot-all.ts`’s `bootSingleHarness` races each harness’s boot against a timeout (default 30s, now operator-tunable via `PAPERCUSP_SUBSTRATE_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS`) — but a timed-out race does NOT unwind the underlying `bootHarness`: it keeps running detached, holding the corestore lock and (once it gets there) the joined swarm topic with no registered handle, so peers see a zombie endpoint that answers announces but never drains/replicates. Live-observed on a 35-substrate boot storm: 16/35 harnesses on one bg-host stuck this way. Until true cancellation lands, the raced boot promise is now retained and, if it settles AFTER the timeout, **adopted** — the handle is registered and the send-side wired exactly as the happy path would — unless a newer boot for the same key already won, in which case the late one is closed to release its corestore. Relevant here because this is the same boot path the per-Hive admission union (above) runs inside; a zombied boot under a large Hive (many member harnesses booting at once) is exactly the failure mode this guards. ## Track A — coord content + presence [Section titled “Track A — coord content + presence”](#track-a--coord-content--presence) * **Content (messages / conversations / threads / work / plans / settings)** rides the **same peer-log P-004 re-keyed**, so it already federates Hive-scoped — no separate Track-A content work was needed (D-011). `hive_settings` federate as first-class Hive state via their own projection (mig 186). * **Presence is the write-side keystone (P-008).** Presence is ephemeral / high-frequency, so it federates via an **announce loop**, not a capture trigger: **`lib/sync/hyperbee/wire-presence.ts`** (`wirePresenceAnnounceForHarness` → `startPresenceAnnounceLoop`), wired per-harness from `boot-all.ts` after the substrate handle returns, **gated on a joined swarm** (a private harness has no peers → returns `null`). Each announce is **stamped with the harness’s home `hive_slug`** (resolved once via `hiveHomeSlugForHarness`) and projected into `shared_presence.hive_slug` (mig 187) — which is exactly what the Hive lock authority elects over. * **2026-07-03 (P-301):** each announced session is now also stamped with `fleet_slug`/`fleet_role`, batch-resolved via `fetchPresenceFleet(ownerIds)` (one lookup for the whole announce, not N) and folded into the dedup hash alongside `owner_id`/`intent`/`plan_slug`. This is what lets `@fleet:<slug>` pattern-awaits and fleet-membership lookups resolve a fleet’s members **across machines** over the same Hive-federated presence channel — best-effort (a lookup failure just leaves `fleet_slug`/`fleet_role` null; it never fails the announce). ## Track B — lock authority is the HIVE’s (P-009) [Section titled “Track B — lock authority is the HIVE’s (P-009)”](#track-b--lock-authority-is-the-hives-p-009) File-claim / claim-lease mutual exclusion can’t ride the eventually-consistent peer-log (an exclusive through last-writer-wins split-brains), so contended acquires serialize at a single **lock authority**. The authority is **not elected** — it’s a deterministic function of live presence: `argmin(device_pubkey)` over fresh `shared_presence` rows (`lib/authority/lock-authority.ts`). * `lockAuthorityFor(harnessSlug)` — harness scope (`WHERE harness_slug`). * `lockAuthorityForHive(hiveSlug)` — Hive scope (`WHERE hive_slug`): **one authority across all of a Hive’s Swarms**. Same `selectAuthorityFromRows` core; only the presence query differs. * `routeToAuthority` / `routeToAuthorityForHive` — run local when we’re the authority, RPC when a transport + `op.remote` exist, else **fail-open** (D-004: git-merge + merge-resolver is the data-safety backstop, so a distributed lock is an optimization, not a correctness requirement). * `lib/authority/file-lock-routing.ts` — `routeFileLockOp(domain, op)` is the file-claim integration: it maps the lock’s `coordination_domain` → harness → (if a Hive member) the Hive, and routes to the Hive authority. A **remote-peers-cache** fast-path makes the common single-box case a cached boolean, not a `shared_presence` query. ## Why a no-op today, load-bearing tomorrow [Section titled “Why a no-op today, load-bearing tomorrow”](#why-a-no-op-today-load-bearing-tomorrow) The dev box runs one shared native PG, so every agent shares one `papercusp_su` lock store and PG advisory locks already serialize — the Hive authority resolves to `{ isSelf:true }` and routing is a direct local call. The **shipping product is a desktop app backed by embedded-pg per machine** (see *Database topology* in the repo CLAUDE.md): each machine then has its own lock store, so a file-claim on a shared file genuinely needs the cross-machine authority. Correct in both worlds; the cross-machine teeth grow in once presence federation populates remote Swarms’ `hive_slug` rows. Proven on real substrate: `two-instance-hive-authority.integration.test.ts` (serialization across two Swarms via `routeToAuthorityForHive` + production `routeFileLockOp`) and `hive-two-peer-federation.test.ts` (Track A content + Track B presence federate A→B over the Hive topic on real Hyperswarm). The *truly cross-machine* proof is layered (the plan’s P-011): the substrate holepunch + bidirectional merge is proven on REAL separate machines (`packaged-two-instance-federation-merge`), and the Hive-federation logic is proven at local parity here — but the combined “one Hive over two physical machines” run is owner-gated paid infra, because **same-host holepunch does not complete at the raw hyperswarm level for ANY topology** (`vm-federation-separate-machine-proof`), so it genuinely needs two separate boxes. ## The re-key surface — full anchor inventory (P-003) [Section titled “The re-key surface — full anchor inventory (P-003)”](#the-re-key-surface--full-anchor-inventory-p-003) The complete enumeration behind the D-010 “the migs-144/150 triggers are a no-op” invariant and the Track-B authority map above — every site that names the federation scope. It is the *evidence* that the re-key was a topic move, not a trigger rewrite: `harness_slug` is the **capture/demux column** everywhere, never the federation domain. Verified against live `staging` 2026-06-08. > **Line numbers below have drifted (re-verified 2026-07-03) and are no longer byte-exact** — this shared tree receives concurrent unrelated edits daily, so a `:281`-style citation from 2026-06-08 can shift by dozens of lines within weeks even when the function/table/gate it names is unchanged. Spot-checked 2026-07-03: every function, table, tag, and gate named below still exists with the described behavior (e.g. `lockAuthorityFor` now sits at line 314, not 281; `queryPresenceRowsForHive` at 189, not 167; `NOTIFY_CHANNEL` at 73, not 54; the `AuthorityOpEnvelope` interface is actually named `AuthorityRpcEnvelope`) — only the exact line numbers are stale, not the structure. Treat every `:NNN` below as “around there” and grep the symbol name to confirm, not as a pinned coordinate. (Origin: `fleet-federation-reanchor-2026-06-06` P-003 — that plan is superseded by this one; the inventory lives here because the surface it maps is live/shipped. Folded into the plan’s D-009.) ### 1 — Capture triggers (`libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/`) [Section titled “1 — Capture triggers (libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/)”](#1--capture-triggers-libspapercusplibsdbsql) Exactly **two** functions INSERT into `substrate_outbox`: `capture_substrate_outbox()` (`000-baseline.sql:10-53`, generic; keycol = `TG_ARGV[0]`) and its clone `capture_hive_members_outbox()` (`189:27`, identical but reads `hive_home_slug` into the slug column). Both write `substrate_outbox(workspace_id, harness_slug, table_name, op, key, row, ts)` and `pg_notify('substrate_outbox', workspace_id||'::'||slug)` — **one** NOTIFY channel. `substrate_outbox.harness_slug` is **NOT NULL** (`baseline:2524`), so there is no operator-scope/NULL federation path by construction. **Capture-ALL** (echo-guard only — no scope gate; # Seed-bundle design — installer-shipped shared-hive snapshot + live-join delta catch-up

> The P-001 design memo for the generic seed-bundle layer: a checkpoint of a replicated store (git + corestore) shipped in the installer so a fresh install pre-positions bytes, and the UNMODIFIED shared-hive join then transfers only the delta. Defines the SeedProvider interface, the manifest schema, the restore-before-join state machine, the security model (epoch-ciphertext corestore + encrypted-at-rest git seed, keys via admission), and resolves the four open questions (installer size, git-seed encryption envelope, cross-core cut skew, epoch read-cut for new members).

> **Status: AS-BUILT (P-001…P-011 landed, 2026-07-04).** Plan: [`hive-seed-bundle-2026-07-04`](/project-docs?harness=papercusp\&path=docs%2Fplans%2Fhive-seed-bundle-2026-07-04.md). Author: su-0824a, 2026-07-04 (AUTO). This memo is the **design** (why + the interface/manifest/state-machine spec); for **operations** — cutting a seed, debugging a restore, the `HIVE_SEED_BUNDLE` kill-switch, every failure mode, and the cold-join canary — see the [seed-bundle runbook](/internal/docs/agent-insights/hive-seed-bundle-runbook). Decisions D-001…D-009 in the plan are binding; this expands them. ## The problem [Section titled “The problem”](#the-problem) A **packaged** Papercusp install today pays two serial waits: the app download, then a first-boot **dogfood join** that is genuinely heavy: * **Git.** `bootstrap-papercusp-hive.ts` clones `github.com/Papercusp/papercup` — a **\~5 GB tree + \~6.2 GB `.git` + 27 submodules** (the module header states the repo is “far too large to bundle”; submodules init best-effort in the background after the hive appears). * **Substrate.** The shared-hive join re-keys the joined harnesses onto the owner’s federation topic and the read-merge (`boot.ts` → `mergeAdmittedLogs`) replays **every admitted peer’s per-peer Hypercore log from block 0** into PG. Cold, over the network, capped at 50k ops/author. We *want* to keep paying the join — it is the best possible test of the real shared-hive join procedure (“the app can’t work if this part doesn’t work”). We just don’t want the user to **wait for the cold, full-history transfer** when the bytes could have shipped in the installer. ## The insight — seed the BYTES, let the join bootstrap the TRUST [Section titled “The insight — seed the BYTES, let the join bootstrap the TRUST”](#the-insight--seed-the-bytes-let-the-join-bootstrap-the-trust) Both stores are **seed-then-catch-up native**. A *seed* pre-positions bytes at a known checkpoint; the **unmodified** join then transfers only the delta on top: | Store | Native checkpoint | Post-seed delta transfer | Self-verification | | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | | Hypercore/corestore | a copy of the corestore with each author core at length `N` | replication fetches only blocks `> N` (`core.update()` → download tail) | per-block **merkle** proof + author **signature** on open | | Git | a `git bundle` | `clone --bundle-uri` then `fetch` = only new objects | git object **hashes** (content-addressed) | **The mantra (D-001): the seed bootstraps bytes; the live join bootstraps trust.** A seed is *untrusted cache*. Every store re-verifies natively, and **admission stays the sole trust/keys path** — the join procedure is not modified, so the dogfood keeps exercising the real thing end-to-end (invite → owner announce → admission → epoch keys → live tail). If a seed is absent, stale, corrupt, or fails verification, the system degrades to today’s cold path (D-007). This is **not** a revival of `_retired/snapshot-system/` (D-006). That was a monolithic-era harness-tarball *distribution* mechanism whose jobs were re-homed to blueprints (distribution), git+PG (backup), and `InstanceSpec` (reproducible clone). A seed-bundle is a different primitive: **a checkpoint of a REPLICATED store, restored before that store’s native catch-up protocol runs.** `InstanceSpec` boots a *fresh* instance from `(blueprintRef, repoSha, deploymentConfig, genome)`; a seed carries *existing replicated content* to skip a cold transfer. A seed-ref may later become an optional `InstanceSpec` field, but the two are orthogonal today. ## Scope — both halves of the dogfood (D-002) [Section titled “Scope — both halves of the dogfood (D-002)”](#scope--both-halves-of-the-dogfood-d-002) The owner’s dogfood is **not just what is in git** — it is also **what is shared over the hive**: plans, work items, features, issues, coordination, hive settings, hive members. Those live in the **federated substrate** (per-peer Hypercore logs → PG projections), so the **corestore seed carries them** and the **git seed carries the code**. A complete seed = `{ git bundle set, corestore copy, manifest }`. ## Architecture [Section titled “Architecture”](#architecture) ### Generic core: `libs/generic/seed-bundle` (D-006, repo generic-first convention) [Section titled “Generic core: libs/generic/seed-bundle (D-006, repo generic-first convention)”](#generic-core-libsgenericseed-bundle-d-006-repo-generic-first-convention) A domain-free library behind a `configure*()` seam (BORROWABLE; `npm run gen:borrowable`). It owns the manifest, packing/unpacking, hashing/verification, and a **provider registry** — but knows nothing about git or Hypercore. The substrate specifics live in **providers colocated with their substrates**. 
```ts
// libs/generic/seed-bundle — the generic contract
export interface SeedManifest {
  seedFormatVersion: number;          // bump on breaking shape change
  hiveId: string;                     // which hive this seed reconstitutes
  cutAtEpoch: number;                 // hive epoch at cut time (see Q-4)
  cutHlc: string;                     // HLC stamp of the cut (ordering anchor)
  cutTs: number;                      // wall-clock ms, provenance only
  stores: SeedStoreEntry[];
}


export interface SeedStoreEntry {
  kind: string;                       // provider id, e.g. "corestore" | "git"
  hash: string;                       // content hash of the payload (verify gate)
  sizeBytes: number;
  source: SeedSource;                 // WHERE the payload bytes come from
  encryption?: SeedEncryptionEnvelope;// present ⇒ payload is ciphertext at rest
  meta?: Record<string, unknown>;     // provider-specific (e.g. per-core lengths)
}


// Open-ended so v2 can CDN/swarm-fetch WITHOUT a schema change (D-003).
export type SeedSource =
  | { type: "resource"; path: string }          // v1: a Tauri bundled resource
  | { type: "url"; url: string; bytes: number }  // v2: resumable CDN blob
  | { type: "swarm"; topic: string };            // v3: peer-fetched


export interface SeedEncryptionEnvelope {
  scheme: string;                     // e.g. "xchacha20poly1305"
  keyRef: SeedKeyRef;                 // HOW the decrypt key is obtained
  nonce?: string;
}
// The key is NEVER in the installer. It is delivered by the live join.
export type SeedKeyRef =
  | { via: "epoch"; hiveId: string; epoch: number }   // unwrap from hive_epoch_keys
  | { via: "seed-key-op"; hiveId: string };            // a dedicated admission content-op


export interface SeedProvider {
  kind: string;
  /** Produce a self-verifying checkpoint of the live store (build/release time). */
  cut(ctx: SeedCutContext): Promise<SeedStoreEntry & { payload: SeedPayload }>;
  /** Cheap integrity check BEFORE restore (hash + shape). Never trusts blindly. */
  verify(entry: SeedStoreEntry, payload: SeedPayload): Promise<VerifyResult>;
  /** Drop the checkpoint into place so the store's NATIVE catch-up resumes from it. */
  restore(entry: SeedStoreEntry, payload: SeedPayload, ctx: SeedRestoreContext): Promise<void>;
}
```
 ### Provider 1 — corestore (colocated in `sync/hyperbee/`) [Section titled “Provider 1 — corestore (colocated in sync/hyperbee/)”](#provider-1--corestore-colocated-in-synchyperbee) Carries the **federated hive state**. From `corestore.ts`, a harness’s substrate is a plain directory tree at `<workspaceRoot>/.papercusp/<harness>/hyperbee/` (Hypercore storage: each author’s signed append-only log, `peer-log.ts`). * **cut** = a consistent copy of that directory with each author core at its current length. Record per-core lengths in `entry.meta`. (The sibling `hyperbee-scoped/` store is per-connection-served and MUST NOT be seeded — it is never `.replicate()`d; seeding it would leak scoped cores. Corestore provider seeds `hyperbee/` only.) * **restore** = drop the tree into the same path **before `bootHarnessSubstrate` opens the store**. Boot then opens the seeded cores; the read-merge replays the *local* seeded ops into PG (rebuilding projections — D-005, no PG dump) and swarm replication fetches only blocks past the seeded length. * **verify** = Hypercore’s own merkle + author-signature on open. A tampered/truncated core fails to open → fall back to cold. **Why this is safe against a malicious seed:** every op in a seeded core is author-signed and the core is merkle-verified; admission independently decides *which* author logs are admitted. A seed cannot inject an op the author didn’t sign, nor admit an unadmitted author. ### Provider 2 — git (colocated near `clone-github.ts` / `git-sync`) [Section titled “Provider 2 — git (colocated near clone-github.ts / git-sync)”](#provider-2--git-colocated-near-clone-githubts--git-sync) * **cut** = a `git bundle` set: the superproject + all 27 submodules (each bundle is a content-addressed pack). * **restore** = `git clone --bundle-uri` (or clone-from-bundle then set remote), point `origin` at `github.com/Papercusp/papercup`, wire submodule bundles, then a normal `fetch` pulls only the delta. Auth continues to flow through the user’s `gh` credential helper exactly as `clone-github.ts` documents (no token in our process). * **verify** = git verifies pack object hashes on index; `git fsck` optional. ## Restore-before-join state machine [Section titled “Restore-before-join state machine”](#restore-before-join-state-machine) 
```plaintext
FRESH INSTALL
   │
   ├─ seed present & manifest parses? ──no──┐
   │            │yes                          │
   ▼                                          │
 VERIFY each store entry (hash/shape) ──fail──┤
   │ pass                                      │
   ▼                                           │
 RESTORE git seed → checkout on disk           │
 RESTORE corestore seed → .papercusp/<h>/hyperbee/
   │ (git seed still CIPHERTEXT until key)      │
   ▼                                           │
 ── UNMODIFIED JOIN ─────────────────────────► │
   invite subscribe → owner announce →         │
   ADMISSION → epoch keys arrive               │
   │                                           │
   ├─ decrypt git seed with admission key      │
   ├─ substrate boot: local replay → PG,       │
   │  swarm replication fetches DELTA blocks    │
   └─ git fetch pulls DELTA objects             │
   │                                            │
   ▼                                            ▼
 USABLE HIVE (delta-only)              COLD PATH (today's full clone
                                        + cold read-merge) ── identical end state
```
 Any restore failure at any point drops to the **cold path** (right column). A `--no-seed` escape hatch forces the cold path unconditionally. ## Security model (D-004) [Section titled “Security model (D-004)”](#security-model-d-004) * **Corestore seed** is **already epoch-ciphertext by construction.** `hive-epoch-content-ops.ts` encrypts every hive *content* op under the current hive epoch key (exclude-set: only admission/key/policy tags stay plaintext). So a bundled corestore seed is **useless bytes until admission delivers the wrapped epoch key** — a removed/never-member replicates the ciphertext but cannot read it. This is why bundling the substrate in a *public* installer is safe (D-003). * **Git seed** of the **private** repo has no such intrinsic protection, so it must be **encrypted at rest** in the installer, with the key delivered **post-admission** (`SeedKeyRef.via: "seed-key-op"` — a dedicated admission content-op wrapped to the member’s device key, mirroring the epoch-key distribution in `hive-epoch-key-provider.ts`). A public installer must never leak the codebase. ## Resolved open questions [Section titled “Resolved open questions”](#resolved-open-questions) **Q-1 — installer size budget (full vs shallow git history).** *Decide by measurement in P-006.* The git `.git` is \~6.2 GB; a full-history bundle roughly doubles installer weight, a `--depth`-shallow bundle is far smaller but loses history (and a later unshallow is a big fetch). **Recommendation:** ship a **shallow** git seed by default (most first-boot value is a working tree + recent history) with the corestore seed full; expose depth as a cutter knob; confirm against real numbers in P-006. Not load-bearing for the design — the manifest is depth-agnostic. **Q-2 — git-seed encryption envelope.** `xchacha20poly1305` over the bundle bytes, key = a per-release seed key wrapped to each admitted member’s device key via a `seed-key` admission content-op (same sealing primitive as `unwrapEpochKey`). Decrypt happens **after** admission, immediately before the git restore’s fetch step. The corestore seed needs no extra envelope (epoch-ciphertext already). **Q-3 — cross-core cut skew.** **Harmless.** Each core is individually consistent at its recorded length, and the LWW read-merge + idempotent `INSERT … ON CONFLICT` projections already reconcile arbitrary interleavings (the exact property `backfill-local-state.ts` relies on). A seed cut with cores at slightly different lengths is indistinguishable from a peer that replicated them in a different order; the delta catch-up fills each core forward independently. No global snapshot barrier needed. **Q-4 — hive epoch read-cut for new members (the one real policy fork).** Content is encrypted per-epoch; a member decrypts an epoch only if it **holds that epoch’s wrapped key** (`hive-epoch-key-provider.ts`, fail-closed). The read cut-off (`hive-epoch-boundary.ts`) is designed to stop **REMOVED** members from reading *future* epochs — it says nothing about whether a **newly-admitted, trusted** member receives **past-epoch** keys. So seeded history that predates an epoch boundary is decryptable by a new member **iff** the owner’s admission wraps the *past* epoch keys for them. * If the dogfood hive has had **no boundary bumps** (members added, never removed — the expected canonical-hive case), all content is under one epoch and a newly-admitted member’s single wrapped key decrypts the entire seed. **Seeded history just works.** * If boundaries exist, seeded pre-boundary content is dead ciphertext to a current-epoch-only member — which is **still correct and still delta-efficient** (they catch up live from the boundary forward). **RATIFIED (owner, 2026-07-04, D-009) — and, on grounding the code, already the guaranteed default, so no new key-distribution code is needed.** The owner-side `grantEpochKeysToMembers` (`hive-epoch-boundary-wiring.ts`) **already wraps EVERY epoch key `[0..current]` to a newly-admitted member**, unconditionally — a documented *correctness* property (“Why \[0..current], not current-only”), because content is encrypted once per epoch and never re-encrypted, so a current-epoch-only joiner could read *zero* pre-join content. Restricting new members to the current epoch is explicitly called out there as a *deferred* forward-secrecy policy that nobody has built. So a newly-admitted member holds keys for every epoch the seed spans, and the corestore seed’s epoch-ciphertext decrypts for free — and where a key hasn’t arrived yet, the existing **decrypt-gate defers the op and drains it on key arrival** (`hive-epoch-op-gate.ts`), so a seeded op for a not-yet-keyed epoch is never lost. P-005b therefore reduces to a **named regression tripwire** (`seed-past-epoch-key-guarantee.test.ts`) that locks the `[0..current]` grant as a seed dependency: if the deferred forward-secrecy policy is ever implemented, that test fails and forces wiring the `manifest.cutAtEpoch` gate (defer a store to the cold path when the member lacks its epoch key) *first*. `manifest.cutAtEpoch` is carried for exactly that future guard. ## Cold path stays first-class (D-007) [Section titled “Cold path stays first-class (D-007)”](#cold-path-stays-first-class-d-007) `--no-seed` + restore-failure fallback + a **scheduled cold-join canary** (a periodic fresh cold join with no seed) keep the full cold path exercised, so the dogfood’s worst-case coverage is preserved even though most installs take the seeded fast path. ## What P-002…P-011 build against this [Section titled “What P-002…P-011 build against this”](#what-p-002p-011-build-against-this) * **P-002** implements the `libs/generic/seed-bundle` contract above. * **P-003/P-004** implement the two `SeedProvider`s (corestore, git) with two-peer / fixture integration tests proving **delta-only** transfer after restore. * **P-005** lands the git-seed encryption + the Q-4 hive-policy nod. * **P-006** builds the release-time cutter + Tauri bundled-resource embedding and **measures** Q-1. * **P-007** wires restore-before-join into `bootstrap-papercusp-hive.ts` (unchanged join after). * **P-008** the fallback + canary. **P-009** a second (test-rig) consumer to prove genericity. **P-010** the fresh-install E2E (cold vs seeded, delta-only assertion + full-join-still-exercised assertion). **P-011** the FLAG (default ON) + docs.

# Seed-bundle runbook — cut/restore model, the flag, failure modes + the cold-join canary

> The AS-BUILT operational runbook for the installer-shipped seed-bundle: how a seed is cut and restored, the restore-before-join state machine, the HIVE_SEED_BUNDLE kill-switch, the encrypted-git deferral, every failure mode and its cold-path fallback, and the cold-join canary + E2E acceptance that keep the cold path proven.

> **Status: AS-BUILT (plan `hive-seed-bundle-2026-07-04`, P-001…P-011 landed).** This is the operational companion to the [design memo](/internal/docs/agent-insights/hive-seed-bundle-design) (the *why* + the interface/manifest/state-machine spec). Read the memo first for the model; read this to **cut a seed, debug a restore, or reason about a failure mode.** ## One-paragraph model [Section titled “One-paragraph model”](#one-paragraph-model) The installer ships a **seed**: a checkpoint of the two replicated stores that back the dogfood hive — a set of **git bundles** (superproject + 37 submodules) and a **corestore snapshot** (every author core at its cut length, carrying the federated hive state: plans, work-items, features, issues, coordination, settings/members). On first boot the operator **restores the seed BEFORE the (unmodified) shared-hive join runs**, so the join transfers only the **delta** on top of the checkpoint instead of the whole history. The seed pre-positions **bytes**; the join still does all the **trust** (admission, epoch keys, delta replication) and every store **re-verifies natively** (git object hashes; corestore per-block merkle + author signatures). Nothing about the join changes — a build with no bundled seed, or with the feature flag off, takes the identical **cold** path. ## The pieces (as built) [Section titled “The pieces (as built)”](#the-pieces-as-built) | Concern | Module | Notes | | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Generic core | `libs/generic/seed-bundle` | manifest types + validation, pack/unpack, hashing, the `SeedProvider` registry — behind a `configure*()` seam (generic-first, `BORROWABLE`). | | Corestore provider | `sync/hyperbee/seed-provider-corestore.ts` | cut = copy each author core at its current length; restore = drop-in before boot. Blocks stay **epoch-ciphertext**. | | Git provider | `sync/hyperbee/seed-provider-git.ts` | cut = a `git bundle` set; restore = clone-from-bundle, re-point origin to GitHub, wire submodules; a later `fetch` = delta only. | | Cut CLI | `apps/operator/lib/release/cut-seed-cli.ts` | `pickGitEncryption()` selects the git-seal key (below). Run at release-build time **on the owner box**. | | Restore entry | `sync/hyperbee/restore-hive-seed.ts` | `resolveSeedDir()` (escape hatch / override / autodetect) + `onlyKinds` scoped restore. | | Deferred git | `sync/hyperbee/deferred-git-restore.ts` | resolves the epoch key **post-admission** and re-restores the encrypted git store. | | Boot wiring | `harness/bootstrap-papercusp-hive.ts` | `seedBundleEnabled()` gate → `defaultRestoreHiveSeed` (pre-join) → join → `defaultRestoreDeferredGitSeed` (post-admission). | | Cold-path guard | `sync/hyperbee/cold-join-canary.ts` + `cold-join-executor.ts` | forces a periodic REAL cold join so the seeded path never lets the cold path bit-rot. | | E2E acceptance | `sync/hyperbee/seed-e2e-measurement.ts` | pure cold-vs-seeded verdict (usable / join-exercised / delta-only / faster). | ## Restore-before-join state machine [Section titled “Restore-before-join state machine”](#restore-before-join-state-machine) 1. **`seedBundleEnabled()`** — the `FLAGS.HIVE_SEED_BUNDLE` master gate (below). OFF ⇒ skip everything, pure cold join. 2. **`resolveSeedDir()`** — resolves the bundled seed dir: `PAPERCUSP_NO_SEED` escape hatch → `PAPERCUSP_SEED_DIR` override → Tauri bundled-resource autodetect (`<resourceRoot>/seed`, accepted only if `manifest.json` exists). No seed ⇒ `null` ⇒ cold join. (The Tauri sidecar sets `PAPERCUSP_SEED_DIR` to `<sidecar_dir>/seed`.) 3. **Corestore restore (pre-join).** The corestore snapshot restores into the hive store dir now — its blocks are epoch-ciphertext, so no key is needed to place the bytes; they become readable once the join delivers the epoch keys. 4. **Git restore split by encryption.** A **plaintext** git seed restores now. An **encrypted-at-rest** git seed (the shipping default for the PRIVATE repo, D-004) **DEFERS** — its key is the hive epoch key, which a fresh member only holds *after* admission. 5. **The unmodified join runs** — invite subscribe → owner announce → admission → epoch keys → swarm delta replication. Only the delta transfers. 6. **`triggerDeferredGitRestore` (post-admission).** Once join reaches `joined` and a git store was deferred, `buildMemberEpochKeyProvider` unwraps the epoch key at `cutAtEpoch` (a fresh member holds it — Q-4 / `grantEpochKeysToMembers [0..current]`) and re-restores just the git store. If it can’t (no device identity yet), the store stays deferred and the join’s normal cold clone back-fills the repo. ## Cutting a seed — the key selection (`pickGitEncryption`) [Section titled “Cutting a seed — the key selection (pickGitEncryption)”](#cutting-a-seed--the-key-selection-pickgitencryption) The encrypted git seed must be decryptable by a **freshly-admitted member**, so the seal key is delivered by the **existing epoch-key path** — not a bespoke channel: * **`--workspace-id …` or explicit `--epoch …`** ⇒ `keyRef = { via: 'epoch', hiveId, epoch: cutAtEpoch }`, sealed with the **owner** epoch key `deriveEpochKey(hive, cutAtEpoch)`. **This is the shipping path.** A joiner unwraps the same epoch key post-admission (step 6). * **`--key-hex …`** ⇒ `keyRef = { via: 'seed-key-op', hiveId }` with that raw 32-byte key. **Fixture / manual only** — there is no joiner delivery path for a seed-key-op, so a member can’t unwrap it; it degrades to a cold clone. Use for tests, never a ship. * **neither** ⇒ **PLAINTEXT** git seed (a warning is logged). Guarded so a bare `cutAtEpoch=0` **never** silently mints a divergent key. > ⚠️ **The cut MUST run on the owner box with the live epoch keychain.** `deriveEpochKey` is **get-or-CREATE**: on a keychain miss it MINTS a fresh random key. Cutting in the wrong keychain context seals the seed under a key **no member can unwrap**. Verify `accounts:status` / the epoch keychain before a release cut. ## The kill-switch — `FLAGS.HIVE_SEED_BUNDLE` [Section titled “The kill-switch — FLAGS.HIVE\_SEED\_BUNDLE”](#the-kill-switch--flagshive_seed_bundle) * Key `papercusp-hive-seed-bundle`, **DEFAULT ON** (not in `KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS` — finished work never ships dark). Flip at `/admin/features`. * Read once at each restore call site via `seedBundleEnabled()` (fail-**open** to ON: a flag-read hiccup must not silently force cold, and the restore is safe-by-construction anyway). * **OFF ⇒ pure cold path, byte-identical to a no-seed build.** The runtime escape hatch if a seed restore ever misbehaves in the field — no redeploy needed. * **Inert** on any build with no bundled seed (`resolveSeedDir → null`), flag or not. ## Failure modes → every one degrades to the cold path [Section titled “Failure modes → every one degrades to the cold path”](#failure-modes--every-one-degrades-to-the-cold-path) The seed is a **pure optimization**; a fresh install is **never bricked** by a bad seed. Each failure resolves to the unchanged cold join: | Failure | Detection | Fallback | | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- | | No seed bundled | `resolveSeedDir → null` | cold join (today’s behavior) | | Flag OFF | `seedBundleEnabled() === false` | cold join | | `--no-seed` set | `resolveSeedDir().disabled` | cold join (operator opt-out) | | Corrupt / hash-mismatch bundle | provider `restore` throws → caught | cold join, warned | | Encrypted git, no epoch key yet | `buildMemberEpochKeyProvider → null` | git stays deferred; join’s cold clone back-fills | | Git sealed `via: 'seed-key-op'` | no joiner delivery path | deferral never resolves → cold clone | | Wrong-keychain cut (divergent key) | member `epoch_decrypt_fail` | deferral fails → cold clone (data-safe, just slow) | ## Keeping the cold path honest — the cold-join canary (D-007) [Section titled “Keeping the cold path honest — the cold-join canary (D-007)”](#keeping-the-cold-path-honest--the-cold-join-canary-d-007) Because a seeded install stops exercising the full cold join on every boot, the cold path can silently bit-rot. The **cold-join canary** (`cold-join-canary.ts` + `cold-join-executor.ts`, wired fail-soft into `routinesTick`) periodically forces a **REAL cold join** (`PAPERCUSP_NO_SEED`) and probes for a **usable hive** (plans + work-items visible, repo usable), recording pass/fail to the shared `hive_watchdog_fires` ledger (debounced) and alerting on a failure. * **DEFAULT DISABLED** (`intervalSec <= 0`) — a cold join is heavy. A canary/release env opts in via `PAPERCUSP_COLD_JOIN_CANARY_INTERVAL_SEC` (e.g. `86400` = daily). * The heavy cold-join spawn genuinely needs a **packaged / rig** environment, so it is an injected seam: `setColdJoinSpawnObserve(fn)` registers a rig’s real forced-cold-join+observe; the default throws `COLD_JOIN_RIG_REQUIRED` (an honest alert, **never a fake pass**). The pure decision (`evaluateColdJoinProbe`) is fully unit-tested headless. ## E2E acceptance (build-dependent) [Section titled “E2E acceptance (build-dependent)”](#e2e-acceptance-build-dependent) `seed-e2e-measurement.ts` turns the P-010 acceptance into a structured verdict: `evaluateSeedE2E(cold, seeded)` asserts the seeded install (a) reaches a **usable hive**, (b) still **exercised the real join** (the seed didn’t bypass federation), (c) transferred **delta-only** (≤ 25 % of cold’s bytes by default), and (d) booted **faster**. The pure verdict is unit-tested; the two-install **measurement** seam (`PackagedInstallMeasure`) needs a fresh **packaged build** to run and is honestly-gated (`PACKAGED_MEASURE_BUILD_REQUIRED`) — it executes only from a rig with a build (deploys are frozen while green-checkpoint is stalled on an internal reference harness; no numbers are fabricated in-process). ## Quick reference — env + flags [Section titled “Quick reference — env + flags”](#quick-reference--env--flags) | Knob | Effect | | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | `FLAGS.HIVE_SEED_BUNDLE` (default ON) | master kill-switch; OFF ⇒ cold path | | `PAPERCUSP_NO_SEED=1` | per-launch escape hatch ⇒ cold path | | `PAPERCUSP_SEED_DIR=<dir>` | override the seed dir (must contain `manifest.json`) | | `PAPERCUSP_COLD_JOIN_CANARY_INTERVAL_SEC=<n>` | opt into the cold-join canary (default 0 = off) |

# The pot:* tool namespace — local hive lifecycle

> The pot:* namespace is the full LOCAL hive lifecycle (a kind:'hive' harness + its Queen/bees) — list/get/create/dissolve/update plus the Queen run-loop verbs (start/pause/wake/declare-wake/status/survey). Gotchas — create/dissolve/update are root-only; create must stamp harness_kind:'hive' (harness:create doesn't); deploy:hive is a DISTINCT cloud step; bee placement stays fleet:*.

## What [Section titled “What”](#what) `pot:*` (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/hive/`) is the **local hive lifecycle** surface — the verbs that manage a hive on this machine: * **`pot:list`** — workspace-local hives (kind:‘hive’ harnesses) + a live-agent count (one batched fleet read, no per-hive fan-out). * **`pot:get`** — one hive in depth: wake schedule + bees `{doing,queued,load}` + todo frontier depth. A pure aggregator. * **`pot:create`** / **`pot:create_from_repo`** — stand up a new hive (home harness + the `hive` blueprint + optional Queen wake), transactional with rollback; the `_from_repo` variant onboards a GitHub URL. * **`pot:dissolve`** — tear one down (clear the wake, cancel bees, delete `hive_members`, tear down the learning loop + sandbox desktop, deregister; optional schema drop), confirm-gated + owner-tier-gated. * **`pot:update`** — edit deployment target / per-instance config overrides. * **`pot:start`** / **`pot:pause`** / **`pot:wake`** / **`pot:declare-wake`** / **`pot:status`** / **`pot:survey`** / **`pot:set-steering`** — the Queen run-loop control surface (start/pause the hive, fire or schedule the next wake, read status, the placement survey, owner steering). It **composes** existing primitives (`fleet:*`, `coord:*`, `harness:create` internals) rather than reinventing them. A hive is read through one seam, `resolveHive` (`_resolve.ts`), which now points onto the first-class Hive entity (`shared-hive-federation`) — the verbs didn’t have to change. (The same `pot:*` namespace also carries the **shared-hive** surface — membership/approval, moderation, and cross-hive ask/grant — covered in the [shared hives guide](/system/shared-hive-guide/).) ## Gotchas [Section titled “Gotchas”](#gotchas) * **Create/dissolve/update are ROOT-ONLY.** They refuse a parented bee (a `bee:spawn` child — `resolveAgentIdentity(ctx).source === 'fleet-spawn'`) up front; the `assertNotNestedHive` guard in `fireLaunchBlueprint` is the runtime backstop. Hives are peers, never nested — a bee that needs structure spins a `kind:'harness'` subharness, never a hive. * **`pot:create` must stamp `harness_kind:'hive'` itself.** `harness:create` never sets `harness_kind`, and `resolveHive`/`pot:list` filter on it — so a hive home harness created any other way (or a pre-existing plain harness) is **invisible** to the namespace until stamped. `createHiveHarness` sets it; that’s the one non-negotiable difference from a plain `harness:create { blueprintId:'hive' }`. * **`deploy:hive` / `deploy:teardown_hive` are DISTINCT** — they are the *cloud execution-plane* (provision/destroy frames for an already-existing hive), not local lifecycle. `pot:create` does NOT deploy; `pot:dissolve` does NOT destroy a cloud frame. Order: `pot:create` → (later) `deploy:hive`; `deploy:teardown_hive` → `pot:dissolve`. * **The Queen run-loop verbs live under `pot:*`.** `pot:start` / `pot:pause` (the hive on/off switch), `pot:wake` / `pot:declare-wake` (fire or schedule the next Queen wake; pause-without-stopping = `pot:declare-wake { mode:'none' }`), and `pot:status` / `pot:survey` are all in the namespace. Bee placement stays `fleet:*`; per-loop error/backoff control is `autoloop:control`. * **`pot:dissolve` leaves workspace-scoped event-wake subscriptions.** The hive time-wake routine is per-home-slug (cleared cleanly), but the hive’s event-wake subscriptions are one row per *workspace* today — so dissolve clears only the time wake to avoid clobbering sibling hives (`dissolve.ts` step 1). The first-class Hive entity makes event subs per-hive. ## Tests [Section titled “Tests”](#tests) `agent-tools/hive/{_resolve,_create,dissolve}.test.ts` + `guard.integration.test.ts`: descriptor shaping, `harness_kind` stamping, create rollback-on-failure, dissolve unwind (incl. the membership / learning-loop / desktop teardown legs), and the root-only + owner-tier refusals — all PG-free (deps mocked). The live create→wake→dissolve path (a real Queen spawn on shared infra) is a manual smoke, not auto-run.

# Hive vs coding blueprint — don't conflate them

> The hive blueprint (Queen + generalist bees, no spine) is the orchestration layer; the coding blueprint (scoper→…→curator spine) is one execution pipeline it runs. Agents repeatedly describe hive bees with coding-spine roles — they are different blueprints at different layers with opposite execution models.

> **⚠️ Blueprints RENAMED 2026-06-18 — the two names below have shifted (and the two “coding”s differ).** Per `orchestrator/src/blueprint/loader.ts`: the orchestration blueprint this page calls **`hive`** is now the **`coding`** dir (`kind: hive`, `decider: queen`); the former `generic-hive` is **`work`**; and the EXECUTION pipeline this page calls **`coding`** (scoper→…→curator spine) is now **`coding-factory`** (single-agent variant `coding-solo`). Legacy ids (`hive`, `generic-hive`) still resolve via the loader aliases. So read the table’s **“hive” column as today’s `coding`** and its **“coding” column as today’s `coding-factory`**. The orchestration-layer-vs-execution-pipeline DISTINCTION below is unchanged — only the names moved. Agents (and humans — and this insight’s author, twice in one session) repeatedly describe **hive** `bee`s as moving through the **coding** spine (scoper → architect → worker → …). They are **different blueprints at different layers with opposite execution models.** Both `extends: base` and both are “blueprints,” which is exactly why they look like siblings — but one *orchestrates* and one *executes*. ## The one-liner [Section titled “The one-liner”](#the-one-liner) * **`coding`** = an *execution pipeline*. Takes ONE `feature` (`F-NNN`) and pushes it through a fixed chain of specialist roles via a deterministic state-machine **spine**. * **`hive`** = the *orchestration layer above it*. A single **Queen** surveys the work frontier and **places ranked work onto generalist `bee`s** (no spine), then declares her own next wake. A hive can itself *create* coding harnesses. They are **not two flavors of the same thing** — the hive sits *above* and runs coding (and research/…) pipelines as needed. ## Contrast [Section titled “Contrast”](#contrast) | | `coding` | `hive` | | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `kind` | `harness` | `hive` (root-only, **never nested**) | | work unit | `feature` (`F-NNN`) | `hive-wake` (`POT-NNN`) for the Queen’s own wake; real work = `work_items` placed on bees | | execution | state-machine **spine**: `director` emits a verb → `deriveNext` → next role | **no spine**: Queen surveys + places work + self-declares wake | | roles | scoper → architect → worker → validator → documenter → curator (+ opt-in tester / security / crosscheck / ui-qa; reviewer = the PR gate) | `queen`/`operator` (decider) + `bee` (one generic worker) | | spine edges | \~20 verbs (`NEXT_WORKER`, `NEXT_VALIDATOR`, …) → role transitions | 3 terminal only: `DONE` / `ESCALATE` / `IDLE` | | `maxTurns` | 200 | 50 | | who drives | orchestrator runs ≤4 feature pipelines, strict plan-priority order | Queen “steers, doesn’t dispatch”; bees own their own sequencing | | trigger | autoloop dispatch (plan-order slot-filling) | self-declared wake (`hive:declare-wake`); **no timer** | | `planner` | `features-import` (plans → features, waves + `blocked_by`) | `inline` | | `requiresRepo` | `true` | `false` | | finalize | `gates.finalize`: DONE → curator → documenter → archive | none — bees complete work-items; the Queen reads state | ## The traps that cause the confusion [Section titled “The traps that cause the confusion”](#the-traps-that-cause-the-confusion) 1. **“worker” is overloaded.** `worker` is a *coding* pipeline role. The hive’s generic agent is a **`bee`** — the glossary says it “carries no pipeline spine and no chunk requirement, **unlike `worker`**.” A bee is NOT a scoper/architect/worker/validator. 2. **“Queen” ≠ “director”.** Both decide, but the `director` emits per-feature verbs *inside a spine*; the **Queen** places work across a fleet *with no spine*. 3. **A bee can create a coding harness** (`blueprint:catalog → harness:create`) for genuinely structured work — so the two appear nested in practice even though they’re distinct layers. (A bee may **not** launch another hive — hives are peers, never nested.) ## Rule of thumb [Section titled “Rule of thumb”](#rule-of-thumb) If you’re naming scoper / architect / validator / reviewer / curator → you’re in a **coding** harness. If you’re describing a **Queen placing ranked work on bees** → you’re in a **hive**, and **there is no spine.** When unsure, read the harness’s `kind` (`harness` vs `hive`) and its `blueprint.yaml` `spine:` block — a hive’s spine has only `DONE` / `ESCALATE` / `IDLE`. *Sources: `blueprints/{hive,coding,base}/blueprint.yaml`, `hive/prompts/bee.md`, `harness/glossary.mdx`, `orchestrator/src/blueprint/{schema,derive-next}.ts`.*

# Hive wake fires but no Queen spawns → it's fleet-spawn starvation, not the hive

> When a hive's wake fires (lastFiredAt advances) yet placements stay empty and liveAgents:0, the cause is almost always the rate-governor's fleet effective concurrency being saturated — NOT your hive config, the work-item kind, or the operator. Diagnose with dev:rate_governor_status, not by recreating the hive.

## Symptom [Section titled “Symptom”](#symptom) You spin up (or own) a hive, seed a deliverable work-item, and `hive_start` / `hive_wake`. `hive_status` shows the wake **fired** — `lastFiredAt` advances, `declaredAt` is set — but: * `placements.items` stays `[]`; the deliverable work-item stays `todo` / unplaced. * `liveAgents: 0`. No Queen agent, no bee, ever appears in `coord:presence` / `fleet:assignments`. * On teardown, `hive_dissolve` reports `cancelledSpawns: []` (nothing was ever queued). ## The red herrings (don’t chase these) [Section titled “The red herrings (don’t chase these)”](#the-red-herrings-dont-chase-these) All three of these are tempting and all three were wrong when this was diagnosed (2026-06-18, `domain-generic-agent-personas` P-016): 1. **“My hive / blueprint is misconfigured.”** No — the symptom appears across **every** hive in the workspace at once. `hive_list` showed all 14 hives with `liveAgents:0`, including `papercup-hive` and `hiveloop-hive` whose wakes had fired minutes earlier. A systemic symptom is not a per-hive bug. 2. **“The work-item kind isn’t in the placement frontier.”** No — re-running with a frontier-native `kind:research-task` (family:feature/todo) instead of `kind:task` placed nothing either. The Queen never ran, so the frontier was never gathered. 3. **“The green operator (:3070) is crash-looping.”** Check `ActiveEnterTimestamp` — a high `NRestarts` is cumulative; if the operator has been up for hours, the crash-loop already settled and a wake that fired *during* that stable window still produced no Queen. ## The real cause [Section titled “The real cause”](#the-real-cause) Hive Queens are spawned through the **fleet autonomous-spawn lane**, which is gated by the rate governor’s fleet-wide `maxSimultaneousAgents` / AIMD **effective** concurrency (see [rate-limit-governor-activation](/internal/docs/agent-insights/rate-limit-governor-activation)). When effective concurrency is small (e.g. **1**) and already consumed by other fleet work (overnight benchmark bees, etc.), there is **no spawn slot** — so the wake-executor records the wake but the Queen spawn never admits. ## Diagnose it in two calls [Section titled “Diagnose it in two calls”](#diagnose-it-in-two-calls) * `dev:rate_governor_status` → `fleet: {cap, inFlight, effective, floor}`. If `effective` is small and `inFlight >= effective` (saturated), that’s the gate. In the 2026-06-18 case: `{cap:8, inFlight:1, effective:1, floor:1}` — one slot, fully consumed by benchmark runs. * `hive_list` → if **many** hives show `liveAgents:0` despite recently-fired wakes, it’s systemic starvation, not your hive. ## Unblock [Section titled “Unblock”](#unblock) The lever is the fleet `maxSimultaneousAgents` / effective cap, live-editable via `operator:rate_limit_config` (or the `/adv` `<FleetRateControl>`). **But raising it is an owner-gated capacity decision** — a larger pool re-pressures PG and can re-trigger the oversized-pool wedge (see [pg-connection-exhaustion-fleet-wedge](/internal/docs/agent-insights/pg-connection-exhaustion-fleet-wedge)), so don’t force it autonomously. Wait for a slot to free, or escalate to the owner. Do **not** recreate the hive or fiddle the work-item kind — neither is the problem.

# HLC merge order must match the PG fed_ts LWW guard (or cells diverge)

> Why two federated cells can "converge" to DIFFERENT values — the merge winners-fold orders by HLC (P-010) but the projection PG LWW guard orders by fed_ts, and HLC stamped at DRAIN disagrees with fed_ts stamped at WRITE. Fix - seed the HLC from the op's own write-time `ts`.

## What [Section titled “What”](#what) A federated write goes through **two** ordering decisions, and they must agree: 1. **The merge winners-fold** (`read-merge.ts` `mergeAdmittedLogs`, whose `beatsStored` comparator — defined in `read-merge.ts` as a hand-mirror of `projection.ts`’s `lwwPick` — decides winners) — since P-010 this orders by the op’s **HLC** when both ops carry one, else falls back to wall-clock `ts`. 2. **The PG projection LWW guard** (`harness-features.ts` etc.) — the `INSERT … ON CONFLICT … WHERE stored.fed_ts IS NULL OR EXCLUDED.fed_ts >= stored.fed_ts` clause — orders by **`fed_ts`**. If these two disagree under same-key contention, the system **silently diverges**: the merge picks op X as the winner and hands it to `apply`, but the PG guard rejects X (its `fed_ts` lost) → no write → the cell keeps its own value. Each cell keeps its own → the two cells “converge” (no more ops to drain, `fixedPoint=true`) to **different** values. The tripwire was `split-brain-queen.integration.test.ts` (both Queens steer opposite orders; cell A ended with a mix, cell B with all-its-own). ## Why they disagreed [Section titled “Why they disagreed”](#why-they-disagreed) * **`fed_ts`** is stamped at the **local write** (migration 214 `stamp_local_federated_write`, `clock_timestamp()`). * **HLC** was stamped at **DRAIN** (`stampOpHlc` in `hlc-stamp.ts` called from `boot.ts`’s `handle.append`, using a bare `clock.now()` = wall-clock-at-drain). Drain happens later than — and in a different order than — the writes (the CDC outbox drains in batches, concurrently across cells), so the HLC ordered ops by **drain-interleave** while `fed_ts` ordered them by **write time**.
