Guard by scanning every line for the package pattern, not just import syntax, and verify against a clean build. Includes the grep -v self-exclusion gotcha that hid a tsconfig path.

Migrating a workspace package from one npm scope to another — here `@restart/{grid,grid-core,bloom-grid,kv-persist,kv-persist-indexeddb,sync}` → `@papercusp/*` in a sibling internal monorepo — looks like a mechanical find-and-replace of import statements. It isn’t. The imports are the *easy* references; the ones that bite are the bare strings that no import-grep matches. ## The miss-class: bare package strings in configs [Section titled “The miss-class: bare package strings in configs”](#the-miss-class-bare-package-strings-in-configs) A grep for `from '@restart/x'` / `require('@restart/x')` / `import('@restart/x')` catches imports and (with a second pattern) `package.json` deps. It does **not** catch these, all of which name the package as a plain string: * **`next.config.js` `transpilePackages: ['@restart/grid', ...]`** — Next won’t transpile the workspace package if the name doesn’t match. * **Astro `noExternal: ['@restart/grid', '@restart/grid-core', ...]`** — SSR bundling silently stops including it. * **`tsconfig.base.json` path maps** — `"@restart/sync": ["libs/sync/src/index.ts"]`. * **Command / script-runner tables** — `command: 'npm run bench --workspace @restart/grid-core'` in a dashboard, a Procfile, a CI matrix. The `--workspace @restart/x` arg fails once the workspace is renamed. A running dev server hides all of this The dev server cached the old config at boot, so hitting routes that use the renamed package returns **HTTP 200** even though the configs are stale. Route smoke checks give false confidence. These references only fail on a **fresh build** (`next build`, `astro build`, `npm ci` + start) or a dev-server restart. Verify a scope rename against a clean build, not just the warm dev server. ## The fix: guard on the package pattern, not import syntax [Section titled “The fix: guard on the package pattern, not import syntax”](#the-fix-guard-on-the-package-pattern-not-import-syntax) Replace the import-syntax matcher with one that flags **any** `@restart/<pkg>` occurrence, scanning every line of every code + json file (excluding `node_modules`, `dist`, the auto-generated `package-lock.json`, and historical docs). That single pattern catches imports, deps, tsconfig maps, and config strings uniformly. Make it **targeted** when some names in the old scope are legitimate (the other app still owns `@restart/{db,ui,shop-sdk,com,...}`): guard only the migrated basenames, allow the rest. See `scripts/check-no-restart-imports.mjs` (papercup), wired as a gating CI step. (The other app’s equivalent `scripts/check-no-restart-scope.mjs` was since removed.) ## Bonus gotcha: `grep -v <substring>` self-exclusion [Section titled “Bonus gotcha: grep -v \<substring> self-exclusion”](#bonus-gotcha-grep--v-substring-self-exclusion) While auditing tsconfig for stragglers I ran `grep '"@restart/sync"' tsconfig*.json | grep -v libs/sync` to drop the submodule — and it silently hid the real offender, because the path-map **line** is `"@restart/sync": ["libs/sync/src/index.ts"]`: the *value* contains `libs/sync`, so `grep -v libs/sync` filtered out the very line I needed. When excluding the submodule, match on the file path (`grep -v '^libs/sync/'` against the filename), never on a substring that can also appear in a line’s content. ## Checklist for a scope rename across a monorepo [Section titled “Checklist for a scope rename across a monorepo”](#checklist-for-a-scope-rename-across-a-monorepo) 1. Imports (`from`/`require`/`import()`), incl. subpath imports `@scope/pkg/sub`. 2. `package.json` deps (and the package’s own `name`, if it’s the one moving). 3. `tsconfig*.json` path maps — `paths` and any project-refs. 4. Build configs: next `transpilePackages`, astro `noExternal`, vite/webpack `optimizeDeps`/aliases, jest/vitest `moduleNameMapper`. 5. Command tables / Procfiles / CI: `--workspace @scope/pkg`, `nx run @scope/pkg:*`. 6. Doc-comments and string literals (cosmetic, but a future grep will re-flag them). 7. Relink `node_modules` (`npm install`) so the new scope resolves; then verify a **fresh build**, not just the running dev server. 8. Add a gating CI guard so the rename can’t silently regress.

# The Scout cycle's in-process ideators/critics bypass the inference gateway (same class as the gym's FB-16)

> Spawned bees get ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at the spawn chokepoint (gatewaySpawnEnv), but Scout's IN-PROCESS ideator/critic/recombine llmCalls never pass through it — so they hit api.anthropic.com directly with the Claude Max SUBSCRIPTION OAuth token (no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set) but WITHOUT the `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` header Anthropic requires for a subscription token on the direct API → every ideator fails INSTANTLY with `403 permission_error: "OAuth authentication is currently not allowed for this organization"` (NOT a 429/rate-limit — an earlier read of this was wrong). Symptom that means READ THIS: a scout_ticks row with status=ran, ideas_generated=0, budget_used_usd=0, detail.stop='no-ideas' — repeatedly, completing fast (no slow 429 retries). Bees avoid it via the `claude -p` CLI path the gateway injects Bearer+oauth-beta for. Fix = mirror the gym (FB-16): gatewayLlmEnv() routes the in-process SDK through the gateway, which injects the oauth-beta — but ONLY works when the gateway's credential injection is healthy. anthropicDirectTransport honors PAPERCUSP_ANTHROPIC_URL, NOT ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL.

## Symptom [Section titled “Symptom”](#symptom) The Scout loop looks like it’s running but produces nothing. In `harness_shared.scout_ticks` you see, over and over: 
```plaintext
status=ran   ideas_generated=0   ideas_routed=0   budget_used_usd=0
detail = {"stop":"no-ideas","reason":"idle-capacity",...}
```
 `stop:"no-ideas"` (not `empty-digest`) means the corpus digest was **non-empty** — the cycle got past `digestIsEmpty(digest)` — but `ideate()` returned an empty array. Combined with **`budget_used_usd = 0`**, that means the ideators ran but **every ideator LLM call failed before charging** (the per-ideator `try/catch` in `ideators.ts` isolates the throw, records `ok:false`, and the error never reaches `scout_ticks`). Real-world incidence: the `@singleton` Scout produced 0 ideas across **49/49** ran-ticks for \~4 days after the 2026-06-14 re-scope, $0 every time, while the old `papercup`-scoped Scout had spent \~$2/cycle for 24 ideas. ## Root cause [Section titled “Root cause”](#root-cause) Scout’s ideator/critic/recombine calls are **in-process** `anthropic-direct` `llmCall`s (`register-scout-action.ts` → `cycle-deps.ts` → `ideators.ts`). The inference gateway is only wired onto **spawned subprocesses**: `operator-spawn.ts` merges `gatewaySpawnEnv()` (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<gatewayPort>`) at the spawn chokepoint, and bees egress through the gateway, which **strips** the incoming `authorization`/`x-api-key` and **injects** `Authorization: Bearer <bound-account-token>` + `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` (the gateway’s `CLAUDE_OAUTH_BETA`, `credential-store.ts`). That beta header is **mandatory** for a Claude Max **subscription OAuth** token on a direct-API call. An in-process call **never passes that chokepoint**, so Scout hits `api.anthropic.com` directly with the subscription OAuth token (the operator has no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — `llm-client.ts` defaults to `~/.claude/.credentials.json`) but **without the oauth-beta** → Anthropic rejects every ideator INSTANTLY with `403 permission_error: "OAuth authentication is currently not allowed for this organization"` → `no-ideas`, `$0`, fast (no retries — 403 is non-transient). This is **the same bug class** the gym hit (see [gym-cycle-inprocess-llm-bypasses-gateway](/agent-insights/gym-cycle-inprocess-llm-bypasses-gateway), FB-16) — a 401/403 OAuth/org error, identical mechanism: in-process anthropic-direct egress bypassing the gateway’s oauth-beta injection. Bees work because the gateway adds the beta for them. Why it’s easy to misdiagnose: (1) the rate-governor buckets show opus with headroom and several accounts available — those reflect the **gateway** pool, which Scout isn’t in. (2) The cycle SWALLOWS the per-ideator error (`ideators.ts` try/catch → `info.error`, never persisted to `scout_ticks`), so all you see is `$0`/no-ideas — which looks identical whether the cause is a 429 (rate) or a 403 (auth). To get the real error, call `runIdeators(digest, {llmCall, maxIdeators})` standalone and inspect `result.ideators[i].error` (an EARLIER pass here mis-read it as a 429 — it is a 403). ## Fix [Section titled “Fix”](#fix) Mirror the gym (`autoloop-cycle.ts`): when `FLAGS.INFERENCE_GATEWAY` is on, point the in-process SDK at the localhost gateway before the cycle’s LLM calls. In `productionScoutRunner` (`register-scout-action.ts`): 
```ts
const { FLAGS } = await import('@papercusp/flags');
const { getFlag } = await import('@papercusp/flags/server');
if (await getFlag(FLAGS.INFERENCE_GATEWAY, 'system')) {
  const { gatewayLlmEnv } = await import('../inference-gateway/spawn-env');
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(gatewayLlmEnv(true))) {
    if (!process.env[k]) process.env[k] = v; // respect a pre-set override
  }
}
```
 Key detail: the in-process `anthropic-direct` transport (`chat-stream.ts` `resolveAnthropicBaseUrl()`) reads **`PAPERCUSP_ANTHROPIC_URL`**, NOT the standard `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (which only the `claude` CLI honors). `gatewayLlmEnv(true)` sets both, so subprocess + in-process egress both route through the gateway. ## Caveat — the fix depends on the gateway’s credential injection being healthy [Section titled “Caveat — the fix depends on the gateway’s credential injection being healthy”](#caveat--the-fix-depends-on-the-gateways-credential-injection-being-healthy) Routing Scout through the gateway only helps if the gateway actually **strips the org-blocked OAuth + reinjects Bearer + `oauth-2025-04-20` beta** for the in-process SDK request. If the gateway is **degraded** — e.g. its account-pool load is failing (`account-resolver.loadPoolOrThrow` fail-closed) or `:8788` is flapping — it can’t resolve a bound account to inject, so the original org-blocked token passes through and you get the **same 403 even through the gateway** (observed 2026-06-18: a standalone repro through `:8788` still 403’d during a pool-load flap, while the gym’s in-process egress was simultaneously down for the same reason). So a `403` *through* the gateway points at the gateway’s credential layer, not the Scout fix. Verify the gateway is healthy (pool loaded, `:8788` stable) before concluding the routing fix failed. If the gateway genuinely can’t inject for the in-process path, the alternates are: set a real `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (a direct-API key sidesteps the oauth-beta requirement entirely), or egress ideators via the `claude -p` CLI path bees use.

# Scout 'ran' ticks with 0 ideas / $0 mean transport death, not a quiet muse

> A scout_ticks row with status=ran, ideas_generated=0, budget_used_usd=0 and stop:'no-ideas' means every ideator LLM call failed SILENTLY (per-stage null absorption is pinned behavior). Two proven causes (2026-06-11): the long-lived operator's Claude-token cache outliving the ~2h on-disk rotation (every anthropic-direct call 401s, fixed under EI-281 with a self-healing expiry-aware cache + rotated-token 401 retry), and raw-OAuth-bucket 429 saturation (see llm-429-check-the-transport-not-the-account). Deploy-restarts of the operator mask the cache bug intermittently — that's why it looks flaky.

## The mistake this prevents [Section titled “The mistake this prevents”](#the-mistake-this-prevents) The papercup Learning tab’s Scout view sat empty after the scout-cycle routine was enabled, while `scout_ticks` showed `ran` rows. An agent (or owner) reads `status=ran` as “the loop works, it just didn’t find anything”. Wrong: the Scout cycle **absorbs failed LLM calls as nulls by design** (pinned in `lib/scout/cycle-failure-modes.test.ts`), so a cycle whose every ideator call dies looks identical to a cycle that generated nothing — `ran`, `stop: "no-ideas"`, `ideas_generated: 0`, `budget_used_usd: 0`. **The tell is `$0 spend`.** A real cycle that genuinely produced no keepable ideas still spends on the ideator calls. `ran` + `0 ideas` + `$0` = no LLM call ever succeeded. ## Where to look [Section titled “Where to look”](#where-to-look) 1. `SELECT * FROM harness_shared.scout_ticks ORDER BY tick_at DESC` — the `detail` jsonb carries `stop` + `cycleId` (the cycleId’s epoch-ms suffix is the cycle START; the row lands at completion). 2. The operator host’s journal for `[anthropic-direct]` warn lines during the cycle window (`[meridian]` in logs before 2026-06-12 — EI-399 renamed the backend). **Transient errors (429/529) log retries; non-transient failures (401, transport-resolution failure) are SILENT** — a cycle window with no such lines at all points at the auth/cache class, not rate limits. 3. Probe the exact path the cycle uses, from a FRESH process: `llmCall` in `packages/operator-core/lib/llm-testing/llm-client.ts` (one haiku call ≈ $0.00002). Fresh-process-green + long-lived-host-dead = the token-cache class. ## The two proven causes [Section titled “The two proven causes”](#the-two-proven-causes) * **Stale in-process Claude token (EI-281, fixed 2026-06-11).** Claude OAuth tokens rotate \~2-hourly on disk (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, `claudeAiOauth.expiresAt`), but `readClaudeOauthToken` in `libs/papercusp-shared/src/agent/chat-stream.ts` cached the boot-time token forever. Any operator host older than the token 401’d on every anthropic-direct call. Fixed with an expiry-aware self-healing cache (re-reads disk when the cached token passes `expiresAt`) plus an invalidate-and-retry on 401/403 when the on-disk token has rotated. Auto-deploy restarts refresh the cache, which made this look intermittent. * **The self-heal lives in the SHARED path only — a HAND-ROLLED loop doesn’t inherit it.** The cache + invalidate-on-401 above is in `chat-stream.ts` (`readClaudeOauthToken` / `invalidateClaudeTokenCache`, used by `runAgentChat` * the one-shot `llmCall`). A hand-rolled in-process Anthropic loop that reads `~/.claude/.credentials.json` itself — e.g. the `su` llm-test target’s tool loop (`llm-testing/targets/su.ts`), which can’t use the one-shot `llmCall` because it needs tool-calling — does NOT get it. Under fleet load the shared credential rotates often, so such a loop **401-cascades** the instant a rotation lands mid-run (every later call uses the stale cached token — observed 2026-06-18: a su-target run died at scenario 3, all 9 remaining scenarios 401). Fix: on a 401/403, re-read the file + rebuild the client + retry (its own budget, separate from the 429 backoff). The su target’s `callWithRetry` does this since 2026-06-18. * **Raw-OAuth bucket 429 saturation.** The stateless anthropic-direct path has its own rate bucket, separate from claude-CLI clients on the same Max account — see [llm-429-check-the-transport-not-the-account](/internal/docs/agent-insights/llm-429-check-the-transport-not-the-account). Escape for a manual cycle: `LLM_TEST_BACKEND=claude-code`. ## Operational notes [Section titled “Operational notes”](#operational-notes) * The Learning tab Scout view reads `harness_shared.scout_routed_ideas` + the newest `scout_ticks` row (`learning-scout-read.ts`); ledger writes push `notifySyncInvalidate('learning.scout')` since 2026-06-11. * The scout-cycle routine self-gates on idle/friction; for a forced bring-up cycle set the routine’s `payload_template.cadence` to `{ idleThreshold: 0, minIntervalSec: 0 }` (restore `0.5`/`3600` after) — `seed-scout-routine.ts --active` reseeds the defaults.

# Scout routine fires are not Scout activity

> The scheduler row can advance before the Scout body records a tick. Use scout_ticks, not routines.last_fired_at alone, when deciding whether Scout is actually alive.

## Failure Pattern [Section titled “Failure Pattern”](#failure-pattern) `harness_shared.routines.last_fired_at` means the routine scheduler claimed the cron row. It does not prove the Scout body ran. DBOS can hold a `routine:<id>` dedup key while a `routineFire` workflow is pending or delayed, so later cron fires collapse after the claim has already advanced the routine row. When that happens, `improvements:learning_loops` can say Scout is `firing` even though `harness_shared.scout_ticks` is stale and no scorecard-driven idea pickup is happening. That is a detector failure: the health surface trusted scheduler activity instead of the loop’s own domain ledger. ## Correct Signal [Section titled “Correct Signal”](#correct-signal) For Scout, read `harness_shared.scout_ticks` as the activity proof: * A `ran` row means a budgeted Scout cycle completed. * A `gated` row means the Scout body ran and withheld itself for a named reason. * An `error` row means the Scout body ran and recorded the failure. A fresh routine fire with no fresh `scout_ticks` row is not healthy Scout activity. Treat it as stale and inspect DBOS `routineFire` dedup/queue state, gateway/account health, and the Scout cycle logs. The 2026-06-25 live failure was a DBOS no-first-output fire: `routineFire` pinned `routine:<scout-id>` and advanced `routines.last_fired_at`, but there were zero `dbos.operation_outputs` rows and no Scout tick. The reaper now cancels that specific no-output class and requeues the routine immediately, but Scout health must still come from `scout_ticks`; otherwise the monitor can miss the next variant of the same scheduler/effect split. Scout also has to bound the cycle body itself. Once the scheduler wins the fire slot, a hung LLM/gateway call must record `status:error` in `scout_ticks` and release the DBOS dedup before the outer two-hour `routineFire` deadline. The scheduler timeout is the class guard for that. ## Regression Guard [Section titled “Regression Guard”](#regression-guard) `packages/operator-core/lib/scout/run.test.ts` verifies pre-scheduler Scout gates record gated tick rows. `packages/operator-core/lib/scout/scheduler.test.ts` verifies a timed-out cycle records an error tick. `packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/learning-loop-health.test.ts` verifies Scout is marked stale when routine fires are fresh but `scout_ticks` activity is stale. `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/dbos-executor-reaper.test.ts` verifies no-first-output routine fires are cancelled and the owning routine is requeued.

# The Sentinel — the always-on voice of the hive

> One role that watches the fleet AND narrates it: always-on, voice-first, short replies, status + suggestions (never deep planning). How to enable it (the SENTINEL flag + the humanFacingRole='sentinel' voice pref repoints the live converse brain), the read-context sources it walks in with (curation:state-of-hive / curation:feed / Overwatch compute-brief / fleet:assignments — never waits on the Queen), the handoff-to-Queen flow (<handoff_to_queen> → high-priority work_item + nudge, tier-gated, hindsight landing report), the live-override settings tab, and the in-progress server-side proactive path (P-018-022).

## What the Sentinel is [Section titled “What the Sentinel is”](#what-the-sentinel-is) The Sentinel is **one role**, not two cooperating hats (`sentinel-herald-2026-06-21` D-001). Watching the fleet is simply *how* it knows what to tell the user — same identity. It is: * **always-on, voice-first** — the same live converse + ElevenLabs voice brain the legacy “operator” ran, re-homed onto the `sentinel` role (D-006: re-home, not rewrite — only the three hardcoded `'operator'` bindings were parameterized). * **short, status + suggestions** — reuse the operator reply caps (\~220 chars for voice, terse for text). The Sentinel answers “what’s the fleet doing / what should I work on next,” and for anything that needs a real plan its move is “want me to hand this to the Queen?” — it is **not** the deep-planning agent (D-004). * **never the placer** — the Queen is the brain/placer; the Sentinel suggests and hands off but **never spawns/places/cancels** (D-002). This is enforced structurally by the capability envelope (`ROLE_ENVELOPES.sentinel` denies fs-write/bash/spawn/place/kill), not by convention — an envelope test asserts the Sentinel cannot place or execute. The boundary with the other autonomous roles: the **Queen** steers and places, the **Overwatch** is the machine-facing supervisor, and the **Sentinel** is the human-facing narrator. The legacy “operator” role was decomposed into those three; only the machine-facing halves shipped, and this plan re-homes the orphaned human-facing concierge brain onto the Sentinel. ## How to enable it [Section titled “How to enable it”](#how-to-enable-it) Two independent toggles, deliberately decoupled (D-015): 1. **`SENTINEL` feature flag** (`papercusp-sentinel`, default **OFF**, mirrors `FLAGS.OVERWATCH`) — gates the **settings UI**. When on, the Sentinel tab appears in the operator-vite left sidebar (`LeftSidebar.tsx` `TABS`, after Overwatch), with the exact OVERWATCH treatment: a `visibleTabs` filter + a `?lst=sentinel` stale-deep-link snap-back to a default tab when the flag is off. Flipping the flag shows/hides the tab; it does **not** by itself repoint the brain. 2. **`humanFacingRole` voice pref** (`'operator'` | `'sentinel'`, default **`'operator'`**) — this is the real switch that **repoints the live brain**. It lives in the voice prefs (it is one of `VOICE_USER_OVERRIDE_KEYS`), and `resolveConfig → ElSessionConfig → start` sets `brainRole` from it. The ElevenLabs agent id / signed-URL are unchanged — only which persona + read-context the converse loop loads changes. The operator persona stays as a flagged migration fallback (D-006). The role threads end-to-end: `role?: string` (default `'operator'`) flows through `converse.ts` → `converse-prompt.ts` → the three persona loaders, and through the voice seam (`askOperator(question, conversationId, role)`) and the text/mobile paths (`operator-converse.ts` + device routes fall back to `humanFacingRole`; an explicit body `role` wins). So the Sentinel persona is consistent across voice / text / mobile. ## The read-context — it never waits on the Queen [Section titled “The read-context — it never waits on the Queen”](#the-read-context--it-never-waits-on-the-queen) The Sentinel walks in already *knowing* the live system, so it can narrate (file + nudge) instead of re-deriving from raw coord. It reads the **ready-made digests directly** (D-009 — never a Queen-maintained status object, which would be stale exactly when she is mid-turn, reintroducing the “wait on the Queen” problem the Sentinel exists to avoid). `sentinel-context.ts` follows the `queen-brief.ts` pattern exactly: a **pure deterministic renderer** (`renderSentinelContext`) over already-shaped input + a **fail-soft deps adapter** (`gatherSentinelContext`, one flaky leg degrades to an empty section, never throws). The four sources: | Section | Source digest | Module | | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | | Live signals (escalations / blockers / decisions / completions, salience-ranked) | `curation:feed` | `gatherFleetSignals` + `rankFleetFeed` | | Anomalies (detected drift + suggested action, severity-ordered) | Overwatch compute-brief | `computeOverwatchBrief` | | Standing patterns + headline (recurring friction / sinks / deferrals / gaps) | `curation:state-of-hive` | `synthesizeStateOfHive` | | Progress (live fleet load + liveness) | `fleet:assignments` | `listFleetAssignments` + `groupByAgent` | It is a **Sentinel slice** of the queen-brief — escalations/anomalies/progress + “what’s worth surfacing,” **not** placement rank (the Queen owns placement; the Sentinel owns surfacing). Each section is capped (`DEFAULT_SENTINEL_CONTEXT_CAPS`) so the block stays a digest; an all-quiet system renders the headings with an explicit “nothing” so silence is a trustworthy signal, not an omission. It is injected into the converse prompt’s SYSTEM sections **only** when `role === 'sentinel'` (the operator path is byte-identical). mem0 is also injected into the Sentinel converse loop (`memory:search` at turn start, `memory:remember` for learnings, honoring the EI-2032 auto-capture kill switch). ## Handoff to the Queen [Section titled “Handoff to the Queen”](#handoff-to-the-queen) When the user says “do it,” the Sentinel does **not** spawn a bee. It emits a `<handoff_to_queen>` tag (parsed in `operator-converse-tags.ts`, dispatched by `operator-sentinel-handoff.ts`), which (D-003): 1. files a **high-priority `work_item`** tagged `user-requested` (`work_items:create { priority: high }`), and 2. **nudges the Queen** via `coord:send`/`escalate { to: queen, wake: true }`. The Queen places it on her next wake — preserving the single-placer invariant while giving the user-requested item visible priority. It is **tier-gated** (D-011): the Sentinel is the user-facing approval tier, reusing the existing standing-approval / tier system (`operator-standing-candidates.ts`). **Low-tier** actions never reach the user (the Queen auto-places); **medium/high-tier** un-approved actions surface as a short voice/text approval prompt (“approve `<slug>`”). After handoff the Sentinel subscribes to the work\_item thread and **reports the landing**; if the session was away it surfaces the outcome via hindsight (“\[While you were away]”, `notifyOperatorHindsight`). An invariant test asserts the Sentinel **never** calls `bee:spawn`. ## The settings tab — live overrides over workspace defaults [Section titled “The settings tab — live overrides over workspace defaults”](#the-settings-tab--live-overrides-over-workspace-defaults) `SentinelTab.tsx` is the left-sidebar “quick live overrides” surface; the full workspace settings hold the **defaults** (D-013). It is the **first consumer of the shared `<OverridableSetting>` primitive** (D-016 / D-020 — not a 9th hand-rolled badge/reset copy): each row shows an override-vs-workspace-default badge + a reset (↺), precedence override > workspace default. Settings surfaced: audience mode (engineer ↔ user-friendly, `audienceMode` `'engineer'`|`'novice'`, D-005), voice on/off, proactive nudges (`proactiveTicksEnabled`), speak-status cadence (`speakCadenceStatus`), and a do-not-disturb (`silenceVoice`). The override read/write reuses the **voice-prefs workspace-default vs per-user-override seam** (`mergeUserOverWorkspace` / `VOICE_USER_OVERRIDE_KEYS`, the same `/settings/user` pattern — no new store, D-014/A). The broader contract is documented in [the unified override-settings backbone](/internal/docs/agent-insights/override-settings-backbone). > Gotcha that bit during the build: `silenceVoice` / `audienceMode` / `proactiveTicksEnabled` were surfaced by the tab but were **absent from `VOICE_USER_OVERRIDE_KEYS`** (and `silenceVoice` was missing from `DEFAULT_VOICE_PREFS`), so the tab’s overrides never reached the brain. If a new Sentinel override doesn’t take effect, check that its key is in the override-key set first. ## Proactive path — in progress (P-018-022) [Section titled “Proactive path — in progress (P-018-022)”](#proactive-path--in-progress-p-018-022) The autonomous “decide to speak” loop is **not new** — it reuses the existing active-mode proactive-tick engine + its full gate set (`proactiveTicksEnabled` / `speakSuggestions` / `speakCadenceStatus`, pause / sleep / budget / DND / single-speaker) and the `broadcastOpVoice → OPV_RESPONSE_AUDIO` injection seam (D-007). The open work is **architectural** (D-008): the loop currently lives in the **browser** React provider (`OperatorConversationProvider.tsx`), so it only runs while the desktop UI is open. For a genuinely always-on Sentinel that speaks with **no UI open**, the proactive loop must move **server-side** (into the voice-node host or a routine), with a single-owner guard so it does not double-fire when a desktop provider is also running, re-aimed at Sentinel fleet-status content and routing voice-off alerts through `attention-notify` / `device-push-dispatcher` (importance-gated), with hindsight on resume (D-010). This is P-018-022 and is still in progress as of `sentinel-herald-2026-06-21`. ## The old operator workspace-scan is retired (D-018) [Section titled “The old operator workspace-scan is retired (D-018)”](#the-old-operator-workspace-scan-is-retired-d-018) The Sentinel **replaces** the old scheduled operator workspace-scan (the “sweep + surface \~5 next-action cards + auto-dispatch on a 4-hourly cron” surface). That cadence is retired: the Queen scans/places continuously and the Sentinel reads the live blackboard directly. Concretely — the `scan` blueprint’s `triggers.schedule` was removed (so nothing materializes an active scan routine; the blueprint stays launchable on-demand for a manual sweep, and its `improvements:capture` curation path is unchanged), `seed-scan-routine.ts` is retired to a defensive deactivate-only no-op, and the old operator-scan persona (`blueprints/base/prompts/scanner.md`) is marked deprecated (its route was already removed with the retired Next operator app; its tables dropped in migration 167). Do not re-point the old scan at the Sentinel — read the live digests instead. ## See also [Section titled “See also”](#see-also) Guidance for the Sentinel converse / voice path: * [Parsing tagged compact tool results](/internal/docs/agent-insights/compact-tool-result-formats) — the read-context tools return compact TOON, not always JSON. * [Coord injection protocol](/internal/docs/agent-insights/coord-injection-protocol) — the continuous `[coord]` push surface the brain reads. * [A streaming-chat error state must survive the stream close](/internal/docs/agent-insights/sse-chat-error-must-survive-stream-close) — the SSE discipline the converse/voice stream must honor. * [The unified override-settings backbone](/internal/docs/agent-insights/override-settings-backbone) — the contract the SentinelTab overrides conform to. Plan: `sentinel-herald-2026-06-21`.

# Sentinel voice-in keys off a single global dock registration — so there must be ONE dock

> ~/.papercusp/sentinel-pane is a single global file every psu-sentinel launch overwrites; with several live pui-dock sessions the last writer wins and voice goes to a background window. reap.rs now enforces one chat dock at a time.

## The race [Section titled “The race”](#the-race) Voice-in writes an STT utterance to the Sentinel pane via `~/.papercusp/sentinel-pane` — a **single global file** holding `<zellij-session> <pane-id>`, written by the `psu-sentinel` wrapper at every dock launch. The endpoint (`routes/operator/sentinel-input.ts`) delegates to the shared `sentinel-pane-input.ts` module (`writeToSentinelPane()`) which reads the file and runs `zellij -s <session> action write-chars --pane-id <id>`. But the desktop can have **several live `pui-dock-*` sessions** at once — multiple desktop windows/workspaces (`:3170`, `:3270`, …), plus `tauri dev` recompile-relaunches and crashed instances that never ran their clean-exit teardown (`main.rs` `ExitRequested`→`child.kill()` only fires on a graceful exit). Every one of those docks’ `psu-sentinel` **overwrites the same global file**, so the *last* dock to launch owns voice-in — even if it’s a background or orphaned window. The user talks to the dock they SEE; voice lands in a different pane; nothing happens. `reap.rs` did not help: it only kills sessions whose **owner pid is dead**, and these orphans’ `pui chat` owners stay **alive**. ## The fix — one chat dock at a time (owner decision 2026-06-25) [Section titled “The fix — one chat dock at a time (owner decision 2026-06-25)”](#the-fix--one-chat-dock-at-a-time-owner-decision-2026-06-25) `reap::plan` now takes the session being launched (`own`) and, **when launching a dock**, also `KillAndDelete`s every *other* live `pui-dock-*` session — not just dead-owner ones. So exactly one chat dock exists, the global registration is unambiguous, and voice-in always targets it. Scope guards: * Only a **dock** launch enforces this (`session_kind(own) == "dock"`); a `wb` (workbench) or `reap` pass keeps the old dead-owner-only behaviour. * `pui-wb-*` and foreign (non-`pui-`) sessions are never touched. This **supersedes the per-window-dock decision of 2026-06-17**: a second desktop window now supersedes the first window’s dock instead of running a parallel one. That’s the accepted trade-off for unambiguous voice routing. Takes effect on the next dock launch after `cargo install --path apps/tui` (the desktop relaunches the dock frequently, so it converges on its own). ## If voice-in still misses after this [Section titled “If voice-in still misses after this”](#if-voice-in-still-misses-after-this) Check the live invariant: `zellij list-sessions | grep pui-dock` should show **one** session, and `cat ~/.papercusp/sentinel-pane` should name it. More than one live `pui-dock-*` means a dock launched with a stale `pui` binary (reinstall) or a foreign session is mis-prefixed.

# The Sentinel's voice-out (voice:say) crosses processes — its buffer MUST be shared (PG), not in-memory

> The dock Sentinel's voice:say runs inside the agent-mcp process its role-scoped MCP connects to (an mcp-proxy on :9071 → the green operator :3070), while the webview drains GET /api/operator/sentinel-output on a DIFFERENT operator process. A process-local in-memory FIFO therefore never bridges push→poll — the user speaks, gets a correct TUI answer, and HEARS NOTHING. The buffer must be a shared store (PG table harness_shared.sentinel_says). When debugging "voice-out is silent", check the buffer on ALL operator hosts, not just the one the webview talks to.

## The trap [Section titled “The trap”](#the-trap) The dock 🛡 Sentinel is a `psu --role=sentinel` Claude-Code TUI. Its **voice-OUT** is the `voice:say` MCP tool → `pushSentinelSay()`; the webview polls `GET /api/operator/sentinel-output` → `drainSentinelSays()` → desktop TTS. The seductive (wrong) implementation is a module-scoped in-memory FIFO: 
```ts
const buffer: string[] = [];
export async function pushSentinelSay(t) { buffer.push(t); }
export async function drainSentinelSays() { const o = buffer.slice(); buffer.length = 0; return o; }
```
 It passes its unit test, works in a single-process dev harness, and is **silently broken in the real topology**. ## Why it’s broken: push and poll hit different processes [Section titled “Why it’s broken: push and poll hit different processes”](#why-its-broken-push-and-poll-hit-different-processes) The psu Sentinel’s role-scoped MCP is configured (in its `.mcp.json`) to an HTTP MCP endpoint — observed as an **mcp-proxy listening on `127.0.0.1:9071` that forwards to the green operator `:3070`**. So `voice:say` (and every other MCP tool the Sentinel calls) executes **inside the `:3070` process** and `pushSentinelSay` fills **that** process’s in-memory array. The webview, meanwhile, drains `/api/operator/sentinel-output` on **whatever operator the desktop is wired to** — a *different* process. Its array is always empty. Net effect: **the user speaks, the Sentinel answers correctly in the TUI, and the user hears nothing.** Nothing errors; the buffer is just never bridged. This is the same class as the storage-policy “no module-scoped Maps for shared state” rule — an in-memory buffer is per-process, and this buffer’s producer and consumer are guaranteed to be in different processes. ## The fix: a shared FIFO in Postgres [Section titled “The fix: a shared FIFO in Postgres”](#the-fix-a-shared-fifo-in-postgres) `voice:say` and the drain must rendezvous in a store both processes share. Every operator/agent-mcp process on the box talks to one database (native `:5432` in dev, embedded in the shipped app), so a single **global** FIFO table is the bridge (migration `390-sentinel-says-pg.sql`): 
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS harness_shared.sentinel_says (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, line TEXT NOT NULL, created_at BIGINT NOT NULL
);
```
 * push = `INSERT` + trim to the most-recent N (bounded). * drain = `WITH d AS (DELETE … RETURNING id,line) SELECT line FROM d ORDER BY id` — race-free, no read-modify-write window. * No `workspace_id`: this is the LOCAL-APP-USER-ONLY desktop TTS channel (owner constraint) — one Sentinel, one webview, one machine — NOT the P2P voice-channel system (`voice_relay` / `operator_voice_channels`). A global queue also sidesteps any cross-process `activeWorkspaceId()` mismatch. * push/drain swallow errors (a relay blip must never fail the Sentinel’s turn). ## 2026-07-01 update — the drain now has TWO gated consumers [Section titled “2026-07-01 update — the drain now has TWO gated consumers”](#2026-07-01-update--the-drain-now-has-two-gated-consumers) Since `voice-unified-sentinel-pipeline-2026-07-01` (P-002), the webview poll is no longer the only drain. While an operator voice SESSION is live, the server-side **sentinel-says pump** (`voice-node/sentinel-says-pump.ts`) owns the FIFO: it drains, broadcasts a response transcript, synthesizes the line into bus audio (`broadcastOpVoice`), and persists it — every attached client displays it and the elected player speaks it. The webview poll stands down while `micOwnedByFullAgent` and still owns local (no-session) mode. Exactly one consumer at a time; the atomic PG drain makes a transition race deliver a line to one of them, never both. Debug rule: know WHICH consumer should own the drain right now (session live → the pump) before concluding rows are vanishing. ## Debugging checklist when “voice-out is silent” [Section titled “Debugging checklist when “voice-out is silent””](#debugging-checklist-when-voice-out-is-silent) 1. **Did the Sentinel actually call `voice:say`?** Dump the pane (`zellij action dump-screen --pane-id <id>`) and look for the tool call. The persona mandates it (`sentinel.persona.md` → “How you speak”); a turn that only writes terminal text is silent to the user. 2. **Check the buffer on ALL operator hosts**, not just the webview’s. With the old in-memory buffer, `GET /api/operator/sentinel-output` on `:3070`, `:3170`, `:3270` each return their OWN array — a false-negative is easy. With the PG fix, any host returns the same shared rows. 3. **Confirm the Sentinel’s MCP endpoint** in its `.mcp.json` (`~/.papercusp-workspaces/<ws>/.papercusp/.mcp.json`) — the `url` tells you which process `voice:say` runs in (e.g. the `:9071` proxy → `:3070`). ## Full-agent engine mode — server-side pump owns the drain (2026-07-01) [Section titled “Full-agent engine mode — server-side pump owns the drain (2026-07-01)”](#full-agent-engine-mode--server-side-pump-owns-the-drain-2026-07-01) Since **voice-unified-sentinel-pipeline** (P-002, 2026-06-30+), a full-agent voice engine (e.g. ElevenLabs Conversational, OpenAI Realtime) can own the voice session — it acts as THE BRAIN and the Sentinel TUI becomes a viewport. When `fullAgentEngine` is active (not `'off'`) and `micOwnedByFullAgent` is true, the **SERVER-side** `sentinel-says` pump takes over: it synths the spoken reply AND fan-outs to every attached client (local TTS, P2P voice relays, etc.). The LOCAL client-side poll in `VoiceAppBridge` (the interval that drains `/api/operator/sentinel-output`) MUST NOT compete when a full-agent owns the mic: 
```ts
// One-brain voice-OUT: while a full-agent session is live, the SERVER-side
// sentinel-says pump owns the FIFO — this local-mode poll must not compete.
if (voiceStateRef.current.micOwnedByFullAgent) return;
void drainSentinelOutput();
```
 So the buffer is STILL shared PG (the architecture remains), but the CONSUMER (local drain vs server-side pump) depends on which engine is driving the session. When the full-agent pump is active, it reads and processes all rows; the local drain backs off to avoid double-draining or losing utterances. ## Sibling gotcha — voice-IN is the mirror image [Section titled “Sibling gotcha — voice-IN is the mirror image”](#sibling-gotcha--voice-in-is-the-mirror-image) Voice-IN (`POST /api/operator/sentinel-input`) does NOT use this buffer: it writes the transcript into the Sentinel pane’s stdin via `packages/operator-core/lib/sentinel/sentinel-pane-input.ts`, reading the pane id from `~/.papercusp/sentinel-pane` (written by the `psu-sentinel` launch wrapper). Its hazards are different — a boot-window race after a dock relaunch, and writing into an EXITED pane (where the trailing Enter re-runs the command and loses the turn). The pane-write mechanics are now SHARED with in-process callers (the server-side EL-utterance relay, deep-delegation answer injection) — they all converge on the `writeToSentinelPane()` function so they apply the same warm-up gate and exited-pane guard.

# Box wedge / session leak → zombie `claude --resume` procs (ended session, live process)

> A climbing claude-proc count toward the ~70 bg-host wedge is usually ZOMBIE `claude --resume <uuid>` procs — adv_session ENDED but the OS process never exited. No DB-roster reaper sees them. How to diagnose + the slice-3 zombie reaper that sheds them.

## Symptom [Section titled “Symptom”](#symptom) The `claude` process count climbs monotonically toward \~70, the box overloads, the **papercup-bg-host DBOS ticker** starves (event-loop-lag spikes, `[routines]` drops to \~1/10min), and everything the ticker drives freezes: git-sync stops committing, the green-checkpoint stalls, agent loops skip. `dev:service_health` shows `:3070 up` (it is — the operator and the bg-host ticker are *different* services; see EI-1832). ## Root cause (EI-1873) [Section titled “Root cause (EI-1873)”](#root-cause-ei-1873) The leak is **zombie processes**, not idle-but-open sessions. Each leaked proc runs `claude --resume <uuid>` whose `harness_shared.adv_sessions` row is **ENDED** (`ended_at` set, `exit_code = 0`, often 16–18h prior) — but the OS process never exited. The session officially concluded; the process lingered, holding LISTEN conns + polling on the `:3070` event loop. Why every reaper misses them: * `idle-session-reaper.ts` slices 1 (dead-ghost) and 2 (live-but-idle) scan **OPEN** adv\_sessions (`ended_at IS NULL`). A zombie is **CLOSED** in the DB → structurally invisible. Running the reaper’s own logic *out-of-band* (a fresh, non-starved process) still reaps **0** — proof it is a criteria miss, not just starvation. * The presence-heartbeat liveness signal is *also* unreliable here: the per-60s supervisor beat is starved by the very overload the reaper is meant to detect, so an alive proc reads as “not live.” Liveness that depends on the starved resource is a feedback loop. ## Diagnose [Section titled “Diagnose”](#diagnose) The reliable proc↔DB join is **`adv_sessions.session_id` = the `claude --resume <uuid>`** on the OS proc (`adv_sessions.pid` is often null; don’t rely on it). 1. Count: `ps -eo comm | grep -c '^claude$'`. 2. For each live `claude --resume <uuid>` proc, look up `adv_sessions` by `session_id = <uuid>`. **`ended_at IS NOT NULL` ⇒ zombie** — safe to kill: the session is done (`exit_code = 0`), it holds no claim/wake/running-bee, and it is **not** any live agent’s current session (a live session has `ended_at IS NULL` — a disjoint set). ## Fix / shed [Section titled “Fix / shed”](#fix--shed) `idle-session-reaper.ts` **slice 3** — `reapZombieResumeProcs()` (+ pure `planZombieReap()` / `discoverResumeProcs()`), wired into the `system:idle-session-reaper` routine to run first each tick. It enumerates live `claude --resume` procs via `/proc`, asks PG which of their sessions are ended, and `SIGTERM`→(grace)→`SIGKILL`s the zombies. **Deterministic** (ended + alive), **starvation-independent** (no heartbeat dependence), **PID-recycle-guarded** (re-verifies the cmdline before EACH signal — before SIGTERM AND again before SIGKILL after the grace pause, so a pid recycled between the two is never hit), **double-gated** (`papercusp-idle-session-reaper` + `…-terminate`). Three additional safety guards (all added post-EI-1873): * **On-desktop spare**: `planZombieReap(procs, ended, onDesktopSessionIds)` — a `claude --resume` proc whose session is currently visible in a live OS window is NEVER signalled, even if its `adv_session` row reads ended. Belt-and-braces atop the foreground-TTY guard below (covers minimized/backgrounded edge cases). Best-effort (wmctrl failure → empty) so a failure can only spare fewer. * **Foreground-TTY guard** (`isForegroundTty` in `discoverResumeProcs`): a proc whose `/proc/<pid>/stat` shows it is a foreground, TTY-attached process (a human at a terminal) is excluded from the candidate set before any PG lookup. Exported as `parseForegroundFromStat` (pure, unit-testable). * **Live-session HAVING fix**: `defaultEndedSessionIds` uses `HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ended_at IS NULL) = 0` — a uuid is a zombie only when it has **no open row at all**. A LIVE resumed session REUSES its `session_id`, so an OLD ended row can coexist with the CURRENT open row. The earlier `AND ended_at IS NOT NULL` matched the old ended row and killed the live session (the `claude --resume` proc of a LIVE operator session was killed in a kill → re-resume → kill loop until it was noticed). The HAVING guard makes the live open row veto. **Manual out-of-band shed during a wedge** (the reaper routine is starved): run it from a fresh process with the flags forced — the flag resolves OFF in a fresh process, so inject it: 
```ts
const m = await import('<repo>/packages/operator-core/lib/idle-session-reaper.ts');
await m.reapZombieResumeProcs({ dryRun: true,  deps: { isFlagOn: async () => true } }); // confirm scope first
await m.reapZombieResumeProcs({ dryRun: false, deps: { isFlagOn: async () => true } }); // then shed
```
 ## Slice 4 — dangling inbox-wake await GC (P-004) [Section titled “Slice 4 — dangling inbox-wake await GC (P-004)”](#slice-4--dangling-inbox-wake-await-gc-p-004) `reclaimDanglingInboxWakeAwaits()` (rides the slice-1 master flag — non-destructive, no second gate). The bug: every idle psu/Queen-launched agent arms a standing `coord:inbox-wake:<self>` await (turn-lifecycle-control always-arm). A clean session end cancels it, but a process that DIES never runs that hygiene — the await row persists forever. `coord:presence/fetchWakeability` reads these rows to derive `wakeable`/`parked`, so a dead session reads as a live dispatch target (`woken:0` when a coordinator tries to dispatch) AND `gatherProtectedSessionOwners` (slice 1’s keep-gate) counts a standing await as alive — these dangling rows also PROTECT their ghost `adv_sessions` from being reaped. Measured live (2026-06-24): 334 inbox-wake awaits, 236 on dead owners. Fix: cancel an inbox-wake await whose owner is NOT live or resumable. “Live or resumable” = fresh presence heartbeat, running bee, in-flight wake delivery, OR an OPEN `adv_session` (a parked session the wake-executor can `--resume`). A parked-but-resumable session keeps its await; only a truly dead session loses it → flips from false `parked` to honest `ended`. ## Still open (follow-ups) [Section titled “Still open (follow-ups)”](#still-open-follow-ups) * 258 no-owner **OPEN** adv\_session rows also accumulate (no `coord_owner_id` → `keptNoOwner`, never reaped) — a separate sweep should end orphaned rows with no live proc. * The **upstream** bug — why a `claude --resume` proc fails to exit after its session ends (exit 0) — is unfixed; slice-3 is the safety net, not the cure. * For full starvation-immunity, run the zombie sweep in the bg-host-watchdog (out-of-band), not only the ticker-driven routine.

# Session search + compaction recovery: your pre-compaction turns survive — retrieve, don't re-derive

> Compaction and cold wakes lose CONTEXT, not DATA. Every agent session transcript (claude/omp/codex + harness chats) is indexed into session_turns and coord messages are a searchable corpus, so anything a compaction summary dropped is still on disk and retrievable verbatim. The failure this prevents: a successor burning turns re-deriving lost state it could have pulled with one sessions:search { session:'self', mode:'verbatim' } call. Covers self-recall after compaction, fleet postmortems via the membership ledger (postmortem-safe when owners are dead), the sessions:* navigation verbs, and the write-through discipline that keeps sessions a safety net rather than the primary store.

Compaction (and a cold wake, and a re-spawn) loses **context, not data**. Your transcript scrolls out of the model window, but every pre-compaction turn still exists on disk and is **indexed** into `harness_shared.session_turns` — across all four corpora (claude / omp / codex + harness agent chats). Coord messages are indexed too. So the single most wasteful thing a successor can do is **re-derive lost state from scratch** when it could **retrieve** it. ## The four memory layers — where sessions fits [Section titled “The four memory layers — where sessions fits”](#the-four-memory-layers--where-sessions-fits) `sessions:*` is the **episodic, verbatim** layer — a peer of the three you already use, not a replacement: * **mem0** (`memory:*`) — what was **distilled** (curated, fuzzy-recalled facts). * **facts** (`facts:*`) — **deterministic** standing conclusions, folded verbatim into every orient. * **coord** (`coord:*`) — what’s **happening** right now (live ephemera). * **sessions** (`sessions:*`) — **what was actually said.** The safety net for everything nobody thought to file. If a conclusion never made it into mem0, facts, or a checkpoint, it is still in the transcript — and still findable. ## Self-recall after a compaction [Section titled “Self-recall after a compaction”](#self-recall-after-a-compaction) Two moves: 1. **First orient after a compaction:** `coord:orient { afterCompaction: true }`. This folds your held work-items’ checkpoints, armed-loop status, and the self-recall pointer back into your context — the deterministic half of recovery. 2. **Anything the summary lost:** `sessions:search { session:'self', mode:'verbatim', query:'…' }`. `'self'` is resolved **server-side** from the call context — you never discover your own transcript path — and a live-tail fallback scans the un-ingested tail of your own JSONL so even the last few minutes are searchable. `mode:'verbatim'` is the exact-quote finder; `mode:'hybrid'` (default) is the semantic/paraphrase finder. Both modes cover pre-compaction turns just the same — compaction only removes them from your live context window, never from the index. The compaction summary you produce should **say this out loud** so the successor knows to retrieve. The rendered compaction floor (`~/.papercusp/compaction-strategy.md`, generated from `apps/operator/prompts/papercusp-compaction.base.md` via `renderCompactionStrategy` — never hand-edit the generated file) now carries both the `afterCompaction` re-orient banner and a “the verbatim record SURVIVES” line for exactly this reason. ## Fleet postmortems + handoff archaeology [Section titled “Fleet postmortems + handoff archaeology”](#fleet-postmortems--handoff-archaeology) `sessions:search` takes a `fleet:<slug>` filter that answers “where did fleet X discuss Y” across **both** member transcripts and coord traffic in one call. The non-obvious part — and the reason there is no `fleet:search` convenience verb — is that the fleet→members resolution runs **server-side against the append-only membership ledger, time-windowed**, *not* against live presence. Why membership history, not live presence An ended agent loses its `fleet_slug` and its presence row is reaped on a TTL. So resolving a fleet’s members from **live presence** silently drops exactly the dead members a postmortem needs. The membership ledger is append-only, so `fleet:<slug>` recall is **postmortem-safe even when every member is dead** — the documented presence-vs-history trap, handled once, in the filter. For sequencing a handoff or reconstructing who-did-what: `sessions:timeline { owner }` joins `session_turns` + `tool_invocations` + coord messages by owner and time; `sessions:list` enumerates sessions across claude/omp/harness-chat surfaces (it absorbs the old `dev:claude_session op=list` and `omp:sessions op=list`). ## The tool surface [Section titled “The tool surface”](#the-tool-surface) * **`sessions:search`** — the fused, one-round-trip verb: search the session corpora → hydrate ±N-turn context windows around the top-k hits → `readMore` pointers into `sessions:read`. Prefer it over raw `search:*` when you want the surrounding turns, not just the hit. Precedent for fusing a search-then-read composition into one tool: `coord:orient`. * **`sessions:read` / `sessions:list` / `sessions:timeline`** — the thin navigation verbs (windowed read, unified enumeration, joined timeline). * **`search:fulltext` / `search:semantic`** — the generic search verbs already cover the `session_turn` and `coord_message` corpora via the SearchSource registry, honoring the structured filter bag (owner, speaker, client, since/until, fleet). `sessions:search` composes these primitives; it does not fork them. ## Write-through discipline — sessions is the net, not the trampoline [Section titled “Write-through discipline — sessions is the net, not the trampoline”](#write-through-discipline--sessions-is-the-net-not-the-trampoline) Retrieval is the backstop, **not** an excuse to skip filing. A durable conclusion goes to `facts:assert` (standing conclusion), `work_items:checkpoint` / `loop:checkpoint` (in-flight continuity), or `memory:remember` (fuzzy fact) **the moment it forms — not when the context gauge fills.** The \~75%-context nudge is the backstop, not the trigger. Sessions search saves you when write-through failed; it is not a substitute for it. Two reasons filing still wins even though the transcript survives: * **Deterministic delivery.** A `facts:assert` conclusion is folded verbatim into every future orient; a transcript quote has to be *searched for*, which means you have to remember it exists. * **Distillation.** mem0/facts carry the *conclusion*; the transcript carries the raw turn you’d have to re-read and re-derive from. Retrieval is cheaper than re-derivation, but filing is cheaper than retrieval. ## See also [Section titled “See also”](#see-also) * Plan `session-search-scope-2026-07-05` (the corpora, the filter bag, the fused tool, adoption) and `compaction-context-loss-2026-07-05` (the write-through + recovery-cost framing). * The memory-layers section of the su playbooks (`papercusp-su-{engineer,power}.tools.md`) and `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` § Memory, which now name `sessions` as the fourth recall layer.

# Spawns silently fell to `omp -p` after a settings save — empty config used to delete the host's AGENT_CMD env

> A /settings/agent save with empty cmd/models deleted the .env.local-provided AGENT_CMD/AGENT_MODELS from the live operator process until restart (EI-337, fixed). Symptom signature + the boot-env-restore rule.

**Symptom signature (what it looked like):** fleet spawns finish in \~4s with exit 0, completely **empty** `out_body`/`err_body`/`jsonl_body` in `harness_run_output`, no `session_id` on the nursery row, no `claude-cfg-spawn-*` dir, no transcript. It looks exactly like a bug in whatever spawn feature you just built (per-spawn model tiers, in our case). **Actual root cause (2026-06-11):** any `POST /api/agent-config` (saving the /settings/agent page) ran `applyToProcessEnv`, which treated an empty config value as “unset the env var” — deleting the **host’s own** `.env.local`-provided `AGENT_CMD`/`AGENT_MODELS` from the live operator process. Every spawn after the save resolved the CLI default `omp -p`, and an omp run with an unresolvable model exits 0 with empty output. The host healed only on the next service restart, so the breakage window was invisible unless you knew a settings save had happened. **Fixed (EI-337):** `applyToProcessEnv` captures the boot-time values at module load and *restores* them when a config field is empty (empty = “no user override → host default”); the `env.sh` mirror likewise stopped emitting `unset` lines. Regression-pinned in `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-config-env.test.ts`. **Rules of thumb:** * Empty-output rc=0 spawns right after any agent-config write → check `GET /api/agent-config` → `envOverrides` against what `.env.local` sets, before debugging your feature. * When mirroring stored config into `process.env`, never `delete` on empty — snapshot the boot env once and restore it. A settings page’s “no value” is an *absence of override*, not an instruction to strip the host’s config. * This matters double on auto-save settings pages (the /settings/agent page is per-field auto-save now): the mirror runs on every debounced save.

# Setup-wizard "workspace setup failed" is usually a transient api.github.com connect-timeout, not auth

> A valid gh token does NOT mean api.github.com is reachable: git-over-github.com (the credential helper) can succeed while direct API calls to api.github.com time out, because GitHub's edge IPs (140.82.0.0/16) can be intermittently unreachable from a given network while github.com git endpoints work. The dogfood bootstrap records clone/submodule/identity failures as a terminal 'failed', which inside the GitHub-centric setup wizard misleads users into (uselessly) re-authing. EI-3548 added a network_timeout classification + auto-retry so a transient blip self-heals.

When the setup wizard reports **“Setting up Papercusp workspace failed”** (or the finish-gate “Workspace download failed”) right after a GitHub sign-in/reauth, the cause is almost never credentials. It is a **transient inability to reach `api.github.com`**. ## The non-obvious part: a valid `gh` token ≠ a reachable GitHub API [Section titled “The non-obvious part: a valid gh token ≠ a reachable GitHub API”](#the-non-obvious-part-a-valid-gh-token--a-reachable-github-api) These three facts can all be true at once, and were on 2026-06-24: * `gh auth token` returns instantly and `gh api user` resolves to the right login → **auth is fine.** * `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` works → **git-over-HTTPS via the credential helper is fine** (it happened to resolve to a reachable edge IP). * `curl https://api.github.com/` / node `fetch` / `gh api user` **time out** → **the GitHub API is unreachable** (DNS handed back an edge IP whose path is currently dropping packets). GitHub serves `github.com` and `api.github.com` from the same anycast range (`140.82.0.0/16`). When a network path to a *subset* of those IPs is lossy, any given operation succeeds or times out depending on which IP DNS returns — so it looks intermittent and IP-specific, not like “GitHub is down” (it isn’t — `curl --resolve api.github.com:443:<reachable-ip>` returns 200). ## Why it surfaced as a scary terminal “failed” [Section titled “Why it surfaced as a scary terminal “failed””](#why-it-surfaced-as-a-scary-terminal-failed) The dogfood bootstrap (`bootstrap-papercusp-hive.ts`) records `clone` / `submodules` `status:'error'` on **any** git/github failure, and the wizard surfaces that as a terminal failure. Inside a GitHub-centric wizard, a generic “failed” reads as “your GitHub sign-in didn’t take” — so users re-auth, which cannot fix a packet-level timeout. ## The fix (EI-3548) — classify + auto-retry [Section titled “The fix (EI-3548) — classify + auto-retry”](#the-fix-ei-3548--classify--auto-retry) * `clone-github.ts` classifies connection failures as **`network_timeout`** (checked before auth, since a connect failure is mutually exclusive with a `403`/“Authentication failed” that only arrives after a successful connect). * `useDogfoodBootstrapProgress` exposes **`networkError`**; the finish gate **auto-retries with backoff (2s/4s/8s, bounded)** before showing any terminal failure, with network-aware copy (“Couldn’t reach GitHub — retrying… / not your GitHub sign-in”). The banner mirrors this. * The best-effort Solution-C share substeps (`adoptShare`/`goShare`/ `shareExisting`, all of which hit the GitHub API) are wrapped so a transient timeout **warns** instead of failing an otherwise-complete workspace setup. Deferred: a shared GitHub-API client with retry + circuit-breaker for the OTHER `api.github.com` callers (`swarm-join`, `revalidate-repo-coords`, `hive-directory`) so one bad window doesn’t 10s-hang fleet-wide.

# "Setup failed" on a fresh clone — a renamed `.gitmodules` URL pointed at a non-existent repo

> THE root cause of the owner's recurring 'Setting up Papercusp workspace failed': the papercup→papercusp identity rename overreached into .gitmodules and rewrote two submodule URLs (libs/papercusp-db, libs/papercusp-shared) to Papercusp/papercusp-db.git / papercusp-shared.git — repos that were NEVER renamed on GitHub (404). Every FRESH dogfood clone then failed submodule init; the dev box was immune (its .git/config kept the correct papercup-* URLs). Fix: restore the URLs to papercup-db.git/papercup-shared.git + a gitmodules-invariants test that fails CI if a submodule URL goes stale again.

The deterministic root cause of the owner’s repeated “Setting up Papercusp workspace failed” — **not** GitHub, **not** the network, **not** git/PATH/auth (those were red herrings / secondary robustness gaps chased first). ## What broke [Section titled “What broke”](#what-broke) The papercup→papercusp identity migration (owner-directed 2026-06-20) ran a blanket `papercup`→`papercusp` rename that **overreached into `.gitmodules`** and rewrote two submodule URLs: | path | URL after the bad rename (404) | real repo | | ----------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | | `libs/papercusp-db` | `Papercusp/papercusp-db.git` | `Papercusp/papercup-db.git` | | `libs/papercusp-shared` | `Papercusp/papercusp-shared.git` | `Papercusp/papercup-shared.git` | The submodule **paths** were correctly renamed on disk, but the GitHub **repos** were never renamed — they still answer only at their `papercup-*` names. So the rewritten URLs 404. These are **load-bearing source** submodules (34+ active imports of `@papercusp/db-org` `getOrgPg` and `@papercusp/papercusp-shared`), not retired — so `git submodule update --init` fails, the dogfood bootstrap reports an error row, and the wizard shows a bare “setup failed”. ## Why only fresh clones — and why it was so hard to see [Section titled “Why only fresh clones — and why it was so hard to see”](#why-only-fresh-clones--and-why-it-was-so-hard-to-see) The dev box (and any checkout that existed *before* the bad edit) was **immune**: its `.git/config` / `.git/modules/<path>/config` already cached the correct `papercup-*` URLs, and `git submodule update` reads those, not `.gitmodules`, once a submodule is initialized. Only a **fresh `git clone`** (exactly the dogfood first-boot path on the owner’s Mac/Mac-VM) reads `.gitmodules` to seed the remotes — so the breakage was invisible to every developer and reproduced only on a brand-new machine. `git submodule sync` is what copies `.gitmodules` URLs into `.git/config`; running it on a stale checkout is also how you’d *propagate* the bug. ## The fix [Section titled “The fix”](#the-fix) 1. Restore the two URLs in `.gitmodules` to `papercup-db.git` / `papercup-shared.git` (git-sync pushes it → every future fresh clone works). 2. On an already-broken clone: edit its `.gitmodules`, `git submodule sync libs/papercusp-db libs/papercusp-shared`, then re-run the bootstrap (the operator’s `POST /api/desktop/bootstrap-hive/start`, which runs in the GUI process that holds the keychain creds — an SSH shell can’t reach the GUI-bound osxkeychain). ## Recurrence guards (a detector failure too) [Section titled “Recurrence guards (a detector failure too)”](#recurrence-guards-a-detector-failure-too) * **`gitmodules-invariants.test.ts`** parses the committed `.gitmodules` and fails the build if any submodule URL matches the known-dead `papercusp-db` / `papercusp-shared` names, if the two load-bearing submodules don’t point at their real `papercup-*` repos, or if any URL is not an `https` `github.com/Papercusp/*.git` URL. A blanket rename can’t silently re-break it. * **`bootstrap-papercusp-hive.ts`** now logs *which* submodule failed and the git stderr tail on a non-zero exit (`fatal:` / `Repository not found` / …) instead of a bare `exited 128` — the missing diagnostic that cost a full live debugging round. ## Lesson [Section titled “Lesson”](#lesson) A repo-wide identity rename must **exclude remote URLs** (`.gitmodules`, `.git/config` remotes, `package.json` repository fields, CI clone URLs) unless the remote was *actually* renamed on the host. Renaming a local path ≠ renaming the upstream repo. When a “setup failed” reproduces only on a fresh machine, suspect a clone-time-only input (`.gitmodules`, lockfile registries, bundled tool paths) before blaming the network.

# Severe-event condition lifecycle: conditionKey alarms + resolution supersede

> Fleet stall alarms are condition-keyed; recovery broadcasts a resolution and coord:inbox annotates the stale alarm resolved:true — don't investigate a resolved condition.

Severe pipeline alarms (`git-sync STALLED …`, `green-checkpoint STALLED …`) are broadcast to every running agent. Before WI-1444 they were **fire-and-forget**: when the watchdog detected recovery it cleared the escalation silently and the broadcast was never superseded — an agent waking hours later read a stale “STALLED” alarm as live truth and burned a turn investigating a dead condition. ## The lifecycle (WI-1444) [Section titled “The lifecycle (WI-1444)”](#the-lifecycle-wi-1444) * **Alarm** — `broadcastSevereEvent({ …, conditionKey })` stamps `condition_key` on the envelope. The watchdogs use stable keys: `git-sync-stall:<install_slug>` and `green-stall:<install_slug>`. * **Recovery** — the watchdog’s recovery branch calls `broadcastSevereEventResolved({ conditionKey, summary })`, which broadcasts a `category: 'severe-event-resolved'` message carrying `resolves_condition: <key>` (and `condition_key`, so resolutions are queryable by key too). * **Read** — `coord:inbox` annotates every returned entry whose `condition_key` has a **strictly-later** resolution with `resolved: true` + `resolved_at`. The scan runs over the full inbox read (pre-`limit`), so a windowed view still resolves correctly. A re-alarm *after* the latest resolution stays un-annotated — it is live again. * **State view** — `coord:conditions` (EI-6138) folds the same stream into live per-condition state: open conditions first (claimable), then recently resolved. Use it to answer “is anything wrong right now?” without inbox archaeology. Sibling read-side hygiene: repeated categorized broadcasts in `coord:inbox` coalesce to one `repeat_count`-annotated row (EI-6144). ## What this means for you [Section titled “What this means for you”](#what-this-means-for-you) * **An alarm with `resolved: true` needs NO action** — the condition already cleared; do not claim or investigate it. * **An un-annotated severe-event alarm is (as far as the log knows) still open** — the claimable signal is unchanged. * Adding a new watchdog/alarm? Pass a stable `conditionKey` on the alarm and broadcast the matching resolution on the recovery edge (guard it on the same transition edge as your `recovered` accounting so healthy passes stay silent). Fail-soft is built in — a broadcast failure never breaks the sweep. ## Verification [Section titled “Verification”](#verification) Unit-pinned in `severe-event-broadcast.test.ts` + `inbox-condition-lifecycle.test.ts`; live-verified 2026-07-01: the `git-sync-stall:papercusp` alarm (22:54Z) was superseded by its resolution (23:08Z) with matching keys in `coord_event_log`.

# shadcn-registry components must be ported to token CSS — there is no Tailwind in the operator build

> @tailwindcss/postcss in apps/operator is Storybook-only; vendoring a shadcn/Kibo component verbatim renders unstyled. Port its classes to var(--bg-*) token CSS instead — recipe + the Kanban precedent.

## The trap [Section titled “The trap”](#the-trap) `apps/operator/package.json` lists `@tailwindcss/postcss` — so it looks like a Tailwind app, and a shadcn-ecosystem registry component (Kibo UI, shadcn/ui blocks, etc.) looks like a drop-in vendor. **It is not.** That dep sits in the Storybook devDeps; there is no `tailwind.config.*`, no `postcss.config.*`, and no `@import "tailwindcss"` anywhere in `apps/operator/app` or `apps/operator-vite`. Tailwind utility classes in vendored code compile to nothing — the component renders bare and unstyled, which reads as “the library is broken” when it’s really the build. ## The recipe (proven on the plan kanban, 2026-06-12) [Section titled “The recipe (proven on the plan kanban, 2026-06-12)”](#the-recipe-proven-on-the-plan-kanban-2026-06-12) Vendoring `shadcnblocks/kibo` `packages/kanban` into `app/harness/Kanban.tsx` + `Kanban.css`: 1. **Keep the behavior source verbatim where possible** — dnd-kit wiring, a11y announcements, context/composition API. That’s the value you’re borrowing. 2. **Port every Tailwind class to a token-CSS class** in a co-located stylesheet (the `app/harness/*.css` convention). Map shadcn vars to ours: `bg-secondary` → `var(--bg-2)`, `Card`/`bg-card` → `var(--bg-raised)`, `ring-primary` → `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--accent)`, `border` → `1px solid var(--border)`, muted text → `var(--fg-dim)`/`var(--fg-mute)`. Keep the upstream class string in a comment above each rule so the next upgrade can diff. 3. **Replace shadcn-only deps with primitives**: `<ScrollArea>` → native `overflow-y: auto`; `cn()` → a 3-line local `cx()`; `tunnel-rat` → an explicit render prop (the Kanban’s `overlay` prop). 4. **Give the component a height constraint upstream assumed from its sized parent** — Kibo-style `size-full` components silently grow unbounded in a page-scrolled pane (the kanban’s columns hit 2300px tall before a `max-height` cap was added). Token catalog: `/internal/docs/design/tokens`. Decision matrix row for the kanban itself: `/internal/docs/design`. ## Verifying visuals on the headless box (what §15.4 doesn’t say) [Section titled “Verifying visuals on the headless box (what §15.4 doesn’t say)”](#verifying-visuals-on-the-headless-box-what-154-doesnt-say) * `tauri-agent-tools screenshot` platform-detects **Wayland from your shell env** and demands `sway`/`grim` even when your target instance is on an X11 Xvfb. Force it: `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11 DISPLAY=:NN tauri-agent-tools screenshot …` — and pass `--title Papercusp`. * Even then the window matcher can pick a 10×10 helper window (or a zombie window from a killed instance — `xdotool windowkill` the leftovers). Fallback that always works: bridge-`eval` a red `el.style.outline='3px solid red'` on the element, `import -window <id>`, crop to the outline. * The debug shell embeds VTE terminal panes beside the webview (the webview gets only part of the window). `PAPERCUSP_DEV_WRAPPER=0` does **not** remove the terminal panes; the control-bar pane switcher (PUI / DEV / …) picks which webview is visible.

# Shared-hive federation — the live-diagnosis toolkit + the two admission paths

> When a fresh joiner rosters a hive but receives no content, the cause is almost always upstream of the apply-guard: an ADMISSION decision, not a merge bug. This is the toolkit to read a live fed-a/fed-b rig (fed.sh: ports/sql/api/mcp/ssh self-discovering ports) and the model to interpret it — the SIGNED-announce identity decider (revoked → bad_sig → verifyBinding → admit/pending/binding_invalid) feeding the TWO same-hive SCOPE paths (owner-log bootstrap-admit vs member-set admission+buffer), the registry-gated substrate boot that decides which hives a node even swarms, the boot-history event log (dogfood-substrate-boot-history), and what binding_invalid actually means (gist-less owner → conclusive reject, NOT retried).

## When to read this [Section titled “When to read this”](#when-to-read-this) You are staring at a live two-machine shared-hive rig (fed-a = owner, fed-b = joiner). Membership/roster federates (fed-b sees the owner in its roster, epoch keys decrypt), **but content does not cross** — features/plans/issues written on one member never materialize on the other, “discovers 0”. You are about to suspect the merge loop or the apply-guard. **Stop. The merge/apply guard is almost never the live cause.** It is unit-green and re-proven over real testcontainer-PG + real swarm (`feature-content-federation.integration.test.ts`). On a live rig the failure is upstream: the peer’s log was never **admitted**, or the node never **swarmed** the hive at all. This doc gives you (1) the toolkit to read the live state, and (2) the admission model you need to interpret what you read. It is the synthesis the public-release diagnosis (`shared-hive-public-release-2026-06-22`, D-005…D-010) converged on after every mechanical apply hypothesis was refuted. > Sibling docs, each a different slice — read them too: [`shared-hive-live-federation-witnessing`](/internal/docs/agent-insights/shared-hive-live-federation-witnessing) (the green-rig/red-binary trap + smoke gotchas), [`federation-rig-restart-runbook`](/internal/docs/agent-insights/federation-rig-restart-runbook) (recovering a wedged rig / missing gh-auth), [`owner-side-cross-member-content-apply-gap`](/internal/docs/agent-insights/owner-side-cross-member-content-apply-gap) (the one genuine apply-guard asymmetry), [`hive-approval-membership-gate-wiring`](/internal/docs/agent-insights/hive-approval-membership-gate-wiring) (the owner-admission approval seam). ## The toolkit — `fed.sh` [Section titled “The toolkit — fed.sh”](#the-toolkit--fedsh) `papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm/fed.sh` is the versioned, reliable way to drive either VM. Its whole reason to exist: the packaged app picks a **fresh dynamic operator + PG port on every boot**, old listeners linger, and the app log’s “latest `[serve] listening on`” line is unreliable (EI-3409 / WI-559 burned hours on exactly this). So `fed.sh` **self-discovers** the live ports on every call by SSHing in and probing — operator = the loopback port answering `GET /api/desktop/preflight` 2xx (other listeners 404 it; dead ones refuse); PG = the port that accepts a `harness_admin` psql to `papercusp`. Discovered ports are cached per-VM under `~/.papercusp/fed-rig-ports.<vm>` for `FED_PORT_TTL` (default 600s) and auto-rediscovered when a target port stops answering. It survives app/VM restarts with **no edits**. | Subcommand | What it does | | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `fed.sh <a\|b> ports` | Show the discovered `operator=` / `pg=` ports (pass `1` to force a probe). | | `fed.sh <a\|b> rediscover` | Clear the port cache and re-probe. Run this FIRST after any restart. | | `fed.sh <a\|b> sql "<SQL>"` | `psql` against the VM’s embedded PG as `harness_admin` / `papercusp`. | | `fed.sh <a\|b> api <METHOD> <path> [json-body]` | Superuser HTTP route (Bearer from the operator’s actual `$HOME/.papercusp/superuser-token`). | | `fed.sh <a\|b> mcp <tool> [json-args]` | Superuser MCP tool over `/api/mcp?superuser=1` (returns just the `data:` SSE payload). | | `fed.sh <a\|b> ssh <cmd…>` | Raw SSH into the VM (e.g. `ssh 'tail papercusp-app.log'`). | Two footguns the script already handles, but you must know: * **`$HOME` is workspace-scoped on a VM whose operator runs workspace-scoped** (`HOME=/home/tester/.papercusp-workspaces/default`, D-007). The superuser token and `gh` auth live under the operator’s *actual* HOME, not `/home/tester`. `fed.sh` derives the token from `/proc/$(pgrep -f serve.mjs)/environ`; if `hive:membership_decide` returns `no_owner_identity`, the operator’s HOME is missing `~/.config/gh` — symlink it. * **EI-3409 superuser-MCP workspace mismatch.** Superuser MCP resolves `ctx.workspaceId='*'` while HTTP routes/queue use `'default'`, so a hive created via `mcp` lands in the wrong workspace and routes then return `not_owner_swarm`. For a workspace-scoped WRITE tool, set `FED_MCP_WS=default` so `fed.sh` injects `workspace:"default"` (OPT-IN — blanket injection breaks READ tools that reject an unknown `workspace` key). * **WI-892 (FIXED 2026-06-26, su-549e0214): the `'*'` sentinel was LEAKING into `harness_shared.hive_members` WRITES.** The hive-membership write tools resolved `args.workspace ?? ctx.workspaceId ?? … ?? activeWorkspaceId()` — a truthy `'*'` wins, so the `activeWorkspaceId()` fallback never fired and `'*'` was persisted as `workspace_id`. A `'*'`-stamped row is **invisible to every concrete-workspace read** (the membership guard, epoch-key grant, and cross-member content federation all filter `WHERE workspace_id='<concrete>'`), so the operator’s member view silently diverged from the raw table (live proof on fed-a: 18 `'*'` rows; `b8recv-hive` 1 row total, 0 visible under `workspace_id='default'`). MERGED rows are unaffected — `projections/hive-members.ts` writes the local concrete `opts.workspaceId`, which is why a federated member can “self-heal” to `default` after a re-merge. **Fix:** `resolveConcreteWorkspaceId(...candidates)` in `workspace-registry.ts` (skips `'*'`/empty, never returns `'*'`) is now used by every hive write tool; `upsertHiveMember`/`addRevokedHivePubkeys`/`remove*` throw on `'*'`/empty; migration `406-hive-members-forbid-wildcard-workspace` backfills + adds `CHECK (workspace_id <> '*' AND <> '')`. **Use `resolveConcreteWorkspaceId` for ANY write that persists a `workspace_id` — `'*'` is a read sentinel, never a storable value.** (The same leak likely affects the `hives` table itself — `hive:create` under unscoped MCP also stamped its hives row `'*'` — a broader-class follow-up; see WI-892.) ## The two-path admission model — the thing you are actually debugging [Section titled “The two-path admission model — the thing you are actually debugging”](#the-two-path-admission-model--the-thing-you-are-actually-debugging) Content reaches a peer only if that peer **admits the source log**. Admission is two layers; read them top-to-bottom because the second only runs after the first passes. ### Layer 1 — the SIGNED-announce identity decider (`read-admission.ts`) [Section titled “Layer 1 — the SIGNED-announce identity decider (read-admission.ts)”](#layer-1--the-signed-announce-identity-decider-read-admissionts) Every inbound announce runs `decideAdmission` with fixed precedence: 
```plaintext
revoked → bad_sig → verifyBinding → admit / pending / binding_invalid
```
 `verifyBinding` is 3-state (D-006): * **`verified`** → channel-2 attestation valid (the announce’s `attestation_gist_id` is a GitHub gist owned by `github_user_id` containing `device_pubkey`) → **admit**. * **`pending`** → OUR transient failure (GitHub unreachable / gist-propagation lag) → `reason:'pending'`, **RETRYABLE** within the grace window. * **`fail`** → **`binding_invalid`** — a CONCLUSIVE attestation failure (gist gone, owner/pubkey mismatch, bad sig on the binding). **Not retried.** This is the layer the public-release live witness is stuck on. A **gist-less owner placeholder** (a hive created without a real GitHub gist, e.g. on a gh-degraded VM) fails `verifyBinding` → `binding_invalid` → the owner’s own log is conclusively rejected, so nothing it authored can ever be admitted.
