Papercusp gives a session four distinct places to park state, each with a different **delivery guarantee** — route by how the state must come back, not by habit. ## The four layers [Section titled “The four layers”](#the-four-layers) | Layer | Verb | Delivery | Use for | | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Work-item checkpoint | `work_items:checkpoint { id, checkpoint }` | Re-injected when the item is next picked up — by you or any successor | In-flight progress on one item: what’s done, what’s left, the next step | | Loop checkpoint | `loop:checkpoint { did, left, insight, next }` | Re-injected on the armed loop’s next wake; a cold wake reconstructs from it | An engine loop’s iteration state | | Standing fact | `facts:assert { scope, scopeRef?, key, body }` | Folded **verbatim** into every relevant orient/brief until retracted (TTL default 7d) | Scoped conclusions future turns must see deterministically (“X is owner-residue — exclude it”) | | Shared memory | `memory:remember` | Semantic recall (orient’s mem0 hit list, `memory:search`) | Fuzzy background worth recalling, not guaranteed delivery | Rules of thumb: a checkpoint is *per unit of work*, a fact is *per conclusion*, memory is *per thing worth knowing*. Live ephemera (intents, handoffs, presence) belong to `coord:*`, not to any of these. ## Where checkpoints actually live [Section titled “Where checkpoints actually live”](#where-checkpoints-actually-live) Work-item, loop, and hive checkpoints are rows in **`harness_shared.carry_notes`**, keyed by scope (`workitem:<harness>:<WI-id>`, `loop:…`, `hive`) — migration 472. Two traps: * `harness_shared.work_item_checkpoints` was the legacy checkpoint table; migration 494 folds any stragglers into `carry_notes` and drops it. * `work_items:get` at the trimmed payload tier does **not** surface an item’s checkpoint — absence of a checkpoint in a `get` is not evidence none exists. Read directly: `select note from harness_shared.carry_notes where scope like 'workitem:%:<id>'`. ## Facts discipline [Section titled “Facts discipline”](#facts-discipline) `facts:list { scope }` before asserting (upsert is by key — don’t fork a second key for the same conclusion). `facts:retract` the moment a fact stops being true: a stale fact delivered verbatim into every future brief is worse than none. Bodies store at ≤500 chars — write tight conclusions, not essays. ## Why this exists [Section titled “Why this exists”](#why-this-exists) Compaction ([context compaction](/internal/docs/agents/compaction)) and session death are routine, not exceptional. State parked on these surfaces survives both losslessly; state carried only in conversation prose degrades into a summary and goes stale. The discipline is: flush first, then let prose point at what was flushed.

# Data Sync overview

> How harness UI panels read from Postgres in real time via the SSE sync-resolver + RichGrid.

Zero is fully decommissioned, not merely retired Zero / zero-cache / ZQL named-queries is **gone from the tree** — `zero-decommission-2026-06-20` (Z-2) removed `@rocicorp/zero` from every `package.json`, deleted the `@papercusp/zero-harness` package (`libs/zero-harness` no longer exists as a directory), and stripped the Zero-specific transport out of `@papercusp/sync`. Zero repo-wide `@rocicorp/zero` deps: **0**. The shipping desktop app uses **SSE-primary** sync (the `:3070` Hono host pushes invalidate/update over Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY` through the v2 sync-resolver registry, described below); zero-cache is not run anywhere. Source of truth: `apps/operator/providers/HarnessSyncProvider.tsx` (transport-selection doc-comment) + the root `CLAUDE.md` deployment-model section. This page describes the current (post-Zero) stack throughout. **How SSE sync works today.** The `:3070` Hono host serves `/api/zero-harness/sse`. `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-sse.ts` opens one dedicated PG `LISTEN` on the `sync_invalidate` channel (on the embedded-PG admin URL), fans each `pg_notify` out to subscribers, and bridges PG-trigger `<schema>.<table>.changed` events to the camelCase query names via `queryNamesForTriggerEvent` in `sync-resolver/table-to-query-names.ts`. **Freshness, restated.** It is not the old \~50ms logical-replication push. Each write fires an invalidate that pushes near-instantly to subscribers; the worst-case staleness for an **unbridged** table is the 180s drift-repair tick (`DEFAULT_SSE_DRIFT_REPAIR_MS` in `HarnessSyncProvider.tsx`), which is a repair sweep, **not** a freshness source. **Degraded fallback.** On sustained SSE failure, `SyncProvider`’s `useTransportFallback` drops SSE → `POLLING` as a last resort. POLLING is intentionally not the default: it re-fetches every subscribed query (\~40 on the dashboard) each interval, saturating the browser’s 6-connection-per-host HTTP/1.1 cap. Default to the data-sync library, not a fresh poll **For any new component that reads server state, default to `useSyncQuery({queryName, args})` from `@papercusp/sync`.** Don’t roll a new `fetch + setInterval` poll. Don’t open a raw `EventSource` for query data. The library is the single audited path: SSE/WS push, payload-on- invalidate, REST refetch fallback, observability shim (`window.__sync_metrics__`), reconnect resilience. Each parallel poll or ad-hoc EventSource forks all of that and accumulates as drift. **Genuine exceptions** (you may roll your own integration): * **Streaming-by-nature payloads** — log tails, terminal output, command-runner progress, LLM token streams. These are byte streams, not query data; raw `EventSource` is the right tool. See the existing uses in `OperatorPanel`, `BranchActionRunner`, `ProvisionStream`, `PiPanel` (pty). * **Pure UI timers** — `setNow(Date.now())` for relative-time refresh, `setInterval` for animation steps. No fetch, not data sync. * **Mobile (`apps/operator-mobile/`)** — uses its own pure-HTTP + EventSource path with `usePolledList` and `sync-stream.ts` for per-device JWT scoping and battery-aware visibility pause. New mobile consumers stay on that pattern. If you think you have another reason to bypass the library, **surface it as a question first** instead of forking quietly. Drift here costs real CPU, battery, and latency that the user only sees as “the app feels sluggish.” **The migration template** (3-line summary): 1. **Read** — add a resolver entry in `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts` (the v2 registry): `'queryName.variant': { argsSchema, resolve }` returning a flat row array. Prefer the structured DB projection if one exists (e.g. read `harness_plans.items` jsonb rather than re-parsing markdown). There is no ZQL path anymore — `libs/zero-harness` doesn’t exist. 2. **Write** — at the write site (the REST route / `defineTool` handler, or a watcher), fire `notifySyncInvalidate('queryName.variant', args)` from `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-sse.ts` after the write commits. For an optimistic write surface use `useSyncMutate('group.verb', restFallback)`; with no WebSocket/Zero client on the operator UI it always takes the REST fallback, and the invalidate above is what pushes the new state back to subscribers. 3. **Component** — `const { data } = useSyncQuery({queryName, args})`. Done. Full recipe in the [Cookbook](/internal/docs/data-sync/cookbook); the v2 registry’s per-entry recipe is in the [adding-a-sync-query](/internal/docs/agent-insights/adding-a-sync-query) insight. ## What this section covers [Section titled “What this section covers”](#what-this-section-covers) This is a reference for agents and humans building UI panels in the harness operator (`apps/operator/app/harness/`). Read this **before** you wire a new panel to data. The stack is two layered conventions, not a single library: 1. **The sync-resolver + SSE push** — Postgres is the source of truth. The v2 registry (`packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts`) resolves named queries; `sync-sse.ts` LISTENs on `sync_invalidate` and pushes invalidations to subscribers over Server-Sent Events. Clients call `useSyncQuery(...)` and refetch when the query’s name/args are invalidated — no manual polling loop to write. 2. **RichGrid** (`@papercusp/grid-core`, mirrored at `papercupai/papergrid`) — the column-driven grid renderer every tabular panel uses. It is a DOM / CSS-grid renderer that virtualizes via `@tanstack/virtual-core` (its sibling `DataGridShell` is the canvas glide-data-grid one). It accepts plain rows + a `ColumnDef[]`, handles sorting, row click, row styling, and (optionally) virtual rendering. It does **not** know about the sync layer — the panel passes `useSyncQuery`’s rows as the `rows` prop. These two are intentionally orthogonal: * A panel can use **sync without RichGrid** (e.g. card or feed UX). * A panel can use **RichGrid without sync** (e.g. data that comes from a one-shot REST call — `ProjectsList` at `apps/operator/app/harness/[slug]/projects/`). * The default for a new tabular panel that displays Postgres-backed data is **both**. ## Why this exists [Section titled “Why this exists”](#why-this-exists) Before this stack was in place, every panel had its own list-rendering code (a `<table>` or a `.map()` over `<div>`s), its own polling loop, its own optimistic-update logic, and its own bug about “stale data after a mutation.” Migrating to RichGrid + the sync library collapses all of that into: 
```tsx
const { data: rows } = useSyncQuery<SnapshotRow>({ queryName: 'snapshotsConsolidated.bySlug', args: { harnessSlug: slug } });
return <RichGrid rows={rows ?? []} columns={columns} getRowId={s => s.id} inline />;
```
 Mutations write directly to Postgres (via a normal `POST /api/...` route). Freshness is invalidate-driven: each write fires a `sync_invalidate` notify that pushes near-instantly to subscribers, and an unbridged table’s worst-case staleness is the 180s drift-repair tick (see the banner above), which is a repair sweep, not the normal freshness path. ## Where each piece lives [Section titled “Where each piece lives”](#where-each-piece-lives) | Concern | Package | Path | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | RichGrid component + `ColumnDef` types | `@papercusp/grid-core` | `libs/generic/papergrid/grid-core/src/RichGrid.tsx` | | Named-query registry (v2 resolver) | `packages/operator-core` | `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts` | | PG-trigger → query-name bridge | `packages/operator-core` | `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/table-to-query-names.ts` | | Sync hooks (`useSyncQuery`, …) | `@papercusp/sync` | `libs/generic/sync/src/SyncContext.ts` | | SSE wiring (LISTEN, invalidate bus) | `packages/operator-core` | `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-sse.ts` | | Sync provider for harness app | local | `apps/operator/providers/HarnessSyncProvider.tsx` | | Postgres database | server | `papercusp` DB on `:5432` | ## Reading order for new contributors [Section titled “Reading order for new contributors”](#reading-order-for-new-contributors) 1. [RichGrid](/internal/docs/data-sync/richgrid) — the renderer; learn this first because it’s the smaller, self-contained surface. 2. [Named queries](/internal/docs/data-sync/named-queries) — the v2 registry: how a row in Postgres becomes a row in your component, and how to add a new query to the shared catalog. 3. [Schema conventions](/internal/docs/data-sync/schema) — per-harness Postgres schemas, `harness_shared` cross-harness views. 4. [Pitfalls](/internal/docs/data-sync/pitfalls) — non-obvious issues that have silently broken every panel in a schema. Read this before debugging. 5. [Cookbook](/internal/docs/data-sync/cookbook) — copy-paste recipes for the most common panel-building tasks. ## Source-of-truth files [Section titled “Source-of-truth files”](#source-of-truth-files) When the docs and the code disagree, the code wins. The docs are kept in sync best-effort, but the canonical references are: * `libs/generic/papergrid/grid-core/src/RichGrid.tsx` — props, `ColumnDef` shape * `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts` — every query name and its `argsSchema`/`resolve` (`knownQueryNamesV2()` enumerates them) * `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/table-to-query-names.ts` — which Postgres table backs which query name, for the PG-trigger invalidation bridge * `apps/operator/app/adv/harnesses/useHarnessData.ts` — a live consumer reading the consolidated queries via `useSyncQuery` (`featuresConsolidated.bySlug`, `issuesConsolidated.bySlug`, `agentRunsConsolidated.bySlug`)

# Cookbook

> Copy-paste recipes for the most common panel-building tasks.

Zero is fully decommissioned, not merely retired — historical reference Zero / zero-cache / ZQL named-queries is **gone from the tree**, not just off the transport path — `zero-decommission-2026-06-20` removed `@rocicorp/zero` from every `package.json` and deleted the `@papercusp/zero-harness` package (`libs/zero-harness` no longer exists as a directory). The `@papercusp/zero-harness` imports in the recipes below are **illustrative of the old pattern only** and will not resolve if copy-pasted. The shipping app uses **SSE for every runtime** — desktop Tauri shell *and* plain browser — where the operator sidecar’s `:3070` host pushes invalidate/update over Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`; zero-cache is **not run** at all. `POLLING` exists only as a degraded last-resort fallback, and the WebSocket transport still lives in `@papercusp/sync` but Papercusp no longer selects it. Treat this whole page as historical reference for the shape of the old recipes — for the CURRENT recipe (sync-resolver v2 + SSE), see the [Data Sync overview](/internal/docs/data-sync) instead. Source of truth: `apps/operator/providers/HarnessSyncProvider.tsx` (transport-selection doc-comment, hardcoded `syncType="SSE"`) + the root `CLAUDE.md` deployment-model section. ## Recipe 1: New panel reading from an existing Zero table [Section titled “Recipe 1: New panel reading from an existing Zero table”](#recipe-1-new-panel-reading-from-an-existing-zero-table) The 80% case. You want to render an existing per-harness table as a new panel. 
```tsx
'use client';


import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { RichGrid, type ColumnDef } from '@papercusp/grid-core';
import type { SnapshotsConsolidatedRow } from '@papercusp/zero-harness';
import { useSyncQuery } from '@papercusp/sync';


interface Props {
  slug: string;
  onSelect?: (id: string) => void;
}


export default function MySnapshotsPanel({ slug, onSelect }: Props) {
  // `useSyncQuery<T>` types T as the ROW element; `.data` is `T[]`.
  // `args` is a named object, not a positional array. The `bySlug` query's
  // Zod arg schema is `{ harnessSlug: string }` — the key must be
  // `harnessSlug`, not `slug`, or the query receives no filter.
  const { data: rows } = useSyncQuery<SnapshotsConsolidatedRow>({
    queryName: 'snapshotsConsolidated.bySlug',
    args: { harnessSlug: slug },
  });


  const columns = useMemo<ColumnDef<SnapshotsConsolidatedRow>[]>(() => [
    {
      key: 'when', header: 'When', width: 1.3,
      sortKey: 'ts', defaultSortDir: 'desc',
      render: ({ row }) => new Date(Number(row.ts)).toLocaleString(),
    },
    {
      key: 'iter', header: 'Iter', width: 0.4, align: 'right',
      sortKey: 'iterNum',
      render: ({ row }) => row.iterNum,
    },
  ], []);


  return (
    <RichGrid<SnapshotsConsolidatedRow>
      rows={rows}
      columns={columns}
      getRowId={(r) => r.snapshotId}
      onRowClick={(r) => onSelect?.(r.snapshotId)}
      inline
    />
  );
}
```
 ## Recipe 2: Migrating an existing `.map()` list to RichGrid [Section titled “Recipe 2: Migrating an existing .map() list to RichGrid”](#recipe-2-migrating-an-existing-map-list-to-richgrid) Source pattern (anti-pattern in this codebase): 
```tsx
{items.map((item) => (
  <div key={item.id} className="row">
    <span>{item.id}</span>
    <span>{item.name}</span>
    <span>{item.status}</span>
  </div>
))}
```
 Migration: 
```tsx
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { RichGrid, type ColumnDef } from '@papercusp/grid-core';


const columns = useMemo<ColumnDef<Item>[]>(() => [
  { key: 'id', header: 'ID', width: 1, sortKey: 'id',
    render: ({ row }) => row.id },
  { key: 'name', header: 'Name', width: 3, sortKey: 'name',
    render: ({ row }) => row.name },
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status', width: 1, sortKey: 'status',
    render: ({ row }) => row.status },
], []);


return (
  <RichGrid<Item>
    rows={items}
    columns={columns}
    getRowId={(i) => i.id}
    inline
  />
);
```
 Steps in order: 1. Add `import { RichGrid, type ColumnDef } from '@papercusp/grid-core'`. 2. Build a `columns` array, one entry per visible field. Wrap in `useMemo`. 3. Replace the `.map()` block with `<RichGrid …>`. 4. Move per-row click handler from each row to `onRowClick`. 5. Drop the manual loading + error CSS (RichGrid renders its own header even when rows is empty; provide a sibling empty-state component if you need a friendlier message). ## Recipe 3: Adding a new column to an existing Zero-synced table [Section titled “Recipe 3: Adding a new column to an existing Zero-synced table”](#recipe-3-adding-a-new-column-to-an-existing-zero-synced-table) Per-harness tables are being retired The per-harness-table model below predates the consolidation migrations. The canonical stores are now the `harness_shared.*_consolidated` tables — writers should target those directly (see the `COMMENT ON harness_features_consolidated` in `000-baseline.sql`), and Zero exposes only the `*Consolidated.bySlug` / `*Consolidated.all` queries (the per-harness named queries — `featuresSheets`, `issuesOrg`, … — were removed; see the comment in `libs/zero-harness/src/queries.ts`). Add columns to the consolidated table (Recipe 5) rather than to per-harness tables. The per-harness table names are **not** uniformly `harness_<table>` — several (e.g. `feature_audit`, `agent_runs`) carry no `harness_` prefix. The published per-harness tables are `harness_features`, `feature_audit`, `harness_issues`, `harness_proposals`, `agent_runs`, `harness_snapshots` (plus `messages`, `supervisor_notes`); see the publication list in `bin/scaffold-harness-schema.sh` and `libs/zero-harness/src/schema.ts`. 
```sql
ALTER TABLE harness_<slug>.harness_snapshots
  ADD COLUMN new_col text;
```
 For each existing harness, repeat. Then: 1. Update the per-harness template SQL (the file `bin/scaffold-harness-schema.sh` `sed`-substitutes `{{SCHEMA}}` into and runs) so future harnesses get it — the column DDL lives in the template, not in the shell script itself. 2. Update `libs/zero-harness/src/schema.ts` — add `new_col: string()` (or the right type — beware TIMESTAMPTZ). 3. The publication already includes the table; the new column flows automatically. 4. Restart `zero-cache-harness`. 5. Update consumers (`useSyncQuery` results now include `new_col`). ## Recipe 4: Adding a new table to all harnesses [Section titled “Recipe 4: Adding a new table to all harnesses”](#recipe-4-adding-a-new-table-to-all-harnesses) Bigger lift. Steps: 1. Add the `CREATE TABLE` DDL to the **per-harness template SQL** (the file `bin/scaffold-harness-schema.sh` renders via `sed "s/{{SCHEMA}}/$schema/g"`), and add the table to the publication list in the scaffold script’s `add_to_zero_publication` array. The script itself contains no DDL — it only substitutes the schema name into the template and runs it. 2. Run scaffold against every existing harness: 
   ```bash
   for slug in $(psql -tAc "SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'harness\_%'" | sed 's/^harness_//'); do
     bin/scaffold-harness-schema.sh "$slug"
   done
   ```
 3. Add the table to `libs/zero-harness/src/schema.ts` (register it in the `createSchema({ tables: [...] })` list). 4. Add a query factory to `queries.ts`. 5. Add a `slugToXxxKey` helper to `queries.ts`. 6. Restart `zero-cache-harness`. ## Recipe 5: Cross-harness consolidated table [Section titled “Recipe 5: Cross-harness consolidated table”](#recipe-5-cross-harness-consolidated-table) When you need to render data across all harnesses (e.g. global feature list). 1. Create a new base table in `harness_shared`: 
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE harness_shared.harness_<name>_consolidated (
     harness_slug text,
     <column>     <type>,
     -- …
     PRIMARY KEY (harness_slug, <pk>)
   );
   ```
 2. For each per-harness source table, add an `AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` trigger that maintains the consolidated table. 3. Add the consolidated table to the `zero_harness` publication. 4. Register a no-arg named query: 
   ```ts
   <name>Consolidated: () => z.query.<name>Consolidated,
   ```
 5. Register the table in `schema.ts` and restart zero-cache. `harness_features_consolidated` is the working example to copy. ## Recipe 6: Mutations that update Zero panels [Section titled “Recipe 6: Mutations that update Zero panels”](#recipe-6-mutations-that-update-zero-panels) You want a button that inserts a row and have every connected client see it appear. 
```tsx
async function addNote() {
  const res = await fetch('/api/harness/<slug>/notes', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ text: 'hello' }),
    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    toast.error('add note failed');
    return;
  }
  // No reload, no refetch. Zero will broadcast the new row in <100ms.
}
```
 The API route writes to PG. Zero broadcasts. `useSyncQuery` re-renders. Done. If you want optimistic UI before the round-trip, hold the new row in component state and clear it when the Zero query result reflects the real one. Don’t try to write through Zero — that’s not how this stack works. ## Recipe 7: Per-row action buttons [Section titled “Recipe 7: Per-row action buttons”](#recipe-7-per-row-action-buttons) Buttons inside a column cell that need to **not** trigger the row’s `onRowClick`: 
```tsx
{
  key: 'action',
  header: '',
  width: 0.6,
  align: 'right',
  render: ({ row }) => (
    <button
      onClick={(e) => {
        e.stopPropagation();
        handleDelete(row.id);
      }}
    >
      delete
    </button>
  ),
}
```
 The `e.stopPropagation()` is required. ## Recipe 8: Selected-row highlight [Section titled “Recipe 8: Selected-row highlight”](#recipe-8-selected-row-highlight) `getRowBg` is called with `(row, rowIndex, isSelected)` — RichGrid already tracks whether a row is selected (from its own internal state, or from the controlled `selectedRowIds`/`onSelectedRowIdsChange` pair if you pass them): 
```tsx
const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>(null);


const getRowBg = (row: Row, _rowIndex: number, isSelected: boolean) =>
  row.id === selectedId ? '#1f2937' : undefined;


<RichGrid
  rows={rows}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(r) => r.id}
  onRowClick={(r) => setSelectedId(r.id)}
  getRowBg={getRowBg}
  inline
/>
```
 Return `undefined` (not `'transparent'`) to fall back to RichGrid’s own default striping/hover background rather than overriding it outright. For a checkbox-style multi-select rather than a single active row, skip the manual `selectedId` state entirely: pass `selectable` (or a controlled `selectedRowIds`/`onSelectedRowIdsChange` pair) and read the built-in `isSelected` argument in `getRowBg` instead of comparing ids yourself. `apps/operator/app/adv/harnesses/WorkItemsPanel.tsx` is a current live example of RichGrid with this exact `getRowBg` selected-row pattern; the retired `SnapshotsPanel.tsx` (see Reference panels below) shows the older, pre-dock version of the same idea. ## Recipe 9: PG-mirrored filesystem store [Section titled “Recipe 9: PG-mirrored filesystem store”](#recipe-9-pg-mirrored-filesystem-store) Use this when a filesystem JSON file must remain authoritative — e.g. an external CLI writes it, or a runtime loader reads it by path — but you also want cross-harness queries and Zero subscriptions over the same data. The pattern in three parts: **1. The PG table** is a derived index of the JSON. Same schema, plus `updated_at`. Add to the `zero_harness` publication. 
```sql
CREATE TABLE harness_shared.plugin_enables (
  harness_slug   text NOT NULL,
  plugin_slug    text NOT NULL,
  version        text NOT NULL,
  config_hash    text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  enabled_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (harness_slug, plugin_slug)
);
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON harness_shared.plugin_enables TO harness_app;
GRANT SELECT ON harness_shared.plugin_enables TO harness_zero;
ALTER PUBLICATION zero_harness ADD TABLE harness_shared.plugin_enables;
```
 **2. A mirror helper.** Reads the JSON for one harness/scope, upserts matching rows, deletes orphans. This is the function every writer calls. packages/operator-core/lib/plugin-enables-pg.ts 
```ts
import { getOrgPg } from '@papercusp/db-org';


export async function mirrorHarness(harness: string): Promise<void> {
  const file = await readEnabled(harness);                  // read JSON
  const enabled = file?.enabled ?? {};
  const { sql } = getOrgPg();
  for (const [pluginSlug, meta] of Object.entries(enabled)) {
    await sql`
      INSERT INTO harness_shared.plugin_enables
        (harness_slug, plugin_slug, version, config_hash, enabled_at, updated_at)
      VALUES (${harness}, ${pluginSlug}, ${meta.version}, ${meta.configHash},
              ${meta.enabledAt}, now())
      ON CONFLICT (harness_slug, plugin_slug) DO UPDATE
        SET version = EXCLUDED.version,
            config_hash = EXCLUDED.config_hash,
            updated_at = now()
    `;
  }
  // Delete rows for plugins removed from the JSON
  const slugs = Object.keys(enabled);
  if (slugs.length === 0) {
    await sql`DELETE FROM harness_shared.plugin_enables WHERE harness_slug = ${harness}`;
  } else {
    await sql`
      DELETE FROM harness_shared.plugin_enables
      WHERE harness_slug = ${harness} AND plugin_slug NOT IN ${sql(slugs)}
    `;
  }
}
```
 **3. Hook every writer.** After each successful JSON write — direct or via subprocess — call the mirror. Best-effort: a mirror failure logs but does not fail the API call. 
```ts
// in the API route that calls the CLI
const r = await spawn(PAPERCUSP_BIN, ['plugin', 'enable', slug, '--harness', h]);
if (r.code === 0) {
  try { await mirrorHarness(h); } catch (e) {
    console.warn('[plugins/enable] PG mirror failed for', h, e);
  }
}
```
 **4. Backfill + drift recovery.** Provide a script that reads ALL JSONs and re-syncs PG. It runs on a fresh checkout, after a direct CLI run that bypassed the operator API, or whenever you suspect drift. scripts/backfill-plugin-enables.mjs 
```js
// Same logic as mirrorHarness, run for every harness directory.
// Idempotent: re-running on already-synced data is a no-op.
```
 ### When to pick this pattern over PG-canonical [Section titled “When to pick this pattern over PG-canonical”](#when-to-pick-this-pattern-over-pg-canonical) | Pick PG-canonical (Recipe 1-2) when | Pick PG-mirror (this) when | | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | You own every writer | A third-party process or runtime path writes the JSON and you can’t change it | | The data has no on-disk consumer | A loader reads the JSON file at runtime by path | | Atomicity of write matters | The JSON is the operational source of truth and PG is a query-side index | Reference implementations: * `packages/operator-core/lib/plugin-enables-pg.ts` (papercusp CLI is the writer) * `packages/operator-core/lib/plugin-configs-pg.ts` (substrate plugin loader reads JSON at runtime) ## Recipe 10: Where to put a new panel [Section titled “Recipe 10: Where to put a new panel”](#recipe-10-where-to-put-a-new-panel) | Panel scope | Location | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Tabular data for one harness, shown in the harness dashboard | `apps/operator/app/harness/<Name>Panel.tsx` | | Dock panel in the per-harness workbench | A `Real<Name>Panel.tsx` under `apps/operator/app/harness/dock/`, registered with `panelRegistry.register('data:<name>', Real<Name>Panel)` in `dock/sample-panels.tsx` (see `RealFeaturesPanel.tsx` / `RealIssuesPanel.tsx` for the shape) | | Cross-harness panel (global view) | `apps/operator/app/<route>/<Name>Panel.tsx` | The live `apps/operator` harness UI is dock-based (`apps/operator/app/harness/[slug]/HarnessDockShell.tsx`); wire a new panel in as a dock panel rather than into a monolithic tab switcher. There is no single `DepartmentHarnessDashboard.tsx` anymore — that file moved to the **retired** `libs/papercusp/_retired/apps-web/app/harness/` tree when the dock rewrite shipped (the `MemoryEntriesGrid` component it once hosted is gone entirely, not just moved); treat it as historical reference only, not a live extension point. ## Reference panels [Section titled “Reference panels”](#reference-panels) When in doubt, copy the structure from one of these live RichGrid consumers: * `apps/operator/app/adv/harnesses/WorkItemsPanel.tsx` — sortable/filterable RichGrid with `getRowBg` selected-row highlighting and resizable columns. * `apps/operator/app/harness/[slug]/projects/ProjectsList.tsx` — RichGrid with `onRowClick` navigation, a small, focused table. The following now live in the **retired** `@papercusp/web` surface (`libs/papercusp/_retired/apps-web/app/harness/`) but still show the canonical RichGrid + sync wiring from before the dock rewrite: * `…/web/app/harness/SnapshotsPanel.tsx` — small, single per-harness table, sortable + per-row delete. * `…/web/app/harness/issues/IssuesList.tsx` — RichGrid, multi-state row, with `rowProps` legacy-class workaround. * `…/web/app/harness/ProposalsPanel.tsx` — inline mutation actions.

# Named queries

> The shared catalog of queries every panel reads from.

Zero is fully decommissioned — this page is historical reference only The Zero / zero-cache / ZQL named-queries / WebSocket-push stack described below is **gone, not just retiring**: `zero-decommission-2026-06-20` (Z-2) removed `@rocicorp/zero` from every `package.json`, deleted the `@papercusp/zero-harness` package (`libs/zero-harness` — the directory itself no longer exists in the tree), and stripped the Zero-specific WS transport out of `@papercusp/sync`. Zero-repo-wide `@rocicorp/zero` deps: **0**. The shipping desktop app uses **SSE-primary** sync (the `:3070` Hono host pushes invalidate/update over Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY` through the v2 sync-resolver registry described below); zero-cache is not run anywhere. Source of truth: `apps/operator/providers/HarnessSyncProvider.tsx` (transport-selection doc-comment), the root `CLAUDE.md` deployment-model section, and [Adding a query to the Zero-free sync resolver](/internal/docs/agent-insights/adding-a-sync-query) for the current, authoritative recipe. The “Query does not implement QueryInternals” section further down describes an error that **cannot recur** — it is kept only so an agent that finds an old comment/plan mentioning it isn’t left guessing what it meant. ## Why named queries [Section titled “Why named queries”](#why-named-queries) Every panel read the harness UI does goes through one **named query** — `useSyncQuery({ queryName, args })` — resolved against a single registry, so “what does the harness sync from Postgres?” always has one answer: open the registry. That principle survived the Zero decommission unchanged; only the registry’s *shape* changed. Today the registry is `REGISTRY` in `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts` (the “v2” resolver) — a flat `Record<string, QueryEntry>` (152 entries as of 2026-07-04) keyed by a **dotted string name** (`'featuresConsolidated.bySlug'`, `'snapshotsConsolidated.bySlug'`, `'storage.usage'`, …), each entry pairing a Zod `argsSchema` with an async `resolve(args)` that runs a normal drizzle/PG query and returns a flat row array. There is no `defineQueries` namespace object, no ZQL, and no separate `schema.ts`/publication step — a dotted name is just a registry key, and adding one is a \~15 LOC addition to that one file. **Full recipe, key points, and gotchas:** [Adding a query to the Zero-free sync resolver](/internal/docs/agent-insights/adding-a-sync-query) — this page won’t duplicate it. ## The current catalog [Section titled “The current catalog”](#the-current-catalog) `knownQueryNamesV2()` (same file) enumerates every registered name — that’s the canonical list; don’t trust an inline copy here to stay in sync with it. The four core per-harness entities are still slug-agnostic consolidated tables in `harness_shared`, each read by a `.bySlug` query keyed on `harnessSlug` (a column, not a schema name): | Query | Returns | Args | | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ----------------- | | `featuresConsolidated.bySlug` | `FeatureRow[]` | `{ harnessSlug }` | | `issuesConsolidated.bySlug` | `IssueRow[]` | `{ harnessSlug }` | | `agentRunsConsolidated.bySlug` (or `agentRunsConsolidated.recent`) | `AgentRunRow[]` | `{ harnessSlug }` | | `snapshotsConsolidated.bySlug` | `SnapshotRow[]` | `{ harnessSlug }` | | `harnessProjects.lite` | `ProjectRow[]` | (none) | | `harnessWorkspaces.byHarness` | `WorkspaceRow[]` | `{ harnessSlug }` | `featuresConsolidated` also carries `featuresConsolidated.byHive` (cross-member browse, WI-259 P-006/D-010) and `featuresConsolidated.byPlanSlug`. The doc text claiming a `needsReview` variant, a `bySourcePlan` form, or an `all` form is drift — those queries do not exist in the registry. Adding a new harness still doesn’t add a query — the slug is a regular row value, not a schema name. ## Adding a new named query [Section titled “Adding a new named query”](#adding-a-new-named-query) See the full recipe (schema check, registry entry shape, the P-067 PG-trigger bridge, the test-count-assertion gotcha, verification) at [Adding a query to the Zero-free sync resolver](/internal/docs/agent-insights/adding-a-sync-query). In short, an entry in `REGISTRY` looks like: packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts 
```ts
'myNewThing.bySlug': {
  argsSchema: z.object({ harnessSlug: z.string() }),
  resolve: async (args) => {
    const { harnessSlug } = args as { harnessSlug: string };
    const { getOrgPg, generated } = await import('@papercusp/db-org');
    const { eq } = await import('drizzle-orm');
    const { db } = getOrgPg();
    return (await db.select().from(generated.myNewThing)
      .where(eq(generated.myNewThing.harnessSlug, harnessSlug))) as unknown[];
  },
},
```
 Then in your panel, read it through the `@papercusp/sync` wrapper. The `useSyncQuery` hook is exported from `@papercusp/sync` (the package lives at `libs/generic/sync`) and is transport-agnostic — it resolves `queryName` + `args` through whichever adapter is active: 
```tsx
const { data: rows } = useSyncQuery<MyNewThingRow>({
  queryName: 'myNewThing.bySlug',
  args: { harnessSlug: slug },
});
```
 The same generic (`libs/generic/sync`) package also exports the companion write hook `useSyncMutate(path, restFallback)` and `useSyncPrefetch()`. On the operator harness UI (SSE transport, no WebSocket client) `useSyncMutate` always takes the `restFallback` — it exists so a call site can adopt the same API a `WEBSOCKETS`-transport consumer of the generic package would use (elsewhere in the monorepo) without a behavior difference on SSE/polling. `useSyncPrefetch()` warms the cache so a later `useSyncQuery` for the same `queryName` + `args` resolves instantly. You also need the PG-trigger bridge entry so writes that bypass app code (raw SQL, MCP-tool writes, migrations) still invalidate the query: add `'harness_shared.your_table': ['myNewThing.bySlug']` to `TABLE_TO_QUERY_NAMES` in `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/table-to-query-names.ts` — see [Adding a query to the Zero-free sync resolver](/internal/docs/agent-insights/adding-a-sync-query) Step 3. Skip it and the query still works for app-code writes (which call `notifySyncInvalidate` directly) but silently misses out-of-band ones. ## ”Query does not implement QueryInternals” (Zero-era, historical) [Section titled “”Query does not implement QueryInternals” (Zero-era, historical)”](#query-does-not-implement-queryinternals-zero-era-historical) This error meant the panel’s `@rocicorp/zero` package and the one Zero instantiated against were different copies, thrown from every `useQuery` call. It cannot recur — `@rocicorp/zero` has zero `package.json` references left anywhere in the repo (`zero-decommission-2026-06-20` Z-2) — but it’s left here in case an old comment, plan, or search result references it and an agent needs to know it’s inert history, not a live failure mode to reproduce or guard against. ## Cross-harness queries (consolidated tables) [Section titled “Cross-harness queries (consolidated tables)”](#cross-harness-queries-consolidated-tables) `harness_features_consolidated` is the **canonical** base table in `harness_shared` — writers target it directly. The data-flow direction was inverted across two migrations: * **Migration 029** made the consolidated table the source of truth. It had started life as a trigger-mirrored copy of the per-harness `harness_features` tables (writers pumped into per-harness, a trigger fanned out into consolidated), but 029 flipped that so writes go straight to the consolidated table. * **Migration 032** dropped the per-harness physical tables entirely and replaced each with an auto-updatable `VIEW` over the consolidated table, filtered by `harness_slug` (`WITH CHECK OPTION` so a write can’t land under the wrong slug). The fan-in trigger functions (`sync_features_consolidated()`, `sync_issues_consolidated()`, `sync_agent_runs_consolidated()`, `sync_snapshots_consolidated()`) were dropped at the same time. The same inversion applies to the other three consolidated entities (`harness_issues` / `agent_runs` / `harness_snapshots`). So a per-harness read still works (it goes through the view), but the canonical store everything resolves against is the single consolidated base table. Why a base table and not a Postgres view at the top? The PG trigger that drives invalidation (`emit_change_notify`, the bridge behind `TABLE_TO_QUERY_NAMES`) fires on the underlying relation’s row-level INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; an auto-updatable view’s writes execute against that same underlying relation, so a trigger on the base table still sees them — but a view is not itself a relation a trigger can attach row-level logic to directly. Historically this table-not-view split was **also** required because Zero’s logical-replication publications couldn’t include views; that constraint is gone along with Zero, but the trigger-attachment reason still holds on its own, so the architecture is unchanged. The cross-harness `/features` page reads from the consolidated table via the `featuresConsolidated.byHive` named query. Earlier versions of this page claimed an all-features query existed; that was drift. If you need another cross-harness aggregation, the recipe is: 1. Add a canonical base table in `harness_shared` and have writers target it directly (optionally expose per-harness views over it, filtered by `harness_slug`, rather than fanning in via triggers). 2. Register the table in `TABLE_TO_QUERY_NAMES` (`table-to-query-names.ts`) so out-of-band writes still invalidate. 3. Register a named query with no slug arg (an `.all`-style query) in the v2 registry.

# Pitfalls

> Specific failure modes that have silently broken every panel in a schema. Read before debugging.

These are catalogued because each one cost real time. If a panel is behaving wrong, work down this list before you start changing code. ## 1. `render: (row) =>` instead of `render: ({ row }) =>` [Section titled “1. render: (row) => instead of render: ({ row }) =>”](#1-render-row--instead-of-render--row--) **Symptom**: every cell in the column renders blank or shows `[object Object]`. **Why**: `ColumnDef.render` is called with a context object `{ row, rowIndex, rowBg, isSelected }`, not the row itself. TypeScript accepts both signatures because the context structurally satisfies many row shapes. (Same gotcha applies to `rowProps` and `cellStyle`, which also receive this ctx.) **Fix**: destructure `{ row }` from the argument. 
```ts
render: ({ row }) => row.name,   // ✓
render: (row) => row.name,       // ✗ row is the ctx; row.name is undefined
```
 ## 2. PG `TIMESTAMPTZ` declared as `string()` in Zero schema [Section titled “2. PG TIMESTAMPTZ declared as string() in Zero schema”](#2-pg-timestamptz-declared-as-string-in-zero-schema) **Symptom**: `SchemaVersionNotSupported` in `zero-cache` logs. WebSocket dies. **Every panel using that schema goes blank.** Reload doesn’t help. **Why**: Zero deserializes `TIMESTAMPTZ` as epoch-ms `number`. If the schema declares it as `string()`, validation fails for every row and the cache disconnects. **Fix**: declare as `number()`. 
```ts
ts: number(),   // ✓
ts: string(),   // ✗ — kills the WS for the whole schema
```
 This has bitten us at least three times. **Always check the column type before declaring a TIMESTAMPTZ field.** > **Era note.** The type rule still holds today, but it’s now enforced by the schema **generator**, not a hand-edited file: `libs/zero-harness/src/schema.ts` is auto-generated and maps `timestamp → number` in `libs/zero-harness/scripts/generate-schema.mjs`. The fix is to correct the Drizzle source type and regenerate — don’t hand-edit `schema.ts`. The `SchemaVersionNotSupported` / WS-disconnect symptom above is zero-cache–era; with SSE-primary sync a type mismatch now surfaces through the SSE/REST path, not a WebSocket drop. ## 3. Two copies of `@rocicorp/zero` in the dep tree [Section titled “3. Two copies of @rocicorp/zero in the dep tree”](#3-two-copies-of-rocicorpzero-in-the-dep-tree) **Symptom**: `Query does not implement QueryInternals` thrown from every `useQuery` call. **Why**: a sub-app declared `@rocicorp/zero` directly in its `package.json` and npm hoisted it into `apps/<name>/node_modules`. The panel’s import resolves to the local copy; Zero’s runtime resolves to the workspace root copy. Two distinct module instances → instanceof fails → `QueryInternals` mismatch. **Fix**: symlink the inner copy to the workspace root. 
```bash
cd apps/<name>
rm -rf node_modules/@rocicorp/zero
ln -s ../../../node_modules/@rocicorp/zero node_modules/@rocicorp/zero
```
 Then preferably remove the direct dep from the sub-app’s `package.json` so the next `npm install` doesn’t reintroduce it. ## 4. Legacy class with `display: grid` in `rowProps` [Section titled “4. Legacy class with display: grid in rowProps”](#4-legacy-class-with-display-grid-in-rowprops) **Symptom**: cells render on top of each other; the whole grid looks collapsed. **Why**: `RichGrid` uses CSS Grid for its cell layout. If `rowProps` returns a `className` that has its own `display: grid`, the two grids fight. **Fix**: override with inline `style: { display: 'block' }`. (`rowProps` receives the cell-render ctx — destructure `{ row }` if you need it.) 
```tsx
rowProps={({ row }) => ({
  className: 'h-issue',
  style: { display: 'block' },
})}
```
 ## 5. Schema change not reflected on clients [Section titled “5. Schema change not reflected on clients”](#5-schema-change-not-reflected-on-clients) **Symptom**: you changed `schema.ts` (added a column, renamed one, changed a type), restarted `zero-cache`, and clients still see the old shape — or worse, throw `SchemaVersionNotSupported`. **Why**: clients cache the schema and the cache wasn’t invalidated. > **Historical.** Older `@rocicorp/zero` carried an explicit `schemaVersion` constant you bumped on every change. The current schema (`libs/zero-harness/src/schema.ts` → `createSchema({ tables: [...] })`) has **no** `schemaVersion` field — that knob is gone. A change there is registered by adding/editing the table in the `tables` list and restarting zero-cache; if a stale shape persists, clear the client’s cached schema. ## 6. Forgot to add the table to the Postgres publication [Section titled “6. Forgot to add the table to the Postgres publication”](#6-forgot-to-add-the-table-to-the-postgres-publication) **Symptom**: the named query returns `[]` always, even though `SELECT * FROM harness_<slug>.harness_<table>` shows rows. **Why**: the table isn’t in the `zero_harness` publication, so logical replication isn’t broadcasting it. **Fix**: 
```sql
ALTER PUBLICATION zero_harness ADD TABLE harness_<slug>.harness_<table>;
```
 …then restart `zero-cache-harness` so it re-reads the publication membership. ## 7. zero-cache port collisions [Section titled “7. zero-cache port collisions”](#7-zero-cache-port-collisions) **Symptom**: zero-cache logs “address already in use” on `:4849` or `:4850`. **Why**: the shop zero-cache (different DB, different config) defaults its change-streamer port to `ZERO_PORT + 1 = 4849`, which collides with the harness zero-cache main port. **Fix**: set `ZERO_CHANGE_STREAMER_PORT=4847` on the shop zero-cache unit. The current allocation is: | Port | Service | | ---- | ------------------------------- | | 4849 | harness zero-cache main | | 4850 | harness change-streamer | | 4847 | shop change-streamer (override) | ## 8. Sync hook outside the provider [Section titled “8. Sync hook outside the provider”](#8-sync-hook-outside-the-provider) **Symptom**: a panel using `useSyncQuery` shows no data and never loads — `data` is `undefined`, `loading` is `false`. Or, if you used `useSyncPrefetch` / `useSyncContext` instead, a thrown `useSyncQuery must be used within a <SyncProvider>`. **Why**: the component is mounted above the `SyncProvider` wrapper. `useSyncQuery` is **tolerant** — outside a provider it returns `{ data: undefined, loading: false, error: null }` instead of throwing (so chrome rendered at the root layout doesn’t crash). The throwing variants are `useSyncContext` and `useSyncPrefetch`. **Fix**: ensure your panel is mounted inside the provider tree. In the operator the provider is `RootSyncProvider` (which wraps `HarnessSyncProvider`), mounted near the root layout, so most components are already inside it — see `apps/operator/app/_components/RootSyncProvider.tsx`. In operator-vite it’s mounted in `apps/operator-vite/src/routes/__root.tsx` as the **outermost** data-layer provider — only the Radix `Tooltip.Provider` sits above it, so ChromeShell, the sidebars, the dev rails, etc. are all inside. That makes “above the provider” a rarely-hit safety net rather than a routine case: confirm your panel is genuinely above it before assuming the empty-result path. If a panel renders above it, hoist the provider or branch on the empty result and supply your own fallback (REST poll, prefetch cache). **Sibling gotcha**: `useSyncMutate` is provider-tolerant the same way. Outside a provider there’s no Zero client, so **every call silently takes the REST fallback** — it never goes optimistic. A write that appears to “work” may never be routed through Zero at all if the provider (or WS) is absent. ## 9. JSON ledger out of sync with PG [Section titled “9. JSON ledger out of sync with PG”](#9-json-ledger-out-of-sync-with-pg) > **Historical.** The `apps/papercup` `projects` JSON-ledger and its file-writing accessor pair have been **removed**: `saveProjects()` no longer exists anywhere in non-retired source, and the projects surface it backed was retired. (A function literally named `loadProjects` still lives in `scripts/migrate-snapshots-to-pg.ts` — but it reads the harness registry `~/.restart-harness-projects.json`, a different artifact, not the retired ledger.) Kept as a cautionary pattern. **Symptom**: a PG-backed accessor returns rows that don’t match what the UI shows (or vice versa). **Why**: a “PG mirror” pattern where a JSON file is primary and PG is best-effort — both were sources of truth and some code paths wrote to one and not the other; the file always drifts ahead. **Fix**: PG is canonical. Do not adopt the file-primary / PG-mirror pattern for app-level state — go full PG (the storage-policy rule). If you must keep a file authoritative for a real reason, drive every writer through one mirror helper plus a backfill/drift-recovery script (see the cookbook’s *PG-mirrored filesystem store* recipe). ## 10. dev:web vs dev:operator confusion [Section titled “10. dev:web vs dev:operator confusion”](#10-devweb-vs-devoperator-confusion) > **Retired (2026-05-30).** `apps/web` (the `@papercup/web` public site) was moved to `_retired/papercup/` and dropped from the workspace; the `dev:web` script no longer exists. Kept for reference. The operator (`:3055`) is the **Vite** SPA — see the **Fix** note. **Symptom**: edits to `apps/web/...` don’t take effect after restart. **Why**: `dev:web` serves `apps/web/.next/standalone/server.js`, **not** a dev server. To see source changes you need `npm run build` (full rebuild — never `npx next build`, which skips the static-asset copy). **Fix**: rebuild apps/web. The operator (`:3055`) uses the **Vite** dev server (`@papercusp/operator-vite`) and picks up source changes via HMR; only the legacy `apps/web` Next standalone is the static-build outlier. ## 11. Replication slot stuck after DB rename [Section titled “11. Replication slot stuck after DB rename”](#11-replication-slot-stuck-after-db-rename) **Symptom**: `zero-cache-harness` won’t start; logs show “replication slot in use.” **Fix**: 
```sql
SELECT pid, application_name FROM pg_stat_replication
  WHERE slot_name = 'zero_harness';
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(<pid>);
```
 If `postgres_app` is the holder, restart it. ## 12. A fetch cap papering over a non-virtualized grid (and a lying count) [Section titled “12. A fetch cap papering over a non-virtualized grid (and a lying count)”](#12-a-fetch-cap-papering-over-a-non-virtualized-grid-and-a-lying-count) **Symptom**: a panel “only shows N rows” when more exist (e.g. the work-items table capped at 300 of 404); a state/search filter mysteriously misses matches; the header count reads like a total but is really the downloaded length. **Why**: two coupled mistakes. (a) `<RichGrid rows={array}>` (legacy mode) mounts **every** row as DOM, so a large set janks — and the usual “fix” is to cap the fetch (`limit: 300`). On a local desktop app the data is already local, so the cap is pure downside, and any client-side filter/search then runs over only the truncated window. (b) The resolver returns a **bare array**, so the panel shows `items.length` (the capped length) as the count. **Fix**: virtualize instead of capping, and carry the true total. * Render with [`VirtualGrid`](/internal/docs/data-sync/richgrid#virtualgrid-the-drop-in-for-large-grids) (owns the virtualizer + scroll element), then lift the cap and load the full local set. * Carry the true total on `rows[0]._meta` via [`attachListMeta` / `readListTotal` / `listCountLabel`](/internal/docs/data-sync/richgrid#honest-counts-the-true-total-via-_meta) so the header shows `"N of TOTAL"`, never the downloaded length. Reference: `WorkItemsPanel.tsx` + the `workItems.byHarness` resolver.

# RichGrid

> Column-driven grid renderer; the preferred tabular UI primitive in the harness.

Zero is being retired — historical reference Zero / zero-cache / ZQL named-queries / WebSocket push is **on the retirement path**. The shipping desktop app uses **SSE-primary** sync (the `:3070` Hono host pushes invalidate/update over Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`); zero-cache is **not run** on desktop. Treat this page as historical reference. Source of truth: `apps/operator/providers/HarnessSyncProvider.tsx` (transport-selection doc-comment) + the root `CLAUDE.md` deployment-model section. ## When to reach for RichGrid [Section titled “When to reach for RichGrid”](#when-to-reach-for-richgrid) Use RichGrid for any panel that renders a list of rows where each row has the same columnar structure. It replaces every `<table>` and every hand-rolled `.map() => <div className="row">` in the codebase. RichGrid is the **preferred / default** tabular primitive — it’s the only grid-core grid with operator-app consumers. `grid-core` also exports `DataGridShell` (a canvas / glide-data-grid renderer for very large or edit-heavy grids) and `GridTable` / `GridSubTable` (declarative HTML tables) as sibling primitives, but neither is used in the harness. Reach for RichGrid unless you specifically need canvas-scale throughput. Do **not** use RichGrid for: * Card-grid feeds where each card shows a different shape (`ArchitectInbox`). * Kanban / column-board layouts (`BoardView`). * Master-detail explorers where the “list” is actually a sidebar to an embedded editor (`MemoryBrowser`, `IdentityPanel`, `PromptsTab`, `CollectionTab`). * Image galleries (`ScreenshotsPanel`). * Timeline / chronological streams (`PulseFeed`, `FeatureTimelinePanel`). If you find yourself adding a “second row of metadata under each grid row” you’re probably building one of the above and should use a card layout instead. ## Minimal usage [Section titled “Minimal usage”](#minimal-usage) 
```tsx
import { RichGrid, type ColumnDef } from '@papercusp/grid-core';


interface Snapshot {
  id: string;
  ts: number;
  iterNum: number;
}


const columns: ColumnDef<Snapshot>[] = [
  { key: 'when', header: 'When', width: 1.3, sortKey: 'ts',
    render: ({ row }) => fmtTs(row.ts) },
  { key: 'iter', header: 'Iter', width: 0.4, align: 'right',
    sortKey: 'iterNum',
    render: ({ row }) => row.iterNum },
];


<RichGrid<Snapshot>
  rows={snapshots}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(s) => s.id}
  onRowClick={(s) => setSelected(s)}
  inline
/>
```
 That’s the entire surface for \~80% of panels. ## Column definition [Section titled “Column definition”](#column-definition) 
```ts
interface ColumnDef<Row> {
  key: string;             // unique within the column array
  header: ReactNode;       // string or arbitrary JSX
  headerText?: string;     // plain-text header for the print mirror + copy payload
  width: number | string;  // number → fr track (1 = 1fr); string → fixed/minmax track
  align?: 'left' | 'center' | 'right';
  sortKey?: string;        // upstream sort field name; emitted via onSortChange
  defaultSortDir?: 'asc' | 'desc';
  filter?: ColumnFilterSpec<Row>;  // opts the column into per-column filtering — see "Filtering"
  render: (ctx: CellRenderContext<Row>) => ReactNode;
  toCopyText?: (row: Row) => string;  // plain-text cell value for print/copy
  cellStyle?: CSSProperties | ((ctx: CellRenderContext<Row>) => CSSProperties);
  headerClassName?: string;
}


// ctx passed to render / cellStyle / rowProps:
interface CellRenderContext<Row> {
  row: Row;
  rowIndex: number;
  rowBg: string;
  isSelected: boolean;
}
```
 ### `render` receives a context object, not a row [Section titled “render receives a context object, not a row”](#render-receives-a-context-object-not-a-row) This trips up agents and humans equally. The signature is: 
```ts
render: ({ row }) => ...   // ✓ correct
render: (row) => ...       // ✗ wrong — row is actually the ctx, every cell renders empty
```
 TypeScript accepts both forms because the ctx object structurally satisfies “the row shape plus extra fields” in many cases. The grid will silently render blank cells. **Always destructure `{ row }`.** ### Width: number → `fr`, string → any CSS track [Section titled “Width: number → fr, string → any CSS track”](#width-number--fr-string--any-css-track) `width` is `number | string`. A **number** becomes an `fr` track — `width: 1.3` means 1.3 fractions of the available width — so the grid flexes to the panel’s container. A **string** is emitted verbatim as a CSS-grid track, so any of `width: '120px'`, `width: 'minmax(80px,1fr)'`, or `width: 'auto'` work for fixed/constrained columns. Internally each column’s width is appended to `grid-template-columns` (`${n}fr` for a number, the string as-is otherwise). Separately, drag-resized columns (see [Resizable columns](#resizable-columns)) override a column’s track with an explicit `px` width. ### Sort key [Section titled “Sort key”](#sort-key) `sortKey` is a string — the upstream field name the data source should sort by (`sortKey: 'ts'`). It is **not** a deriving function; the grid passes the string back to you via `onSortChange`, it does not read the row. Sort is **controlled**: a column’s header is only clickable when it has a `sortKey` *and* you pass `onSortChange`. RichGrid does not sort the data itself — it emits a `SortState` (`{ column, dir }` or `null`) and you apply it. Clicking cycles `defaultSortDir` → opposite → unsorted (`null`). Wire it with the `applySort` helper: 
```tsx
const [sortState, setSortState] = useState<RichGridSortState | null>(null);
const sortedRows = useMemo(() => applySort(rows, sortState), [rows, sortState]);


<RichGrid
  rows={sortedRows}
  sortState={sortState}
  onSortChange={setSortState}
  ...
/>
```
 For large datasets, push the sort into the data source (SQL `ORDER BY`, Zero `.orderBy(...)`) instead of `applySort`. ### Filtering [Section titled “Filtering”](#filtering) Per-column filtering is the symmetric sibling of sort. A column opts in by setting `filter`, and — exactly like sort — RichGrid renders **no** filter UI and applies **no** predicate itself. The consumer holds the `ColumnFilterState` (typically a nuqs URL param) and calls the pure `applyColumnFilters(rows, state, columns)` helper before passing rows in (mirroring the `applySort` flow above). `filter` is a discriminated union on `type`: 
```ts
filter: { type: 'text',    accessor: (row) => row.name }          // case-insensitive substring
filter: { type: 'enum',    accessor: (row) => row.status }        // membership in selected set
filter: { type: 'number',  accessor: (row) => row.count }         // inclusive min/max range
filter: { type: 'boolean', accessor: (row) => row.archived }      // strict equality
```
 Wire the consumer-owned state and apply it before sorting: 
```tsx
const [filterState, setFilterState] = useState<ColumnFilterState>({});
const visibleRows = useMemo(
  () => applySort(applyColumnFilters(rows, filterState, columns), sortState),
  [rows, filterState, sortState, columns],
);


<RichGrid rows={visibleRows} columns={columns} ... />
```
 Other exported helpers from `@papercusp/grid-core`: `deriveEnumOptions` (discover distinct enum values + live counts from the rows), `encodeColumnFilters` / `decodeColumnFilters` (serialize state for a nuqs param), and `filterChipLabel` (render an active-filter chip). As with sort, this is small-dataset oriented — push the predicate into the data source for very large sets. ## Common props [Section titled “Common props”](#common-props) | Prop | Type | Notes | | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `rows` | `Row[]` | Source data (legacy/non-virtual mode). Memoize upstream if mapping from sync results. | | `columns` | `ColumnDef<Row>[]` | Wrap in `useMemo` to avoid rebuilding on every render. | | `getRowId` | `(row: Row) => string` | Required. Used as React key + selection set. | | `onRowClick` | `(row: Row, index, e) => void` | Optional. Whole row becomes click target. | | `getRowBg` | `(row, rowIndex, isSelected) => string \| undefined` | Per-row background override; return `undefined` to fall back to default striping. | | `rowProps` | `(ctx: CellRenderContext<Row>) => HTMLAttributes` | Per-row class/style — **receives the ctx, not the row** (use `ctx.row`). **See pitfall below.** | | `inline` | `boolean` | Skip the outer flex + scroll wrapper; render header/body as siblings for parent-owned scroll. Almost always pass this — but see the caveat below. | | `virtualMode` | `{ virtualizer, totalRows, rowAt, measureAll? }` | Opt-in virtualization. Pass instead of `rows`; flip on for >500 rows. `measureAll` measures every visible row (only needed for genuinely variable-height rows). | | `empty` | `ReactNode` | Shown when rows is empty / virtual total is 0. | | `sortState` / `onSortChange` | `SortState \| null` / `(next) => void` | Controlled sort — see above. | `inline` skips copy, print, and load-more `inline` mode renders only `[topSlot, header, body, footerSlot]` as siblings, so the consumer owns the scroll element. As a consequence, inline mode **skips the Ctrl+C copy handler, the print mirror, and `onLoadMore` / scroll-edge detection.** If a panel needs copy, print, or infinite scroll, don’t use `inline` (or wrap the grid in your own outer element and handle those yourself). ### Advanced props [Section titled “Advanced props”](#advanced-props) | Prop | Type | Notes | | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `selectable` | `boolean` | Render a left checkbox column with a select-all header — see [Multi-select](#multi-select). | | `selectedRowIds` / `onSelectedRowIdsChange` | `ReadonlySet<string>` / `(next) => void` | Controlled selection. Omit both for uncontrolled. | | `resizableColumns` | `boolean` | Enable drag-to-resize header handles — see [Resizable columns](#resizable-columns). | | `columnWidths` / `onColumnWidthsChange` | `Record<string, number>` / `(next) => void` | Controlled drag-resized widths (px, keyed by column key). | | `onLoadMore` | `() => void` | Fires when scrolled near the bottom (legacy mode only; ignored when `inline`). | | `loadMoreThreshold` | `number` | Pixels-from-bottom that triggers `onLoadMore`. Default `1500`. | | `isLoadingMore` | `boolean` | Renders a “Loading…” affordance at the bottom of the list. | | `onRowHover` | `(row \| null, index \| null) => void` | `mouseenter` / `mouseleave` per row (both `null` on leave). | | `topSlot` / `footerSlot` | `ReactNode` | Content rendered above / below the body (summary bar, footer, pagination). | | `headerStyle` / `headerHeight` | `CSSProperties` / `number` | Extra style merged onto the sticky header; header height in px (default `36`). | | `scrollContainerRef` | `MutableRefObject<HTMLDivElement \| null>` | Captures RichGrid’s internal scroll element (e.g. to tie an external virtualizer). Ignored when `inline`. | | `renderLoadingRow` | `(rowIndex, gridTemplateColumns) => ReactNode` | Virtual-mode placeholder for a not-yet-loaded row. Defaults to a “loading…” line. | | `getRowBg` | `(row, rowIndex, isSelected) => string \| undefined` | Per-row background override; `undefined` falls back to default striping. | | `rowMinHeight` | `number` | Min row height in px. Default `36`. | | `printRows` / `disablePrintMirror` / `disableCopySupport` | — | Copy & print toggles — see [Copy & print](#copy--print). | ## Pitfall: `rowProps` + a CSS class with `display: grid` [Section titled “Pitfall: rowProps + a CSS class with display: grid”](#pitfall-rowprops--a-css-class-with-display-grid) If `rowProps` returns `{ className: 'h-issue' }` and the legacy class has its own `display: grid`, that grid clashes with RichGrid’s internal cell grid and every cell renders on top of itself. Fix: override with inline `style: { display: 'block' }` (note `rowProps` receives the cell-render ctx, so destructure `ctx.row` if you need the row): 
```tsx
rowProps={({ row }) => ({
  className: 'h-issue', // legacy
  style: { display: 'block' },
})}
```
 The retired `IssuesList.tsx` (`libs/papercusp/_retired/apps-web/app/harness/issues/IssuesList.tsx`) is the original example of this pattern. ## Patterns: per-row action buttons [Section titled “Patterns: per-row action buttons”](#patterns-per-row-action-buttons) Action buttons in a column need `e.stopPropagation()` if the row also has `onRowClick`, otherwise a click on the button will also fire the row handler: 
```tsx
{
  key: 'action',
  header: '',
  width: 0.6,
  align: 'right',
  render: ({ row }) => (
    <button
      onClick={(e) => { e.stopPropagation(); onRemove(row.id); }}
    >
      delete
    </button>
  ),
}
```
 ## Patterns: virtual rows [Section titled “Patterns: virtual rows”](#patterns-virtual-rows) For grids that may show >500 rows (audit logs, agent runs across years), pass `virtualMode` (a `{ virtualizer, totalRows, rowAt }` object) **instead of** `rows`. You own the TanStack virtualizer + the windowed `rowAt(index)` lookup; `rowAt` may return `undefined` for not-yet-loaded rows, in which case RichGrid renders `renderLoadingRow` (or a “loading…” line). Row sizing defaults to `rowMinHeight` (36px); override per grid if rows are taller. By default the virtualizer trusts its `estimateSize` for every row and only re-measures the expanded row (each measurement is a forced layout read in the scroll path). Pass `measureAll: true` on `virtualMode` only when rows are genuinely variable height (multi-line cards, day-grouped feeds) so the virtualizer measures each visible row and keeps offsets exact. ## VirtualGrid: the drop-in for large grids [Section titled “VirtualGrid: the drop-in for large grids”](#virtualgrid-the-drop-in-for-large-grids) `virtualMode` (above) is the low-level seam — you own the virtualizer, the scroll element, `rowAt`, and the re-`measure()` on data change. That boilerplate was being copy-pasted and, more often, **skipped**: `<RichGrid rows={bigArray}>` (legacy mode) mounts **every** row as DOM, so teams hid the resulting jank by capping the fetch (the classic `limit: 300`). On a local desktop app that cap is pure downside — the data is already local, so load it all and just window the render. `VirtualGrid` (also from `@papercusp/grid-core`) owns all of it. Pass an in-memory array; only the visible window mounts: 
```tsx
import { VirtualGrid } from '@papercusp/grid-core';


<VirtualGrid<Row>
  columns={columns}
  rows={filteredRows}        // the FULL array — VirtualGrid windows it
  getRowId={(r) => r.id}
  onRowClick={(r) => setSel(r.id)}
  rowMinHeight={30}
  estimateRowHeight={30}     // optional; defaults to rowMinHeight ?? 30
/>
```
 * Every other RichGrid prop passes straight through (selection, resizable columns, sort, expansion, `getRowBg`, `empty`, …). * VirtualGrid renders its **own** scroll container, so do **not** wrap it in a scrolling `<div>`. By default the container is `flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto`, so give it a flex-column parent with a bounded height. To cap height or own the container yourself, pass `scrollClassName` / `scrollStyle`. * Reach for raw `virtualMode` only when you need an **external/shared** scroll element, or paged/infinite-scroll sync (`@papercusp/sync`’s `useSyncVirtualizer`). For “I have an array, render it cheaply”, use VirtualGrid. * **Copy & print:** VirtualGrid re-wires **Ctrl+C copy** itself (over the full `rows` array, built at copy-time — so `toCopyText` columns still work). It does **not** restore the full-page **print mirror** — that renders every row into a hidden `<table>`, which would defeat virtualization, so Ctrl+P prints only the on-screen window (copy → paste is the path for the full set). Pass `disableCopySupport` to opt out of the copy handler. **Rule of thumb:** any grid whose row count is unbounded or can exceed a few hundred uses VirtualGrid. Capping the fetch to keep render cheap is the anti-pattern — virtualize, then load the full local set. Reference migration: `WorkItemsPanel.tsx`. ## Honest counts: the true total via `_meta` [Section titled “Honest counts: the true total via \_meta”](#honest-counts-the-true-total-via-_meta) `useSyncQuery` resolvers return a **bare array** — there is no `{rows, total}` envelope. So a capped read (`LIMIT n`) has no channel to report the true total, and panels end up showing the **downloaded length** as if it were the count (e.g. “(300)” when 404 exist) — and any client-side filter then runs over only the truncated window. The convention (pioneered by `coord.feed`, now a shared helper) stashes page metadata on the **first row’s `_meta`**, preserving the flat-array contract. Helpers live in `@papercusp/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/list-meta`: **Server — in the resolver:** 
```ts
import { attachListMeta } from './list-meta';


const [rows, total] = await Promise.all([listX({ limit }), countX()]);
return attachListMeta(rows, { total }); // stashes { total } on rows[0]._meta
```
 **Client — in the panel:** 
```ts
import { readListTotal, listCountLabel } from '@papercusp/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/list-meta';


const total = readListTotal(items); // true total; falls back to items.length
api.setTitle(`Work items · ${slug} (${listCountLabel(items.length, total)})`);
// → "404" when nothing was truncated; "300 of 404" when the read was capped.
```
 `listCountLabel(shown, total)` is the rule: show just the total when nothing was truncated, `"N of TOTAL"` when it was — **never** the downloaded length alone. Even a paginated view should surface the true total this way, not the page size. Reference: `workItems.byHarness` (resolver) + `WorkItemsPanel.tsx` (panel). ## Multi-expand [Section titled “Multi-expand”](#multi-expand) RichGrid supports per-row expanded detail via `renderExpandedRow` plus an expansion-key prop. The caller fully owns the expanded-state — RichGrid does not toggle on click. Use `expandedRowKey` (single id) or `expandedRowKeys` (a `ReadonlySet<string>` for multiple rows; the two are unioned): 
```tsx
<RichGrid
  rows={features}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={f => f.id}
  expandedRowKeys={expanded}
  renderExpandedRow={(row) => <FeatureDetail feature={row} />}
/>
```
 Multiple rows can be expanded simultaneously when you pass `expandedRowKeys`. ## Multi-select [Section titled “Multi-select”](#multi-select) Set `selectable` to render a left checkbox column with a header “select-all” checkbox. Selection follows the same controlled/uncontrolled split as sort: pass `selectedRowIds` (a `ReadonlySet<string>`) plus `onSelectedRowIdsChange` to control it, or omit both to let RichGrid keep selection internally. 
```tsx
const [selected, setSelected] = useState<ReadonlySet<string>>(new Set());


<RichGrid
  rows={rows}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(r) => r.id}
  selectable
  selectedRowIds={selected}
  onSelectedRowIdsChange={setSelected}
/>
```
 When the grid root has focus, **Ctrl+A** selects all rows (the same set the header checkbox toggles). ## Resizable columns [Section titled “Resizable columns”](#resizable-columns) Set `resizableColumns` to add drag handles on the header cells. Resized widths override the column’s track with an explicit `px` width. By default those widths live in RichGrid’s internal state and **reset on remount**. To persist them, make widths controlled with `columnWidths` (a `Record<string, number>` of px keyed by column key) + `onColumnWidthsChange` — the same controlled/uncontrolled split as selection. The exported `usePersistedColumnWidths` hook wires that pair to storage so widths survive remounts: 
```tsx
const [widths, setWidths] = usePersistedColumnWidths('agents-grid');


<RichGrid
  rows={rows}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(r) => r.id}
  resizableColumns
  columnWidths={widths}
  onColumnWidthsChange={setWidths}
/>
```
 ## Copy & print [Section titled “Copy & print”](#copy--print) This is the reason `toCopyText` and `headerText` exist on `ColumnDef`. In the **non-inline** grid the root is focusable and supports: * **Ctrl+A** — select all rows. * **Ctrl+C** — copy the current selection (or all rows if none selected) to the clipboard as both TSV (`text/plain`) and `<table>` markup (`text/html`). Excel / Sheets prefer the HTML payload and paste rows into cells correctly; plain editors get the TSV. * **Ctrl+P** — print the full dataset. RichGrid renders a hidden native `<table>` print mirror so printing isn’t limited to the virtual viewport; the browser handles pagination and repeating `<thead>`. `toCopyText(row)` supplies the plain-text value for each cell in both the copy payload and the print mirror; `headerText` supplies the plain-text header (default: the `header` string, but JSX headers need it for spreadsheet fidelity). Columns without `toCopyText` copy/print empty for that cell — fine for pure-affordance columns (action buttons, icons). Toggles: * `disableCopySupport` — opt out of the Ctrl+C handler (Ctrl+C falls through to native browser text selection). * `disablePrintMirror` — skip the hidden print mirror. * `printRows` — **virtual mode only**: the full dataset for the print mirror (the lazy `rowAt` API can’t supply every row up front). Without it, virtual-mode Ctrl+P prints just the viewport. Remember the [`inline` caveat](#common-props): inline mode skips all of the above (copy handler, print mirror, and the scroll-edge `onLoadMore`). ## Testing a migrated panel [Section titled “Testing a migrated panel”](#testing-a-migrated-panel) After migrating from a hand-rolled list: 1. Visual: open `localhost:3055/harness/<slug>` and confirm columns line up. If a cell is blank, check the `render: (row) =>` vs `({ row })` bug above first. 2. Sort: click each header with a `sortKey` and confirm direction indicator updates. 3. Click: confirm `onRowClick` fires (and that buttons inside cells stop propagation). 4. Empty state: rows = `[]` should render the grid header with no content; provide a sibling empty-state component if the panel needs one.

# Schema conventions

> Per-harness Postgres schemas, shared schemas, publications, scaffolding.

Zero is being retired — historical reference Zero / zero-cache / ZQL named-queries / WebSocket push is **on the retirement path**. The shipping desktop app uses **SSE-primary** sync (the `:3070` Hono host pushes invalidate/update over Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`); zero-cache is **not run** on desktop. Treat this page as historical reference. Source of truth: `apps/operator/providers/HarnessSyncProvider.tsx` (transport-selection doc-comment) + the root `CLAUDE.md` deployment-model section. ## Database [Section titled “Database”](#database) The harness DB is `papercusp` on `localhost:5432`. (It was renamed from `restart_harness` in April 2026 — old references will still appear in older code.) Three Postgres roles see it: * `harness_app` — read/write from API routes and agent code. * `harness_admin` — DDL, used by scaffolders. * `harness_zero` — read-only via logical replication, used by `zero-cache-harness`. ## Schema layout [Section titled “Schema layout”](#schema-layout) The baseline (`libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/000-baseline.sql`) creates two schemas, `harness_shared` and `papercup_shared`. A fully migrated DB has **more than two** global schemas, though: migration `109-global-schemas-and-grants` also (re)creates `papercusp_auth` (operator identity — `users`, `sessions`, `magic_link_requests`) and `audit` (`operator_actions`, `action_executions`), which the squashed baseline’s narrow `pg_dump` had dropped, and `papercusp_marketplace` is created at runtime by the plugin layer. The four core per-harness entities are now **consolidated base tables in `harness_shared`**, keyed on a `harness_slug` column; the old physical `harness_<slug>.*` tables were dropped (archived migration `032-drop-per-harness-tables-replace-with-views`) and replaced with auto-updatable VIEWs for back-compat with writers that still pass a slug. The slug is a row value, not a schema name. 
```plaintext
papercusp database
├── harness_shared
│   ├── projects                            (cross-harness portfolio)
│   ├── harness_features_consolidated       (PK harness_slug, feature_id)
│   ├── harness_issues_consolidated         (PK harness_slug, issue_id)
│   ├── agent_runs_consolidated             (PK harness_slug, run_id)
│   ├── harness_snapshots_consolidated      (PK harness_slug, snapshot_id)
│   ├── agent_chats_consolidated            (PK workspace_id, harness_slug, id)
│   ├── feature_audit_consolidated          (PK id)
│   └── audit_log, harness_decisions, harness_phases, …
├── papercup_shared
│   ├── messages
│   ├── message_recipients
│   ├── message_comments
│   ├── directive_summaries
│   └── briefings
└── harness_<slug>                          (one schema per registered harness;
    ├── harness_features  (VIEW)             created at install time, NOT by the
    ├── harness_issues    (VIEW)             baseline — auto-updatable VIEWs over
    └── …                 (VIEW)             the consolidated tables, back-compat)
```
 Note the per-harness back-compat VIEWs are **not** nested inside `harness_shared`: each registered harness gets its own `harness_<slug>` schema, created at install/scaffold time (the baseline only defines `harness_shared`). Note also that not every consolidated table is keyed `(harness_slug, <entity_id>)`: `agent_chats_consolidated` is also workspace-scoped (`(workspace_id, harness_slug, id)`) and `feature_audit_consolidated` is keyed on `id` alone. ## Consolidated tables, not schema-per-harness (Option A) [Section titled “Consolidated tables, not schema-per-harness (Option A)”](#consolidated-tables-not-schema-per-harness-option-a) The original design was schema-per-harness (“Option B” — one `harness_<slug>` schema with its own physical tables). That was **reverted**: the system now uses a single consolidated table per entity in `harness_shared` with a `harness_slug` column (“Option A”). The physical per-harness tables were dropped (archived migration `032`) and replaced with auto-updatable VIEWs so older slug-passing writers keep working. Why the switch: * Adding a harness no longer requires DDL — the slug is a regular row value at install time, so there’s nothing to scaffold or add to Zero. * One hot table per entity is simpler to back up, index, and reason about than N near-identical per-slug copies. * Cross-harness reads (the `/features` page, the consolidated `.all` queries) are a plain `WHERE` filter, not a UNION across N schemas. Trade-off accepted: a single hot table per entity (the original concern about replication-slot lag on one hot table) in exchange for far less operational and DDL surface. ## Per-harness scaffolding (largely superseded) [Section titled “Per-harness scaffolding (largely superseded)”](#per-harness-scaffolding-largely-superseded) `bin/scaffold-harness-schema.sh <slug>` is the historical per-harness scaffolder — it rendered a per-harness DDL template into a `harness_<slug>` schema and added its tables to the `zero_harness` publication. With the move to consolidated tables, the per-harness physical tables (and the template `002-per-harness-template.sql`) are gone, so this path is **mostly vestigial**: adding a harness no longer creates a schema or runs any DDL — the slug is just a new row value in the consolidated tables. The schema itself is defined by the migration baseline (`000-baseline.sql` + incrementals from `107+`), not by a runtime scaffold. To change the schema today, add an idempotent migration under `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/<NNN>-*.sql` (never runtime DDL), then `node libs/papercusp/libs/db/scripts/pull-schema.mjs`. ## The `zero_harness` publication [Section titled “The zero\_harness publication”](#the-zero_harness-publication) Postgres logical replication needs a `PUBLICATION` listing every table to broadcast. Ours is named `zero_harness` and contains every relevant table from every per-harness schema plus the shared schemas. Inspect it:
