When a feature originates from a remote peer (`featureOrigin === 'remote'`), the durable content re-injected into the fresh prompt — feature history, plan context — is wrapped in `<untrusted-peer-content>` delimiters (`prompt-build.ts` `wrapUntrusted`: a per-call nonce plus a delimiter-stripping sanitizer) so a fresh spawn re-reads replicated peer state as inert data rather than being prompt-injected by it. ## The cost question [Section titled “The cost question”](#the-cost-question) A naive read of “fresh context” is “you pay full prompt tokens every spawn.” The Anthropic prompt cache changes the math — and the current prompt assembler is explicitly structured for it: a **byte-stable cacheable preamble** (role prompt → overrides → shared guides → identity → curated memory, ordered by descending stability) followed by a **volatile tail** (live substrate context, runtime context, brief) appended after the preamble so it never invalidates it (`prompt-build.ts` header, “Cache discipline”). In the bash era this design measured a **99.94% cache hit rate** (180M cache-read vs 106K fresh-input tokens over a 5-iteration mission) — the cost of “fresh” was effectively zero. The numbers and the levers are on [Why prompt-cache-dominant](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/prompt-cache). ## Tradeoffs we accept [Section titled “Tradeoffs we accept”](#tradeoffs-we-accept) * **No conversational repair.** A role can’t say “you misunderstood, try again” to itself; correction arrives as new durable state (a validator verdict, a message, an updated work item) read by the next fresh spawn. * **Cache-read fees.** Even cached, tokens aren’t free — cheaper than fresh-input by an order of magnitude, but not zero. * **Startup I/O.** Every spawn re-assembles its prompt and re-queries state. Negligible next to LLM latency. ## Where this stands today [Section titled “Where this stands today”](#where-this-stands-today) The autonomous DBOS pipeline (`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`) spawns each pipeline role as a one-shot agent process via the orchestrator’s headless `invoke-once` bin: the runner registers `setPipelineInvokeRunner`, which spawns `invoke-once` (→ `invoke.ts`) as a detached child process per agent run. Interactive role sessions (`psu --role <role>`) and the `bootstrap-role` console route take a different entry point — the launch spec (`packages/operator-core/lib/role-launch-spec.ts`, `buildRoleLaunchSpec`), the primitive for sessions a human drives. The two paths converge only on the shared `session-launch-dirs` leaf (per-session `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, signed-MCP dir keying, native session id), not on the launch spec itself. Long-lived *chat* surfaces (the operator, oracle) are conversations by design — the fresh-context rule is about the autonomous pipeline, where unattended drift is the failure mode.

# Decision log (harness design history)

> The chronological design decisions of the first-generation harness, which of them survive in the current engine, and where decisions are recorded today.

This page preserves the design-decision history of the **first-generation (bash) harness** — the rationale trail that shaped the current system — and maps which decisions survive in today’s engine. Historical entries are kept as written; they describe the system *as it was*. ## Where decisions are recorded today [Section titled “Where decisions are recorded today”](#where-decisions-are-recorded-today) This log is frozen history. Current design decisions live on **plans** — each plan document carries a `## Decisions` section of dated `D-NNN` entries (written via `plans:add-decision`), and the event-maintained rationale projection (`rationale:feed`) serves the topic-keyed “why” across plans, work items, and insights. If you’re about to record a decision, put it on the relevant plan, not here. ## The bash-era decision log (historical) [Section titled “The bash-era decision log (historical)”](#the-bash-era-decision-log-historical) | When | Decision | Rationale (as recorded) | | ------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Initial | **bash + claude as the runtime** | No agent-runtime opinion; \~1500 lines of supervisor anyone can read in an afternoon. | | Initial | **Disk-only state** | Any role can be invoked from a fresh shell and re-derive everything. | | Initial | **Fresh context per role** | No drift across iterations; the prompt cache absorbs the cost (99.94% hit rate observed). | | Initial | **Per-role markdown prompts** | Improvements compound without code changes; cache-key-stable. | | Initial | **Curator role** | Without compaction, raw memory grows unboundedly. | | Mid | **Plan-reviewer gate** | Catches scope drift before any worker fires. | | Mid | **Debugger role** | Stuck features (attempts ≥ 3) deserve root-cause analysis, not blind retry. | | Mid | **Crosscheck role** | A different model re-validates the validator’s pass; catches “confidently wrong”. | | Late | **Cost-cap removed** | Miscounted spend + owner wanted unbounded cost; soft-warn, later disabled. | | Late | **TDD iron law in validator** | Behavioral assertions need a test that failed before the change. | | Late | **”Boil the lake” principle** | Sprawling roles got an explicit “do fewer things perfectly” section. | | Late | **Evidence rule** | Every PASS claim must quote source output; reports without evidence revert to failing. | | Late | **Identity file per role** | Cross-mission append-only memory; curator promotes recurring patterns. | | Late | **Named checkpoints** | Pre-agreed milestones gate progress, distinct from escalations. | | Late | **Git worktrees** | Each parallel lane gets its own filesystem dir; no git race possible. | | Late | **Service smoke-test** | Real curl + service startup before declaring DONE. | | Late | **Two-mode parallelism** | `lane` (different features) vs `competition` (same feature, validator picks winner). | | Late | **Decisions timeline + ghost rate** | Orchestrator parse-ghost telemetry as a first-class signal. | ## Which of these survive today [Section titled “Which of these survive today”](#which-of-these-survive-today) Verified against the current engine: * **Fresh contexts, prompt-cache discipline, curator** — survive as core design, each with its own page: [fresh-contexts](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/fresh-contexts), [prompt-cache](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/prompt-cache), [curator](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/curator). * **Per-role markdown prompts** — survive, but the global `prompts/<role>.md` tier is gone (deleted in Phase 5, D-012). A role’s persona now resolves by walking the blueprint **extends-chain** — `blueprints/<id>/prompts/<role>.md` (the blueprint’s own override and each ancestor), always terminating at `blueprints/base/prompts/<role>.md`, the universal role library that is consulted for every blueprint (see [Roles](/internal/docs/harness/roles)). * **Validator disciplines** — survive in the layered validator persona (`blueprints/base/prompts/validator.base.md` + `validator.md`). The **default-reject disposition** is there verbatim (“Your default is *reject*”). The **evidence rule** survives as discipline, not as a named clause: “Generate independent evidence. Don’t trust the worker’s claims” and “Record each assertion `[PASS]` / `[FAIL]` with evidence” — the old “EVIDENCE RULE” label is no longer a literal heading in the persona. The validator also carries a curator-maintained, append-only `identity/validator.md` it reads at startup — the concrete instance of the surviving “Identity file per role” decision (cross-mission memory of prior-mission lessons). * **Debugger + crosscheck** — survive as blueprint roles in `blueprints/coding-factory/blueprint.yaml`: the debugger is a *reactive overlay* that fires before a worker retry once `knobs.debuggerThreshold` (default `3`) attempts accrue (`reactive: { beforeRole: worker, minAttempts: 3 }`); crosscheck is an opt-in quality gate (`NEXT_CROSSCHECK`). Note the blueprint name: the per-feature director spine moved to `coding-factory` in the 2026-06-18 rename — see the blueprint-rename note below. * **Decision telemetry + ghost rate** — survives; see [Decision telemetry](/internal/docs/harness/decisions-timeline). * **Named checkpoints** — **deprecated**: `CHECKPOINT` now finalizes as an escalation; milestone gates are `needs-human` plan items. * **Competition mode** — removed (replaced by the synthesizer pre-cutover, itself dormant since the run-loop retirement); lane-style isolation lives on — see [Worktrees & isolation](/internal/docs/harness/worktrees). Parallelism is now two-tiered: at the fleet level the Hive/Queen places ranked tasks onto bee slots (free slot / graceful-evict+fresh / warm-inject), and the per-feature `coding-factory` pipeline carries `dispatch.concurrency: 4` (`priority: plan-order`) for parallel feature pipelines. * **Disk-only state** — superseded: Postgres is the runtime store-of-record (see [Storage policy](/internal/docs/system/storage-policy)); the fresh-shell re-derivability *goal* survives, now via PG + the operator API. ## A note on the blueprint rename (`coding` is now the Hive) [Section titled “A note on the blueprint rename (coding is now the Hive)”](#a-note-on-the-blueprint-rename-coding-is-now-the-hive) This page was written when `coding` *was* the per-feature director spine. The 2026-06-18 domain-generic-hive-architecture rename (D-011/D-024) shuffled the blueprint ids, so the names mean different things today: * The bash-era per-feature spine — scoper → architect → worker → validator → reviewer → documenter → curator, with the debugger/crosscheck overlays — survives as **`blueprints/coding-factory/blueprint.yaml`** (the retired per-feature director loop, lifted into declared spine edges). * **`blueprints/coding/blueprint.yaml`** is now a different system entirely: the **Hive/Queen operator blueprint** (`kind: hive`, roles `operator` and `queen`) — the judgment layer over the bee fleet, not a validation spine. Following the old pointer expecting validator/debugger/crosscheck will land you on the Queen instead. ## Later eras (condensed) [Section titled “Later eras (condensed)”](#later-eras-condensed) Two further decision clusters in the original log concerned systems that are now fully retired, kept here as one-line summaries: the **org layer** (five fixed LLM directors with typed message kinds and file-based state under `~/.restart-org/` — retired; its jobs live in work items, coord, and the Pot operator) and the **public-site extraction** (a slim public repo + Cloudflare-Workers static hosting for papercupai.com — site retired to `_retired/papercup/`). The full tables remain in this page’s git history and the retired source (`_retired/papercup/`). ## Decisions explicitly rejected (historical, still instructive) [Section titled “Decisions explicitly rejected (historical, still instructive)”](#decisions-explicitly-rejected-historical-still-instructive) | Rejected | Why | | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | AutoGPT-style infinite loop | Drift catastrophe; supervised iterations with explicit decision verbs instead. | | LangChain orchestration | Heavyweight runtime + abstractions we didn’t need. | | External task-source integration (Linear/Notion) | Owner explicitly declined an external task source. | | Vector-DB memory for the harness loop | Bounded markdown memory was sufficient at harness scale. (Semantic memory later arrived as a *separate* system — the `memory:*` store — without replacing curated harness memory.) | | Discord/Slack as the control surface | Couples the harness to one chat UI; HTTP API + dashboard instead. | | Tmux-based agent messaging | Couples state to a terminal multiplexer. |

# Why prompt-cache-dominant

> The harness is designed so the Anthropic prompt cache absorbs the cost of fresh-context-per-role — prefix stability is an explicit, tested property of the prompt assembler.

The harness spawns a [fresh agent process per role invocation](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/fresh-contexts). That is only affordable because the prompt assembler is designed for Anthropic’s prompt cache: keep the expensive prefix byte-stable across spawns, and only a small volatile tail is fresh-billed. ## The design, in the current code [Section titled “The design, in the current code”](#the-design-in-the-current-code) `buildPromptParts` (`libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/prompt-build.ts`) assembles every pipeline spawn’s prompt as two halves — the file’s header documents this as the explicit “cache discipline”: * **Cacheable preamble** — byte-stable across spawns of the same role, ordered by *descending stability* so a change invalidates the smallest possible suffix: the role’s prompt file → per-role config override → tools playbook + shared guides → MCP-tool-access recipe → shared-base constants → per-role identity (`identity/<role>.md`, cross-mission, append-oriented) → curated memory (`memory/summary.md`) last, because it changes most often. The **MCP-tool-access recipe** (section 2d, after the shared guides and before the shared-base constants) is static text too: it teaches the deferred-tools `ToolSearch` contract and the sanctioned `mcp-call.mjs` curl-fallback, so a spawned backend that defers or drops its MCP tools reloads them rather than improvising raw curl or going silent. The **shared-base constants** are a growing set of exported strings in `prompt-build.ts` — memory discipline, the friction trip-wire and observation-rubric nudge, the yield policy, the account-routing/concurrency-first/deploy-pipeline notes, the reuse-first nudge, the testing/verification standard, and an optional per-hive vocabulary block — several gated by role (the curator skips memory discipline, friction, the observation-rubric nudge, and curated memory). * **Volatile tail** — per-spawn content (live substrate context, runtime context, the Queen/Overwatch wake-briefs, the spawn/wake handoff hydration block, brief, plan context, feature history) appended *after* the preamble so it never invalidates it. The Queen and Overwatch wake-briefs ride the tail as `<system-reminder>` blocks (each wake changes them), the handoff hydration block rides the tail too, and remote-authored content (plan context / feature history when `featureOrigin === 'remote'`) is wrapped in `<untrusted-peer-content>` delimiters — all reinforcing that the tail never invalidates the preamble. The split is exposed precisely so tests can assert the preamble is byte-identical across volatile-input changes (the prefix-hash assertion in `prompt-build.ts`’s test suite). Prefix stability is a **tested invariant**, not a hope. The newer per-hive knobs are tuned to preserve it: `acceptanceKind` and `lexicon` both *default* to emitting the coding-default text (the `tests`/undefined acceptance kind picks the testing standard; an absent or empty lexicon emits no vocabulary block) precisely so the coding fleet’s cached prefix stays byte-identical — a generic hive opts into the divergent text, the coding fleet never moves. Cache behavior is also observable: every sampled spawn records `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_creation_tokens` alongside input/output tokens and cost to Postgres (`usage-sample-pg.ts`), so a cache-hit-rate regression is a queryable signal. Samples also carry `session_id`, `plan_id`, and `tool_name`, so the analysis goes beyond per-spawn hit-rate: grouping by `session_id` makes a warm-inject/resume bee’s **carry-cost** — `cache_read` growth across successive tasks within one native session — queryable, while `plan_id`/`tool_name` give per-plan and per-tool cache attribution. ## What the bash era measured [Section titled “What the bash era measured”](#what-the-bash-era-measured) The numbers that motivated this design (measured on the first-generation bash harness, 5-iteration mission, 13 role invocations): | Metric | Value | | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- | | Cache read tokens | 180,049,624 | | Fresh input tokens | 106,471 | | **Cache hit rate** | **99.94%** | | Output tokens | 24,533 | | Total cost | \~$0.31 (vs \~$3.10 if everything were fresh-billed) | A non-cached harness cost \~10× more. The cache hit rate was treated as a primary observability signal — a sudden drop means *something is rewriting state the design expects to be stable*. ## How to keep the hit rate near 100% [Section titled “How to keep the hit rate near 100%”](#how-to-keep-the-hit-rate-near-100) The levers are the same today as in the bash era, mapped to current surfaces: 1. **Stable role prompts.** Don’t edit a role’s prompt file mid-mission; each edit costs one cache-miss spawn per role. Role prompts resolve from the blueprint extends-chain — `blueprints/<blueprintId>/prompts/<role>.md`, then each ancestor, then `blueprints/base/prompts/<role>.md` (the universal role library, always consulted) — under `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/`. There is **no** legacy global `prompts/<role>.md` tier (it was deleted in Phase 5 of blueprint-role-bundling, D-012 option A). Concretely, the spine roles (scoper, reviewer, curator, …) resolve from `blueprints/base/prompts/`, and the coding HIVE roles (queen/bee/operator/overwatch) from `blueprints/coding/prompts/`. 2. **Append-oriented identity files.** The curator appends to `identity/<role>.md` rather than rewriting (its persona instructs exactly this), so each change shifts the cache key minimally. 3. **Bounded curated memory.** `memory/summary.md` is hard-capped (40 lines / \~800 tokens, enforced by the curator persona) and sits **last** in the preamble — a curator pass costs one miss, then subsequent spawns hit again. 4. **Volatile content at the end.** Anything per-spawn rides the tail, never the preamble. What still breaks the cache: editing prompt sources mid-run, rewriting (vs appending) identity/summary files, or switching model mid-mission (the cache is keyed on model). ## Where this stands today [Section titled “Where this stands today”](#where-this-stands-today) The discipline was re-audited and re-asserted in the DBOS era (`token-usage-reduction-audit-2026-06-09` P-009 — the header of `prompt-build.ts` cites it): the preamble/tail split, the stability ordering, and the prefix-hash test all live in the current assembler. The same instinct applies beyond spawn prompts — e.g. long-lived interactive sessions schedule their idle wake-ups around the cache TTL — but the load-bearing, tested implementation is the pipeline prompt assembler above.

# Glossary (harness runtime)

> The runtime terms you meet working with a live harness, each traceable to the defining code.

Runtime terms, alphabetical, each pointing at its defining code. For spec-level/product vocabulary (Install, Goal, Plugin, marketplace `kind`, …) see [Vocabulary](/internal/docs/spec/vocabulary); for the user-facing brand lexicon (Hive/Queen/bee display strings) see the `papercusp-the-hive` [flag](/internal/docs/posthog/feature-flags) — those are presentation-layer names over the code terms below. **Bee** · The generic “do this task” agent of the hive blueprint — carries no pipeline spine and no chunk requirement, unlike `worker`. — `packages/agent-mcp/src/role-config.ts` **Blueprint** · A harness’s declarative shape: roles, spine, triggers, gates, dispatch policy, `knobs`, and declared `params`. Built-ins extend `base`. — `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/`, schema in `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/schema.ts` **Brain** · The RBAC *principal* role marking the operator’s own orchestration intelligence — gates spawn-approval tools at the dispatch layer. Not an agent role. — `role-config.ts :: BRAIN_PRINCIPAL_ROLE` **Chunk** · A feature-family work-item kind: a feature sub-unit sized for one worker turn, executed by the worker chunk loop (per-chunk file locks + a typecheck gate). — `packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts` **Claim / lease** · Taking ownership of a work item (`work_items:claim`); a live lease with a dead holder is an *orphaned claim*, surfaced by `fleet:assignments`. **Coding blueprint** · The default *execution pipeline* (`kind:'harness'`, `id: coding-factory`): a per-feature `director` drives a deterministic **spine** — scoper → architect → worker → validator → documenter → curator (+ opt-in tester / security / crosscheck / ui-qa; reviewer = the PR gate) — over one `feature` (`F-NNN`). The 2026-06-18 rename moved this spine off the `coding` id (now the Hive) and onto `coding-factory`; it remains the active fallback pipeline and the `extends` base for repo-detected harnesses. Contrast the **Hive blueprint** (orchestration, *no* spine): different layers, not flavors. — `blueprints/coding-factory/blueprint.yaml`, [hive-vs-coding](/internal/docs/agent-insights/hive-vs-coding-blueprint) **Curator** · The memory-compaction pipeline role; the only role that deletes harness memory. Its persona, like every role’s, resolves under the owning blueprint as `blueprints/<id>/prompts/curator.md` (base default in `blueprints/base/`) — the legacy global `prompts/` dir is retired. — [Why a curator](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/curator) **Decision verb** · The single verb a deciding agent emits per iteration (`NEXT_WORKER` / `NEXT_ARCHITECT` / `NEXT_VALIDATOR` / `DONE` / `ESCALATE`); interpreted by the blueprint spine. — [Decision telemetry](/internal/docs/harness/decisions-timeline) **Director** · The role that emits per-feature decision verbs in the durable pipeline; a real `AGENT_ROLES` id (registered by blueprint-role-bundling). Its persona resolves under the owning blueprint as `blueprints/<id>/prompts/director.md` (base default: `blueprints/base/prompts/director.md`) — the global `prompts/` dir is retired, and legacy ids resolve via `BLUEPRINT_ID_ALIASES`. — `role-config.ts :: AGENT_ROLES`, `blueprints/base/prompts/director.md` **Dispatch** · The blueprint-declared policy for when/what the engine runs next; concurrency knobs resolve via their own path (not the effective-config overlay). — `blueprints/*/blueprint.yaml` **Effective config** · Blueprint knobs overlaid *under* the per-harness instance config (instance wins). — [Configuration](/internal/docs/harness/config) **Escalation** · A pipeline finalizing with `ESCALATE`: the `on-escalate` hook fires and the `onEscalate` recipe (default: curator) runs; the harness surfaces the reason for a human. — `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/orchestrator-finalize.ts` **Feature** · The classic feature-family work-item kind (`F-NNN`), routed through the coding blueprint’s spine. — `work-items.ts` **Finalize recipe** · The blueprint’s `gates.finalize` step list run on terminal outcomes (`onDone` / `onEscalate`). — `blueprints/coding-factory/blueprint.yaml` **Ghost** · A deciding-agent output that fails to parse as a known decision verb; tracked as a rate and a health signal (`low_ghost_rate`). — `packages/operator-core/lib/harness-readers.ts` **Harness** · One managed work pipeline (repo + work queue + runs), instantiated from a blueprint; slug-identified. **Hive blueprint** · The *orchestration* layer (`kind:'hive'`, `id: coding`, root-only, **never nested**): a **Queen** surveys the work frontier and *places* ranked `work_items` onto generic **bees** — **no spine**, self-declared wake (`hive:declare-wake`) — and can create coding/research harnesses. The 2026-06-18 rename moved this blueprint from `hive` to `coding`; the legacy `hive` id survives only as a runtime alias (`BLUEPRINT_ID_ALIASES = { hive: 'coding' }`). Contrast the **Coding blueprint** (one pipeline it runs). — `blueprints/coding/blueprint.yaml`, [hive-vs-coding](/internal/docs/agent-insights/hive-vs-coding-blueprint) **Hook** · An out-of-band shell script at `.papercusp/hooks/<name>.sh` run at pipeline boundaries. — [Lifecycle hooks](/internal/docs/harness/hooks) **Identity file** · `identity/<role>.md` — cross-mission per-role lessons, PG-mirrored to `harness_shared.identity_files`. — [Memory](/internal/docs/harness/memory) **Instance config** · Per-harness overrides stored in workspace-PG and delivered via the `HARNESS_CONFIG_JSON` env transport; `.papercusp/config.json` is deprecated and not read. — `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/effective-config.ts` **Knobs** · Shape-level defaults a blueprint declares (e.g. `debuggerThreshold: 3`). — `blueprints/coding-factory/blueprint.yaml` **Overwatch** · The autonomous system-health *supervisor* (a sibling to the Queen): runs a sense → decide → act loop over the whole running system, but nudges / observes / escalates *only* — it never re-places work and its role envelope denies `capability:fs-write` + `capability:bash`. A built-in `AGENT_ROLES` id, but it ships dark behind the `papercusp-overwatch` flag (default OFF). — `role-config.ts`, `blueprints/coding/prompts/overwatch.md` **Params** · A blueprint’s *declared tunables*, keyed by instance-config dot-paths, unioned across `extends`; the schema-driven settings layer validates writes against them. — `blueprint/params.ts` **Phase** · One of up to three worktrees per project — `staging` (the main path), `testing`, `production` (sibling `<path>--<phase>` checkouts). — `packages/operator-core/lib/harness-phases.ts` **Planner** · An interactive plan-authoring session role (drafts one plan via `plans:*`); not the spec-level Planner pipeline role. — `role-config.ts` **Queen** · The steering intelligence of a hive/Pot — schedules, places, and prioritizes work (the role the lexicon surfaces as “Queen”); distinct from the watching `sentinel`. — `role-config.ts :: AGENT_ROLES` (`queen` entry) **Redundancy / replica** · BOINC-style multi-dispatch of one work item to independent replicas with a judge step (`work_items:set_redundancy` / `claim_replica` / `record_replica_result` / `judge_redundancy`, plus the `work_items:redundancy_status` read view); feature-family only. Opt-in and **OFF by default** — a `set_redundancy` marker stays inert (the item still runs exactly-once) until the owner sets `PAPERCUSP_WORKITEM_REDUNDANCY=1`. **Role** · A named agent function with its own persona + tool surface. The runtime registry is `AGENT_ROLES`. — [Roles](/internal/docs/harness/roles) **Run / spawn** · One agent invocation: the spawn is the envelope (workspace * harness + role + work item + signed MCP URL), the run is the execution; tracked in `harness_shared.spawned_agents`. **Sentinel** · The read-mostly fleet watcher (stuck spawns, lock hogs, coord staleness); its only writes are alarms. — `role-config.ts` **Spine** · The blueprint’s declared role-routing model; the `deriveNext` interpreter maps (state, decision verb) → next action. — `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/derive-next.ts` **Summary memory** · `.papercusp/memory/summary.md` — curator-maintained, 40-line cap, auto-injected into every pipeline spawn. — [Memory](/internal/docs/harness/memory) **Task** · An issue-family work-item kind recording delegated work; excluded from the default `issues:*` listing. — `work-items.ts` **Work blueprint** · The non-coding work Hive (`kind:'hive'`, `id: work`, `extends: coding`): the same Queen + bees orchestration as the coding Hive but for non-code work. Renamed from `generic-hive` by the 2026-06-18 rename (`BLUEPRINT_ID_ALIASES = { 'generic-hive': 'work' }`). — `blueprints/work/blueprint.yaml` **Work item** · The unified unit of work, one type discriminated by `kind`: feature family (`feature` / `research-task` / `chunk`) + issue family (`bug` / `change` / `task`), served by the `work_items` UNION view over the per-kind tables (migration 159). — `packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts` **Workspace** · One Papercusp install: many harnesses, one PG database, one credential set.

# Lifecycle hooks

> Out-of-band shell scripts in .papercusp/hooks/ that the DBOS finalizer runs at mission boundaries — plus how plugin hooks fire alongside them.

Lifecycle hooks are user-supplied shell scripts that the harness runs at fixed pipeline boundaries. Drop an executable script at `<project>/.papercusp/hooks/<name>.sh` and the engine invokes it when the matching event fires. The runner is `runHook()` in `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/hooks.ts`: it looks up `<stateDir>/hooks/<name>.sh`, skips silently if the file is missing or not executable (any execute bit set — `mode & 0o111`, so owner, group, **or** other counts), runs it with `cwd` set to the project directory, captures combined stdout+stderr to `<stateDir>/logs/hooks/<unix-seconds>-<name>.log`, and logs a non-zero exit as a warning — a failing hook never halts the mission. On Windows the script needs `bash` on `PATH` (Git for Windows ships one); the desktop bootstrap surfaces that prerequisite. ## Why hooks instead of in-prompt actions [Section titled “Why hooks instead of in-prompt actions”](#why-hooks-instead-of-in-prompt-actions) This is design intent carried over from the first harness generation, and it still holds: hooks are **out-of-band**. They consume no tokens, add no latency to any LLM call, and fire **deterministically** — not “if the agent decides to”. Anything you’d otherwise bolt onto a role prompt as “and also send a Slack message” belongs in a hook, keeping each prompt focused on the role’s one job. ## Hooks that fire today [Section titled “Hooks that fire today”](#hooks-that-fire-today) The legacy bash run-loop fired ten hook events; that loop is retired (`libs/papercusp/_retired/orchestrator-run-loop/`). In the current DBOS pipeline, hooks fire from the **finalizer** — the step list that `planFinalization()` builds when a feature pipeline ends in DONE or ESCALATE (`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/orchestrator-finalize.ts`). Two hook names are wired: | Hook | Fires | Event-specific env | Call site | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | | `on-escalate` | Pipeline finalizes with **ESCALATE**, before the `onEscalate` recipe roles run | `REASON`, `PROJECT_DIR`, `STATE_DIR` | `orchestrator-runner.ts:930` | | `afterDone` | Pipeline finalizes **DONE** (and the done-gates pass), after the `onDone` recipe roles run | `TRIGGER=done`, `FEATURE_ID`, `PROJECT_DIR`, `STATE_DIR` | `orchestrator-runner.ts:952` | A blocked DONE skips the whole finalization step list, hook included. `planFinalization()` blocks completion on **any** of three conditions: an open needs-human plan item, a configured smoke gate that ran and failed (`smokeEnabled && smokePassed === false`), or — for a `human-gate` acceptance blueprint — an approval that hasn’t been granted yet (`acceptanceKind === 'human-gate' && !acceptanceApproved`). Any of these and the `afterDone` hook never runs. The roles that surround the hooks are **declarative**, not hardcoded: `planFinalization()` resolves the finalize recipe from the harness’s `.papercusp/blueprint.yaml` `gates.finalize`, defaulting to the coding blueprint’s recipe (`onDone`: curator → postCuratorOutputs → documenter → `[archive]`; `onEscalate`: curator). A non-coding HIVE blueprint can override `gates.finalize`, so the hooks fire around whatever finalize recipe that harness declares. A `judge`-acceptance blueprint additionally inserts a `judge`-role acceptance gate before the `onDone` recipe whose `revise` verdict hard-blocks the **rest** of the finalize recipe: the runner `break`s out of the finalize step loop, so every remaining step — including the `afterDone` hook, which the finalizer appends last — is skipped. `afterDone` fires only on a normal accepted `DONE` finalize. `runHook()` itself accepts any name — the engine isn’t limited to these two — but no other call site exists in the live tree, so no other event fires. The pre/post-worker, validator, smoke, checkpoint and competition hooks from the bash era retired with the run-loop. ### The `afterDone` builtin [Section titled “The afterDone builtin”](#the-afterdone-builtin) `afterDone` has a TS builtin behind it: when **no** user hook script ran, the finalizer calls `notifyParentOnDone()` (`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/notify-parent-done.ts`), which posts a `Completion` message to this harness’s parent — so a parent that spawned this harness as a child learns the sub-work is done. The parent slug is read from PG (`harness_shared.projects.parent_slug`, sealed server-side at scaffold time by `doScaffoldHarness`), **not** from config. The message fires **only when the harness’s feature queue has fully drained** — every other feature is `passed` or `deprecated`, excluding the feature that triggered this finalize. A non-drained queue is a **silent no-op**: the builtin returns a typed reason (`no_parent` / `queue_not_drained` / `send_failed` / `lookup_failed`) and posts nothing. A per-harness `hooks/afterDone.sh` **overrides the builtin entirely** (parity with the retired bash builtin resolver). Plugin hooks fire regardless (below). ## Environment a hook receives [Section titled “Environment a hook receives”](#environment-a-hook-receives) On top of the event-specific variables in the table, `runHook()` auto-injects context so scripts can query the operator instead of scraping harness files (`hooks.ts:105–113`): * `HARNESS_SLUG` — the current harness slug (defaults to the project directory’s basename when not passed explicitly) * `WORKSPACE_ID` — the active workspace, when known * `OPERATOR_BASE` — operator API base URL; defaults to `$PAPERCUSP_OPERATOR_BASE`, then `http://localhost:3070` (the operator API port — `:3055` is the Vite content port with no `/api` routes, the EI-113 wrong-stack default that audit P-038 fixed) The full process environment is inherited too; the caller’s explicit env wins over the injected values on conflict. **Hooks must not read harness state from the filesystem.** Files like `lanes.json` no longer exist at runtime — PG is the runtime store-of-record (see [Storage policy](/internal/docs/system/storage-policy)). The contract in `hooks.ts` is: query the operator API instead. 
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Example: .papercusp/hooks/afterDone.sh — look up feature state via the API
features=$(curl -fsS "$OPERATOR_BASE/api/harness/$HARNESS_SLUG/features")
status=$(echo "$features" | jq -r '.[] | select(.id == "'"$FEATURE_ID"'") | .status')
```
 
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Example: .papercusp/hooks/on-escalate.sh — page a Slack channel
curl -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"text\":\"Mission escalated: $REASON\"}" \
  "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"
```
 Make scripts executable (`chmod +x`) — a non-executable file is skipped without error. ## Plugin hooks fire alongside [Section titled “Plugin hooks fire alongside”](#plugin-hooks-fire-alongside) User hook scripts are per-harness; **plugins** hook the same lifecycle globally. At the `afterDone` step the finalizer fires the in-process typed hook `firePluginLifecycle('afterDone', …)` on every loaded plugin that declares a handler (one of the FROZEN legacy fire-points — plugin-system-hive-port D-003), then emits the `pipeline:done:<slug>:<feature>` event. Plugin hook failures are logged by the host and ignored; plugin hooks fire whether or not a user hook script ran. (The old per-plugin shell-out via the `papercusp-fire-hook` CLI was retired 2026-06-12 — plugin-system-hive-port P-006.) New pipeline integrations should not use typed hooks at all: declare **event-reaction rules** on the pipeline event vocabulary instead — see [Plugins](/internal/docs/spec/plugins). ## Managing hook scripts over the API [Section titled “Managing hook scripts over the API”](#managing-hook-scripts-over-the-api) `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/harness/hooks.ts` exposes CRUD for hook scripts: `GET /api/harness/:slug/hooks` (list known hooks with content + executable bit), `PUT`/`DELETE /api/harness/:slug/hooks/:name` (write with `chmod 755` / remove), and `GET /api/harness/:slug/hook-logs/:logId` to read a hook-run log. The `hooks:known` tool returns the same name list. The known-hooks list comes from `getKnownHooks()` (`packages/operator-core/lib/known-hooks.ts`), which returns the `live` rows of a static `DBOS_PIPELINE_HOOKS` registry — yielding `['afterDone', 'on-escalate']` (sorted). So the API lists, and accepts writes to, `afterDone`/`on-escalate` (the two that fire) and **rejects** names that aren’t live, such as the bash-era `pre-worker` (catalogued `status: 'lost'`, not returned). A drift guard (`known-hooks.test.ts`) greps the live firing sites under `lib/dbos/` and asserts set equality with the registry’s `live` rows, so adding a `runHook(...)` call without a registry row fails the build. `runHook()` itself never consults this list, so scripts created directly on disk run regardless of whether the API would have allowed the name. (Earlier the registry was instead derived by grepping the now-retired `main-loop.ts`, which always found nothing and fell back to `['pre-worker']` — advertising a hook that never fires and hiding the two that do. The static registry replaced that grep in `papercusp-full-app-audit-2026-06-09` P-016 (EI-94).) ## Related [Section titled “Related”](#related) * [Orchestrator + pending\_events](/internal/docs/spec/orchestrator) — the DBOS pipeline whose finalizer fires these hooks * [Plugins](/internal/docs/spec/plugins) — plugin lifecycle states and hook handler semantics * [Storage policy](/internal/docs/system/storage-policy) — why hooks query the API instead of reading harness files

# Memory

> The three memory layers — curator-maintained harness working memory, the semantic memory store behind memory:*, and procedural knowledge in agent-insights — and what carries live state instead.

“Memory” in Papercusp is three different systems with three different jobs. Confusing them causes drift, so the boundaries are the point of this page. ## 1. Harness working memory (curator-maintained files) [Section titled “1. Harness working memory (curator-maintained files)”](#1-harness-working-memory-curator-maintained-files) Each harness keeps a small, bounded set of memory files under `.papercusp/memory/` — the direct descendants of the first-generation design: * **`raw.md`** — append-only one-liner observations; any role writes here without coordination. * **`MEMORY.md`** — the curated mission-scoped store (\~200-line bound), merged from raw observations by the curator. * **`summary.md`** — hard-capped at 40 lines / \~800 tokens and **auto-injected into every pipeline spawn’s prompt — every role *except* the curator**, which authors it (and so also skips the memory-discipline / friction clauses, since the file changes between iterations). It rides the cacheable preamble of `prompt-build.ts`, placed **last** in that preamble on purpose: an update invalidates only itself, not the static prefix above it (see [Why prompt-cache-dominant](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/prompt-cache)). * **`identity/<role>.md`** — per-role lessons that carry *across* missions; the orchestrator mirrors them into Postgres (`harness_shared.identity_files`) via `POST /api/internal/identity-snapshot`, making PG the durable, queryable copy. Only the [curator](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/curator) compacts or deletes these; everyone else appends. ## 2. Semantic memory (`memory:*` — the cross-client store) [Section titled “2. Semantic memory (memory:\* — the cross-client store)”](#2-semantic-memory-memory--the-cross-client-store) Durable facts that should survive sessions and be recalled by *every* client (Claude / Codex / OMP / spawned agents) live in the semantic memory store behind the `memory:remember` / `memory:search` / `memory:list` / `memory:forget` / `memory:update` tools. * **Canonical store:** Postgres — `harness_shared.memory_canonical` (embedded rows; `last_surfaced_at` powers injection dedup). * **Swappable backend:** the store core is the generic `@papercusp/memory` lib behind a `MemoryBackend` seam. The lib itself seeds two built-ins in its registry — `mem0` (the canonical PG store) and `noop`; the operator registers the rest in `packages/operator-core/lib/memory/configure.ts` — `claude-file` (the `~/.claude` topic-file store) and **`hybrid`**, which fuses the claude-file lexical leg with the mem0 cosine leg via reciprocal-rank fusion (default mode `floored-union`: the FP-floored cosine hits *unioned* with the lexical hits that clear the identifier bar, so an exact-id target the cosine leg missed is still captured; `cosine-gated` — lexical re-ranks only — stays selectable as the strictest discipline, but the production wiring constructs it with no opts, so it runs the default). Hybrid **writes** delegate to the mem0 leg, so PG stays canonical — and the same fact is *also* best-effort projected into the lexical (claude-file) leg, stamped with the canonical id as `link_id` so fusion can dedupe a memory that surfaces from both legs; a cold or missing lexical leg is non-fatal and recall degrades cleanly to cosine-only. Selecting an unregistered backend name **throws loud at first use** — a deliberate fail-fast so a typo’d `PAPERCUSP_MEMORY_BACKEND` is never masked as “memory is just empty”. * **Live selection:** which backend serves is an operator-wide setting (`harness_shared.operator_settings`, key `memory_backend`), changeable from the settings UI with no restart; resolution is persisted setting → `PAPERCUSP_MEMORY_BACKEND` → `mem0` (`packages/operator-core/lib/memory/backend-selection.ts`). * **Injection:** relevant memories are surfaced into a session pre-turn (`packages/operator-core/lib/memory/injection.ts`), with a time-recency window over `last_surfaced_at` so the same memory isn’t re-pushed turn after turn — a candidate surfaced within the last \~120s (`PAPERCUSP_MEMORY_REINJECT_WINDOW_MS`, default 120000) is dropped from this turn. The window is global/recency-based — it filters the turn’s candidate ids, not a per-session watermark. Every `memory:remember` declares one of four **kinds** — `user` / `feedback` / `project` / `reference`. Scoping: pass a `harness_slug` for project facts; omit it for personal facts; or pass a `hive_slug` (mutually exclusive with `harness_slug`) to write into a Hive’s *shared* pool, for discovered conventions — test command, build path, design system — the whole hive should inherit. Client-local file memories (e.g. Claude Code’s topic files) are a per-client layer — the shared store is the one every agent recalls from. ## 3. Procedural knowledge (agent-insights) [Section titled “3. Procedural knowledge (agent-insights)”](#3-procedural-knowledge-agent-insights) Runbooks — “how X works / how to not lose an hour on Y” — are **docs, not memory rows**: PR-reviewed MDX under [agent-insights](/internal/docs/agent-insights). Short facts go to semantic memory; multi-step explanations go here. ## What is NOT memory: live state [Section titled “What is NOT memory: live state”](#what-is-not-memory-live-state) In-flight state belongs to its own systems, never to a memory store: work items carry task state, **coord** carries presence/intents/handoffs, plans carry decisions (projected by `rationale:feed`). The legacy instinct “write it to a file so the next role sees it” maps today to “write it to the durable store the next spawn queries” — see [Storage policy](/internal/docs/system/storage-policy). ## Choosing the right layer [Section titled “Choosing the right layer”](#choosing-the-right-layer) | You have… | Put it in | | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | | A one-liner observation mid-mission | `.papercusp/memory/raw.md` (curator will file it) | | A durable preference / convention / gotcha | `memory:remember` (semantic store) | | A multi-step runbook | an agent-insights page | | Task progress, blockers, hand-offs | the work item / coord — not memory | | A design decision | the plan’s `## Decisions` (D-NNN) |

# Inbound PR review & merge loop

> How a fork→PR contribution is autonomously noticed, tracked, agent-reviewed, gated, and (in owner auto-mode) merged — the as-built inbound spine (PR-1..5 of pr-system-completion-dogfood), its S0 safety invariants, and the manual/auto owner modes.

## The loop at a glance [Section titled “The loop at a glance”](#the-loop-at-a-glance) 
```plaintext
 new/updated PR on a shared harness (pr_reviewer_role_enabled)
        │
   [poll daemon]  system:pr-poll routine (per harness, ~60s + exp backoff)
        │  list open PRs → diff vs last-seen (routine metadata)
        │  per NEW/CHANGED PR:
        │    • getPr + fetch check-runs → refresh pr_check_status_cache
        │    • upsert harness_feature_prs            (WI↔PR producer)
        │    • trigger the agent-reviewer            (in-process or blueprint)
        ▼
   [agent-reviewer]  runPrReviewTask → report {summary, recommendation,
        │            rationale, risks, checksObserved}  → pr_review_reports
        ▼
   decideAutoReview(pr, settings)  +  report gate  +  revocation gate
        │   (auto mode, all gates pass)
        ▼
   tryAutoApprove → tryAutoMerge → stampCompletionRefOnMerge
        │                                   │
        ▼                                   ▼
   GitHub review/merge              feature status='shipped' +
                                    harness_feature_prs.pr_state='merged'
```
 ## Components [Section titled “Components”](#components) | Stage | Module | What it does | | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Poll daemon** | `pr-host/poll-daemon.ts` (`system:pr-poll`, seeded by `pr-poll-routine.ts`) | The spine. Per harness with the reviewer role enabled, lists open PRs, diffs against a `last_seen` `{updated_at, head_sha}` snapshot on the routine metadata, and drives the per-PR flow. 60s cadence + exponential backoff (`retry-policy-types.ts`) on host errors; crash-safe (one durable step, idempotent). Registered via `registerSystemAction('pr-poll', …)` like git-sync. | | **WI↔PR producer** | `harness/feature-pr-producer.ts` | `upsertFeaturePrOnOpen` / `markFeaturePrState` link a feature ↔ its PR ↔ state, recording the human operator’s `author_github_user_id` (per-operator identity), `COALESCE`’d on conflict so a later poll can’t wipe the operator attribution. The daemon also best-effort upserts a row, but writes only state/url (no author id), so a subsequent daemon poll can’t overwrite the at-open attribution. | | **Agent reviewer** | `pr-host/agent-reviewer.ts` + `pr-review-report-types.ts` | `runPrReviewTask` reviews the PR diff and emits a safety-guarded report. `assembleReport` forces the recommendation no more permissive than the facts: a suspected secret → `reject`, failing checks / empty diff → `request_changes` (the LLM can never talk these down). Default model `claude-sonnet-4-6` (override per-deploy with `PAPERCUSP_PR_REVIEW_MODEL`), run `anthropic-direct` at temperature `0` with a 90s abort timeout and a 1500-token output budget. The model sees a diff bounded to 60k chars (`DEFAULT_MAX_DIFF_CHARS`), but the deterministic secret/test/file scans still run over the **full** diff — so the safety floors hold even when the prompt is truncated (`diff_truncated` flags only the prompt budget, not the scans). Stored in `pr_review_reports`. | | **Decision gate** | `pr-host/auto-review-decision-types.ts` (`decideAutoReview`) | Pure gate: role-enabled → `auto_review` → PR open → not draft → not self-authored → author trusted → not already-approved / changes-requested → then (`auto_merge` ∧ checks-green ∧ mergeable) ⇒ `approve_and_merge`, else `approve`. | | **Report + revocation gates** (in the daemon) | `poll-daemon.ts`, `contribution-admission.ts` | A **revoked** contributor’s PR is refused before any auto-approve/merge action and before the report gate (`isPrAuthorRevoked`, S0). Note the loop order: the agent review itself is still *triggered* for a revoked author (`triggerReviewer` → `decideAutoReview` gate → `isAuthorRevoked` → report gate → approve/merge) — the review is harmless (it never posts or merges), so a revoked PR may have a report but never an auto-action. Then for a non-revoked author: report **absent** ⇒ *defer* (await the review; the PR is excluded from `last_seen` so the next poll re-checks) — never auto-approve before the agent reviews; report **non-approve** ⇒ veto; **approve** ⇒ proceed. The read is head\_sha-aware (a report for an older diff reads as absent ⇒ defer + re-review). | | **Approve / merge** | `pr-host/auto-approve.ts`, `auto-merge.ts` | Idempotent; both write `auto_review_audit`. Merge is `squash` by default, pinned with `expected_head_sha`. | | **Completion stamp** | `harness/completion-ref-writer.ts` | On merge, `resolveMergedPrFeatureId` → `stampCompletionRefOnMerge`: feature `status='shipped'` + `completion_ref`. | | **Report GUI + modes** | `apps/operator/app/harness/PrsTab.tsx` / `PrRow.tsx` + the `pr-reviewer-settings` route | Renders the agent report (recommendation chip, rationale, risks, observed checks) + the linked WI. **Manual** mode: a human reads the report and clicks Approve / Approve+merge. **Auto** mode: a claimed-owner-gated toggle. ON flips **three** settings — `pr_reviewer_role_enabled` (the master kill-switch that gates the whole auto path) **and** `auto_review` **and** `auto_merge`; OFF clears only `auto_review`/`auto_merge` and leaves the role enabled. The daemon then auto-applies. (The single owner-facing `autoModeOn` state is `role-enabled ∧ auto_review ∧ auto_merge`; granular per-lever control stays in the settings modal.) UI state that an agent/human may drive is URL-backed via nuqs: `prs_filter`, `prs_scope`, `prs_settings`, `prs_selected`, and `prs_report`. When the viewed harness belongs to a hive, `PrsTab` uses the audited `harnessProjects.lite` sync query plus `groupByHive` to expose a harness-vs-whole-hive scope; hive-scope rows route Approve / Approve+merge to the owning `member_slug`. Auto-status is shown only for open PRs on the viewed harness, because hive-scope rows from other members do not carry that member’s auto-mode settings and merged/closed rows should not render misleading “blocked: not open” noise. | | **Fork GC + dogfood witness** | `harness/fork-gc.ts`, `pr-host/dogfood-roundtrip.ts` | GC keeps a fork on merge, collects only abandoned operator-owned forks (dry-run by default). `verifyDogfoodRoundTrip` asserts the loop round-tripped (prTracked ∧ merged ∧ shipped ∧ linked). | ## S0 safety invariants [Section titled “S0 safety invariants”](#s0-safety-invariants) These are teeth-tested (`pr-host/*.test.ts`, `inbound-pipeline.test.ts`); keep them when editing the daemon: 1. **No auto-merge without checks-green + trusted author + `auto_merge` + not-revoked**, and — when a review report exists — a present `approve` report. `decideAutoReview` returns `approve_and_merge` only when checks are `success`; a red/pending/unknown check, untrusted/self/revoked author, or a `request_changes`/`reject` report can never reach `tryAutoMerge`. 2. **Fail-closed on a checks-fetch error** — if the check-run fetch errors, `checks_state` stays `unknown`, so the gate yields `approve` (never `approve_and_merge`); a checks-API outage cannot sneak a merge through. The safety here is a two-layer arrangement: `tryAutoMerge` on its own *permits* `checks_state=unknown` (it reads `unknown` as no-checks-configured), but the daemon never reaches it with `unknown` because `decideAutoReview` requires strictly `success` (`isChecksGreen` — `unknown` is **not** green) to return `approve_and_merge` — so `unknown` always degrades to approve-only. 3. **The agent never self-approves**, and **re-poll is idempotent** (the last-seen guard + `tryAutoApprove`/`tryAutoMerge` audit-state checks; a merged PR drops off the open list). 4. **First-sight race closed** — a brand-new trusted+green PR is *deferred*, not auto-merged, until its review report lands. ## Related [Section titled “Related”](#related) * **Vaporware guard** (`packages/operator-core/lib/plan-claim-guard.ts`): a separate hygiene check that a plan item flipped shipped/done naming a repo file actually has that file — born from this arc (P-042 was marked shipped but never built). * **Live dogfood runbook**: `platform:enable` → member `platform:contribute` → daemon review → owner approve → `platform:dogfood_verify`. Outward-facing (opens a real PR to the canonical repo) — owner-authorised, not part of CI.

# Roles — the operational reference

> Every built-in agent role — where it's defined, where its persona lives, and when it fires.

This is the operational reference for agent roles: what exists *now*, where each is defined, and when each fires. For the spec-level model (the four core roles and install shapes) see [The four core roles](/internal/docs/spec/roles). ## The registry [Section titled “The registry”](#the-registry) **`AGENT_ROLES`** in `packages/agent-mcp/src/role-config.ts` is the single runtime source of truth for built-in role ids — tool `roles:` allowlists, quota keys, and `byRole` guidance all key off it. The set is open: plugins contribute namespaced `<plugin>:<role>` ids at runtime. The built-ins, grouped as the file orders them: | Group | Roles | | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Pipeline | `scoper` · `architect` · `worker` · `validator` · `reviewer` · `debugger` · `documenter` · `curator` | | Chat surfaces | `operator` · `oracle` | | Hive | `bee` (the generic “do this task” agent — no pipeline spine, no chunk requirement) · `queen` (the Hive’s placement decider — the `coding`/`work` Hive blueprint’s `spine.decider`; steer-don’t-dispatch placement) · `overwatch` (read-everything system-health supervisor; nudge/observe/escalate only — its role envelope **denies** `fs-write` + `bash`) · `planner` (interactive plan-authoring session) | | Cross-cutting | `orchestrator` · `promote` · `security-reviewer` · `infra-reviewer` · `crosscheck` · `ui-qa` · `auditor` (read-only adversarial screen for remote-authored features) · `merge-resolver` (git-sync conflict resolution) · `content-fixer` (git-sync content-guard repairer — fixes quarantined files so they pass the content detector, leaves the tree clean, does **not** push) · `release-manager` (deploy go/no-go) · `release-fixer` (green-checkpoint gate fixer — reproduces a failing test, then fixes the code or quarantines a proven flake) · `sentinel` (read-mostly fleet watcher) | Two adjacent ids that are *not* agent roles: **`brain`** (`BRAIN_PRINCIPAL_ROLE`) is an RBAC role on the operator’s own *principal* — “only the brain approves spawns” is enforced at the dispatch layer, never carried by a spawned agent — and the per-feature **director** is a persona (`blueprints/base/prompts/director.md`) that emits the decision verbs (`NEXT_WORKER` / `NEXT_ARCHITECT` / `NEXT_VALIDATOR` / `DONE` / `ESCALATE`; see [Decision telemetry](/internal/docs/harness/decisions-timeline)) rather than an `AGENT_ROLES` entry. (The director is the **coding-factory** spine’s decider; the Hive’s deciders are real `AGENT_ROLES` entries — `queen` for placement automation, `operator` for decision-tree wakes.) ## Personas and layered resolution [Section titled “Personas and layered resolution”](#personas-and-layered-resolution) Built-in personas live at `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/base/prompts/<role>.md` — the shared role library — with blueprint-specific overrides at `blueprints/<blueprintId>/prompts/<role>.md`. (The old global harness `prompts/` dir was deleted in blueprint-role-bundling; there is no per-directory resolution `README` — the rules live in code, in `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/prompt-resolve.ts`.) Resolution walks the blueprint’s **extends-chain** and returns the first match: the blueprint’s own dir → each `extends` ancestor → `blueprints/base/prompts` (the universal library, always consulted). The old phase/department override axis was deleted with it — `ctx.phase` / `ctx.dept` are no longer consulted. Where a role splits a generic prefix from a blueprint specialization, the shared leaf is named `<role>.base.md` (e.g. `validator.base.md`, `worker.base.md`), *not* `base/<role>.md`. Post-bundling, **`AGENT_ROLES` is the complete built-in role universe** — the registry, not the filesystem, is the source of truth (blueprint-role-bundling D-008). The const deliberately enumerates the blueprint-shipped specialist roles too (`researcher`, `research-director`, `transformer`, `judge`, `gym-director`, `migration-director`, …), so the persona file set and `AGENT_ROLES` are intended to be co-extensive for built-ins. Only the program-blueprint-scoped roles (`advocate` / `voter`, resolved via `blueprints/vote`) and retired org-model roles (`ceo` / `coordinator`) remain as bare strings. Chat roles (`operator`, `oracle`) are assembled differently — by `packages/operator-core/lib/prompt-assembly.ts` from `apps/operator/prompts/<role>.persona.md` + the generated tools catalog. ## When pipeline roles fire (the `coding-factory` blueprint) [Section titled “When pipeline roles fire (the coding-factory blueprint)”](#when-pipeline-roles-fire-the-coding-factory-blueprint) The pipeline spine lives in the **`coding-factory`** blueprint (`libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/coding-factory/blueprint.yaml`) — *not* `coding`. (The 2026-06-18 rename moved the strict spine `coding` → `coding-factory` and **reused** the `coding` id for the Hive blueprint: `kind: hive`, `spine.decider: queen`, with only `DONE` / `ESCALATE` / `IDLE` edges and no `scoper → … → curator` spine.) The `coding-factory` blueprint declares the wiring: * **Spine:** `scoper → architect → worker → validator → reviewer → documenter → curator` — each work item’s kind/state determines the next role; the spine’s `deriveNext` interpreter consumes the director’s decision verbs. * **Reactive overlay:** the `debugger` fires *before a worker retry* once a feature accrues `knobs.debuggerThreshold` failed attempts — read-only root-cause notes for the next worker. * **Opt-in quality gates:** `tester` / `security` / `crosscheck` / `ui-qa`, e.g. `NEXT_CROSSCHECK` re-validates a pass with a different model. * **Finalize recipe:** `onDone: [curator, postCuratorOutputs, documenter, archive]`; `onEscalate: [curator]` — the curator always runs on terminal outcomes (see [Why a curator](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/curator)). Other blueprints are different shapes on the same engine — `blueprint:catalog` lists what each one runs. ## How a role spawn happens [Section titled “How a role spawn happens”](#how-a-role-spawn-happens) The DBOS pipeline (`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`) dispatches each role as a fresh one-shot agent process (see [Why fresh contexts](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/fresh-contexts)). The autonomous path and the interactive path are **two builders**, not one: autonomous spawns go through `invoke.ts` (invoke-once), which keeps its own richer inline assembly (substrate + feature-history + the G3 untrusted-peer wrapping a headless run needs), while `buildRoleLaunchSpec` (`packages/operator-core/lib/role-launch-spec.ts`) is the **interactive** primitive that powers role sessions (`psu --role <role> [--feature F-NNN]`). They converge on shared *leaves* — `resolvePromptFile` + `buildPrompt` over the same role `.md` personas, the `session-launch-dirs` helper, and the spawn-signing key — so the prompt is built identically and launch/resume can never drift; what differs is the mode-specific context fed into that one builder, and it should. ## Role disciplines that survive from the first generation [Section titled “Role disciplines that survive from the first generation”](#role-disciplines-that-survive-from-the-first-generation) Verified in the current persona files: * **Validator: default-reject.** “Your default is *reject*. The worker has to earn approval” (`blueprints/base/prompts/validator.md`). * **Validator: run it or it didn’t pass.** Evidence is enforced through the persona’s test-gate Protocol — every test-requiring claim VAL needs a covering test that *passed*, an untested claim VAL is itself a `[FAIL]`, and black-box first: “Never read the worker’s implementation code before running the tests.” The rule that overrides any “looks reasonable” intuition is “Don’t accept ‘looks reasonable.’ If you didn’t run it, it didn’t pass” (`blueprints/base/prompts/validator.md`). * **Curator: sole memory compactor.** Only the curator deletes/compacts harness memory ([details](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/curator)). The first-generation “role design rules” — one job per role, read-mostly where possible, default-skeptical gates — are visible throughout the current registry (the `auditor` and `sentinel` are explicitly read-only/read-mostly by design, per their `role-config.ts` entries).

# Smoke-test gate

> The DONE-blocking smoke gate — why it exists, what's wired today (gate machinery, a manual run+persist+notify loop, the health signal), and what still awaits its port (the automatic DONE-gate invocation).

Validators verify code-level claims; they don’t always start the real service and hit real endpoints. A feature can “pass” — unit test green, contract documented, migration applied — while the deployed service 500s from config drift, a missing env var, or a startup race. The **smoke-test gate** exists to catch that class of failure *before* a pipeline declares DONE. The principle (“quality through truth”: verify service startup, don’t trust test output alone) came from the first harness generation and still holds. ## What is wired today [Section titled “What is wired today”](#what-is-wired-today) **The gate.** The durable finalizer’s planner (`planFinalization` in `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/orchestrator-finalize.ts`) treats the smoke result as a first-class DONE gate, exactly like an open `needs-human` plan item: when `smokeEnabled` is set and `smokePassed === false`, finalization is **blocked** — no curator/documenter recipe runs and the pipeline does not complete. **A manual run.** A live, registered route runs the smoke script on demand: `POST /api/harness/:slug/smoke-test/run` (`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/harness/orchestration-actions.ts`, loopback-auth; flattened into the route table at `routes/index.ts`) spawns `service-smoke-test.sh`, which writes the `smoke-pass.md` / `smoke-failure.md` sentinels (clearing the failure sentinel on pass). It is also reachable through the device-tier shim `POST /api/device/harnesses/:slug/smoke-test` (`routes/device/harnesses.ts`). The script then POSTs its aggregated result to `POST /api/internal/smoke-test-event`, which upserts the `harness_shared.harness_smoke_test` row and — on a pass→fail *transition* only — pushes a high-importance `smoke-fail` attention item. So the sentinels `smoke_test_clean` reads are exactly what this live endpoint writes; they are not only “earlier engines / out-of-band”. **The health signal.** A smoke failure surfaces through two differently-named composite checks with **different data sources**: `smoke_test_clean` (the harness-readers composite health in `packages/operator-core/lib/harness-readers.ts`) fails when the `smoke-failure.md` FS sentinel exists in the harness state dir; `smoke_passing` (the operator-UI `HealthBadge`) fails when the latest PG `harness_smoke_test` row has `status: 'fail'` (the “see smoke-failure.md” text it shows is only a label, not its source). That same `harness_smoke_test` row (written by the smoke-test-event route above) is also what the Planning attention feed reads to list failing harnesses — so a failed smoke run is visible across the FS-fed health check, the PG-fed badge, and the Planning feed. **The hooks.** `on-smoke-pass` / `on-smoke-fail` are catalogued in the hook registry (`packages/operator-core/lib/known-hooks.ts`) with `status: 'lost'` — bash-era [lifecycle](/internal/docs/harness/hooks) points the bash→DBOS migration dropped (EI-95 backlog): “not fired, not advertised”. `runHook(name)` itself takes any string and just looks for a `<name>.sh` file (no validation, and a test exercises `on-smoke-pass` only for its `<ts>-<name>.log` log-file naming, not an env shape), but `getKnownHooks()` returns only the `live` set (`afterDone`, `on-escalate`), and the hook write/delete API rejects any non-live name with `unknown hook: <name>`. So an operator cannot install an `on-smoke-pass.sh` / `on-smoke-fail.sh` hook through the API, and nothing in the live pipeline ever fires them. ## What is NOT yet wired: the automatic DONE-gate invocation [Section titled “What is NOT yet wired: the automatic DONE-gate invocation”](#what-is-not-yet-wired-the-automatic-done-gate-invocation) The manual/on-demand loop above runs and persists a smoke result, but the durable finalizer never *calls* the smoke runner itself as part of declaring DONE. The runner call site passes the gate explicitly off (`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/orchestrator-runner.ts`: > “Smoke gate is config-gated-off for \~all harnesses; not yet ported into the durable finalizer (`runSmokeTest` is a main-loop-internal). Tracked as a Phase F follow-up; pass not-run so it never blocks here.” — `smokeEnabled: false, smokePassed: null`). Because the finalizer always hands the gate `smokeEnabled: false`, the DONE-gate machinery — which *would* block on `smokeEnabled && smokePassed === false` — never trips on the automatic path. A smoke run that fails today still records its sentinel + PG row + attention item, but it cannot, on its own, stop a pipeline from completing until that Phase F follow-up wires the finalizer to invoke and consume the runner. In short: **gate machinery live, manual runner wired, automatic gate invocation pending.** If you need a service-level check on a harness today, run it on demand (`POST /api/harness/:slug/smoke-test/run`) or lean on the testing surface (the project’s own test/E2E suites — see [Testing](/internal/docs/testing)). ## The runner shape (and the bash-era gating still awaiting port) [Section titled “The runner shape (and the bash-era gating still awaiting port)”](#the-runner-shape-and-the-bash-era-gating-still-awaiting-port) `service-smoke-test.sh` is what the manual endpoint above spawns, and its behavior is the shape the automatic gate will reuse: read the smoke config (`urls` of `{ url, expectStatus, expectText? }`, optional `startupCmd` + `startupWaitSeconds`, default 30), start the service if the first URL isn’t responding, curl each URL, then on all-pass write `smoke-pass.md` (clearing any `smoke-failure.md`) and on any-fail write `smoke-failure.md` and reopen the most-recently-passed feature as failing. The config is OFF by default (`smokeTest.enabled: false`). What did **not** survive the bash→DBOS migration is the two automatic *gating modes* the bash main loop ran: `onDone` (block mission completion) and `onFeaturePass` (revert a feature before the documenter runs, so docs are never generated for a broken state) — these are the Phase F follow-up the finalizer still passes `smokeEnabled: false` in lieu of. ## Related [Section titled “Related”](#related) * [Lifecycle hooks](/internal/docs/harness/hooks) — `on-smoke-pass` / `on-smoke-fail` * [Decision telemetry](/internal/docs/harness/decisions-timeline) — the health-check family `smoke_test_clean` belongs to

# Steering & chat

> Which surface to use to steer running agents — durable messages, role-scoped chats, live coord nudges, turn interruption, and human gates.

The first-generation harness had one steering surface: a chat box in the retired web UI. Today steering is several purpose-built surfaces; picking the right one matters because they differ in durability, latency, and who reads them. ## Which surface for which job [Section titled “Which surface for which job”](#which-surface-for-which-job) | You want to… | Use | | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | Leave durable direction/context for whoever works a feature next | `messages:send` (work-item-scoped) | | Have an interactive conversation with a role agent inside a harness | `agent_chats:*` | | Nudge a *live* agent right now (or wake an idle one) | `coord:send` (with `wake: 'required'`/`'optimistic'`) | | Make a running agent stop / wrap up | `turn:interrupt` | | Answer a question an agent asked | the decision card / `conversations:answer` / `coord` escalation | | Steer the whole Pot (not one agent) | the operator chat surface | ## Durable messages — `messages:*` [Section titled “Durable messages — messages:\*”](#durable-messages--messages) `messages:send` (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/messages/send.ts`) writes a durable message that survives across spawns — the right surface for inter-agent hand-offs and human direction tied to work. Messages are **work-item-scoped**: with `to_feature_id` set they form that feature’s thread; without it they’re harness-level (`packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/messages/inbox.ts`). Every fresh spawn working that item reads the thread via `messages:inbox` — this is how direction reaches a [fresh context](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/fresh-contexts) that didn’t exist when you wrote it. ## Role-scoped chats — `agent_chats:*` [Section titled “Role-scoped chats — agent\_chats:\*”](#role-scoped-chats--agent_chats) For an interactive back-and-forth with a role agent inside a harness (the “pair” primitive): `agent_chats:create` opens a persistent chat, `agent_chats:chat` streams a turn (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/agent_chats/chat.ts` — transcripts, cost rollup, and feature-lock checks handled server-side), and `agent_chats:send_message` is the fire-and-forget non-streaming append used by autonomous dispatches. Use this when you want a conversation; use `messages:*` when you want durable direction. ## Live coordination — `coord:*` [Section titled “Live coordination — coord:\*”](#live-coordination--coord) `coord:send` reaches a *live* (or wakeable) agent’s coordination inbox; deltas are injected into the recipient mid-turn after its tool calls. The default (no `wake`) is inject-only — the message lands in the inbox and is seen on the recipient’s next natural turn. Set `wake` to *also* re-invoke an idle recipient now; agents are armed for inbox-wake at session start. The arg carries an intent (`'required' | 'optimistic'`), not a plain toggle: * `wake: 'required'` — the wake MUST land. A clean miss (it reached wakeable addressees but no awake/watching session, and none were staged for a Pause) returns `recipient_absent: true` plus an explanatory note rather than failing silently. The message is still injected to the inbox for the next turn; only the re-invoke missed. * `wake: 'optimistic'` — silent best-effort over a durable backstop (wake if present, shrug if not — e.g. the Queen survey re-dispatches anyway). A miss is *not* surfaced; the inbox row persisted regardless. The legacy boolean still coerces: `true` → `'required'`, `false`/omitted → no wake. `coord:escalate` raises a durable escalation a human (or the operator) must resolve. Don’t use coord for state that must outlive the session — that’s what messages and work items are for. ## Turn interruption — `turn:interrupt` [Section titled “Turn interruption — turn:interrupt”](#turn-interruption--turninterrupt) To make a running agent stop, `turn:interrupt` (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/turn/interrupt.ts`) supports two modes — operator-mediated, reason-required, audited, and storm-rate-limited (max 10 interrupts per actor in a rolling 60s window, sourced from the audit log): * **cooperative** — injects a high-priority `yield` line into the target’s coord stream; the agent finishes its atomic step, releases locks, checkpoints state, and ends its turn. But when the target holds file locks (a critical section), the cooperative interrupt **DEFERS** — it returns `deferred: true` and injects *no* yield, so the peer can finish its atomic edit and release its locks. Retry shortly, or escalate to `force` (which warns it may orphan a half-written edit). * **force** — ends the turn *now*, mid-thought (Ctrl+C to a managed pty / SIGINT headless); no checkpoint is guaranteed. You cannot interrupt your own turn. ## Human gates: questions, escalations, approvals [Section titled “Human gates: questions, escalations, approvals”](#human-gates-questions-escalations-approvals) Agents pause for humans through structured gates rather than free chat: a mid-tool decision card (`ctx.askUser` / `chat:ask_choice`; with the `papercusp-inbox-durable-escalations` flag the card is also mirrored to a durable coord escalation so it can be answered later from the inbox), knowledge-first questions routed by topic (`coord:ask` → a conversation answered via `conversations:answer`), pipeline escalations (`harness:escalation` surfaces the blocker; resolution re-enters the pipeline), and plan items marked `needs-human` (which also block a DONE finalization — see [Smoke-test gate](/internal/docs/harness/smoke-test) for the gate family). ## Observing without steering [Section titled “Observing without steering”](#observing-without-steering) `fleet:bee_mail` renders what a specific agent has received/sent (the bee-dossier view) — for *inspection*, not for reading your own inbox (`coord:inbox`) or deriving who’s-on-what (`fleet:assignments`). The fleet-wide steering surface — scheduling, placement, prioritization — is the operator/Queen’s job; see [Operator persona](/internal/docs/agents/operator-persona).

# Worktrees & isolation

> Where git worktrees are (and deliberately are not) used today — phase worktrees, transient scratch envs for verification, and the shared-tree rule for the dev fleet.

The first-generation harness used a git worktree per parallel lane (`.harness/worktrees/<feature-id>/`) so concurrent workers couldn’t race each other’s `git checkout`. That mechanism retired with the bash loop, but the underlying idea — *give a unit of work its own filesystem view instead of fighting over HEAD* — survives in three distinct, narrower forms. ## 1. Phase worktrees (staging / testing / production) [Section titled “1. Phase worktrees (staging / testing / production)”](#1-phase-worktrees-staging--testing--production) A harness project can have up to three phased worktrees (`packages/operator-core/lib/harness-phases.ts`): * **staging** → the project’s main path * **testing / production** → an explicit per-phase `path` override carried on the project’s workspace-registry entry, falling back to a sibling checkout at `<path>--testing` / `<path>--production` when no override is set. The override takes precedence; the sibling is the default. The override lives on the registry `phases` blob and is not read from `config.json` (`deprecate-harness-config-json-2026-06-06`). Every `?phase=` API route resolves through `phasePath()`. The FS watcher is phase-aware — it walks all three phases’ `.papercusp/` directories — but as of `fs-watcher-retirement-2026-05-10` its only remaining mirror is proposals (`harness_shared.harness_proposals_shared`, keyed by `(harness_slug, phase, proposal_id)`). Every other former mirror (tests, escalations, git log, decisions, checkpoints, hook logs, screenshots, plan review, smoke, branch actions, and the `harness_phases` mirror itself) is now retired: that state is written to PG at *producer* time (POSTs to `/api/internal/*`) rather than mirrored from disk. Agents resolve a phase’s absolute path with the `harness:phase_path` tool. The multi-phase surface is gated by the `papercusp-harness-phases` [feature flag](/internal/docs/posthog/feature-flags). ## 2. Transient scratch worktrees for verification [Section titled “2. Transient scratch worktrees for verification”](#2-transient-scratch-worktrees-for-verification) The worker chunk loop wants to typecheck a worker’s pending edits **before** committing them, in a tree that can’t see other concurrent workers’ WIP. The primitive is `scratch-env.ts` (`libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/scratch-env.ts`): create a transient git worktree at integration HEAD, apply the worker’s pending edits for its locked files, symlink the heavy gitignored cache dirs (`node_modules`, `.turbo`, …) back to the main repo so caches stay warm, run the check, tear down. Setup is \~60 ms; `git worktree prune` at setup self-heals orphans from crashed runs; many workers can hold scratch envs simultaneously. The verification check runs shell-free: the config-sourced command is whitespace-split into a plain argv and spawned without a shell (audit P-030). A command containing shell metacharacters is rejected (exit 126), and missing or non-executable commands map to 127 / 126 — all of which route to the “unrunnable / fail-open” lane. A misconfigured gate therefore never blocks a commit. This is the direct descendant of the legacy lane-worktree insight: parallel workers sharing one working tree contaminate each other’s verification signal, and a cheap throwaway worktree is the cleanest cross-platform fix. A sibling primitive, `tmpfs.ts`, hands subprocesses RAM-resident scratch *directories* for their inputs (`/dev/shm` on Linux) — state is PG-canonical, but external agent CLIs still need a path on disk to read. ## 3. What deliberately does NOT use worktrees: the dev fleet [Section titled “3. What deliberately does NOT use worktrees: the dev fleet”](#3-what-deliberately-does-not-use-worktrees-the-dev-fleet) For Papercusp’s own development, concurrent agents work **one shared checkout on `staging`** — no per-agent worktrees, no feature branches.
