Isolation comes from coordination instead of tree-splitting: the per-edit file-lock hook serializes same-file edits (`locks:*`), declared intents make work visible (`coord:*`), and a background git-sync routine owns commit + push. The trade — messy interleaved history for zero merge-reconciliation tax — is deliberate; see the repo guide (`CLAUDE.md`, “Branch discipline”). The two models coexist because they solve different problems: worktrees isolate *machine verification* (a typecheck must not see foreign WIP); locks + coord serialize *human-scale collaboration* (two agents shouldn’t edit one file at once, but they *should* see each other’s work immediately). ## Historical note: competition mode [Section titled “Historical note: competition mode”](#historical-note-competition-mode) The bash harness briefly ran a Conductor-inspired **competition mode** — N workers attacking the same feature in sibling worktrees, the validator picking a winner. It was replaced pre-cutover by the **synthesizer** (read every lane’s diff, compose one shipping branch), which has itself been dormant since the legacy run-loop retired (`libs/papercusp/_retired/orchestrator-run-loop/`). Today’s analogue for “multiple independent attempts, judged” is work-item **redundancy** (replica dispatch + `work_items:judge_redundancy`), which operates at the work-item layer rather than the git layer. ## Related [Section titled “Related”](#related) * [Decision log](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/log) — the original worktree decision and its rationale * [Storage policy](/internal/docs/system/storage-policy) — why state moved off the filesystem even as worktrees stayed for code

# Marketplace implementation

> Ship state of papercuspai.com — what's live, what's planned, what's still missing.

> **Webapp retired (2026-05-14).** Any `localhost:3055` or `localhost:3070` URL on this page is only reachable while the **Tauri dev shell** is running. Start it with `cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev`. Superseded — describes the retired papercuspai.com marketplace This page documents the standalone **`papercuspai.com` marketplace** (`papercupai/papercusp-registry`, Cloudflare Pages + Tunnel + a Hono `marketplace-api` on `:3057`) as of the 2026-04-27 handoff. That public marketplace surface is **no longer the current distribution path.** What replaced it: the in-app **Cupboard** — a GitHub-backed listing service served by `apps/operator-public` (Cloudflare Workers + Hono + D1), with the desktop operator owning the listing UI. Listings span five kinds (`harness | blueprint | plugin | tool-pack | learning-pack`); the `snapshot` kind was retired (Cupboard migration 008 drops it from the `listing_kind` CHECK constraint — see `retire-snapshots-instance-spec-2026-06-09`). Publish/install flow through the `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/cupboard.ts` operator routes and the `apps/papercusp-publish` Worker, with agent verbs `blueprint:*` (`catalog`/`create`/`extend`/`validate`/`publish`). There is no `snapshots:*` verb — the reproducible clone is the lightweight InstanceSpec, not a published snapshot. Read the rest of this page as a historical record of the earlier design, not the current system. Handoff notice — last updated 2026-04-27 This page is the canonical handoff document for marketplace implementation. If a future agent or operator picks up the work, **read this in full first**. Specifically: 1. The OAuth client\_secret was leaked in a chat session and **may not have been rotated yet** — check `~/.papercusp/marketplace-secrets.env` and rotate at github.com → Developer Settings → Papercusp Marketplace. 2. The marketplace was extracted to its own repo `papercupai/papercusp-registry` (private) — **NOT in `papercupai/papercusp` anymore**. 3. Both `localhost:3055` and `papercuspai.com` exist intentionally; see “Two surfaces, often confused” below. 4. The CF API token at `~/.cloudflare-token` lacks Tunnel:Edit and (likely) R2:Edit scopes. Tunnel + R2 changes need user action in CF dashboard. The marketplace is the public-facing component of Papercusp described in [§11 Distribution](/internal/docs/spec/distribution). This page tracks what’s actually shipped vs. what’s still spec’d-only. ## Two surfaces, often confused [Section titled “Two surfaces, often confused”](#two-surfaces-often-confused) There are **two distinct user-facing apps** in this project, both legitimate, both needed. They serve different audiences: | Surface | URL | Source | Audience | Purpose | | -------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Substrate operator dashboard** | <http://localhost:3055> | `libs/papercusp/apps/web/` (in [papercupai/papercusp](https://github.com/papercupai/papercusp) submodule) | Anyone running their own Papercusp install | Manage local API keys, browse the catalog with installed-state, view harness state, sign in for publishing | | **Public marketplace** | <https://papercuspai.com> | `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-site/` (in [papercupai/papercusp-registry](https://github.com/papercupai/papercusp-registry) submodule) | Anyone on the internet discovering Papercusp | Browse the catalog read-only, read docs, see featured packages, get install instructions | ### Why both exist (not a duplicate, not a stale-link mistake) [Section titled “Why both exist (not a duplicate, not a stale-link mistake)”](#why-both-exist-not-a-duplicate-not-a-stale-link-mistake) * The substrate operator UI is **part of every Papercusp install** — anyone self-hosting gets it. Its `/marketplace` page hits a LOCAL `/api/marketplace/catalog` route, which proxies to `api.papercuspai.com/catalog` and adds local install state (“you have this installed”, “newer version available”, etc.). That’s only meaningful if you have an install. * The public marketplace at papercuspai.com is **install-free** — it just shows the catalog. No login, no install state, no API keys. Anyone evaluating Papercusp lands here first. The substrate UI and public site share the same data source (`api.papercuspai.com`) but render different concerns. **Not a stale duplicate.** ## Live URLs [Section titled “Live URLs”](#live-urls) | URL | What | Status | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | | <https://papercuspai.com/> | Marketplace landing page (CF Pages, static Next.js) | ✅ Live | | <https://papercuspai.com/marketplace/> | Catalog grid + client-side search | ✅ Live | | [https://papercuspai.com/marketplace/\[slug\]/](https://papercuspai.com/marketplace/%5Bslug%5D/) | Package detail page (manifest, README, install command, versions) | ✅ Live | | <https://papercuspai.com/docs/> | Quickstart docs (placeholder) | ✅ Live | | <https://api.papercuspai.com/healthz> | Liveness probe | ✅ Live | | <https://api.papercuspai.com/catalog> | Full catalog JSON | ✅ Live | | <https://api.papercuspai.com/catalog/:slug> | Per-package detail | ✅ Live | | <https://api.papercuspai.com/catalog/:slug/:version> | Per-version detail (manifest + README) | ✅ Live | | <https://api.papercuspai.com/download/:slug/:version> | Tarball stream | ✅ Live | ## Architecture (current state) [Section titled “Architecture (current state)”](#architecture-current-state) 
```plaintext
papercuspai.com  (Cloudflare Pages — static Next.js export)
   │
   │ runtime fetch (CORS-allowed origin)
   ▼
api.papercuspai.com  (Cloudflare Tunnel — public ingress)
   │
   │ tunnel → cloudflared (token mode)
   │   tunnel UUID c53515b3-edfe-4e99-813b-e3916ae9d02c (papercupai-api)
   ▼
http://localhost:3057  (marketplace-api — Hono on Node)
   │   ../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/
   │
   │ filesystem read
   ▼
~/.papercusp/marketplace-storage/<slug>/<version>/
   ├── papercusp.json          (manifest)
   ├── README.md               (rendered on detail page)
   └── <slug>-<version>.tar.gz (the install)
```

Deployed via `wrangler pages deploy ./out --project-name papercuspai --branch main`. | | CF Tunnel ingress | `api.papercuspai.com` → `localhost:3057` | Routed through existing `papercupai-api` tunnel; managed via Zero Trust dashboard. | | Build pattern | Two-base env split | `BUILD_API_BASE=http://localhost:3057` for `generateStaticParams`; `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE=https://api.papercuspai.com` for client bundle runtime fetches. | | Process supervision | `~/.config/systemd/user/marketplace-api.service` | systemd —user transient unit; auto-restart on failure; logs at `~/.papercusp/logs/marketplace-api.log`. | | Sample packages | `papercup-coding@0.1.0`, `papercup-org@0.1.0` (stub) | Filesystem-backed at `~/.papercusp/marketplace-storage/`. | ### Endpoints implemented in marketplace-api [Section titled “Endpoints implemented in marketplace-api”](#endpoints-implemented-in-marketplace-api) 
```typescript
GET    /healthz                          → "ok"
GET    /catalog                          → { catalog: [{...manifest, versions[]}], storageRoot }
GET    /catalog/:slug                    → { slug, versions, latest: manifest }
GET    /catalog/:slug/:version           → { slug, version, manifest, readme }
GET    /download/:slug/:version          → tarball stream (application/gzip)
POST   /publish/:slug/:version           → multipart upload (manifest + tarball + readme)
DELETE /catalog/:slug/:version           → unpublish (dev-only)
```
 POST `/publish` is currently in **open** mode (no auth). It supports a PAT-auth mode via `PAPERCUSP_MARKETPLACE_AUTH=pat` that verifies the Authorization header against the GitHub user API and records the verified login as `publishedBy`. ### Marketplace site features [Section titled “Marketplace site features”](#marketplace-site-features) * **Landing page** (`/`) — live-fetches 3 featured packages from `/catalog`; “How it works” section; “Publish your own harness” CTA with sample command. * **Catalog grid** (`/marketplace/`) — live fetch + client-side search by name/description/author. Cards show name, version, author, description, role count, plugin count. * **Package detail** (`/marketplace/[slug]/`) — manifest + rendered README; install command with copy button; download tarball link; sidebar listing roles (with preferred models), plugins, schema files, version history, substrate compat range. * **Docs** (`/docs/`) — quickstart placeholder with CLI install/run commands. Full reference link to spec site. ## Implementation plan — by spec section [Section titled “Implementation plan — by spec section”](#implementation-plan--by-spec-section) For each spec’d feature in §11, this is the planned implementation route. Items are ordered by priority (auth → reliability → UX → discovery → governance). ### Phase M1 — Auth on publish (§11.6) [Section titled “Phase M1 — Auth on publish (§11.6)”](#phase-m1--auth-on-publish-116) **Goal:** Anyone publishing under `@user/foo` must prove ownership of GitHub user `user`. **Plan:** 1. Add GitHub OAuth app at `github.com/papercupai` (or repurpose existing). Redirect URI: `https://api.papercuspai.com/v1/auth/github/callback`. 2. Add session middleware to marketplace-api (signed cookies; HMAC key from env). 3. New endpoints: * `GET /v1/auth/github/login` → redirect to GitHub authorize URL * `GET /v1/auth/github/callback` → exchange code, verify token, set session cookie * `GET /v1/auth/me` → return verified GitHub identity * `POST /v1/auth/logout` → clear cookie 4. Modify `POST /publish/:slug/:version`: * Reject if no session cookie OR session’s GitHub login doesn’t match the `@owner` namespace prefix in `:slug`. * Stamp manifest with `publishedBy: <github-login>` server-side. 5. CLI `papercusp publish` — open browser to `/v1/auth/github/login`, capture session cookie, persist to `~/.papercusp/credentials.json` (mode 0600). 6. Rejection messages must be specific: `"foo/bar" requires GitHub user "foo"; you're authenticated as "baz"`. **Estimate:** 3-4 hours work. CSRF protection, scope validation, retry-on-token-expiry are the hard parts. ### Phase M2 — R2 storage backing ✅ CODE SHIPPED (gated, awaiting credentials) [Section titled “Phase M2 — R2 storage backing ✅ CODE SHIPPED (gated, awaiting credentials)”](#phase-m2--r2-storage-backing--code-shipped-gated-awaiting-credentials) **Status:** All code paths shipped. Activates the moment R2 credentials are added to the env. **No code changes needed when the user has the bucket + token.** **What shipped:** * New module `apps/marketplace-api/src/r2.ts` — S3-SDK against R2 endpoint; `isR2Configured()`/`putFile`/`putBytes`/`presign`/`exists`/`deleteKey`. Lazy client init, throws clearly if env missing. * Schema delta `sql/006-r2-backing.sql` — adds `r2_key`, `r2_signature_key`, `r2_uploaded_at` columns to `package_versions` (idempotent). * `POST /publish/:slug/:version` — after the FS write, also uploads tarball + `signature.json` to R2 (best-effort, non-fatal). Records `r2_key` in DB. Response now includes `r2: { key }` or `r2: { configured: false }`. * `GET /download/:slug/:version` — when R2 is configured AND the version has been uploaded there, redirects to a 60s presigned URL (or to `R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/<key>` when set). Falls back to FS streaming otherwise. * New endpoint `GET /v1/storage/status` — returns `{ configured, account?, bucket?, publicBaseUrl? }` for ops visibility. * New endpoint `POST /v1/storage/backfill-r2` — operator-token-gated; uploads up to 100 unbackfilled versions per call. Idempotent (skips versions with `r2_key` already set). * npm deps added: `@aws-sdk/client-s3`, `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner`. **To activate:** 1. Create R2 bucket in Cloudflare dashboard (account `f896982ea2f6d507e4f29eeecbd26e94`) 2. Generate an R2 API token (R2 → Manage API Tokens → “Object Read & Write” on the bucket) 3. Append to `~/.papercusp/marketplace-secrets.env`: 
   ```plaintext
   R2_ACCOUNT_ID=f896982ea2f6d507e4f29eeecbd26e94
   R2_BUCKET=papercusp-marketplace-tarballs
   R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<from token>
   R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<from token>
   # Optional: R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://r2.papercuspai.com (if you set up a public bucket / CDN)
   ```
 4. `bin/overmind-all restart marketplace` 5. Verify: `curl localhost:3057/v1/storage/status` → `"configured": true` 6. Backfill existing tarballs: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAPERCUSP_MARKETPLACE_OPERATOR_TOKEN" localhost:3057/v1/storage/backfill-r2` After backfill, all downloads transparently 302-redirect to R2. Future publishes dual-write FS + R2. **Verified:** marketplace-api boots cleanly in disabled mode (`[r2] disabled — set ...`); `/v1/storage/status` returns `{"configured":false}`; `/download/...` still serves from FS. No regressions. ### Phase M2.5 — Postgres metadata table [Section titled “Phase M2.5 — Postgres metadata table”](#phase-m25--postgres-metadata-table) **Goal:** Replace `listSlugs` / `listVersions` filesystem walks with a Postgres-backed catalog. **Schema** (in `papercusp_marketplace` schema): 
```sql
CREATE TABLE packages (
  slug          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,         -- @owner/package
  owner         TEXT NOT NULL,            -- verified GitHub login
  description   TEXT,
  homepage      TEXT,
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  retracted     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'  -- 'active' | 'deprecated' | 'withdrawn' | 'quarantined'
);


CREATE TABLE package_versions (
  slug              TEXT REFERENCES packages(slug),
  version           TEXT NOT NULL,
  manifest_json     JSONB NOT NULL,
  readme_md         TEXT,
  install_shape     TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'iterative' | 'scheduled' | 'reactive' | 'passive'
  capability_tiers  JSONB,                  -- { low: N, medium: N, high: N } counts
  service_pins      JSONB,                  -- { tasks: '^1.0', secrets: '^2.0', ... }
  signature         TEXT NOT NULL,          -- Ed25519 base64
  tarball_size      BIGINT NOT NULL,
  tarball_sha256    TEXT NOT NULL,
  tarball_r2_key    TEXT NOT NULL,
  published_by      TEXT NOT NULL,          -- GitHub login
  published_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  yanked_at         TIMESTAMPTZ,
  yanked_reason     TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (slug, version)
);


CREATE INDEX idx_package_versions_published_at ON package_versions(published_at DESC);
```
 **Estimate:** 1 hour for schema + 1 hour migrating reads. Bundle with M2. ### Phase M3 — Tarball signing (Ed25519) [Section titled “Phase M3 — Tarball signing (Ed25519)”](#phase-m3--tarball-signing-ed25519) **Goal:** Detect tampering between publish and install. **Plan:** 1. Generate marketplace’s Ed25519 keypair; private key stored at `~/.papercusp/marketplace-key.pem` on the marketplace-api host (mode 0600); public key published at `https://api.papercuspai.com/v1/keys/marketplace.pub`. 2. At publish: * Compute SHA-256 of the tarball. * Sign `${slug}\n${version}\n${sha256}\n${published_by}\n${published_at}` with the marketplace key. * Store the signature in `package_versions.signature`. 3. At install: * CLI fetches the marketplace public key (cached locally with TTL of 1 day). * Verifies signature against the metadata it received from `/catalog/:slug/:version`. * Independently SHA-256 the downloaded tarball and verify it matches the signed sha256. 4. Failure modes: * Signature invalid → install hard-fails with “tarball tampered or marketplace key changed”. * Public key fetched but doesn’t match cached → CLI prompts user to confirm rotation (single line, audit logged). **Estimate:** 2 hours. The crypto is `tweetnacl`-grade primitives. ### Phase M4 — Search + tags (Typesense) ✅ SHIPPED real fuzzy search [Section titled “Phase M4 — Search + tags (Typesense) ✅ SHIPPED real fuzzy search”](#phase-m4--search--tags-typesense--shipped-real-fuzzy-search) **Status:** Live with Typesense backend; falls back gracefully to LIKE-based SQL when Typesense is unavailable. **What shipped:** * New module `apps/marketplace-api/src/typesense.ts` — collection schema, `indexPackage` / `unindexPackage` / `searchTypesense` * `marketplace_packages` collection (slug, description, owner, latest\_version, capabilities\[], plugins\[], shape, retracted, downloads\_30d, updated\_at) * `/v1/search?q=…&shape=…` hits Typesense first with fuzzy matching (2-typo tolerance + prefix), falls back to SQL LIKE on failure * `&shape=` filter facet (iterative / scheduled / reactive / passive) * Response includes `backend: 'typesense' | 'sql'` so callers know which path served them * Sync hooks: every `POST /publish/...` upserts the doc; every `withdraw`/`quarantine` removes it; `unwithdraw`/`unquarantine`/(un)`deprecate` re-syncs the retracted state * Operator endpoint `POST /v1/admin/reindex-typesense` — bulk re-index existing packages (idempotent) **Verified:** typo `codign` correctly resolves to `papercup-coding` (“Did you mean?” semantics for free); responses through tunnel show `backend: 'typesense'`. ### Phase M5 — Update / uninstall flows (§11.7, §11.8) [Section titled “Phase M5 — Update / uninstall flows (§11.7, §11.8)”](#phase-m5--update--uninstall-flows-117-118) **Goal:** `papercusp update <name>` and `papercusp uninstall <name>` work per spec. **Plan:** 1. Substrate-side state: `installed_plugins` table tracking `{ slug, version, applied_migration_index, granted_capabilities, install_path, installed_at }`. 2. CLI `papercusp update <slug>` flow per [§11.7](/spec/distribution/#117-update-flow): * Fetch latest version from marketplace * Diff capabilities (added/removed/renamed/major) * Prompt only for additions (unless major version → re-prompt all) * Snapshot old version to `~/.papercusp/installed/<slug>/.snapshots/<old-version>/` (manifest + schema dump + granted-caps) * Apply new migrations from `applied_migration_index` * Reconcile routines (delete renamed, insert new, update existing in-place) * Replace plugin code on disk 3. CLI `papercusp uninstall <slug>` flow per [§11.8](/spec/distribution/#118-uninstall-flow): * Default: stop code, leave data * `--purge-data`: also drop plugin schema 4. CLI `papercusp rollback <slug>`: re-mount snapshot version (DB rollback is user’s responsibility — substrate doesn’t run down-migrations). **Estimate:** 5-6 hours. The capability-diff logic is the hard part; everything else is filesystem + Postgres mechanics. ### Phase M6 — Retraction (§11.9) [Section titled “Phase M6 — Retraction (§11.9)”](#phase-m6--retraction-119) **Goal:** Server-side package status — Deprecated / Yanked / Withdrawn / Quarantined. **Plan:** 1. Add `retracted` column to `packages` (already in M2.5 schema). 2. Add `yanked_at` / `yanked_reason` to `package_versions` (already in M2.5 schema). 3. New endpoints: * `POST /v1/packages/:slug/deprecate` (owner-only) * `POST /v1/packages/:slug/withdraw` (owner OR operator) * `POST /v1/packages/:slug/quarantine` (operator-only) * `POST /v1/packages/:slug/versions/:version/yank` (owner OR operator) 4. Marketplace-api list endpoints (`/catalog`, `/v1/search`) filter by `retracted` status: * `deprecated` → still returned with a flag in the response * `yanked` versions → hidden from listings * `withdrawn` packages → hidden from listings * `quarantined` packages → hidden + tarball returns 410 immediately 5. Substrate periodically polls `/v1/installed-status?slugs=A,B,C&versions=...` (every hour) to detect retractions of installed plugins. On `quarantined`, auto-pause routines from that plugin and surface UI alert. 6. Public audit log at `papercuspai.com/security/quarantines` (page generated at build, sourced from `/v1/admin/quarantine-log`). **Estimate:** 3-4 hours including the polling client in the substrate. ### Phase M7 — Detail page rich UX [Section titled “Phase M7 — Detail page rich UX”](#phase-m7--detail-page-rich-ux) **Goal:** Detail page surfaces install shape, service pins, capability tiers (already mentioned in §11.4). **Plan:** 1. Update `/marketplace/[slug]/page.tsx` to read these fields from `manifest`: * `manifest.shape` (from §4.1) — render as a colored badge * `manifest.services` (from §8.4.1) — render as a list with version ranges * `manifest.capabilities` — bucket by tier (§10.6.1) and show “low: N · medium: N · high: N” with a warning icon if high > 0 2. Add a “Trust” badge: * ✅ Verified (signed + verified GitHub identity) * ⚠ Unverified (valid namespace, no signature) 3. Add a “Last updated” date and version count. 4. Show `publishedBy` (GitHub login with link to user profile). **Estimate:** 2-3 hours. Pure UI; data is already in the manifest once M1 + M3 land. ### Phase M8 — Author profiles + reviews ✅ SHIPPED [Section titled “Phase M8 — Author profiles + reviews ✅ SHIPPED”](#phase-m8--author-profiles--reviews--shipped) **Status:** Live in production. **What shipped:** * Schema `papercusp_marketplace.{authors, reviews}` + view `v_package_review_summary` (one review per `(slug, author)`, 1-1000 char body, rating 1-5) * OAuth callback (web + device flows) auto-upserts the author from GitHub login response * Endpoints: * `GET /v1/authors` — list known authors (build-time enumeration) * `GET /v1/authors/:login` — public profile * `GET /v1/authors/:login/packages` — packages where slug is `@login/...` OR `owner = login` * `PATCH /v1/authors/me` — author-only profile edit (bio, homepage) * `GET /v1/packages/:slug/reviews` — public read; returns summary + reviews joined with author info * `POST /v1/packages/:slug/reviews` — auth-gated; rejects self-reviews + retracted-package reviews * `DELETE /v1/packages/:slug/reviews/me` — author-only delete * Marketplace site: * `/authors/` index page (lists all authors with package + review counts; “Authors” tab in header nav) * `/authors/[login]/` route with avatar/bio/homepage + their packages grid * `ReviewsSection` on every detail page (rating histogram + per-review cards with linked author) * Author byline on detail pages now links to `/authors/[login]/` (was external GitHub) **Verified end-to-end** at <https://api.papercuspai.com/v1/authors/avi> (200) + <http://localhost:3060/authors/avi/> + reviews showing on /marketplace/signed-test/. ### Phase M9 — Stats + popularity ✅ SHIPPED + popularity surface [Section titled “Phase M9 — Stats + popularity ✅ SHIPPED + popularity surface”](#phase-m9--stats--popularity--shipped--popularity-surface) **Status:** Live with download counters + popularity surface on the homepage. **What shipped:** * `papercusp_marketplace.package_downloads` (slug, version, day, downloads) * Async bump on every `/download/:slug/:version` (non-blocking) * `GET /v1/stats/:slug` — total / last30d / by-version / by-day * `GET /v1/popular?limit=N` — top N packages by 30-day download count * Homepage now shows `<FeaturedClient>` rendering popular packages with `↓N (30d)` badges * Falls back to /catalog when no downloads recorded yet ### Marketplace operator dashboard ✅ SHIPPED [Section titled “Marketplace operator dashboard ✅ SHIPPED”](#marketplace-operator-dashboard--shipped) **Status:** Live at `http://localhost:3001/papercusp-marketplace-ops` (internal reference app admin). **What shipped:** * Marketplace API endpoint `GET /v1/admin/overview` (operator-token-gated) — returns aggregate health: package counts by state, authors, reviews, downloads-today, SBOM scan backlog, vulnerability severity histogram, webhook subscription health, R2 status, recent publishes (10), recent retractions (10). * Admin route `/papercusp-marketplace-ops` (internal reference app admin) — server-renders the dashboard reading the operator token from `~/.papercusp/marketplace-secrets.env` (token activity tables. Counts go red when severity warrants (failed webhooks, critical vulns, etc.). 4. Site uses `popularity` field (last 30 days’ downloads) to: * Sort the catalog grid by default (most-downloaded first) * Compute a “Trending this week” section (biggest week-over-week % gainers). 5. Stats are public; no PII. **Estimate:** 2-3 hours. ### Phase M10 — Size & bandwidth quotas (§11.10) [Section titled “Phase M10 — Size & bandwidth quotas (§11.10)”](#phase-m10--size--bandwidth-quotas-1110) **Goal:** Enforce the per-package, per-publisher, per-IP limits to prevent abuse. **Plan:** 1. **Per-package limits at upload:** * Reject `POST /publish` early if `Content-Length` > 50 MB. * Validate manifest size ≤ 64 KB before parse. * Validate README size ≤ 256 KB after extraction. 2. **Per-publisher quotas** — table `publisher_quotas { github_login, day, publishes_count, total_bytes }`: * 50 publishes/day check at upload time. * Aggregate-storage check by summing `package_versions.tarball_size` for all of the publisher’s packages. 3. **Per-IP throttling** — middleware on the marketplace-api Hono router: * In-memory `Map<ip, { count, windowStart }>` with 1-minute windows for read endpoints. * For `/download/`, hourly windows. * For `/publish/`, per-authenticated-user windows (not IP). * Returns HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` header. 4. **Cloudflare-side rate limit rules** for the `api.papercuspai.com` zone. Currently no token scope to configure these via API; must be added via CF dashboard. **Estimate:** 3-4 hours (most of it is plumbing the in-memory rate limiter and the publisher-quota table). ### Phase M11 — Catalog webhooks (§11.11) [Section titled “Phase M11 — Catalog webhooks (§11.11)”](#phase-m11--catalog-webhooks-1111) **Goal:** CI / mirrors / external monitors get notified on catalog events. **Plan:** 1. Schema: 
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE webhook_subscriptions (
     id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
     owner           TEXT NOT NULL,           -- '@avi' or '*' (operator only)
     url             TEXT NOT NULL,
     events          TEXT[] NOT NULL,         -- ['version.published', ...]
     secret          TEXT NOT NULL,           -- HMAC key
     created_by      TEXT NOT NULL,           -- GitHub login that registered it
     created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
     last_delivery   TIMESTAMPTZ,             -- updated on success
     consecutive_fails INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
     disabled_at     TIMESTAMPTZ
   );


   CREATE TABLE webhook_deliveries (
     id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,        -- 'wh_evt_01J6...' (event id)
     subscription_id TEXT REFERENCES webhook_subscriptions(id),
     event           TEXT NOT NULL,
     ts              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
     payload         JSONB NOT NULL,
     attempt         INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
     status_code     INT,
     completed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ
   );
   ```
 2. Endpoints: * `POST /v1/webhooks` — register subscription; auth-gated (only namespace owner can subscribe to events for that namespace). * `DELETE /v1/webhooks/:id` — owner-only. * `GET /v1/webhooks` — list subscriber’s webhooks + delivery history (last 100 attempts each). 3. Producer side: `version.published`, `version.yanked`, `package.withdrawn`, `package.quarantined` events insert into `webhook_deliveries` with attempt=0 within the publish/retract transaction. 4. Worker process: long-lived loop polls `webhook_deliveries` where `completed_at IS NULL`, dispatches with HMAC-SHA-256 signature header, retries per spec schedule. Could run inside marketplace-api or as separate microservice; start in marketplace-api. 5. After 90 days of failed delivery, mark subscription `disabled_at`. Send one warning email (via Resend or similar) before disable. **Estimate:** 4-5 hours. The worker loop is the hard part — must be exactly-once enough that owners can dedup confidently. ### Phase M12 — Vendored / offline install (§11.12) [Section titled “Phase M12 — Vendored / offline install (§11.12)”](#phase-m12--vendored--offline-install-1112) **Goal:** `papercusp pack` produces a self-contained mirror; substrate can install from `file://` URL. **Plan:** 1. **CLI command** `papercusp pack <slug>[@<version>] [<slug2>]... --output <dir>`: * Authenticates against the configured registry. * For each requested package, downloads the tarball + manifest + README. * If signed (per §11.5/M3), bundles the signature file too. * Bundles the marketplace’s public verification key. * Writes a `marketplace-snapshot.json` with the catalog state as of pack time (lets the offline substrate respond to “what versions exist?” queries). * Writes `index.json` per package (the “latest” pointer + version list). 2. **Substrate resolver changes** in `@papercusp/cli`: * `papercusp config set registry file:///path/to/dir/` accepted. * Loader uses `node:fs/promises` for `file://` URLs; same JSON shapes as HTTP. * Signature verification works identically (the public key is bundled). 3. **Refresh tooling**: * `papercusp pack --refresh <existing-mirror-dir>` — re-fetches all packages currently in the mirror, updating to latest. * `papercusp pack --diff <existing-mirror-dir> <other-dir>` — show what changed between two pack snapshots. **Estimate:** 5-6 hours. The `file://` resolver + bundled public key are the new mechanics; rest is filesystem walks. ### Phase M13 — Multi-registry resolution (§11.13) [Section titled “Phase M13 — Multi-registry resolution (§11.13)”](#phase-m13--multi-registry-resolution-1113) **Goal:** Support scope-based registry routing, no automatic fallback. **Plan:** 1. CLI parses `~/.papercusp/config.json` for `registries[]`. 2. For each install/update/lookup request, walk the list: * Find the first registry whose `scope` matches the requested package. * Issue the request to ONLY that registry. * On failure: if `trustOnFail` is `false` (default), return error to user; if `true`, log warning and try next. 3. Validation at config-set time: reject ambiguous scope patterns (overlapping wildcards), warn about scope `*` not being last. 4. CLI surfaces `resolved from <registry>` on every install for transparency. **Estimate:** 1-2 hours. Almost entirely CLI logic; no server-side changes. ### Phase M14 — SBOM attestation (§11.14) [Section titled “Phase M14 — SBOM attestation (§11.14)”](#phase-m14--sbom-attestation-1114) **Goal:** Verified packages can attach an SPDX or CycloneDX SBOM at publish time; marketplace surfaces it with vulnerability scanning. **Status:** Live in production. **What shipped:** * Schema `papercusp_marketplace.{package_version_sboms, package_version_vulnerabilities}` + view `v_package_vuln_summary` * SBOM ingest (`POST /v1/packages/:slug/:version/sbom`, JSON body): auto-detects SPDX-2.3 vs CycloneDX-1.5, validates JSON, caps at 5 MB, hashes with sha256 * Background scan worker (60s tick): pops `scan_status='pending'`, extracts package URLs from SBOM, batch-queries osv.dev `/v1/querybatch`, persists vulns with severity bucketing * Endpoints: * `GET /v1/packages/:slug/:version/sbom` — metadata + summary * `GET /v1/packages/:slug/:version/vulnerabilities` — full vuln list (sorted by severity) * CLI: `papercusp publish --sbom <path>` flag (uploads after publish, queues scan) * Marketplace site: * `SbomBadge` next to version pill (”✓ No CVEs” green / ”⚠ N CVEs” amber/red by worst severity) * `SbomSection` at the bottom of detail page (severity chips + collapsible vuln list with deep links to cve.org / github.com/advisories) **Verified end-to-end:** seeded an SBOM for `signed-test@0.1.0` (lodash\@4.17.20 + minimist\@1.2.5 components) → osv.dev returned 6 GHSAs (5 lodash + 1 minimist) → all persisted, summary aggregated, exposed at <https://api.papercuspai.com/v1/packages/signed-test/0.1.0/sbom> + /vulnerabilities. ## What’s still missing — quick reference [Section titled “What’s still missing — quick reference”](#whats-still-missing--quick-reference) | Concern | Status | Phase | | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------- | | Anyone can publish under any name | ✅ **Shipped 2026-04-27** | M1 | | Tarballs on local FS (single point of failure) | ⚠ Local; The internal reference app now has both as sibling submodules at `libs/papercusp/` and `../papercusp-registry/`. ### What landed this round (M3 + M10 + M13) [Section titled “What landed this round (M3 + M10 + M13)”](#what-landed-this-round-m3--m10--m13) **M3 — Tarball signing (Ed25519)** * Server: keypair auto-generated at startup at `~/.papercusp/marketplace-keys/marketplace-ed25519.{pem,pub}`. New endpoint `GET /v1/keys/marketplace.pub`. Every published tarball gets a `signature.json` sibling file with sha256, signature, and the public key for offline verification. Signed message canonical form: `${slug}\n${version}\n${sha256}\n${publishedBy}\n${publishedAt}\n`. * Client: `papercusp install` fetches the public key (24h cache at `~/.papercusp/marketplace-keys-cache.json`), recomputes sha256 of the downloaded tarball, and calls `crypto.verify` against the signature. Tampering hard-fails with cleanup of the partial install. Legacy packages without `signature.json` warn but proceed (backward compat). `--no-verify` flag bypasses for offline / debug paths. * Verified: tampering test (corrupt + retry) correctly rejects with sha256 mismatch error. **M10 — Size & bandwidth quotas** * Tarball cap 50 MB (HTTP 413 with clear message), manifest cap 64 KB, README cap 256 KB — all checked at upload before disk write. * Per-IP rate limit middleware: 600 req/min for read endpoints, 60 tarballs/hour for `/download/`, 5 publishes/min per authenticated publisher (per-IP for unauthenticated). Returns HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` header. * Per-publisher daily quota tracking at `~/.papercusp/marketplace-storage/.publisher-quotas.json`: 50 publishes/day, 1 GB aggregate storage. Resets at UTC rollover. Only enforces when authenticated. * Verified: 70 KB manifest correctly rejected; 605 rapid requests yielded 596 × 200 + 9 × 429. **M13 — Multi-registry resolution** * CLI reads `~/.papercusp/config.json` for `registries[]` array. * `resolveRegistry(slug)` walks scopes in order; first match wins. `*` matches anything; `@owner/*` matches `@owner/anything`. * `--registry <url>` flag overrides config for one-off installs. * No automatic fallback — if no registry covers the slug, errors with explicit message listing configured scopes. * Slug regex extended to accept scoped names (`@owner/package`); version splitter handles `@avi/foo@1.2.0` correctly. * Verified: 4 scenarios — scoped → internal, no-match → error, `--registry` override → bypasses config, no config → falls back to `PAPERCUSP_MARKETPLACE_URL`. Files touched this round: * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-api/src/server.ts` — keypair gen, signing, public key endpoint, rate limit middleware, manifest/README size caps, publisher quota tracking * `libs/papercusp/packages/cli/src/papercusp.ts` — signature verification on install, `--no-verify` and `--registry` flags, scoped-slug support, registry resolver Production state after this round: * `https://api.papercuspai.com/v1/keys/marketplace.pub` — returns Ed25519 public key * `https://api.papercuspai.com/catalog/signed-test/0.1.0` — includes `signature` field in the response * Existing legacy packages (papercup-coding, papercup-org) continue to work without signatures **Original estimate**: 42-52 hours total. **After three rounds shipped (M2.5 + M3 + M4 + M5 + M6 + M7 + M9 + M10 + M13)**: \~17-22 hours remaining. **Remaining work**: M1 (auth — needs your OAuth app), M2 (R2 backing), M8 (authors+reviews), M11 (webhooks), M12 (vendored install), M14 (SBOMs). ### What landed in `/v1/packages/:slug/versions/:version/yank`. * 4-tier model per spec §11.9: Deprecated → Yanked → Withdrawn → Quarantined. * Quarantine + unquarantine require operator token Empty query returns most-recently-updated packages. Files touched in round 3: * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-api/sql/002-retraction-and-stats.sql` — new migration * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-api/src/db.ts` — applyRetraction, bumpDownload, getDownloadStats, getPackageState, listInstalledStatus, getMarketplaceSql exported * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-api/src/server.ts` — 9 new endpoints, retraction guard on /download/, async stats counter Verified end-to-end: * Deprecate/yank/withdraw all log to audit table ✓ * Quarantine requires operator token (401 without; idempotent for re-runs. * All 3 existing packages (papercup-coding, papercup-org, signed-test) backfilled successfully. **M5 — Update / uninstall / rollback CLI** * New state file at `~/.papercusp/installed-plugins.json` tracking each install: slug, version, install path, applied migration index, granted capabilities, manifest snapshot. * `papercusp install` now records into this state on success. * `papercusp update <slug> [--yes]`: * Fetches latest from registry; no-op if up to date. * Diffs capabilities (added / removed) and reports. * Snapshots old version to `~/.papercusp/snapshots/<slug>/<old-version>/` (full files dir + manifest + granted-caps.json). * Re-installs the new version atomically. * Records new state. * `papercusp uninstall <slug> [--purge-data]`: * Default: removes plugin code + state, **preserves Postgres data**. * `--purge-data`: also flags schema for cleanup (manual review since manifest doesn’t yet declare a schema name). * `papercusp rollback <slug>`: * Re-mounts most recent snapshot. * Updates state to reflect rolled-back version. * Surfaces “DB rollback is your responsibility” warning per spec §11.7. **M7 — Detail page rich UX** * Site: `/marketplace/[slug]/` now surfaces: * **Verified (signed) / Unverified badge** — green if signature present, amber otherwise. * **Install shape badge** (Iterative / Scheduled / Reactive / Passive) when `manifest.shape` set, with tooltip explaining the shape. * **Capability tier breakdown** — colored counts (high / medium / low), expandable to see all caps. * **Service ABI pins** sidebar when `manifest.services` set. * **publishedBy** linked to GitHub profile when stamped. * **publishedAt** human-readable. * **Signature provenance** sidebar with algo + sha256 + signed-by. * Helper `tierCapabilities()` and `SHAPE_LABEL` constants in `lib/format.ts` shared with the catalog grid for future filters. * Built + deployed to Cloudflare Pages (deployment `0aba4673`) — verified the new strings are in the JS chunks served from `papercuspai.com`. Files touched in round 2: * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-api/sql/001-marketplace-schema.sql` — new migration * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-api/src/db.ts` — new postgres-js client + upsertPackageVersion + categorizeCapabilities * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-api/src/server.ts` — dual-write call in publish handler * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-api/src/backfill.ts` — new one-time backfill script * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-api/package.json` — added `postgres` dep + `backfill` script * `libs/papercusp/packages/cli/src/papercusp.ts` — installed-plugins state, update/rollback commands, uninstall expansion, help text * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-site/lib/api.ts` — new types for shape / capabilities / services / signature * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-site/lib/format.ts` — tierCapabilities helper + SHAPE\_LABEL * `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-site/app/marketplace/[slug]/PackageClient.tsx` — new badges + sidebar sections ### Suggested phase ordering [Section titled “Suggested phase ordering”](#suggested-phase-ordering) Not all phases are equal priority. Here’s the order I’d run them in, by what unblocks the most usage: 1. **M1 (auth)** — block until landed; everything downstream assumes verified identities. 2. **M2 + M2.5 (R2 + Postgres metadata)** — durability + scale; necessary before significant publishing. 3. **M3 (tarball signing)** — supply chain integrity; prerequisite for verified-tier display. 4. **M7 (detail page UX)** — surface what M1+M3 enable to users. 5. **M5 (update/uninstall)** — close the install loop; users need this before they install anything important. 6. **M10 (quotas)** — anti-abuse before the marketplace is opened publicly. 7. **M6 (retraction)** — operational maturity; needed before a real security incident. 8. **M11 (webhooks)** — unlocks ecosystem integrations. 9. **M4 (search)** — only needed once catalog > \~100 packages. 10. **M9 (stats)** — nice-to-have signal; not blocking. 11. **M8 (reviews)** — community feature; needs moderation tooling. 12. **M12 (vendored)** — enterprise / air-gapped customers. 13. **M13 (multi-registry)** — corporate mirrors with public fallback. 14. **M14 (SBOMs)** — supply chain compliance; v2.0-shaped feature. ## Operational notes [Section titled “Operational notes”](#operational-notes) ### First-party seed templates (re-publishing) [Section titled “First-party seed templates (re-publishing)”](#first-party-seed-templates-re-publishing) The bundled templates `papercup-coding` and `papercup-org` are **first-party** — they’re owned by `@papercupai`, not by whoever happens to run the seed script. Their canonical source-of-truth lives in the marketplace repo at `../papercusp-registry/seeds/papercupai/<slug>/`. They’re published via the **same publish pipeline as any user package** — no SQL backfill, no special case in the server. Two auth modes cover this: **Service token (recommended for CI / seed scripts):** A static bearer token bound to a publisher login. The marketplace operator issues it via `PAPERCUSP_MARKETPLACE_SERVICE_TOKENS` env (JSON array of `{token, login}` entries). Then: 
```bash
PAPERCUSP_SERVICE_TOKEN=<your-token> \
PAPERCUSP_MARKETPLACE_URL=http://localhost:3057 \
  papercusp publish     # from inside seeds/papercupai/<slug>/
```
 The CLI sends the token as `Authorization: Bearer ...`; the server matches it against the configured table and stamps `publishedBy` from the bound login. No OAuth round-trip, no browser, fully scriptable. **OAuth Device Flow (for human publishing as @papercupai):** `papercusp login` then `papercusp publish`. Requires the @papercupai GitHub account/org to exist and you to be able to authenticate as it. **Don’t** insert seed packages directly via SQL or backfill scripts — that bypasses the publish pipeline (signing, indexing, webhook events) and creates orphan-attribution problems. The seeds README at `../papercusp-registry/seeds/README.md` documents the policy. ### Local development [Section titled “Local development”](#local-development) The marketplace-api runs as a systemd —user transient unit named `marketplace-api`, defined at `~/.config/systemd/user/marketplace-api.service`. It’s started automatically alongside `bin/dev` and survives shell exits. 
```bash
# Status / restart / logs
systemctl --user status marketplace-api
systemctl --user restart marketplace-api
journalctl --user -u marketplace-api -f
# or: tail -f ~/.papercusp/logs/marketplace-api.log


# Manual run (if you need to iterate without the unit):
cd ../papercusp-registry && npm run dev:api      # listens on :3057


# Build + serve site locally
cd ../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-site
BUILD_API_BASE=http://localhost:3057 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE=https://api.papercuspai.com npm run build
npx serve out -l 3060        # http://localhost:3060
```
 ### Production deploy [Section titled “Production deploy”](#production-deploy) 
```bash
cd libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-site
BUILD_API_BASE=http://localhost:3057 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE=https://api.papercuspai.com npm run build
npx wrangler pages deploy ./out --project-name papercuspai --branch main --commit-dirty=true
```
 The marketplace-api process must be running on `localhost:3057` for the build’s `generateStaticParams` step (which fetches the catalog to pre-render `/marketplace/[slug]/` pages). After M2 lands, this becomes optional — Postgres metadata can serve build-time too. ### Cloudflare touchpoints [Section titled “Cloudflare touchpoints”](#cloudflare-touchpoints) * **Pages project:** `papercuspai` (domain attached, deploys via wrangler) * **Tunnel:** `papercupai-api` (UUID `c53515b3-edfe-4e99-813b-e3916ae9d02c`) — same tunnel as papercupai.com, with two ingress rules (one per hostname) * **DNS apex:** `papercuspai.com` → `papercuspai.pages.dev` (CNAME, proxied) * **DNS api:** `api.papercuspai.com` → tunnel UUID via Zero Trust dashboard ### Known operational gotchas [Section titled “Known operational gotchas”](#known-operational-gotchas) * New publishes appear instantly in `/marketplace/` grid (live API fetch) but **404 on `[slug]` detail until site is rebuilt + redeployed** (`dynamicParams = false` on the static export). Future option: add an SSR fallback at the edge for unknown slugs. * The CF token at `~/.cloudflare-token` has Pages and a few zone scopes but **NOT** `Account · Cloudflare Tunnel · Edit`. Tunnel changes require dashboard clicks today. * `cloudflared` runs in token mode → ingress rules managed via Zero Trust dashboard, not `~/.cloudflared/config.yml`. * Marketplace dirs were moved on 2026-04-27 from `libs/papercusp/apps/{marketplace-api,marketplace-site}` → `../papercusp-registry/apps/{marketplace-api,marketplace-site}`. If you see stale paths anywhere, that’s why. * The `papercusp` CLI (`libs/papercusp/packages/cli/src/papercusp.ts`) lives in the **substrate** repo, not the marketplace repo. It talks to the marketplace via HTTP, so the split makes sense — but if you change the api shape on the server side, update the CLI in lockstep across both repos. ## Handoff — detailed implementation specs for remaining phases [Section titled “Handoff — detailed implementation specs for remaining phases”](#handoff--detailed-implementation-specs-for-remaining-phases) This section is the precise roadmap for the **3 remaining phases** if a future agent picks up. Each phase has been spec’d in §11 and partially designed earlier; here’s what an implementer needs to actually ship them. ### M2 — R2 storage backing (3-4h, **blocked on CF token scope**) [Section titled “M2 — R2 storage backing (3-4h, blocked on CF token scope)”](#m2--r2-storage-backing-3-4h-blocked-on-cf-token-scope) **Why it’s blocked:** Need a CF API token with `Account · R2 · Edit` to create the bucket and obtain S3-compatible credentials. The current `~/.cloudflare-token` has Pages + selected zone scopes only. **Plan once unblocked:** 1. Create R2 bucket `papercusp-marketplace-tarballs` (CF dashboard or API): 
   ```plaintext
   curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/f896982ea2f6d507e4f29eeecbd26e94/r2/buckets" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_R2_TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"name":"papercusp-marketplace-tarballs"}'
   ```
 2. Get S3-compatible access keys (CF dashboard → R2 → Manage R2 API Tokens). Add to `~/.papercusp/marketplace-secrets.env`: 
   ```plaintext
   R2_ACCOUNT_ID=f896982ea2f6d507e4f29eeecbd26e94
   R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...
   R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
   R2_BUCKET=papercusp-marketplace-tarballs
   ```
 3. Add `@aws-sdk/client-s3` to `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/package.json`: 
   ```json
   "dependencies": {
     "@aws-sdk/client-s3": "^3.700.0",
     "@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner": "^3.700.0"
   }
   ```
 4. Create `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/src/r2.ts`: * `S3Client` configured with `endpoint: https://${R2_ACCOUNT_ID}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`, `region: 'auto'` * `uploadTarball(slug, version, buf)` → `s3.send(new PutObjectCommand(...))` * `getDownloadUrl(slug, version)` → `getSignedUrl(s3, new GetObjectCommand(...), { expiresIn: 300 })` * Key format: `tarballs/${slug}/${version}/${slug}-${version}.tar.gz` 5. Modify `server.ts` publish handler: * After existing FS write to `tarballPath`, also call `uploadTarball(slug, version, buf)` * Continue dual-writing FS for now (rollback safety) 6. Modify `server.ts` `/download/:slug/:version`: * First try the R2 signed URL: redirect 302 to it * On any error (R2 down or migration not complete), fall back to existing FS stream * `papercusp_marketplace.package_versions.tarball_r2_key` column tracks if uploaded — add a migration 7. Migration script: `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/src/migrate-to-r2.ts` — iterates existing FS packages, uploads each to R2, marks `tarball_r2_key` in the DB. 8. Delete FS storage AFTER verifying R2 + signed URLs serve correctly for a week. **Schema delta (002b):** 
```sql
ALTER TABLE papercusp_marketplace.package_versions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS tarball_r2_key TEXT;
```
 **Testing:** * Unit: upload + signed URL roundtrip * Integration: publish via CLI, verify install pulls from R2 (302 redirect chain visible) * Failure mode: simulate R2 outage with bad credentials, verify FS fallback engages ### M8 — Author profiles + reviews (4-5h) [Section titled “M8 — Author profiles + reviews (4-5h)”](#m8--author-profiles--reviews-4-5h) **Schema** (003b-reviews.sql in `../papercusp-registry/sql/`): 
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS papercusp_marketplace.reviews (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                  -- 'rv_' + 24 hex
  slug          TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES papercusp_marketplace.packages(slug) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  reviewer      TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- verified GitHub login
  rating        SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (rating BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  body          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(body) BETWEEN 10 AND 5000),
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  hidden_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,                       -- non-null = operator hid
  hidden_reason TEXT,
  UNIQUE (slug, reviewer)                          -- one review per user per package
);


CREATE INDEX reviews_slug_idx ON papercusp_marketplace.reviews(slug);
CREATE INDEX reviews_reviewer_idx ON papercusp_marketplace.reviews(reviewer);


GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON papercusp_marketplace.reviews TO harness_app, harness_admin;
```
 **Endpoints in `server.ts`:** * `GET /v1/packages/:slug/reviews` — list reviews (excludes hidden\_at IS NOT NULL); 50 most recent * `POST /v1/packages/:slug/reviews` — auth-required, insert/update by `(slug, reviewer)`. Reject if reviewer is the package’s `publishedBy` (no self-reviews). Reject if account < 7 days old (anti-spam). * `DELETE /v1/packages/:slug/reviews/:id` — owner of the review only * `POST /v1/admin/reviews/:id/hide` — operator-only; sets `hidden_at` + `hidden_reason` * `GET /v1/authors/:login` — public profile + their packages + their reviews (last 10) **Site changes** (`../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-site/`): * New page `/authors/[login]/page.tsx` with `generateStaticParams` from `package_versions.published_by DISTINCT` * New section on `/marketplace/[slug]/` (PackageClient.tsx) with reviews list + write-review form (auth-gated) * Average rating badge on the catalog grid **Anti-abuse rules** (per spec §8 of M8 plan): * Reviewers from accounts < 7 days old: visible but flagged “new account” * Reviews can be reported via `POST /v1/packages/:slug/reviews/:id/report` * Operator UI later (deferred) for moderation queue ### M14 — SBOM attestation + CVE scanning (6-8h) [Section titled “M14 — SBOM attestation + CVE scanning (6-8h)”](#m14--sbom-attestation--cve-scanning-6-8h) **Schema** (005-attestations.sql): 
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS papercusp_marketplace.package_attestations (
  slug              TEXT NOT NULL,
  version           TEXT NOT NULL,
  format            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (format IN ('spdx', 'cyclonedx')),
  sbom_json         JSONB NOT NULL,
  scanned_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
  vulnerabilities   JSONB,                         -- [{ purl, advisory_id, severity, fixedIn }]
  PRIMARY KEY (slug, version),
  FOREIGN KEY (slug, version) REFERENCES papercusp_marketplace.package_versions(slug, version) ON DELETE CASCADE
);


CREATE INDEX attestations_unscanned_idx
  ON papercusp_marketplace.package_attestations(scanned_at) WHERE scanned_at IS NULL;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON papercusp_marketplace.package_attestations TO harness_app, harness_admin;
```
 **Publish handler change:** * `POST /publish/:slug/:version` accepts an additional multipart field `sbom` (JSON file). Validate against the format’s JSON schema before storing. If valid, insert into `package_attestations` with `scanned_at = NULL`. **Scan worker** (`../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/src/sbom-scanner.ts`): * Long-lived loop (1-min tick) drains rows where `scanned_at IS NULL` * For each: extract package list (SPDX `packages[]` or CycloneDX `components[]`) * For each package: query `https://api.osv.dev/v1/query` with PURL or CPE * Store findings in `vulnerabilities[]` * Re-scan all attestations weekly (set `scanned_at = NULL` for rows older than 7d) * Rate limit: max 10 osv.dev queries/sec; back off on 429 **Endpoints:** * `GET /v1/packages/:slug/:version/sbom` — raw SBOM JSON * `GET /v1/packages/:slug/:version/sbom/viewer` — formatted HTML (server-side render via marked.js or similar) * `GET /v1/packages/:slug/:version/vulnerabilities` — current findings **Site changes:** * “Has SBOM” badge on detail page (already wired UI: just add a check) * Vulnerability count badge if `vulnerabilities.length > 0` * Optional: SBOM diff between two versions (deferred to v2) **CLI:** * `papercusp publish --sbom ./sbom.spdx.json` — multipart upload * `papercusp install` warns if installed plugin has unpatched CVEs (queries `/v1/packages/:slug/:version/vulnerabilities` after install) ### Smaller cleanup items [Section titled “Smaller cleanup items”](#smaller-cleanup-items) * **Reviews UI** — see M8 above; deferred until M8 is in progress. * **Spec docs site relocation** — the spec is now embedded as the Fumadocs `(docs)` route group inside `apps/papercusp` (served at `localhost:3055/docs`).
