# Multi-harness spawning / communication

> Plan to make harness-spawning + cross-harness coordination first-class substrate features. Auth-bound identity from day one; papercup-org is the first consumer, not a special case.

> **Webapp retired (2026-05-14).** Any `localhost:3055` or `localhost:3070` URL on this page is only reachable while the **Tauri dev shell** is running. Start it with `cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev`. Shipped, then evolved — read this as the original plan The multi-harness substrate described here **did ship** and has since moved. Treat the inline file paths below as the plan’s original targets, not current locations: * `POST /api/admin/execute-action` lives in **`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/admin/execute-action.ts`** (Hono), alongside `rotate-token.ts` and `prune-executed-actions.ts`. Cross-harness reads are under **`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/cross-harness/`**. * The per-harness `config_token` design was later **retired** (migration `121-retire-per-harness-config-token-and-proposals.sql`); token identity was reworked. The orchestrator-emitted spawning is now the `fleet:*` / cross-harness substrate (`packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/operator-spawn.ts`). * The orchestrator the plan refers to (`run.sh` → TS) was ported and its run-loop later retired; see [orchestrator-port](/internal/docs/implementation/orchestrator-port). * **Completion-reporting moved engine entirely.** It no longer runs through the `run.sh` `afterDone.sh` bash builtin (run.sh itself is gone, so the bash `run_hook` / builtins resolver the body describes in Step 4.5 no longer exists). It is now the DBOS TS builtin **`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/notify-parent-done.ts`**, which fires on per-feature-queue drain (a feature’s DONE finalize, only when no other non-terminal feature remains) and reads the server-sealed `parent_slug` from `harness_shared.projects` (PG) — **not** from `.papercusp/config.json`, which is deprecated as a live config source. A per-harness `hooks/afterDone.sh` still overrides the builtin. (promote-spawn-child-harness-2026-05-31; deprecate-harness-config-json-2026-06-06.) * **Several §3/§10 non-goals later shipped** in `packages/operator-core/lib/execute-action.ts`: per-caller `send_message` rate limiting (`PAPERCUSP_SEND_MESSAGE_RATE_LIMIT`, default 50 per 60s), spawn cycle + depth detection (`PAPERCUSP_MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH`, default 8, walking the `parent_slug` chain), and `dryRun: true` on `scaffold_harness` (validate-only — no shell-out, no FS writes). Read the §3/§10 entries for these as plan-time scope, not current state. * **The executeAction dispatcher grew past the four planned verbs.** `dispatchAction` in `packages/operator-core/lib/execute-action.ts` now implements nine verbs — beyond `send_message` / `mark_message_status` / `spinup_project` / `scaffold_harness` it also handles `create_feature`, `pause_project`, `resume_project`, `mark_campaign_published`, and `add_directive_summary` (several of which §3 lists as non-goals). * **API host is `:3070`, not `:3055`.** The Tier 3 curl examples (Step 3c) and the agent-facing snippets point at `:3055`, which is only the Vite SPA dev server (it proxies `/api → :3070` in dev and is absent on the release operator). The real Hono API host that serves `/api/admin/execute-action` and the read endpoints is `:3070` (`PAPERCUSP_HONO_PORT`); internal / loopback calls must target it. See `packages/operator-core/lib/operator-api-base.ts`. ## 1. Goal [Section titled “1. Goal”](#1-goal) Make harness-spawning and cross-harness coordination first-class capabilities of the standard harness substrate, with auth-bound identity from day one. Concretely: * Any harness whose role config declares `allowedActions: [..., "scaffold_harness"]` can spawn children. * Any marketplace template that declares `spawnable: { kind, requires }` can be spawned as a child. * Children whose `parent_slug` is set automatically report completion back to their parent — no per-template hook authoring required. * Every orchestrator understands it’s running inside Papercusp, can see its parent / children / siblings at a glance, and can pull full state of any other harness on demand via authenticated read APIs. * Any harness whose role config grants `send_message` can message any other harness, with a declared `reason` recorded in the audit log. * **Every executeAction call is authenticated against a per-harness shared-secret token; harness identity is derived from the token binding, not from caller-supplied body fields. `parent_slug` and message `from_slug` are derived (not trusted), so spoofing is impossible at the protocol level.** * The `papercup-org` template is the first template that uses these features, not a special case. The user-facing demo: drop a directive into the `papercup-org` parent’s inbox, manually invoke its director, watch it spawn children with full context of the org, watch them run while the parent can intervene mid-mission, watch completion flow back. ## 2. Scope [Section titled “2. Scope”](#2-scope) Closed-loop manual demo via standard substrate. End-to-end smokes must pass: * **Smoke A** — papercup-org happy path (directive → spawn → first non-trivial file → completion message in parent inbox) * **Smoke B** — generic non-`papercup-org` harness can also spawn children (proves the feature is substrate, not template-specific) * **Smoke C** — neighbor visibility works (a child’s prompt sees its parent’s status; a parent’s prompt sees its children’s statuses; cross-harness supervisor message arrives in child’s prompt-build) * **Smoke D** — auth model holds: a request without a valid token, with a token bound to harness X claiming to be harness Y, or with a forged `callingHarness` body field, is rejected with 401/403 Autonomy (routine ticker, coordinator dispatch, auditor cadence) is a **separate plan** — not included here. ## 3. Non-goals [Section titled “3. Non-goals”](#3-non-goals) * Coordinator dispatch — `NEXT_HARNESS` parses but doesn’t fire children autonomously. * Auditor cadence — file exists, no scheduler invokes it. * `add_directive_summary` — context bounded by prompt-build truncation instead. * `mark_campaign_published`, `pause_project`, `resume_project` — useful, not needed for the loop. * Briefings plugin — gone, dropped from manifest until source is restored or rebuilt. * Many-directive scale, multi-week autonomy, KPI dashboards. * Cross-machine spawn (parent on machine A, child on machine B). * Spawn quotas / rate limiting per parent. * Permission tiers beyond `allowedActions[]` and the auth token. * Per-role addressing (`to: [<harness>:<role>]`); messages address harnesses, not roles within. * `dryRun: true` for `scaffold_harness` — defer to v1.5. * Cache-and-verify idempotency replay — v1 is cache-is-authoritative. * Token rotation for compromised harnesses — manual reissue only in v1. ## 4. Architecture decisions (locked before code) [Section titled “4. Architecture decisions (locked before code)”](#4-architecture-decisions-locked-before-code) ### Auth & identity [Section titled “Auth & identity”](#auth--identity) | Decision | Choice | Rationale | | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Per-harness shared secret | `harness_<slug>.config_token` (random 256-bit, base64url) generated at scaffold time, written to `.papercusp/config.json` mode 0600 | Cryptographic identity binding; token serves as both authn and authz | | Auth header | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every executeAction request | Standard, simple | | Identity derivation | Executor looks up token in `harness_shared.token_index` to find which harness slug owns it. **`callingHarness` in the request body is REJECTED if it doesn’t match the derived identity.** | Body fields are forgeable; token binding is not | | `parent_slug` sealing | `parent_slug = <derivedCallingHarness>` on `scaffold_harness`; never read from body | Real seal, not security theater | | `from_slug` on messages | Always = `<derivedCallingHarness>`; body’s `from` field rejected on mismatch | Stops cross-harness spoofing in the audit log | | Token rotation | Out of scope for v1; manual deletion of harness + re-scaffold if compromised | v1 is correctness-floor; rotation is hardening | ### Action execution [Section titled “Action execution”](#action-execution) | Decision | Choice | Rationale | | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Endpoint shape | Slug-less `POST /api/admin/execute-action` with `targetSlug` in action body | Many actions cross harnesses; URL-as-context is the wrong frame | | Verb dispatch | Single endpoint with `op` discriminator | Matches the deleted `org.ts` contract; matches `actions-block.ts`’s POST shape | | State backend | PG (per-harness `harness_<slug>.messages`, `harness_shared.projects`) | Universal Schema + Zero sync already in place | | Caller-supplied idempotency | `actionId` (UUID) supplied by caller; server returns same `result` on replay | Workers retry on flake; double-spinup is unrecoverable | | Idempotency replay semantics | **Cache-is-authoritative.** Cached response returned without verifying side effects still exist. | Documented as v1 boundary; out-of-band mutations break replay correctness; v1.5 can add cache-and-verify | | Per-action error shape | `{ok, actionId, error?, result?}`; ACTIONS array continues past mid-array failures | Matches `actions-block.ts` loop semantics | | Per-verb timeouts | `scaffold_harness`: 5 min. All other verbs: 60s. | Scaffold legitimately needs minutes (`papercusp init`, schema scaffold, etc.); the rest are SQL or fast | | `send_message` addressing | Any harness → any harness; receiver decides whether to consume via prompt-build | Open bus, gated by receiver | | `send_message` reason field | Required `reason: string` (min 10 chars; warn on placeholder regex but don’t block) | Friction filters trivial chatter | | `spinup_project` partial-failure semantics | Wrapped in a single PG transaction across all affected per-harness schemas. All-or-nothing. | Atomicity > diagnostic detail at v1 | | `scaffold_harness` slug uniqueness | `INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; if conflict → 409 with `error: 'slug already in use'` | Don’t write to someone else’s schema | ### Parent / child structure [Section titled “Parent / child structure”](#parent--child-structure) | Decision | Choice | Rationale | | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Parent/child relationship | Optional `parent_slug` column on `harness_shared.projects`, mirrored to `.papercusp/config.json.parent_slug` | Structural fact at the registry level; substrate code reads it | | Completion-reporting hook | Default `afterDone.sh` ships in `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/hooks/builtins/` and fires when the harness has `parent_slug` set | One canonical impl, opt-in by config | | Hook resolution chain | `<harness-dir>/.papercusp/hooks/<name>.sh` → `<libs>/packages/harness/hooks/builtins/<name>.sh`. **Resolver scans `builtins/` generically; afterDone is the only v1 builtin shipped.** | New builtins (e.g. `onPostValidator.sh`) are then a one-file PR in v1.5+ | | User-supplied per-harness hook | Wins over builtin | Standard hook resolution; backward compatible | ### Marketplace contract [Section titled “Marketplace contract”](#marketplace-contract) | Decision | Choice | Rationale | | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | | Template “spawnable” contract | New manifest field `spawnable: { kind: 'coding'\|'service'\|..., requires: [...] }` in `papercusp.json` | Marketplace knows which templates a director can pick from | | Spawnable-templates discovery | `GET /api/marketplace/spawnable` returns catalog filtered to `spawnable` entries | Director prompt builds available templates list at runtime | | `scaffold_harness` template validation | Executor rejects `template` not in spawnable catalog | Prevents directors from spawning marketing-only templates | | Adding `spawnable` to existing templates | Bumps patch version (`0.1.0` → `0.1.1`) and re-publishes; documented as the marketplace contract for “additive manifest field” | Avoids undefined-behavior on cached clients | ### Cross-harness visibility (tiered) [Section titled “Cross-harness visibility (tiered)”](#cross-harness-visibility-tiered) | Decision | Choice | Rationale | | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Tier 1 — Substrate self-description | Every prompt includes a fixed ”## About Papercusp” preamble (\~300 tokens, identical across all harnesses) | Coherence: orchestrators understand they’re running inside a multi-harness framework | | Tier 2 — Neighbor view | Every prompt includes a depth-1 view of: parent (if any), children (if any), siblings sharing same `parent_slug` | Bounded growth, sufficient for relational coordination | | Tier 2 detail level | Parent: slug + recent activity 1-liner + last message between us. Children: slug + feature status counts + last activity ts + **`spawned_count: N`** for grandchild visibility hint. Siblings: slug + status counts. **Plus an aggregate roll-up.** | \~50 tokens each + \~20 tokens roll-up; prevents prompt bloat while flagging where Tier 3 inspection is warranted | | Tier 3 — Inspect-on-demand | Read APIs (`/api/harness/projects`, `/api/harness/<slug>/status`, `/api/harness/<slug>/inbox`, `/api/harness/all/recent-activity`) listed in prompt as “available capabilities”; agent invokes when relevant | Full visibility achievable; pay only when needed | | Tier 3 invocation mechanism | **Verified in Step 0.5** — either `Bash` is wired into `--allowed-tools` (so curl works), or a new MCP tool server `mcp__papercusp__inspectHarness({slug})` etc. ships in Step 2.5. **Without this, Tier 3 is dead text.** | Don’t promise Tier 3 in prompts the agent can’t act on | | Cross-harness inbox consumption | Each harness’s orchestrator/scoper/worker prompt-build includes its own bounded inbox; consumed messages auto-ack ONLY when orchestrator decision ∈ `{DONE, NEXT_*}`; `ESCALATE`/`REVIEW` leave pending | Parent → child mid-mission supervision reaches the agents; user-escalation messages aren’t eaten | ### Autonomy (deferred to v2 plan) [Section titled “Autonomy (deferred to v2 plan)”](#autonomy-deferred-to-v2-plan) | Decision | Choice | Rationale | | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Autonomy substrate | TBD pending Step 0 spike | Routine plugin if substrate is durable across operator restarts; otherwise PG-backed work queue or systemd timer | ## 5. Steps [Section titled “5. Steps”](#5-steps) ### Step 0 — Routine substrate spike *(\~30 min)* [Section titled “Step 0 — Routine substrate spike (\~30 min)”](#step-0--routine-substrate-spike-30-min) Read `libs/papercusp/packages/plugin-loader/src/routines.ts` (or wherever routines live) and answer: **Does the routine ticker survive operator process restart?** * If yes: commit to routine plugin for v2 autoLoop. * If no: pivot to `pending_events` table + a separate ticker process (systemd timer or sidecar daemon). **Output:** decision note in `docs/decisions/routine-durability.md`. **Gate:** none — informational only; this plan doesn’t depend on the answer. ### Step 0.5 — Action-body + auth contract *(\~2 hours)* [Section titled “Step 0.5 — Action-body + auth contract (\~2 hours)”](#step-05--action-body--auth-contract-2-hours) Single 2–3 page document at `apps/operator/app/api/_hono/execute-action.contract.md`: **Auth model:** * Per-harness token: 256-bit random, base64url, generated at scaffold time, stored at `.papercusp/config.json:harness_token` mode 0600 * Auth header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` required on every request * Identity derivation: server queries `harness_shared.token_index` to derive `<derivedCallingHarness>`; if no match → 401 * Body’s `callingHarness`: must equal `<derivedCallingHarness>` or be omitted; mismatch → 403 * Body’s `from` (in `send_message`): must equal `<derivedCallingHarness>`; mismatch → 403 * `parent_slug` (in `scaffold_harness`): NEVER body-controlled; always set by server to `<derivedCallingHarness>` **Tier 3 verification (the inspect\_harness capability):** * Confirm whether `claude -p` invocations from `run.sh` include `Bash` in `--allowed-tools`. * If yes: agent can curl Tier 3 endpoints directly. Step 2.5 is just docs. * If no: ship `mcp__papercusp__inspectHarness` MCP tools in Step 2.5 wrapping the read endpoints. * Document the chosen mechanism in this contract. **Endpoint:** * `POST /api/admin/execute-action` * Request body: 
  ```ts
  {
    actionId: string,        // UUID supplied by caller, idempotency key
    callingHarness?: string, // optional; must match Bearer-derived if present
    callingDept?: string,    // backwards-compat for run.sh (informational only)
    action: { op: '...', ... }
  }
  ```
 * Per-verb request fields: * `send_message`: `to[], kind, subject, body, parentMessageId?, reason: string` *(`from` derived)* * `mark_message_status`: `messageId, status: 'acknowledged' | 'archived'` * `spinup_project`: `directiveId, projectName, projectVertical, projectBudgetCents, departments[]` * `scaffold_harness`: `projectSlug, template, spec, goal` *(`parent_slug` derived)* * Response: `{ok, actionId, result?, error?}` * Idempotency: same `actionId` → cached response, no re-execution, no side-effect verification (cache-is-authoritative) * Error categories: `validation_error` (400), `auth_error` (401|403), `not_found` (404), `conflict` (409), `internal` (500) * Per-verb timeouts: `scaffold_harness` 5 min, others 60s **Gate:** committed to repo. ### Step 1 — PG schema migration *(\~1d)* [Section titled “Step 1 — PG schema migration (\~1d)”](#step-1--pg-schema-migration-1d) Update `bin/scaffold-harness-schema.sh` to add to every per-harness schema: 
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS harness_<slug>.config_token (
  token TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);


CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS harness_<slug>.messages (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  from_slug TEXT NOT NULL,
  to_slug TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL,
  subject TEXT NOT NULL,
  body TEXT,
  parent_message_id UUID,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  acknowledged_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'acknowledged', 'archived'))
);
CREATE INDEX ON harness_<slug>.messages (status, created_at);
CREATE INDEX ON harness_<slug>.messages (to_slug, status);
CREATE INDEX ON harness_<slug>.messages (from_slug, created_at);


CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS harness_<slug>.supervisor_notes (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  body TEXT NOT NULL,
  source TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);


CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS harness_<slug>.executed_actions (
  action_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  op TEXT NOT NULL,
  caller_slug TEXT NOT NULL,
  target_slug TEXT,
  reason TEXT,
  request JSONB NOT NULL,
  response JSONB NOT NULL,
  executed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX ON harness_<slug>.executed_actions (caller_slug, executed_at);
CREATE INDEX ON harness_<slug>.executed_actions (target_slug, executed_at);
CREATE INDEX ON harness_<slug>.executed_actions (op, executed_at);
```
 And to `harness_shared`: 
```sql
ALTER TABLE harness_shared.projects
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS parent_slug TEXT;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_projects_parent ON harness_shared.projects (parent_slug);


CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS harness_shared.token_index (
  token TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  harness_slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```
 **Idempotent migration script** `bin/migrate-installed-harnesses-add-messages.sh`: * For each row in `harness_shared.projects`: * If the project path doesn’t exist on disk → log “skip (orphaned registry row)” and continue * Else: provision new tables in `harness_<slug>` (idempotent via `IF NOT EXISTS`) * Generate a fresh token, write to `<project_path>/.papercusp/config.json` (chmod 0600), insert into both `harness_<slug>.config_token` and `harness_shared.token_index` * At end, print summary: `provisioned: N, skipped: M (broken rows), errors: K` **Verify:** apply against an existing harness; confirm tables; re-run; confirm idempotent. Apply against the 7 currently-broken `papercup-org*` rows; confirm “skipped: 7.” **Gate:** all installed harnesses (with valid project paths) have the new tables + tokens; broken rows logged but not failed. ### Step 2 — executeAction with 4 verbs + auth *(\~3.5d)* [Section titled “Step 2 — executeAction with 4 verbs + auth (\~3.5d)”](#step-2--executeaction-with-4-verbs--auth-35d) New file `apps/operator/app/api/admin/execute-action/route.ts`. **Auth middleware *(\~0.5d)*:** * Reject if no `Authorization: Bearer` header (401). * Look up bearer in `harness_shared.token_index`; if no match → 401. * Set `derivedCallingHarness = <slug from match>` on request context. * If body has `callingHarness` and it doesn’t match → 403 with clear error. * If verb is `send_message` and body has `from` and it doesn’t match → 403. * If verb is `scaffold_harness` and body has `parent_slug` → 400 (validation error). **Three SQL-only verbs *(\~1d)*:** * `send_message`: validate `reason` ≥ 10 chars; placeholder-regex match logs warning to `executed_actions.reason` but proceeds. INSERT into `harness_<to_slug>.messages` with `from_slug = <derivedCallingHarness>`. If `kind === 'Directive'`, also append to `harness_<to_slug>.supervisor_notes`. * `mark_message_status`: UPDATE `harness_<derivedCallingHarness>.messages` (only your own inbox/outbox is yours to mark) `SET status = $2, acknowledged_at = now() WHERE id = $1`. * `spinup_project`: opens a PG transaction across all affected schemas; INSERT into `harness_shared.projects`; for each requested department, recurse-in-process to fire follow-up `send_message` (kickoff/priority/budget) within the same transaction. Single COMMIT or single ROLLBACK. Returns `{subActions: [{actionId, op, ok}, ...]}` for diagnostic detail. **`scaffold_harness` *(\~1.75d)*:** * Validate `projectSlug`, `template`, `spec`, `goal`. * Look up `template` in the spawnable catalog. If not present or `spawnable` field absent, reject with `validation_error: 'template not spawnable'`. * Check slug uniqueness: query `harness_shared.projects WHERE slug = $1`. If exists → 409 `slug already in use`. * Shell out to `papercusp init <projectSlug> --from <template>` with **5-minute** timeout. * After init succeeds, atomically merge `parent_slug: <derivedCallingHarness>` into the new harness’s `.papercusp/config.json`. * Generate `harness_token`, write to the new harness’s `.papercusp/config.json` (chmod 0600). * Call internal harness-projects registration with `parent_slug` (which provisions the per-harness PG schema, including the new `config_token` + `token_index` rows). * On partial scaffold (init succeeded, register failed): error response includes the partially-created path so retry with same `actionId` cleans up + retries. Idempotency check on `executed_actions` short-circuits before any FS work. * On `papercusp init` failure: rollback any partial directory creation, return `internal` error with stderr. * On 5-min timeout: SIGTERM → SIGKILL → rollback, return `internal` error with `timeout: true`. **Idempotency wrapper *(\~0.25d)*:** 
```ts
const cached = await getExecutedAction(actionId, callerSlug);
if (cached) return cached.response;  // cache-is-authoritative; documented
const result = await dispatch(action);
await saveExecutedAction({
  actionId, op: action.op, callerSlug: derivedCallingHarness,
  targetSlug: extractTargetSlug(action), reason: action.reason ?? null,
  request: action, response: result,
});
return result;
```
 Verify each verb individually with curl (using a real bearer token), including auth-failure paths; commit each verb as its own commit. **Gate:** all four verbs return 200 on happy path + 4xx on validation failures + 401/403 on auth failures + 409 on slug conflicts + idempotent on `actionId` replay. ### Step 2.5 — Verify or wire the `inspect_harness` capability *(\~0.5d)* [Section titled “Step 2.5 — Verify or wire the inspect\_harness capability (\~0.5d)”](#step-25--verify-or-wire-the-inspect_harness-capability-05d) Outcome from Step 0.5 verification dictates this step: * **If `Bash` is already in `--allowed-tools`:** validate that an agent can curl `localhost:3055/api/harness/projects` from inside a tool call.
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Built-in: notify parent harness on mission completion.
# Fires only when this harness has parent_slug set in .papercusp/config.json.
# User-supplied .papercusp/hooks/afterDone.sh overrides this entirely.
set -e
PARENT_SLUG="$(jq -r '.parent_slug // empty' .papercusp/config.json 2>/dev/null)"
[ -z "$PARENT_SLUG" ] && exit 0  # no parent, silent success


TOKEN="$(jq -r '.harness_token // empty' .papercusp/config.json 2>/dev/null)"
[ -z "$TOKEN" ] && { echo "afterDone: no harness_token in config; skipping" >&2; exit 0; }


SELF_SLUG="$(jq -r '.slug // empty' .papercusp/config.json 2>/dev/null)"
[ -z "$SELF_SLUG" ] && SELF_SLUG="$(basename "$PWD")"


ACTION_ID="$(uuidgen)"
BASE="${PAPERCUSP_OPERATOR_BASE:-http://localhost:3055}"


curl -sS --max-time 30 -X POST "$BASE/api/admin/execute-action" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "$(jq -nc \
    --arg id "$ACTION_ID" \
    --arg to "$PARENT_SLUG" \
    '{actionId: $id, action: {op: "send_message", to: [$to], kind: "Completion", subject: "mission DONE", body: "", reason: "afterDone substrate hook: notifying parent of mission completion"}}')" \
  > /dev/null
```

# Run.sh → TS orchestrator port (handoff)

> TypeScript port of the bash autonomous-harness orchestrator. State as of 2026-04-27.

The ported run-loop is now RETIRED (2026-06-06) This is a **historical handoff doc**. The TS run-loop this port produced (`main-loop.ts`, `bin/run.ts`, `pre-loop.ts`, the checkpoints/snapshots/dispatches cluster) was retired and archived to `libs/papercusp/_retired/orchestrator-run-loop/` (plan `archive-legacy-orchestrator-deadcode-2026-06-06`; git tag `legacy-orchestrator-run-loop-retired-2026-06-06`) — superseded by the **DBOS durable pipeline** (`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`). Parts of the port were deliberately kept LIVE rather than moved: `invoke.ts`, `lanes.ts`, the worker chunk-loop (`worker-chunk-loop.ts` / `chunk-loop-driver.ts`), `cost-cap.ts`, and `decision-parse.ts` all remain in the `@papercusp/orchestrator` package (`libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/`) and are **consumed** by the DBOS pipeline via `@papercusp/orchestrator` imports (e.g. `parseDecision`, `parseDecisionFor`, `DECISION_VERBS` in `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`). They do **not** live inside the `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/` directory. The `papercusp-orchestrate` bin and the `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR` fall-through described below no longer exist. Note also that `bash run.sh` itself was deleted entirely (2026-05-30): the TS path became the canonical, only main-loop driver well before this retirement, and `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR=0` is now a warning-only no-op, **not** a working bash fallback. The body below — describing `run.sh` as the live fall-through target and the flag as opt-in — is historical and no longer accurate. ## Why this exists [Section titled “Why this exists”](#why-this-exists) The autonomous-harness orchestrator was historically a 2,122-line bash script (`libs/papercusp/packages/harness/run.sh`). The desktop app needs to drop the bash prereq for Windows users (Git for Windows is currently required to run the loop). A TypeScript port of `run.sh` achieves that without losing Claude Max subscription support — the port keeps the agent CLI (`omp -p` by default, `claude -p` opt-in) as a child-process spawn rather than switching to the SDK. Hard constraint for handoff Do **not** swap the agent CLI (`omp -p` or `claude -p`) for `@anthropic-ai/sdk`. Both CLIs handle Claude Max auth via the user’s Claude Code session (omp via Meridian’s SDK-bridge, claude directly); the SDK route requires API keys and breaks Max users. The whole point of the port is to drop bash, not the CLI layer. ## Where it lives [Section titled “Where it lives”](#where-it-lives) New package `@papercusp/orchestrator` at `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/` (in the `papercupai/papercusp` submodule). Feature-flagged via `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR=1` — currently opt-in. The CLI entry `bin/run.ts` handles the flag and falls through to bash for any decision branch the TS port doesn’t yet cover. ## Stage table [Section titled “Stage table”](#stage-table) | Stage | Status | Tests | Notes | | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 0. # Pi (oh-my-pi) integration

> Two-track integration — pi as worker-role CLI (Option

[`oh-my-pi`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi) (binary `omp`) is a 3.5k★ open-source AI coding agent for the terminal — strong tool harness (read / bash / edit / write / grep / find / lsp / python / browser / subagents / hooks / plugins), `--mode=rpc/json` structured output, multi-model fuzzy matching, session resume, and a TUI. It complements Papercusp at a different layer: **pi has strong in-loop autonomy; Papercusp has strong mission orchestration**. Together: pi as the worker, Papercusp as the conductor. This page covers two integration tracks. ## Track A — Pi as the worker-role CLI [Section titled “Track A — Pi as the worker-role CLI”](#track-a--pi-as-the-worker-role-cli) The smallest valuable integration. Papercusp’s per-role config already supports overrides; add `cliBin` to the schema so individual roles can specify a non-default CLI. 
```json
// config.json (in any harness)
{
  "primaryRole": "orchestrator",
  "roles": {
    "worker": { "cliBin": "pi", "model": "opus" },
    "validator": { "cliBin": "claude" },
    "orchestrator": { "cliBin": "claude" }
  }
}
```
 **What lands:** pi runs the worker pipeline (where tool breadth matters); claude stays on plan / validate / orchestrate (where structured-decision reliability matters). Each invocation is `pi -p --no-session --append-system-prompt=<file>` so the fresh-context contract holds. **Effort:** \~½ day. The bash run.sh’s `invoke()` and the TS orchestrator’s `invoke.ts` both already shell out to a configurable CLI binary; this is wiring per-role config through to that spawn. **Output parsing.** Pi’s `--mode=json` emits a JSONL event stream with the same shape papercusp already parses for claude (session header, then events). Empirically verified: first event is `{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"…","cwd":"…"}` followed by tool/message events. The adapter to map pi’s event names to papercusp’s audit schema is \~30 lines, not a deal-breaker. **Auth.** Pi inherits the sidecar’s environment, including `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN`. Users logged into Claude Code see no auth prompt when papercusp invokes pi — the same Claude Max subscription that drives `claude -p` drives `pi -p`. Other providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, …) flow the same way via their respective env vars. ### Cost-mixing example [Section titled “Cost-mixing example”](#cost-mixing-example) The interesting payoff is fine-grained cost control across roles. Pi’s four model slots ([see §16.4 in the spec](/spec/cli-pluggability/#two-layer-pluggability-a-worked-example)) let a single config dial each role independently: 
```json
// config.json — opinionated mid-budget setup
{
  "roles": {
    "scoper":       { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--plan=opus"] },
    "planner":      { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--plan=opus"] },
    "worker":       { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--model=sonnet", "--smol=haiku"] },
    "validator":    { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--model=gemini-2-flash"] },
    "orchestrator": { "cliBin": "claude" }
  }
}
```
 Reasoning: opus on the rare planning calls, sonnet on hot-path worker calls (with haiku for tool-plan subtasks via pi’s `--smol`), gemini flash on cheap validator passes, claude on the orchestrator for stable decision-verb output. Pairs naturally with papercusp’s [hard-stop budget enforcement](/spec/state/#53-hard-stop-budget-enforcement) — the substrate enforces the hard cap; this config tunes the per-call cost. See [§16 CLI pluggability](/internal/docs/spec/cli-pluggability) for the substrate concept this builds on. ## Track B — Embedded pi TUI as a peer pane [Section titled “Track B — Embedded pi TUI as a peer pane”](#track-b--embedded-pi-tui-as-a-peer-pane) A new `pi` tab in the harness dashboard that hosts an interactive `omp` process inside the desktop app. The autonomous loop continues in the background; the human can drop into pi mid-mission for surgical override. ### Goal [Section titled “Goal”](#goal) Surface an interactive pi TUI inside the Papercusp Desktop harness UI alongside the existing `vscode` / `git` / `brainstorm` panels. (Phase 3b adds a “open in pi” button per feature that scopes pi to that feature’s worktree.) ### Design decisions [Section titled “Design decisions”](#design-decisions) 1. **PTY runs in the Node sidecar for the web/cloud path; the desktop build uses a Tauri-native pty.** The original decision was sidecar-only `node-pty` (the same sidecar code runs in desktop and cloud modes, and a Rust-side PTY would fork the codebase). That still holds for the web/cloud case. **For the native desktop build this was revised** (plan `desktop-ipc-transport-completion-2026-05-20`): inside the Tauri webview, `PiPanel` detects `isTauriNative()` and skips HTTP/WS/SSE entirely — it forks the pty in the Tauri Rust process via `openNativeSession()` and streams over Tauri IPC end-to-end, consulting `POST /pty/resolve` only to build harness-aware args/cwd/env without spawning. The Node-sidecar `node-pty` path (HTTP control plane + WS/SSE data channel) remains the transport for the web/cloud case. 2. **I/O transport: WebSocket preferred, SSE + POST fallback.** A full-duplex WebSocket transport shipped: `PiPanel.tsx` connects via `ptyWsUrlForId()` and attaches xterm’s `AttachAddon` (binary frames, no base64), backed by the `packages/operator-core/lib/pty-ws.ts` WS server. It falls back to SSE output + POST input only when the WS server is unreachable (proxy doesn’t pass upgrades, `PAPERCUSP_PTY_WS=0`, etc.). The HTTP control plane (`POST /spawn`, `/kill`, …) is identical either way — only the data channel differs. SSE was the original v1 transport (Next.js’s standalone server didn’t natively support raw WS-upgrade on arbitrary routes); WS is now primary and SSE is the compatibility path. 3. **`pi` is a user-installed prerequisite, not bundled.** Matches the existing `claude` pattern. The desktop preflight UI already surfaces missing-prereq state — extend with a `pi` check. 4. **No session persistence in v1.** Pi has `--no-session` for ephemeral runs; persistent resume across pane reopen is v2 polish. 5. **Slot into the existing `MainPanel` union.** `HarnessDashboard.tsx` lists every embedded-tool tab (`brainstorm`, `proposals`, `git`, `dashboard`, `vscode`, `insights`, etc.) — adding `'pi'` follows the established pattern. The `vscode` tab (which embeds `code-server` in an iframe) is the direct precedent: same shape, different embedded tool. ### Rejected alternatives [Section titled “Rejected alternatives”](#rejected-alternatives) * **Rust-side PTY (`portable-pty` crate)** — originally rejected (forks desktop/cloud paths, more native build pain on Windows, couples a UI feature to the platform shell). This was **effectively revised for the native desktop transport**: the desktop build now does fork the pty Rust-side (see design decision #1). The web/cloud path keeps the sidecar `node-pty`, so the “forks the codebase” concern is contained to the desktop transport seam rather than the whole stack. * **SSH/wetty-style HTTP terminal services** — another process, another auth surface, another port. The `node-pty + xterm.js + SSE` stack runs entirely inside the existing sidecar. ### Pi command surface used by Track B [Section titled “Pi command surface used by Track B”](#pi-command-surface-used-by-track-b) The pane spawns one of: * `omp` — pi’s interactive default mode. Best for general use. * `omp shell` — pi’s “interactive shell console” subcommand. Slightly different surface; useful for shell-flavored workflows. Useful flags to pass: * `--no-pty` — disable pi’s *internal* PTY-based bash execution. We already have a PTY (the one we bridge to xterm.js); pi nesting another inside it can confuse signal handling and resize semantics. Set this in the embedded pane. * `--session-dir=$STATE_DIR/.pi-sessions/` (or env `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) — point pi’s session store at the harness state dir so sessions are scoped to the harness, not the user’s home. Falls back to `~/.omp/agent` if unset. * `--append-system-prompt=<file>` — for Phase 3b feature-scoped opens, inject the feature’s spec/lineage as additional system prompt. * `--export=<session-file>` — Phase 3d candidate. After a session ends, exporting it to HTML and storing under the harness audit dir makes the in-pane work part of the durable record. ### Phasing [Section titled “Phasing”](#phasing) **Phase 3a — MVP terminal pane (\~1 day).** ✅ shipped. A new `pi` tab in the harness dashboard. Click → opens xterm.js connected to a fresh `pi` process in the harness’s project directory. Keystrokes in, output out. Close tab → kill pi. **Phase 3b — peer pane layout + feature-scoped launch (\~1 day).** ✅ shipped (tab-scoped, not split-pane). Each feature’s `FeaturePeekPanel` gets an “open in pi” button → pi spawns in `<stateDir>/worktrees/<fid>` (falls back to project root if no worktree). The pty is deliberately **not** killed when the client disconnects: the SSE stream’s `onClose` keeps the handle alive (PiPanel unmounts on every dashboard tab switch), and PiPanel’s own unmount cleanup explicitly skips the kill so a remount can resume the same session via `resumePtyId`. Genuinely-abandoned handles are reaped by the 5-minute idle reaper in `pty-bridge`, not by a disconnect kill. The plan called for a split-pane layout; we shipped tab-pattern instead (matches the existing `vscode` tab; no layout-shift, full pane width). True split-pane is a future affordance if needed. **Phase 3c — desktop polish (\~½ day).** ✅ shipped. `pi` added to preflight checks (PATH + well-known-paths probe). Install-hint UI surfaces missing-pi with `brew install can1357/oh-my-pi/oh-my-pi`. README documents pi as an optional prereq. Pi missing does NOT block the app from booting — only the pi tab degrades. **Phase 3d — partially shipped.** * **Feature-scoped system-prompt injection** ✅ shipped. When the user clicks “open in pi” on a feature, the spawn endpoint reads `harness_features` for that `(slug, featureId)` (columns `feature_id`, `title`, `summary`, `status`), formats them as markdown via the shared kickoff factory, writes the brief to a fresh `mkdtemp` dir under `/dev/shm` (tmpdir fallback) named `<feature-id>.md`, and adds `--append-system-prompt=<path>` to the omp args. The temp dir is scheduled for removal after 30s. Pi launches already aware of the feature it’s working on. Falls back silently when the feature lookup fails — no error surface, just no injection. * **Per-harness session persistence** ✅ shipped via `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=<stateDir>/pi-sessions/`. Each harness has its own pi history under its state dir; sessions persist across pane reopens automatically. Future polish: explicit “resume last session” button using `omp -c` / `omp -r <id>`. * **Audit export** ✅ shipped. `attachAuditExport()` registers an `onExit` hook that runs `exportPiSessions()`, which finds the session jsonls created during the pty’s lifetime and shells out to `omp --export <sessionFile>` per session, storing the resulting HTML under `<stateDir>/audit/pi-sessions/`. Two GET endpoints serve the exports — `GET /pi-sessions/audit` (lists them) and `GET /pi-sessions/audit/:filename` (serves one HTML, basename-validated against path traversal) — and PiPanel’s “past sessions” chip + popover lists and links them. * **Pi extension** ✅ shipped and wired into spawns. The spawn endpoint resolves `global-plugins/pi/extension.ts` and, when it exists, pushes `-e <path>` onto the omp args (the `-e <path>` extension flag — not `--plugin-dir`). The extension registers `papercusp_status`, `papercusp_list_features`, `papercusp_lineage`, `papercusp_audit`, `papercusp_proposals`, `papercusp_decisions`, and `papercusp_issues` (underscore-namespaced). `GET /pty/tools` enumerates them (returning `extensionAvailable: false` with an empty list when the extension isn’t present). The extension reads papercusp state through the existing API (so no extra trust boundary). * **Subagent cross-pollination** — deferred. `omp agents unpack` ships curated subagent personas. Wrap each as a papercusp plugin so they appear in the marketplace catalog. Cross-pollinate the ecosystems. * **Multi-pane** — shipped via the dockview `PiTerminalsDock.tsx` (see the file tables below). Multiple concurrent pi panes scoped to different features, capped per the process-wide, host-scaled pty cap in §Risks. ### File-level changes (Phase 3a + 3b + 3c) [Section titled “File-level changes (Phase 3a + 3b + 3c)”](#file-level-changes-phase-3a--3b--3c) #### New files [Section titled “New files”](#new-files) | Path | Purpose | | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/pty/index.ts` | Router mounted at `/api/harness/:slug/pty/*` (+ `/pi-sessions/audit/*`). Endpoints: `POST /spawn`, `POST /resolve`, `POST /prewarm`, `GET /:id/stream` (SSE), `POST /:id/input`, `POST /:id/resize`, `POST /:id/kill`, `GET /pty/tools`, `GET /pi-sessions/audit[/:filename]`. Mutating routes are `auth: 'loopback'`; the read/stream routes are `auth: 'public'`. Handles live in a module-level `Map` (in `pty-bridge`) plus a prewarm pool. | | `apps/operator/app/harness/PiPanel.tsx` | xterm.js React component (xterm + addon-fit + addon-web-links). SSE on mount, POST keystrokes on input, POST resize on container resize. Cleanup on unmount. | | `apps/operator/app/harness/PiPanel.css` | Pane chrome (header bar, “open new”, spinner) + xterm theme matching papercusp dark colors. | | `packages/operator-core/lib/pty-bridge.ts` | Server-side `@lydell/node-pty` wrapper. `spawnPty({command, args, cwd, env, cols, rows})` → typed handle with `onData` / `write` / `resize` / `kill`, an owner-SID tag, a 1 MB byte ring, and a per-handle `xterm-headless` + `SerializeAddon` mirror for bounded screen-state replay. The HTTP control plane is unchanged. | | `packages/operator-core/lib/pty-tauri.ts` | Native desktop data path — `isTauriNative()` + `openNativeSession()`.
```plaintext
POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/spawn
  body: { command?, args?, laneId?, cols?, rows?,
          env?, resumePtyId? }
  → { id, command, args, cwd, pid }   // (+ prewarmed:true if adopted
                                       //  from the pool, resumed:true
                                       //  if resumePtyId matched a live pty)
  cwd is derived from laneId (the lane's worktree if it exists, else the
  project root) — there is no ctxPrompt or cwd field in the body.


POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/resolve
  Same body shape; returns { command, args, cwd, env } WITHOUT spawning.
  Used by the Tauri-native path to build harness-aware args.


POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/prewarm
  Reserves a warm omp (same body shape) so /spawn can adopt it and hide
  omp's ~1.2s startup. → { reserved: true } (or reused:true).


GET /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/stream    (text/event-stream — SSE fallback)
  ← event: data\ndata: <base64-bytes>\n\n
  ← event: exit\ndata: {"code": 0}\n\n
  On connect, replays the full byte history into the new subscriber.


POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/input    { data: <base64-bytes> }
POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/resize   { cols, rows }
POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/kill


GET /api/harness/:slug/pty/tools          enumerates the pi extension's tools
GET /api/harness/:slug/pi-sessions/audit  lists exported session HTML
GET /api/harness/:slug/pi-sessions/audit/:filename  serves one export
```
 On the WS path the data channel is binary frames of raw pty bytes (no base64). On the SSE fallback, bytes are base64-encoded over JSON to keep the stream uniform regardless of encoding (xterm.js handles arbitrary byte streams; pi may emit non-UTF-8 in edge cases like binary file contents). Idle PTYs (no input, no consumer marking activity) auto-kill after 5 minutes. **Auth split.** Only the read/stream routes are `auth: 'public'` (`/:id/stream`, the two `/pi-sessions/audit` routes, and `/pty/tools`). The mutating routes — `spawn`, `resolve`, `prewarm`, `input`, `resize`, `kill` — are `auth: 'loopback'`. **Reconnect / replay.** The server keeps two replay sources per handle: an `xterm-headless` mirror fed every byte (bounded screen-state serialization, \~tens of KB, VS Code’s approach — used for WS reconnect), and a 1 MB raw-byte ring (full-history replay, used by the SSE path). A dashboard tab switch therefore resumes the same pty with prior output intact rather than starting fresh. **Cross-agent wake routing.** Each managed pty is tagged with its owner SID (`PAPERCUSP_SID` from the spawn env) so the await-event wake executor can route a wake turn into the correct session. `findPtyByPid` carries a recycled-pid guard (EI-151): a recorded pid recycled by the OS to a *different* owner’s live pty is not treated as a match. ### Critical files to read first [Section titled “Critical files to read first”](#critical-files-to-read-first) | File | Why | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `apps/operator/app/harness/PiTerminalsDock.tsx` + `PiPanel.tsx` | The current pi-pane surface — dockview multi-pane container + the xterm/SSE panel. (Supersedes the original `HarnessDashboard.tsx` `MainPanel`-union integration.) | | `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/index.ts` | Hono route-table assembly. The pty router registers the same way the harness/plugins routers do. | | `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` | Sidecar spawn — confirms env passes through (`PATH`, etc.) which pi needs. | | `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/desktop/preflight.ts` | Pattern for prereq checks. The `pi` check mirrors the `claude` check (plus well-known-path probing). | | `papercusp-desktop/web/index.html` | `renderHint()` switch — the pi case. | ### Verification [Section titled “Verification”](#verification) **Phase 3a:** 1. Launch the desktop shell: `cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev` (the only supported run path; it boots the operator sidecar + webview). 2. In the Tauri window, open a harness (`/harness/<some-slug>`). 3. Click the new pi tab. 4. Pi prompt appears; type `pwd` + Enter; output shows the harness’s project directory. 5. Type `exit`; pane shows “(pi exited 0)” and the spawn lifecycle cleans up (verify `pgrep -af omp` returns nothing). 6. Resize the window; xterm-fit addon resizes; pi sees the new width (`tput cols`). **Phase 3b:** 7. Two-pane layout works: dashboard left, pi right; resizable divider; both visible. 8. On a feature row, “Open in pi” puts pi inside that feature’s worktree directory (verify with `pwd`). 9. Pi’s first prompt includes the feature spec + lineage (visible when asked “what are you working on?”). **Phase 3c:** 10. `pi` shows as `missing` in the bootstrap UI when uninstalled; install hint card appears with a brew/install command. 11. Once installed, `pi` flips to `ok` on next preflight tick; pi tab works. 12. README quick-start mentions pi as optional. **Cross-cutting:** * No native-binary load errors at sidecar boot on macOS, Linux, Windows. * The desktop bundle still ships within size budget (no inadvertent +100MB from xterm assets). * No stray pty processes survive sidecar shutdown. ### Risks [Section titled “Risks”](#risks) | Risk | Mitigation | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `node-pty` native binding fails under Next.js `output: 'standalone'` (Next traces deps and may miss the `.node` file). | Verify on day 1. If `next.config.js` `outputFileTracingIncludes` doesn’t capture `node_modules/node-pty/build/Release/*.node`, add an explicit include. Fallback: ship pty-bridge as a separate child process the Next handler shells out to. | | `node-pty` Windows ConPTY initialization fails on older Win10. | Document min Windows version (10 1809+) in README. Surface a clear inline error in the pane. | | Pi binary not on `PATH` despite being installed (Mac homebrew + Tauri-Cocoa launches without a login shell). | Probe `/usr/local/bin/omp`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/omp`, `~/.cargo/bin/omp` in addition to `which`. Fall back to user-configurable `pi.binPath` in `config.json`. | | Concurrent pi panes spawn many processes / use lots of memory. | A **process-wide, host-scaled** cap, not a fixed per-harness number: `livePtyCap()` = `min(host-scaled backstop, fleet maxSimultaneousAgents)`, where the backstop = `min(2× the resource-profile agent budget, ceiling 16)`. Spawning past the cap throws `pty cap reached (n/cap)`; the pane surfaces it inline. On a small box this floors low (a 4-core laptop’s backstop is \~2–4); on a typical box it sits well above 4. | | Pi’s nested PTY (its `bash` tool) conflicts with the outer xterm.js PTY — terminal corruption or signal loss. | Spawn with `--no-pty`. Pi degrades gracefully (loses interactive bash but keeps every other tool). | | Auth state drifts: user logged into Claude Code in their normal shell, but the desktop app launches without that env. | Surface `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` presence in the preflight UI; document the GUI-app-no-login-shell gotcha in the README. | ## What is explicitly NOT in scope [Section titled “What is explicitly NOT in scope”](#what-is-explicitly-not-in-scope) * Replacing the `vscode` tab — pi sits alongside it, not instead of it. * Web (non-desktop) deployment of the pi pane — works the same way (sidecar is identical), but rollout is separate. (The original “not in scope” list also named the pi plugin and session-persistence/resume; both shipped under Phase 3d — see the phasing notes above.)

# Plugin + marketplace pipeline — state as of 2026-05-11

> One-page reference for the TS plugin/template/snapshot/marketplace system as it stands today. Where the code is, what's covered by tests, what's deferred, and where to look first.

Dated snapshot — paths and the marketplace surface have moved Preserved as the 2026-05-11 milestone. Reading it today, note: * The operator is now **`apps/operator/`** and its `app/api/**` routes were ported to **Hono routers under `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/**`**; `apps/operator/lib/*` (e.g. `plugin-host-runtime.ts`, `plugin-grants.ts`) now lives under **`packages/operator-core/lib/`**. The Next route paths in the tables below are stale. * Migrations **`051`** and **`052`** were folded into **`000-baseline.sql`** and archived (`libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/archive/`); they are no longer live numbered migrations. `harness_shared.plugin_capability_grants` is defined in the baseline. * The `localhost:3057` / `papercuspai.com` marketplace-api was superseded by the in-app **Cupboard** (`apps/operator-public`, CF Workers + Hono + D1). * The “use git worktrees for non-main work” hard rule is **reversed** under the current model: the shared tree stays on `staging` and you do **not** branch/worktree — concurrency is serialized by the `locks:*` + `coord:*` systems. See the repo `CLAUDE.md` “Branch discipline” section. ## TL;DR [Section titled “TL;DR”](#tldr) Three publishable kinds (`plugin`, `template`, `snapshot`) share one marketplace pipeline. Operator at `localhost:3055` serves the install/discover surface; marketplace-api at `localhost:3057` is the registry. Plugins run in-process under a two-tier capability check (manifest ∩ user-granted). Tests cover every helper and DB-backed function shipped in this session. *As of today:* the `snapshot` publishable kind was **retired** (see the snapshot note below); the `:3057`/`papercuspai.com` registry was superseded by the in-app **Cupboard**; plugins also load as **WASM** or **daemon** runtimes, not only in-process JS. ## Source layout [Section titled “Source layout”](#source-layout) | What | Where | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Plugin SDK (types, capability strings, manifest schema) | `packages/plugin-sdk/` | | Plugin loader (manifest validate, capability check, reaction rules, action registry, audit) | `packages/plugin-loader/` | | Plugin host runtime in operator | `apps/operator/lib/plugin-host-runtime.ts` | | Per-(plugin, harness) grants | `apps/operator/lib/plugin-grants.ts` + `harness_shared.plugin_capability_grants` in `000-baseline.sql` | | Audit log (PG writer) | `apps/operator/lib/plugin-audit-writer.ts` | | Marketplace API routes | `apps/operator/app/api/{marketplace,plugins,templates,snapshots,harness/[slug]/save-as-template}/` | | Marketplace UI components | `libs/marketplace-public-ui/src/` (shared with public site) | | Operator-side marketplace pages | `apps/operator/app/marketplace/{,templates,plugins,snapshots}/` | | Operator-side installed pages | `apps/operator/app/installed/{harnesses,plugins,snapshots,templates}/` | | Marketplace registry server | `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/` (separate repo `papercupai/papercusp-registry`) | | CLI (`papercusp install`, `plugin enable/disable/lint/init/doctor`, `snapshot {fork,publish}`) | `libs/papercusp/packages/cli/src/` | | Snapshot capture / restore | `libs/papercusp-export-state/src/` — **RETIRED**, moved to `_retired/snapshot-system/papercusp-export-state` (see snapshot note below) | ## What runs end-to-end today [Section titled “What runs end-to-end today”](#what-runs-end-to-end-today) ### Plugin lifecycle [Section titled “Plugin lifecycle”](#plugin-lifecycle) 1. **Install** — *(superseded)* The original `POST /api/marketplace/install-plugin` path that shelled out to `papercusp install <slug>@<version>` (atomic staging-dir tarball download/extract/validate) is **dead**. Install now goes through **`POST /api/cupboard/install-plugin`** (revive-cupboard-distribution D-003/P2), which **git-clones** the Cupboard listing’s GitHub repo (resolved from `listingId`, or a direct `githubUrl`) and runs the capability-gate + install-consent path. The route header itself describes the old `:3057`/CLI tarball install as dead. 2. **Enable** — `POST /api/plugins/enable { slug, harnesses[], disable? }` adds to `enabled-plugins.json` for each harness and writes the boot-time silent grant backfill. `enabled-plugins.json` stays the on-disk source of truth (the CLI is its only writer), but it is now **mirrored into `harness_shared.plugin_enables`** (`plugin-enables-pg.ts`) so read paths use one cross-harness PG query instead of fanning over the filesystem; an FS watcher (`harness-fs-watcher.ts`) re-mirrors on direct CLI/file edits. 3. **Consent** — `/installed/plugins/<slug>/permissions` renders a harnesses × capabilities grid; toggling `POST /api/plugins/grants { plugin, version, harness, capabilities, action }` mutates `harness_shared.plugin_capability_grants`. Two-tier check: every `hasCapability(ctx, cap)` ANDs manifest with the granted set. 4. **Run** — The typed `PluginHooks` shape is now a **frozen back-compat surface** (plugin-system-hive-port D-003); the host fires it by direct iteration. Members: `onLoad`, `onUnload`, `onHarnessCreated`, `beforeMissionStart`, `afterDone`, `onFeaturePassed`, `onProposalAccepted`, `onPostOrchestrator`, `onPostWorker`, `onPostValidator`, `contributeOperatorSuggestions`, `getStateForReload`, `restoreFromReload`. The WordPress-style **HookBus** (`addAction`/`addFilter`, plus topic strings like `mission.start` / `task.passed` / `feature.completed` / `proposal.accepted`) was **retired and deleted** from loader/SDK/host (P-006/D-003) — those topics no longer exist as fire targets. The live extension surface is capability-scoped **event-reaction rules** (see the extension axes below). 5. **Action invocation** — `POST /api/plugins/[...path]` proxies through `ctx.actions.register(...)`’d handlers. Every invocation produces an audit row via `PgAuditWriter` (fail-closed — action fails if audit write fails). 6. **Update** — `GET /api/plugins/updates` diffs installed vs catalog; `/installed/plugins` shows “Update → vX.Y.Z” with new-cap re-consent prompt before bumping. 7. **Uninstall** — `POST /api/plugins/uninstall { slug }` removes the global plugin dir + disables from every harness it was enabled in. ### Plugin runtime model + extension axes [Section titled “Plugin runtime model + extension axes”](#plugin-runtime-model--extension-axes) *(Added post-snapshot — the runtime surface grew well beyond the action registry described above.)* Each plugin instance gets a per-(plugin, harness) `ctx` carrying: * `ctx.actions` — the action registry (`register(...)`’d handlers behind `/api/plugins/[...path]`). * `ctx.spawn` — capability-gated `compute:exec` with a frozen PATH (`makePluginSpawn`). * `ctx.kv` — plugin-private, quota’d K/V backed by `harness_shared.plugin_kv` (quota from `manifest.kvQuota`; left `undefined` in test/no-PG contexts, so plugins must tolerate absence). * `ctx.oauth.token(field)` — acquires a fresh access token, resolving the backing provider from the plugin’s manifest `oauth[]` entries. * `ctx.recordResource(...)` — writes a record to the provision WAL (for in-process plugins that create external resources from a hook handler rather than a setup script). The **primary** extension surface is no longer the typed lifecycle hooks — it is two manifest-declared axes the host wires at load: * **Tool axis** (main consumer): `manifest.tools[]` entries are projected as agent tools `<plugin>.<verb>` over both HTTP and MCP (`registerPluginTools`). * **Event-reaction axis**: `manifest.reactions[]` rules — when a trigger `on` settles, the rule fires one of the plugin’s **own** tools through normal capability-scoped dispatch. Each `on` trigger requires an `events:listen:<on>` capability (`registerPluginReactionRules`). Plugin-emitted events (the WASM event sink, `plugins:fire_event`) feed the same reaction registry as synthetic events. The **RoutineDefinition** and **RoleDefinition** manifest axes were **retired** in the hive port (`collectRoutines`/`collectRoles` deleted, zero callers). The manifest `roles` field stays schema-tolerated as inert data (so existing plugins that declare it still load); routines authors are pointed at blueprint triggers / event-reaction schedules. ### Template lifecycle [Section titled “Template lifecycle”](#template-lifecycle) 1. **Save** — “Save template” button on harness dashboard → `POST /api/harness/<slug>/save-as-template { slug, version, description?, author? }` forks the recipe (SPEC.md, AGENTS.md, `.papercusp/config.json`, `.papercusp/validation-contract.md` + plugin recommendations from `enabled-plugins.json`) into `~/.papercusp/templates/<slug>/<version>/`. 2. **Publish** — `POST /api/templates/<slug>/<version>/publish` tars + signs + uploads to marketplace-api. 3. **Install** — `POST /api/marketplace/install { slug, projectName, targetPath? }` scaffolds a new project. **Slug-collision recovery (PR #5)**: returns `{ code: 'project_name_taken', suggestedName: '<base>-2' }` on conflict; UI auto-offers via `confirm()`. Partial-init cleanup wipes half-scaffolded dirs on `papercusp init` failure. ### Snapshot lifecycle [Section titled “Snapshot lifecycle”](#snapshot-lifecycle) Publishable-snapshot system RETIRED The publishable-snapshot / snapshot-**export** pipeline below was **retired** (retire-snapshots-instance-spec-2026-06-09, shipped). `libs/papercusp-export-state` moved to `_retired/snapshot-system/papercusp-export-state`; `@papercusp/export-state`, the `snapshots:*` tools, all `/api/snapshots/*` publish routes, and the Cupboard `kind=snapshot` were retired (migration 199 drops `snapshot_index`). The fork route `instantiate.ts` — the **only** non-test caller of `copyGrantsToNewHarness` — now lives under `_retired/`. The reproducible replacement is the **InstanceSpec** system (`packages/operator-core/lib/instance-spec/`). The surviving `/api/harness/:slug/snapshots` route is a **different** feature — per-harness iteration snapshots (FS rollback of `.papercusp/snapshots/<ts>-iter-<n>/`), not publishable snapshots. *Historical (pre-retirement) flow:* 1. **Capture** — `POST /api/snapshots/create` writes a tarball under `<harness>/.papercusp/snapshots/`. 2. **Publish** — `POST /api/snapshots/<id>/publish` uploads to marketplace. 3. **Fork** — `POST /api/snapshots/<id>/instantiate` (or `papercusp snapshot fork`) creates a new harness with schema rename. **Grants carry over (PR #2)**: `copyGrantsToNewHarness` copies every `(plugin, version, capability)` grant on the source harness to the new fork via `INSERT … SELECT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. 4. **Republish** — *pending*. PR-B paused per `@plugin`’s reply on coord, awaiting v1 plan greenlight (Batch G+1 bumps `SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 2). ## Hard rules in this code (don’t break) [Section titled “Hard rules in this code (don’t break)”](#hard-rules-in-this-code-dont-break) * **No TS deletion** anywhere in `apps/operator/` or `libs/papercusp/`. Set by `shared.jsonl` 2026-05-10T05:50. * **Rust port is opt-in** via `?backend=rust`; default routes always go to TS. * **Paperclip stomps** `apps/operator/app/harness/*` periodically. `pgrep -af paperclip` before editing harness UI; race-and-recommit if it stomps you. * **Schema ownership**: `packages/plugin-sdk/papercusp-plugin.schema.json` is `@plugin`’s territory going forward (per their handoff on coord 2026-05-11T15:30). Transitional additions get a `kind: contract` post first. * **Use git worktrees** for any non-main feature work — never branch-switch the canonical `papercup/` checkout while other agents may be writing. ## Test coverage [Section titled “Test coverage”](#test-coverage) Plugin-loader tests (vitest, `packages/plugin-loader/`): * 91 cases covering manifest validation, capability matching (incl. two-tier), action registry, semver, audit, api-factory, tools. *(Snapshot-era count; the suite has since grown and the HookBus tests were removed with the HookBus — new specs include the daemon/WASM runtimes, reaction rules, and `plugin doctor`.)* Operator unit tests (vitest, `apps/operator/`): * 67 cases on pure helpers from PRs #2-#5: `isNewerVersion`, `computeCapChange`, `suggestNextFreeName`, `SLUG_RE`, `SEMVER_RE`, `explainCapability`, `tierBadgeColor`. Operator integration tests (vitest + testcontainers PG, `apps/operator/test/`): * 25 cases covering every public function in `lib/plugin-grants.ts`: `copyGrantsToNewHarness` (8), `grantCapabilities/revokeCapabilities/getGrantsForPluginInHarness` (11), `backfillGrantsFromEnabledPluginsAndLegacyFile` (6). Total: **183 tests** specifically on the plugin/marketplace surface. ## What’s deferred / out of scope [Section titled “What’s deferred / out of scope”](#whats-deferred--out-of-scope) Documented in `/docs/spec/plugin-runtime-roadmap` (Batch F deferrals — **all shipped**): * Typed `ctx.kv` with quotas — **shipped** (`plugin-kv.ts`, backed by `harness_shared.plugin_kv`, per-plugin quotas wired from `manifest.kvQuota`). * Hot-reload state preservation — **shipped** (`getStateForReload`/`restoreFromReload` SDK hooks, gated on `manifest.hotReload.preserveState`, backed by `harness_shared.plugin_reload_state`). * `papercusp plugin doctor` (declared-vs-used capability static analysis) — **shipped** (`plugin-doctor.ts`, wired into the CLI `case 'doctor'` → `cmdPluginDoctor`). Awaiting user greenlight (Batches G/G+/H/I in `papercup-native/docs/ts-plugin-system-v1-plan.md`): * WASM plugin runtime via `@bytecodealliance/jco` — **shipped** (Batch G3/I): loads a `wasm32-wasip2` component via `@papercusp/plugin-loader/wasm` (`initializeWasmPlugin`). * Subprocess daemon runtime via `bwrap` — **shipped** (Batch G3/I): loads a `bwrap`-sandboxed stdio JSON-RPC peer via `@papercusp/plugin-loader/daemon` (`initializeDaemonPlugin`). * Sandboxed iframe UI surface — **shipped** (`apps/operator/lib/PluginIframe.tsx` + the `/api/plugins/iframe-entry` route). * Manifest schema now declares `runtime.kind` of `js` | `wasm` | `daemon`. Out-of-band gated: * **PR-B (snapshot republish UI)** — paused pending G+1/G+2 schema bump * **`feat/bundle-runtime-deps`** in `papercusp-desktop` — only Claude+Meridian on-demand installer is unique; owner’s call ## Key APIs at a glance [Section titled “Key APIs at a glance”](#key-apis-at-a-glance) 
```plaintext
GET   /api/marketplace/catalog                  — proxies marketplace-api with hide-filter
POST  /api/marketplace/install                  — template install (slug-collision aware)
POST  /api/cupboard/install-plugin              — plugin install: git-clone the listing's GitHub repo (replaces the dead marketplace/install-plugin tarball path)
DELETE /api/marketplace/uninstall               — template uninstall
GET   /api/plugins/global                       — installed plugins
GET   /api/plugins/manifest?slug=<id>           — declared capabilities for consent UI
GET   /api/plugins/updates                      — installed-vs-catalog diff with capChange
GET   /api/plugins/grants?plugin=&version=&harness=
POST  /api/plugins/grants                       — toggle a (plugin, harness, cap) grant
POST  /api/plugins/enable                       — enable/disable a plugin in harness(es)
POST  /api/plugins/uninstall
# /api/snapshots/* (create, publish, instantiate, retract) — RETIRED; the
#   publishable-snapshot system moved to _retired/snapshot-system. Replacement:
#   the InstanceSpec system (packages/operator-core/lib/instance-spec/).
#   The surviving /api/harness/:slug/snapshots is a DIFFERENT feature
#   (per-harness iteration snapshots / FS rollback).
POST  /api/harness/<slug>/save-as-template
POST  /api/templates/<slug>/<version>/publish
```
 ## First places to look [Section titled “First places to look”](#first-places-to-look) * New plugin author: `/docs/spec/plugin-quickstart` — five-command flow from blank dir to published plugin. * Plugin runtime contract: `packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts` — capability strings + lifecycle hook signatures. * Capability semantics: `packages/plugin-loader/src/capabilities.ts` — wildcard matching, two-tier AND. * Manifest schema: `packages/plugin-sdk/papercusp-plugin.schema.json` — `additionalProperties: false`. * Lifecycle wire-up: `apps/operator/lib/plugin-host-runtime.ts` — fire-points + audit + grants integration. * Marketplace registry: `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/src/server.ts` — catalog, signing, retraction, SBOM.

# Implementation status

> Phase-by-phase ship state of the Papercusp reference runtime.

Dated phase-status snapshot — paths have since moved This is a historical implementation-status record (Phase 1–§MHS work, through mid-2026). It’s preserved as a dated milestone log; **the file paths and a few component names below are stale** after later refactors. The big renames to keep in mind when reading: * `apps/papercup/**` and `apps/papercusp/**` → the operator now lives at **`apps/operator/`**; its Next.js `app/api/**` routes were ported to **Hono routers under `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/**`**. * The operator-side process-level lifecycle host moved to **`packages/operator-core/lib/plugin-host-runtime.ts`**. The React-render layer named below (`lib/plugin-runtime.ts`, `lib/PluginTabs.tsx`, `lib/PluginReactTab.tsx`) did **not** move — it still lives under **`apps/operator/lib/`**. * The `run.sh` → TS orchestrator port shipped and its ported run-loop was later **retired** (see [orchestrator-port](/internal/docs/implementation/orchestrator-port)); the live pipeline is the DBOS runner in `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`. * The `papercuspai.com` marketplace described in the “After all of the above” table was superseded by the in-app **Cupboard** (`apps/operator-public`). The reference runtime lives in this monorepo (`papercupai/papercup`). Local Linux x86\_64 build → signed → GitHub Release. No CI involved. | | macOS code signing | \~1 day my work + your $99/yr Apple cert | Requires a real Mac to build + notarize on; alpha skips macOS. | | Windows code signing | \~½ day my work + your $200-500/yr OV cert | Local cross-build via `WITH_WINDOWS=1`; signing is a separate step against the OV cert. Eliminates SmartScreen warning (\~1-2wk reputation curve). | | Auto-updater wiring (Tauri) | ✅ shipped | Runtime endpoint resolution + channel-aware manifest (`/api/updates/manifest`) + signed releases via local builds (see desktop `SHIPPING.md`). | | Embedded-Postgres on desktop (drop Postgres prereq) | ✅ shipped | Desktop sidecar bundles `embedded-postgres` (real PG binary with logical replication) and spawns it per-workspace on a TCP port. Default ON via `PAPERCUSP_USE_EMBEDDED_PG=1`; pglite-server remains as a legacy fallback. Zero WS works on desktop in this mode (same as browser). See `libs/papercusp/packages/embedded-postgres-server/`. | | Real branded icons | \~½ day | Replace placeholder paper-cup glyph with designed icons. Pure aesthetics; doesn’t gate anything. | ### After all of the above [Section titled “After all of the above”](#after-all-of-the-above) | Item | Scope | Notes | | ----------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Spec page MDX cleanup | \~1 day | The current MDX is JSX-heavy (preserved from React conversion). Convert tables to markdown tables, strip residual `<p>` / `<ul>` tags, normalize callouts to Starlight `<Aside type="note">` components. Cosmetic but improves authoring ergonomics. | | Move spec to its own repo | \~½ day | After v1.0 freeze. # Performance — rules every agent must follow

> Render, bundle, network, layout, and measurement guidelines distilled from the apps that feel fastest, plus concrete anti-patterns from real audits of this codebase. Apply to all new code.

> **Webapp retired (2026-05-14).** Any `localhost:3055` or `localhost:3070` URL on this page is only reachable while the **Tauri dev shell** is running. Start it with `cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev`. Stack note — Next.js has been removed This page was written when the operator app was a **Next.js App Router** project, and several rules below were framed around RSC / Server Components / Next-specific tooling. **That framework is gone.** The operator is now a **Vite SPA on TanStack Router** (`apps/operator-vite`, dev server on `:3055`) fronting a **Hono host** (`apps/operator/bin/hono-host.ts`, `:3070`). There is no `next` dependency, no RSC, no Server Components, and `'use client'` is an inert vestige. The `next/*` import surface (`next/image`, `next/dynamic`, `next/link`, `next/navigation`) is satisfied by TanStack-Router-backed shims under `apps/operator/lib/router-compat/{dynamic,link,navigation}.tsx`. RSC-only advice (“ship zero JS”, “push `'use client'` to the leaf”) does **not** apply to a SPA — read those rules as historical context. The *measured* perf wins (parallelize fs/PG, request-scoped read caches, virtualize/memoize lists, animate only transform/opacity) still hold; only the **named cause** “Next.js dev mode” and any Next-specific tool are stale. See `apps/operator/docs/plans/finish-next-removal-2026-06-01.md` and `apps/operator/docs/plans/operator-vite-migration-2026-05-20.md`. Read this BEFORE making any changes **Every agent must read this page before changing code in this repo.** “It works” isn’t the same as “it’s fast.” This page captures (a) practices from apps users consider best-in-class — Linear, Notion, Vercel, Figma, Discord, Stripe — and (b) **real anti-patterns we’ve shipped** that have caused production slowdowns. The “What not to do” section near the bottom is **load-bearing**: it lists specific traps with measured impact and the correct alternative. If a pattern in your change matches one of those traps, change the approach before continuing. ## What “fast” actually means here [Section titled “What “fast” actually means here”](#what-fast-actually-means-here) The targets are stricter than the typical web app baseline: | Metric | Target | Why | | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | | Time to interactive (TTI) on the harness page | < 1.5 s on a warm cache | Operators sit on this page all day | | Frame rate during list updates / animation | 60fps minimum, 120fps when transform-only | Anything below 60 feels sluggish | | Re-renders per keystroke in a 50-row form | ≤ 1 per field | Anything more is a re-render storm | | Bundle delta per new feature | < 10 KB gzip / route | Death-by-a-thousand-cuts kills warm-cache TTI | | Web Vitals (LCP / INP / CLS) | “Good” (2.5s / 200ms / 0.1) | Google’s standard; passes user perception threshold | You can verify the first three locally with React DevTools’ Profiler. The last two need Lighthouse or Web Vitals in production. ## Lessons from the apps that feel fastest [Section titled “Lessons from the apps that feel fastest”](#lessons-from-the-apps-that-feel-fastest) | App | What they do | What you can copy | | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Linear** | Local-first sync — every action mutates the local store first, then syncs to the server in the background. Zero “loading…” spinners on normal operations. Fine-grained subscriptions: components only re-render when *their slice* of state changes. | Use `useSyncQuery` (`libs/generic/sync`) the way it’s already wired — it’s **transport-agnostic**, so local-first/optimistic behavior is what you get on the Zero/WebSocket transport, with REST fallback on polling/SSE. Optimistic UI for every mutation that runs on WS. Don’t subscribe to whole tables when one row is enough. | | **Notion** | Block-level memoization in the editor — every block is a `React.memo` with a stable identity, and they avoid re-rendering ancestors when a block changes. Service worker for offline. View Transitions API for sidebar nav. | Memoize list items by stable key. Use `React.memo` + `areEqual` on FeatureList row, IssuesList row, ProposalsPanel item. | | **Vercel** | Server Components by default; `'use client'` only at leaves. Streaming SSR with Suspense boundaries around slow data. Edge-runtime for routes that don’t need Node. | *(RSC/SSR pattern — not applicable: the operator is a Vite SPA with no Server Components.)* What still transfers: keep route chunks lean and code-split heavy pieces, and wrap slow client data-fetching in `<Suspense>` with `React.lazy`. | | **Figma** | UI is React (chrome only). The canvas is custom Rust→WebAssembly. They explicitly *don’t* try to make React fast enough for the design surface — they use the right tool for the right surface. | When you have a hot rendering loop (canvas, graph), don’t reach for React. Drop down to imperative DOM / canvas / WebGL. | | **Discord** | Virtualized chat list. Workers for syntax highlighting and search indexing. Replaced setState chains with Flux to avoid double-renders. | Virtualize any list > 50 rows (`@tanstack/react-virtual` already in deps). Move CPU-heavy work off the main thread (Web Workers). | | **Stripe** | Inline critical CSS. Defer all non-critical JS. `preconnect` to API hosts. Prerender hot paths. | Eager-load (don’t lazy/defer) above-the-fold images and set explicit dimensions. `<link rel="preconnect">` for cross-origin APIs (Anthropic, Cloudflare, etc.) in `apps/operator-vite/index.html`. | | **Airtable** | Virtualized grid. WebWorker for formula compute. Optimistic UI everywhere. | Same patterns.
