```json
    }
  }
}
```
 ### Behavior per surface when setup hasn’t yet run [Section titled “Behavior per surface when setup hasn’t yet run”](#behavior-per-surface-when-setup-hasnt-yet-run) The `setup-required` state affects every plugin surface, not just actions: | Surface | Behavior when setup hasn’t run | | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Action invocation** | Substrate returns `{ok: false, error: "setup-required", setupUrl: "..."}`. Matches existing capability-denied shape. UI shows a “this plugin needs initial setup” banner with a one-click button. No UI hang. | | **Lifecycle hook fire** (e.g., `onMissionDone`) | Hook event is **queued** (FIFO, capped at 10 events per `(plugin, harness)`). After setup completes within `setupCompletionWindowMin: 30` (default), queued events replay in order. After 30 min or 10-event overflow, dropped events are written to the audit log. | | **Routine fire** (cron-style scheduled) | Same queue-and-replay as hooks, with the same 10-event cap. | | **Incoming webhook** | Substrate responds 503 to the webhook caller. **Not queued** — incoming webhooks shouldn’t accumulate, and the external caller can retry with their own backoff. Audit log records the rejection. | ### Queue overflow surfacing [Section titled “Queue overflow surfacing”](#queue-overflow-surfacing) The 10-event hook queue cap is a real ceiling. When events are dropped: * Audit log entry per dropped event (kind, payload, original-fire-time, drop-reason) * **Persistent badge on the plugin’s settings tile**: “N hook events dropped during setup. \[View audit log]” — until user explicitly acknowledges by clicking the badge The badge prevents the silent-drop failure mode where the user has no idea their plugin missed events because setup took too long. ### Run-timing options [Section titled “Run-timing options”](#run-timing-options) (The shipped SDK `runAt` enum is `'fork' | 'install' | 'first-action'`; `"install"` runs setup at plugin-install time rather than at fork. The `"manual"` mode described here is a design target not yet in the enum.) `runAt: "manual"` puts setup behind a “Run setup” button in plugin settings, never auto-fires. Useful for heavyweight optional plugins (e.g., a plugin that provisions a managed K8s cluster — defer until the user explicitly opts in). `runAt: "first-action"` defers setup until the first action / hook / routine that needs it. The first such fire returns `setup-required` (for actions) or queues + prompts (for hooks/routines). Useful for plugins where many users install but only some end up using the provisioned infra. ## Skip-teardown banner (V1.1) [Section titled “Skip-teardown banner (V1.1)”](#skip-teardown-banner-v11) When a user picks “skip teardown” during uninstall, the orphan-resources marker is written and the plugin is removed. To prevent silent cost leak (a user who skipped teardown in haste and forgot), the operator’s home tile surfaces a passive banner after 7 days: 
```text
You have 3 orphan resources from 2 uninstalled plugins.
   • aws.lambda.function (from @papercupai/aws-lambda, uninstalled 14 days ago)
   • aws.iam.role × 2


Run `papercusp orphans cleanup` to inspect and (optionally) tear them down.
```
 No budget enforcement here — that’s V1.1’s `budgetCap` work. This is just visibility for “I forgot I left infra running.” V1.1 line item. ## Plugin “host activity” settings tile (V1) [Section titled “Plugin “host activity” settings tile (V1)”](#plugin-host-activity-settings-tile-v1) A plugin that uses both `compute:exec:<bin>` (for in-action shell-outs) *and* `provision.{setup,...}` (for one-time provisioning) has two distinct host-execution surfaces with two consent flows. From the user’s point of view that’s confusing — “this plugin runs scripts on my host” is true twice. The plugin’s settings tile gains a single **“Host activity”** section listing both: 
```text
Host activity
─────────────────────────
Provisioning scripts (one-time, with consent gate):
  ✓ provision/setup.sh    (run 14 days ago, exit 0)
  ✓ provision/verify.sh   (last run 2 min ago, healthy)
    provision/teardown.sh  (not yet run)


In-action shell-outs (runs on every action invocation, capability-gated):
  • git, gh                   (compute:exec:*)
```
 Single visual surface, two underlying mechanisms. User sees the full host-activity surface in one place; substrate’s internal capability distinction stays as documented. ## What’s NOT in V1 [Section titled “What’s NOT in V1”](#whats-not-in-v1) | Item | Why deferred | | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `provision.setup.costEstimateAdvisory` | The two reviewers correctly flagged this as theater: a number with no enforcement is worse than no number. **V1.1** adds `provision.setup.budgetCap: { aws: { monthlyUsd: 5 } }` wired to AWS Budgets via a substrate helper (\~150 LOC, AWS-only). When that lands, costs are *enforced*, not advertised. | | Layer-7 network proxy with TLS interception | V1 enforces network restrictions via the OS sandbox (bwrap blocks the syscall when a host is undeclared). V2 adds a layer-7 proxy with TLS interception for richer per-request observability. | | Encrypted-at-rest token storage | V1 target is single-user dev/desktop; encryption-at-rest matters for shared-host scenarios that aren’t the V1 target. | | `runAt` scheduling | V1.1, per above. V1 always runs at install/fork. | | Interactive subprocess support | V2 may relax with a richer interactive-prompt protocol; V1 forbids. | | Per-cloud `budgetCap` helpers beyond AWS | V2. AWS-Budgets ships in V1.1 as the dogfood; GCP/Azure/Cloudflare follow as plugin authors demand them. | | Marketplace moderation gate | The plan acknowledges this as a known gap (no review currently happens at publish time). A separate spec doc will cover the moderation layer. | ## Open issues moved to dedicated review [Section titled “Open issues moved to dedicated review”](#open-issues-moved-to-dedicated-review) The remaining design questions (cross-platform commitments, signing infrastructure rollout, multi-publisher trust accumulation) are in the [Open Questions](./open-questions) page with explicit V1 / V1.1 / V2 disposition.

# OAuth integration

> A generic substrate-level OAuth helper so plugins can mark a credential field as oauth, and users get a "Connect" button instead of pasting tokens. Plugins read tokens via ctx.oauth.token() — substrate handles refresh transparently.

## Why OAuth [Section titled “Why OAuth”](#why-oauth) The current credential UX for BYO plugins is paste-a-token-into-a-field. Users have to: 1. Read the plugin’s docs to learn what scopes they need. 2. Navigate to the provider’s token-creation UI. 3. Manually pick scopes (often selecting too many “to be safe”). 4. Copy-paste a sensitive string. 5. If the token expires, repeat all four steps. OAuth replaces all of that with one button click. Plus: * Provider-side audit trail of which app got authorized. * Refresh-token mechanics for long-lived authorization. * Standard revocation flow (user revokes papercusp’s app, all derived tokens die). ## Manifest surface [Section titled “Manifest surface”](#manifest-surface) A `configSchema` field can declare OAuth support inline: 
```json
{
  "github_token": {
    "type": "string",
    "secret": true,
    "oauth": {
      "provider": "github",
      "scopes": ["repo"],
      "tokenType": "access"
    }
  }
}
```
 When the operator’s `/settings/plugins` page or the snapshot-fork completion UI sees this annotation, it renders a **Connect with GitHub** button instead of a password input. Click → OAuth dance → field gets populated by the substrate. The field is still a plain `string` and a plain `secret`. OAuth is just *how* the value gets filled. Plugins that prefer to support both can leave the field editable; users who want to paste a PAT can click “advanced” and do that. (See “Hybrid mode” below.) ### Field reference [Section titled “Field reference”](#field-reference) | Field | Required | Notes | | ---------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `provider` | yes | Must be a substrate-registered provider. V1 supports `github`. V2 adds `slack`, `linear`, `notion`, `jira`. | | `scopes` | yes | Array of provider-specific scope strings. The substrate forwards these unchanged in the authorize URL. | | `tokenType` | no | `access` (default), `refresh`, or `both`. Determines what gets stored in the config. `refresh` is required if the plugin needs to operate without re-auth for >24h. | | `userInfoFields` | no | *(Design-only, not yet implemented.)* Optional list of extra fields to populate from the provider’s user-info endpoint, e.g. `["login", "email"]` for GitHub, intended to write `<field>_user_<key>` into the plugin config. The callback does not currently fetch user info, and nothing reads the provider’s `userInfoUrl`. | ## Substrate-level provider config [Section titled “Substrate-level provider config”](#substrate-level-provider-config) Each provider is a one-time platform-owner registration. Config lives at: 
```text
~/.papercusp/oauth-apps.json
{
  "github": {
    "clientId": "Iv1.abc123",
    "clientSecretFile": "/etc/papercusp/oauth/github-secret",
    "authorizeUrl": "https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize",
    "tokenUrl": "https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token",
    "userInfoUrl": "https://api.github.com/user",
    "redirectUri": "http://localhost:3055/api/oauth/callback?provider=github"
  }
}
```
 Sensitive values (`clientSecret`) live in a separate file with `0600` perms. The substrate reads them at start, never logs them, never includes them in audit output. For production, `redirectUri` should be HTTPS — `http://localhost` is the dev/desktop default. `redirectUri` is a literal field in `~/.papercusp/oauth-apps.json` (read verbatim, no host-env substitution); edit it there per deployment. The papercusp root that file is read from is governed by `PAPERCUSP_HOME` (default `~/.papercusp`), not any host env var. ## Endpoints [Section titled “Endpoints”](#endpoints) 
```text
GET /api/oauth/start?provider=<p>&plugin=<plug>&harness=<h>&field=<f>&scopes=<comma-separated>
  → 302 to provider authorize URL with HMAC-signed state in the URL `state` parameter
  → the requested scopes are passed as a comma-separated query param and
    forwarded unchanged to the authorize URL (not derived from the manifest
    at the route level — the caller, e.g. the settings page, supplies them)


GET /api/oauth/callback?provider=<p>&code=<c>&state=<s>
  → exchanges code for token
  → writes token (+ optional _refresh / _expires_at, and _expired:false) to
    plugin's per-harness config[field]
  → 307 redirect to /harness/<harness>?panel=config&oauth_connected=<plugin>
    (on success), or .../?panel=config&oauth_error=<msg> on provider/exchange error


POST /api/oauth/verify-paste
  → hybrid mode: introspect a pasted PAT's granted scopes against the
    plugin's required scopes (exact/superset accept, subset reject)
```
 ### State design (URL parameter, not cookie) [Section titled “State design (URL parameter, not cookie)”](#state-design-url-parameter-not-cookie) State lives in the URL `state` parameter end-to-end. **No cookies are used in the OAuth flow.** This means concurrent flows (user opening 3 OAuth tabs simultaneously to install 3 plugins from a fresh fork) have independent state values — no cookie collision is possible. State token is: * HMAC-signed with a substrate-only secret. The secret is `PAPERCUSP_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` (must be ≥32 chars); when unset, dev falls back to a per-process random key, so restarting the process invalidates in-flight OAuth states. * 5min expiry * Single-use (server-side nonce table; first callback consumes the nonce) * Includes `(plugin, harness, field, providerHost)` as keyed claims The HMAC + nonce combination prevents both CSRF (state can’t be forged without the substrate’s secret) and replay (each state can only be consumed once). The nonce ledger is the Postgres table `harness_shared.oauth_nonces` (migration 030 — it replaced an earlier process-local `Map` that broke across restarts and multi-instance deploys). `signState` `INSERT`s the nonce; `verifyAndConsumeState` atomically claims it via a single `UPDATE … WHERE consumed = false RETURNING` (concurrent callbacks racing the same nonce resolve to exactly one winner, the rest get `already-consumed`). An opportunistic sweep deletes expired rows once the table grows past \~1000. ## Provider matrix [Section titled “Provider matrix”](#provider-matrix) | Provider | OAuth available | Scopes for our plugins | Notes | | ---------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | GitHub | ✓ | `repo` (private + public access), `read:user` | OAuth App or fine-grained PAT both work; OAuth App is what the spec assumes. | | Slack | ✓ | `incoming-webhook`, `chat:write` | Each Slack workspace authorizes once. | | Linear | ✓ | `read`, `write` | Linear’s OAuth scopes are coarse. | | Notion | ✓ | (Notion uses public-integration mode, no scopes per se) | Slightly different flow — no `scope` param, integration ID is the scope. | | Jira | ✓ | `read:jira-work`, `write:jira-work` | Atlassian’s OAuth 2.0 (3LO) flow; uses `audience` param. | | Cloudflare | ✗ | — | CF doesn’t expose OAuth for API tokens. BYO token only. | V1 ships GitHub. V2 sweeps the rest in one PR after the V1 surface is proven. ## Hybrid mode (paste OR connect) [Section titled “Hybrid mode (paste OR connect)”](#hybrid-mode-paste-or-connect) Default UX shows the Connect button when `oauth` is declared. But a power user might want to paste a PAT instead (e.g., for a service account). Settings UI offers an “Advanced: paste token” expander: 
```text
github_token *
  [ Connect with GitHub ]
  ▼ Advanced


  Or paste a token directly:
  [ ghp_••••••••••••••••••••••• ]
```
 ### Paste-PAT scope verification [Section titled “Paste-PAT scope verification”](#paste-pat-scope-verification) When the user pastes a token, the substrate hits the provider’s introspection endpoint to verify the granted scopes match what the plugin’s manifest requires: | Provider | Introspection endpoint | Notes | | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | | **GitHub** | `GET /user` with a `Bearer` token; read the `X-OAuth-Scopes` response header. This works uniformly for OAuth-app tokens, classic PATs, and fine-grained PATs. | V1 | | Slack | `auth.test` returns scopes in response headers | V2 | | Linear | GraphQL `viewer { id }` errors with explicit scope-required messages | V2 | | Notion | `/v1/users/me` echoes integration capabilities | V2 | | Jira | `/rest/api/3/myself` + `accessible-resources` | V2 | Verification rules: | Granted scopes | Substrate behavior | | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Exactly the requested set | Accepted silently | | Superset of requested (more permissions than needed) | Accepted with a warning toast: “this token has more scopes than the plugin needs; consider creating a more narrowly-scoped one” | | Subset of requested (missing required scopes) | **Rejected.** Toast names the missing scopes. User regenerates and re-pastes. | | Token doesn’t belong to this OAuth app’s client\_id | Rejected for OAuth-app PATs. Allowed for fine-grained PATs (no client\_id binding exists). | A provider with no introspection endpoint is a special case: the substrate accepts the pasted token **unverified** and the response carries `outcome: 'no-introspection'`. Only providers that implement `introspect()` run the exact/superset/subset comparison above. The plain input writes the token to the same config field. The substrate doesn’t care which path produced the token — both end up at `config.github_token`. ## Refresh mechanics [Section titled “Refresh mechanics”](#refresh-mechanics) Plugin authors never think about expiry. Instead of reading `config.github_token` directly, action handlers call 
```typescript
const token = await ctx.oauth.token('github_token');
const r = await fetch('https://api.github.com/...', {
  headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
});
```
 The substrate’s `ctx.oauth.token(field)` helper: 1. Reads the stored token from `config[field]`. 2. Checks `config[field + '_expires_at']`. 3. If `expires_at` is past, or within 5 minutes of expiring, hits the provider’s refresh endpoint *before* returning. Updates `config[field]` and `config[field + '_expires_at']` atomically. 4. Returns the (possibly-refreshed) access token. The helper itself stops there: `ctx.oauth.token(field)` does the expiry-check, refresh, and concurrent-refresh dedup, but does **not** do 401 retry. The 401-retry-once logic lives in a separate exported `withRetry()` wrapper that a plugin must opt into — it is not wired into `ctx.oauth.token`, and currently has no production callers. `withRetry()` semantics: if a wrapped provider call returns a 401 (e.g., the token was revoked between refresh and use), it forces a refresh by zeroing the cached expiry, re-acquires the token, and retries once. A second 401 surfaces to the plugin as a normal error, plus the substrate flags `oauth_expired: true` on the config so the operator UI shows a “reconnect” button. ### Storage [Section titled “Storage”](#storage) For providers that issue refresh tokens (`tokenType: "refresh"` or `"both"`), the substrate stores both the access token and the refresh token plus the access-token expiry: 
```json
{
  "github_token": "ghp_access_token",
  "github_token_refresh": "ghp_refresh_token",
  "github_token_expires_at": "2026-05-08T20:14:32Z"
}
```
 These fields are siblings inside the same plugin-config JSON. They share the same `secret: true` flag for snapshot purposes (all three are stripped together). At rest, the PG mirror of plugin configs is already encrypted (migration 039 — pgcrypto `config_ct` column; the writer NULLs the plaintext `config` column after encryption), and the on-disk `~/.papercusp/harnesses/<slug>/plugin-configs/<plugin>.json` is written with mode `0600`. The one remaining plaintext surface is that on-disk file itself, which the substrate plugin loader reads synchronously and cannot decrypt — see [Open Questions](#open-questions) #4. ### Concurrent refresh storm [Section titled “Concurrent refresh storm”](#concurrent-refresh-storm) If 10 actions fire in parallel and the access token is past `expires_at`, all 10 calls would naively hit the provider’s refresh endpoint simultaneously. Provider rate-limits would bite; some refreshes would fail; the user would see a flurry of “reconnect needed” errors. The substrate caches an in-flight `Promise<token>` per `(plugin, harness, field)`: 
```typescript
// Inside ctx.oauth.token() helper
const inFlight = refreshCache.get(key);
if (inFlight) return inFlight;       // share the in-flight refresh


const promise = doRefresh().finally(() => {
  refreshCache.delete(key);
});
refreshCache.set(key, promise);
return promise;
```
 Concurrent callers wait on the same Promise. The first refresh wins; the rest get the result. Provider sees one refresh request, not ten. ### Offline / desktop-laptop scenario [Section titled “Offline / desktop-laptop scenario”](#offline--desktop-laptop-scenario) The original draft proposed a 30-minute background job that proactively refreshes near-expired tokens. The reviewer correctly noted that doesn’t help the desktop case where the laptop is closed for a week — the background job hasn’t run, the next action’s first call is past `expires_at`, the plugin gets a 401 with no chance to react. The `ctx.oauth.token(field)` helper covers this case directly: **every action invocation** does an expiry check + refresh-if-needed before returning the token. The action’s first network call always uses a token that was either fresh enough to skip refresh, or just-refreshed. The 30-minute background job remains as a *secondary* optimization for long-running operators (so the very first action after a long idle isn’t delayed by the refresh round-trip), but it’s no longer the load-bearing mechanism. Plugins that go through the `ctx.oauth.token()` helper are safe even if the background job never runs. ### When refresh fails [Section titled “When refresh fails”](#when-refresh-fails) If refresh fails (revoked authorization, provider outage), the substrate marks the plugin’s config as `oauth_expired: true` and surfaces a “reconnect” button in the plugin’s settings tile. The plugin’s own action handlers can also detect this state by checking `config[field + '_expired']` if they want to show a richer “reconnect needed” message in their own UI. ## Revocation [Section titled “Revocation”](#revocation) Two revocation paths: 1. **From the operator UI**: clicking “Disconnect” on a plugin’s settings clears `config[field]` + calls the provider’s revoke endpoint (best-effort) + marks the plugin as needing-auth. (The dedicated disconnect route is not yet broken out as its own endpoint; clearing the field via the existing `PUT /api/plugins/config` path is the current mechanism.) 2. **From the provider’s UI**: user revokes papercusp’s app on github.com → next API call from the plugin returns 401 → substrate marks `oauth_expired: true` → user re-clicks Connect. Either way, the plugin’s own data on the provider side is preserved; only papercusp’s authorization is gone. ## Implementation [Section titled “Implementation”](#implementation) | Surface | Change | LOC | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | | `@papercusp/plugin-sdk` | `oauth` field on the property schema + `PluginOAuthRequirement[]` manifest entries. | \~15 | | `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/oauth/start.ts` | Generate state, redirect to provider authorize URL. | \~60 | | `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/oauth/callback.ts` | Exchange code, write access token (+ optional `_refresh`/`_expires_at`, and `_expired: false`) to plugin config. Does *not* fetch user info — the `userInfoFields` manifest feature is unimplemented. | \~100 | | `packages/operator-core/lib/oauth/{providers,token,state,storage-fs}.ts` | Provider registry (GitHub), token-exchange + `ctx.oauth.token()` refresh logic, HMAC state, fs-backed token storage. | \~120 | | `apps/operator/app/settings/plugins/page.tsx` | Render Connect button when `oauth` is declared on a field. | \~50 | | `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/oauth/verify-paste.ts` | Hybrid mode — introspect a pasted PAT’s scopes against the plugin’s required scopes. | \~40 | Total: **\~385 lines.** Slightly bigger than the share-semantics work, slightly smaller than build-scripts. (Implemented: `ctx.oauth.token()` lives in `packages/operator-core/lib/oauth/token.ts`, wired from `plugin-host-runtime.ts`; the three `/api/oauth/*` routes and the provider registry are shipped. A dedicated `/api/oauth/disconnect` route is not yet broken out — see [Revocation](#revocation).) ## Multi-tenancy callout (V1.1) [Section titled “Multi-tenancy callout (V1.1)”](#multi-tenancy-callout-v11) V1 OAuth assumes a single-tenant operator (one Papercusp install → one user → one OAuth app per provider). For self-hosted papercusp.com serving multiple users: * **All users share the same OAuth app’s redirect URI.** GitHub TOS may consider this fine for first-party apps, but rate-limits are per-app, shared across all users. A burst of OAuth flows from one popular template could exhaust the rate limit for everyone. * **No per-tenant isolation** of OAuth state at rest — all stored at `~/.papercusp/harnesses/<slug>/plugin-configs/<plugin>.json` for the operator’s single user. V1.1 plan: * Per-tenant OAuth apps (each tenant registers its own GitHub/Slack/etc. app, recorded in tenant config) * Per-tenant rate-limit budgeting in the substrate * Tenant-scoped storage paths V1 ships single-tenant only. The substrate prints a warning at startup if it detects a multi-user host (per [shared-host detection](./build-scripts#single-user-host-detection)) and recommends self-hosting a separate operator per user. ## Library decision: `arctic` vs roll-our-own [Section titled “Library decision: arctic vs roll-our-own”](#library-decision-arctic-vs-roll-our-own) Earlier drafts of this plan proposed adopting `arctic` (Lucia’s OAuth provider library) to save \~150 LOC of provider-specific token-exchange boilerplate. **This is now gated on a supply-chain audit**, given the plan as a whole is about supply-chain hygiene: | Audit step | What’s checked | | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Direct deps | How many top-level deps does arctic add? Are they widely-used or boutique? | | Transitive deps | Total dep tree size; flag any dep with single-maintainer status or unsigned releases | | Maintainer count | How many active maintainers? Single-maintainer libraries are higher xz-utils-precedent risk | | Signing posture | Does `arctic` publish signed npm releases? Provenance attestations? | | Coverage | Does arctic cover Atlassian 3LO including the `audience` parameter quirk? | | Lock posture | Pin the exact arctic version + record sha256 in substrate’s lockfile; explicit re-audit on every version bump | Outcomes: * **Arctic passes audit** → adopt with audit recorded as a `LIBRARY_AUDIT.md` entry. V1 OAuth ships with arctic. Total OAuth surface \~250 LOC (was 385). * **Arctic fails audit** → roll our own provider implementations. V1 OAuth ships with \~385 LOC of in-house provider modules. Slightly more substrate code but zero new supply-chain link. The wrong path is “adopt arctic to hit the LOC budget without doing the audit.” LOC is not a hard target; supply-chain hygiene is. ## Open questions [Section titled “Open questions”](#open-questions) 1. **Where does the OAuth client\_secret live?** A separate `~/.papercusp/oauth/<provider>-secret` file with `0600` perms is what’s proposed. Some operators may prefer environment variables (k8s-style). Should both be supported? 2. **Multi-tenancy**: if the operator is hosted publicly (not self-hosted), every user shares the same OAuth app’s redirect URI. Is that fine? Or do we shard providers per tenant? 3. **PKCE**: required for public clients. Substrate is a confidential client (has a secret), so PKCE is optional but harmless. Probably worth implementing for defense-in-depth. 4. **Token storage at rest**: the PG mirror of plugin configs is already encrypted at rest (migration 039, pgcrypto `config_ct`), and the on-disk `~/.papercusp/harnesses/<slug>/plugin-configs/<plugin>.json` is written `0600`. The remaining open item is just that on-disk plaintext file — the substrate plugin loader reads it directly and cannot decrypt, so encrypting it would mean teaching the loader a decryption path. Worth doing for a multi-user host? 5. **Per-plugin OR per-harness OR per-user authorization**: GitHub OAuth gives the same access regardless of which harness asks; we just write the token to a different per-harness config. Should the substrate offer to *share* an authorization across harnesses (one GitHub Connect, applies to all your harnesses)? Trade-off: convenience vs. blast radius if one harness’s config leaks. See [Open Questions](./open-questions).

# Open questions and V1/V1.1/V2 split

> Each design decision rated by impact and assigned to V1 (gates "safe to release publicly"), V1.1 (improves the system, ships fast-follow), or V2 (separate workstream). Updated through round 6.

V1 launch criterion: “**shippable to a vetted-publisher alpha** where the worst a malicious vetted-publisher can do is fail at the consent gate or be sandboxed.” Anything that fails to meet that criterion is V1; anything that improves the system but isn’t a security or correctness gate is V1.1+. Public marketplace launch is V1.1+, gated on the moderation layer. ## V1 — gates “safe to release to a vetted-publisher alpha” [Section titled “V1 — gates “safe to release to a vetted-publisher alpha””](#v1--gates-safe-to-release-to-a-vetted-publisher-alpha) ### Idempotency, safety, sandboxing [Section titled “Idempotency, safety, sandboxing”](#idempotency-safety-sandboxing) | Item | Why V1 | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Idempotency contract: done-marker hashes `(configHash, scriptHash, pluginVersion)`; `aliases` for renames + `null` for removals; structural fields default to forcing re-provision; `skipReprovisionOnPatch` governs `pluginVersion` only, never `scriptHash` | Re-runs silently corrupt state; edits to `region`/`accountId` orphan resources; a malicious patch with same major.minor and `skipReprovisionOnPatch: true` cannot slip through because the script-hash always forces re-consent | | Sandbox by default for *all* scripts | Without it, build scripts are an unconditioned arbitrary-code-execution vector for any approved publisher (npm event-stream / xz-utils precedent). Signing proves provenance, not safety. | | **Linux: bwrap with bundled binary + install-time smoke test** | Bundled bwrap covers distro variance; smoke test catches kernels with disabled unprivileged user namespaces. Failure → permanent `sandbox_available: false` → signed-only mode for substrate’s lifetime | | **macOS: sandbox-exec + signed-only mode (no unsigned scripts at all)** | sandbox-exec is deprecated but functional — meaningful boundary against accidents. Refusing unsigned scripts on macOS plugs the “unsigned + no real sandbox” gap | | **Network policy floor**: 169.254.169.254/32, 169.254.0.0/16, 127.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, `fc00::/7` always blocked, regardless of `allowedHosts` or `cloudProvider` | Closes IMDS-credential exfiltration and lateral-movement attack classes. (Shipped `DENY_FLOOR_CIDRS` is IPv4 RFC1918 + IMDS + loopback plus the IPv6 ULA range `fc00::/7`; there is no separate `::1` entry.) | | **`cloudProvider: { id, region }` presets** with `${region}` templating (shipped ids: `aws`, `gcp`, `azure`, `cloudflare`) | Replaces the old `network: "open"` mode which gave plugins effectively unbounded outbound network access. Per-region presets close the cross-region leak surface. **Implementation note:** the four presets are compiled-in TypeScript constants (`PRESETS` in `network-policy.ts`) with `${region}` placeholders expanded per declared region; the originally-designed “monthly signed update channel” for preset distribution is **not built** — updating a preset means shipping a new substrate build. | | **Static-analysis warnings** on common destructive patterns (`curl \| bash`, `sudo`, `rm -rf $HOME`, `eval` of untrusted input, `chmod -R 777`, base64-blob-smuggle) | Cheap and high-signal; catches “I copy-pasted destructive command and didn’t notice” failure mode | ### Trust, signing, and consent [Section titled “Trust, signing, and consent”](#trust-signing-and-consent) | Item | Why V1 | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Trust granularity per-(publisher, plugin)** keyed on signing-key fingerprint | Coarser-grained trust silently gives @publisher’s malicious new plugin the same trust as their existing benign one. **Implementation note:** trust now lives as a single-row-per-workspace PG record in `harness_shared.operator_trust_store` (encrypted-at-rest), superseding the earlier `<workspace>/trust.json` mode-0600 file. | | **Ownership transfer invalidates trust** — different `publisher_id` on a new version triggers fresh consent | Closes the xz-utils-in-miniature attack class | | **Key rotation events must be marketplace-countersigned** | ”Publisher rotated their key, re-trust?” prompt is otherwise a phishing surface; without marketplace’s infrastructure-key signature the prompt is just trust-me-bro-from-attacker | | **Quarantine clears trust** for the affected `(publisher, plugin)`. Publisher-key compromise advisory clears all of `(publisher, *)` | Cached trust must die when marketplace flags anything bad | | **`papercusp plugin install --dev`** path with per-machine ad-hoc signing key + `dev: true` trust flag | Plugin authors can iterate on macOS / signed-only platforms without publishing each save to a marketplace | ### Recovery, lifecycle, observability [Section titled “Recovery, lifecycle, observability”](#recovery-lifecycle-observability) | Item | Why V1 | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Provision concurrency + crash-recovery owned by the DBOS provision workflow** (the workflow’s `deduplicationID` is the cross-request mutex; DBOS recovery is the liveness) | File-based locks don’t survive multi-machine harness sharing (laptop ↔ desktop split-brain). **Superseded design:** an earlier PG `harness_shared.operator_claims` table with advisory locks + 30s heartbeat-renewed `expires_at` was *built and then dropped* in the DBOS-only cutover (migration 112 drops the table; no claims table, no heartbeat remain). See [revisions § Round 3 item 10](./revisions) and plan `dbos-durable-flows-adoption-2026-06-02`. | | **`papercusp_record_resource <kind> <id>`** helper for recording created resources | Plugin authors aren’t infra engineers; partial-failure rollback should not require defensive idempotency-handling logic in setup.sh. **Implementation note:** the helper writes newline-delimited JSON to a FIFO/record file (`PAPERCUSP_RECORD_FIFO`); the substrate tails that file on a 200ms tick and folds each entry into the PG-backed provision-state row (the row IS the authoritative state — there is no `state.json` file). | | **Recovery contract**: partial-failure offers automatic teardown of recorded resources | Killed/crashed setup leaves undiagnosable orphan resources. **Implementation note:** stale-lock detection is gone — crash-recovery is now DBOS workflow recovery, and recorded resources live in the PG provision-state row, not a `state.json` file. | | **Teardown contract**: plugin’s `teardown.sh` is the dispatcher; receives the recorded resource list and dispatches per `kind` | Locks Path 1 explicitly so plugin authors don’t ship empty teardown.sh assuming substrate magic. The resource list comes from the PG-backed provision-state row (formerly `state.json`). | | **OAuth `ctx.oauth.token(field)` helper** with pre-emptive refresh + 401 retry-once + Promise-cache for concurrent-refresh storm | Every plugin reinvents refresh logic poorly; offline-laptop case produces inscrutable failures; concurrent calls without Promise-cache race the provider’s refresh endpoint | | **PAT scope introspection** (V1 GitHub) | Hybrid-mode pastes silently produce under-scoped tokens that break action handlers at runtime | | **OAuth state in URL parameter, not cookie** (HMAC + single-use nonce) | Cookies collide on concurrent flows; URL state is per-flow by construction | | **Hook / routine queue-and-replay** when fired before setup completes; queue cap of 10 with persistent badge on overflow | Without queueing, hooks silently fail; with silent overflow, user has no signal | | **Webhook reject** (503) when fired before setup completes; not queued | Incoming webhooks shouldn’t accumulate; external caller retries with their own backoff | ### Snapshot, schema, identity [Section titled “Snapshot, schema, identity”](#snapshot-schema-identity) | Item | Why V1 | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Schema evolution**: per-property `aliases` array for both renames (`["oldName"]`) and removals (`[null]`), walked from current installed plugin’s manifest | A single plugin version bump silently breaks every snapshot pinned to the old version | | **`versionPin: { mode }`** — shipped defaults: `"semver"` for JS plugins, `"hash"` for WASM/daemon plugins; `"exact"` is the mapping for legacy `pluginVersionPinned: true` | Alias-walk only happens on explicit “fork against latest” opt-in. **Correction:** the canonical SDK type and JSON schema both default JS plugins to `"semver"` (accept any version satisfying the captured range), *not* `"exact"`. (The CLI metadata-display fallback in `snapshot-cli.ts` shows `"exact"` only when the field is absent on a legacy snapshot — a display quirk, not the canonical default.) | | **`securityAdvisories` field** on marketplace catalog per-version; The manifest `auditLogCapMb` argument still parses but is **ignored** by `appendAudit` (the removed file-based version capped at 10 MB, not 50 MB). The symmetric key is bootstrapped at `~/.papercusp/db-encryption-key` (or `PAPERCUSP_DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY`). *(Earlier drafts listed this under V2; it is already implemented.)* | | **Single-user host detection**: primary `who \| sort -u \| wc -l > 1`; reviewed within N business days; allowlist published; appeals via issue thread | Without a public process, “vetted alpha” is opaque-by-default — defeats the moderation framing | | **Interactive-subprocess ban**: `requiresInteractive: false` enforced; substrate refuses scripts that read from stdin or open browsers mid-run | `aws sso login`-style scripts hang the operator with no UI feedback | | **Visibility-aware `verify` polling**: foreground-only by default, no periodic background polling unless explicitly opted in | 5 plugins × 100 harnesses × 10-min polling = 3,000 cloud-API calls/hour just for health checks; rate-limit collateral | | **Plugin “host activity” settings tile**: shows both `compute:exec:*` and `provision.*` surfaces side-by-side | ”This plugin runs scripts on my host” was true twice via two consent flows; single tile reduces confusion | **V1 LOC honest total: \~2,000–2,100 LOC.** Adopting `arctic` for OAuth (post supply-chain audit) reduces by \~150 LOC. ## V1.1 — improves the system, ships fast-follow [Section titled “V1.1 — improves the system, ships fast-follow”](#v11--improves-the-system-ships-fast-follow) | Item | Why deferred | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Phasing inversion (share-semantics PR before OAuth PR) | Pure PR ordering, not new code | | Cost: drop field for V1, add `provision.setup.budgetCap` + AWS-Budgets helper | Real feature with teeth; \~150 LOC plus per-cloud helpers. Dropping for V1 is the right call (no enforcement = theater) | | `compute:exec:*` vs build-scripts docs clarification | Pure docs; V1 substrate ships, V1.1 adds the explanatory cross-references | | Audit log policy formalization + browse-logs UI | V1 ships sane defaults; V1.1 adds settings UI | | `runAt: "fork" \| "install" \| "first-action"` for `provision.setup` (shipped SDK enum; `"manual"` is a further design target) | V1 always runs at fork; V1.1 adds the install / first-action escape hatches | | Skip-teardown 7-day passive banner (“you have N orphan resources”) | Visibility-only; not a safety gate | | github-repo dogfood (re-implement repo creation as build script) | Smaller dogfood than cloudflare-pages-hosted; exercises full stack (OAuth + share-semantics + provisioning) more economically | | **Marketplace moderation layer** (separate spec doc) | V1 ships safely under vetted-publisher alpha; public marketplace launch is V1.1+ gated on moderation | | **Per-tenant OAuth multi-tenancy** (separate OAuth apps per tenant; per-tenant rate-limit budgets; tenant-scoped storage) | V1 single-tenant. Multi-tenant hosted papercusp.com is V1.1+ | | Cross-platform per-script paths: `setup.path.linux` / `setup.path.darwin`; bashism linter at publish time | V1 supports a single platform-agnostic `setup.path`; V1.1 adds explicit per-platform with linter | | Copy-edit: sync index.mdx vs open-questions.mdx | Trivially fixable | **V1.1 LOC: \~500.** ## V2 — separate workstreams [Section titled “V2 — separate workstreams”](#v2--separate-workstreams) | Item | Why V2 | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **macOS Tauri sidecar with restricted entitlements** (`Info.plist`-declared) | Defense-in-depth on top of V1’s sandbox-exec; the operator already runs on Tauri so the surface exists | | Per-cloud `budgetCap` helpers beyond AWS (GCP, Azure, Cloudflare) | Ship AWS in V1.1; add others as plugin authors demand | | Layer-7 network policy proxy with TLS interception | V1 enforces via OS sandbox + cloudProvider presets; V2 adds richer per-request observability (requires CA cert provisioning, real install pain) | | AST-level static analysis on provision scripts | V1 pattern matcher catches dumb-pattern attacks; AST-level catches more sophisticated ones (per-language parsers required) | | Windows sandboxing (Job objects + restricted tokens) | V1 is Linux-primary, macOS-supported, Windows-banner-only | | Substrate-level teardown dispatcher (substrate knows how to delete `aws.lambda.function`, etc.) | V1 keeps `teardown.sh` as the dispatcher; V2 adds built-in handlers for common kinds | ## Sign-off checklist [Section titled “Sign-off checklist”](#sign-off-checklist) Before V1 implementation begins, these need explicit sign-off: * [ ] **V1 list above is the full set** — anything in V1.1 that should actually be V1? * [ ] **V1 line-count target (\~2,000–2,100 LOC)** is realistic * [ ] **Sandbox-by-default for all scripts** is the locked design * [ ] **`bwrap` bundling + install-time smoke test** — substrate ships its own copy * [ ] **macOS: signed-only mode + sandbox-exec, no unsigned-script path** in V1 * [ ] **`PAPERCUSP_DEV_UNSIGNED=<sha256>`** + `papercusp plugin install --dev` is the only macOS dev escape * [ ] **Network policy floor (IMDS + RFC1918 + loopback) always blocks**, regardless of `allowedHosts` or `cloudProvider` * [ ] **`cloudProvider` presets with `${region}` templating** (shipped ids `aws`/`gcp`/`azure`/`cloudflare` as compiled-in constants; the “monthly signed update channel” is a design target, not built) * [ ] **Trust per-(publisher, plugin)** keyed on signing-key fingerprint * [ ] **Ownership transfer invalidates trust** * [ ] **Key-rotation events marketplace-countersigned** * [ ] **Cost field dropped from V1**; budget enforcement comes via real `budgetCap` helper in V1.1 * [ ] **Audit log is PG-backed and uncapped** (no 1y retention / 50 MB cap / eviction — that design was superseded; `auditLogCapMb` is parsed but ignored) + fail-loud on encrypted-locked volumes * [ ] **`aliases` covers both renames and removals** * [ ] **`versionPin: { mode }` defaults** — `"semver"` for JS plugins, `"hash"` for WASM/daemon; `"exact"` is the legacy `pluginVersionPinned: true` mapping (not the default); security advisories prompt loudly at fork * [ ] **`runAt: "first-action"` synchronization contract** (action returns `setup-required`; hooks queued + replayed; webhooks 503’d) is the locked design * [ ] **Default for structural-vs-operational fields is `structural`** * [ ] **`papercusp_record_resource` helper** + plugin’s `teardown.sh` as dispatcher * [ ] **DBOS provision workflow owns concurrency** (`deduplicationID` = cross-request mutex; DBOS recovery = liveness) — the earlier PG `operator_claims` advisory-lock + heartbeat was built and then dropped (migration 112) * [ ] **`who`-based shared-host detection** + one-time acknowledgement banner * [ ] **Vetted-publisher allowlist process documented** as part of V1 launch criterion * [ ] **`arctic` adoption gated on supply-chain audit**; rolled-our-own is the fallback * [ ] **Phasing**: share-semantics + OAuth ship in one PR; build-scripts in a second PR * [ ] **V1.1 follow-up list** is acceptable as fast-follow Once these are checked, implementation begins. The order is: 1. **PR 1** (\~600 LOC): Snapshot share-semantics + OAuth substrate + GitHub provider + `ctx.oauth.token()` helper + paste-PAT scope check + version pinning (`versionPin`) + security-advisory consultation 2. **PR 2** (\~1,400–1,500 LOC): Build-script lifecycle (manifest, runner, sandbox with bwrap-bundling + smoke test, audit, crash-recovery + concurrency via the DBOS provision workflow, PG-backed provision state, consent flow, cloudProvider presets, network floor, trust per-(publisher, plugin) with rotation/transfer, hook queue-and-replay, single-user-host detection, helper library) + dogfooded against the existing `cloudflare-pages-hosted` Worker deploy 3. **PR 3** (V1.1 onward): github-repo refactored to use build scripts + `runAt` scheduling + `budgetCap` + AWS-Budgets helper + skip-teardown banner + marketplace moderation layer (separate spec) ## Long-tail design questions [Section titled “Long-tail design questions”](#long-tail-design-questions) 1. **`secret: true` implying `shareable: false`?** Round-1 reviewer said keep separate. Standing. 2. **Array-shaped configs** (`apiKeys: [...]`) — fine to require named-field objects. 3. **`.shape.json` location** — next to the redacted config. 4. **PKCE for OAuth** — defense-in-depth, V1.1. 5. **OAuth client\_secret storage** — V1 supports both `clientSecretFile` (`0600`) and env-var. 6. **Concurrent setup for multi-plugin snapshots** — V1 sequential; `parallel: true` opt-in deferred. 7. **`state.json` resource validation** — V1 trusts the script; plugin authors build into `verify`. These will be answered as the implementation surfaces them; none gate V1 sign-off.

# Revisions

> Mapping from each review item across the two rounds of feedback to the section that addresses it (or to the deferred bucket with reasoning). Future readers ask "why is X complicated" — the answer lives here.

Historical design-review log — code is the source of truth This page is the round-by-round design-review record for the snapshots V1 design as it stood in May 2026. It is **not** a description of shipped behavior. Since these reviews, much of the build-script / OAuth substrate *was* implemented (`packages/operator-core/lib/provision/` and `/oauth/`), and the separately-scoped snapshot-**export** subsystem was later **retired** (`@papercusp/export-state`, the `snapshots:*` tools, and the `kind=snapshot` Cupboard were dropped — see `retire-snapshots-instance-spec-2026-06-09`, migration 199). Several decisions below were superseded during implementation; the most load-bearing divergences are flagged inline. Where this log and the code disagree, **trust the code.** This page tracks the substantive design decisions made during review. Each item links back to the review prompt that surfaced it and forward to the section that addresses it (or to the deferred bucket with the reasoning). The plan went through **six rounds of external review** before implementation. Each round’s reviewer was rigorous; their feedback is preserved here verbatim in summary so future readers can audit the design rationale. A seventh sign-off review was planned before implementation; the “implementation begins” framing below is preserved as the historical record (see the banner above). ## Round 1 (2026-05-08) [Section titled “Round 1 (2026-05-08)”](#round-1-2026-05-08) The first reviewer raised 18 items across top, mid, and lower tiers. The `auditLogCapMb` field still exists on the manifest type and is still threaded through the runner, but `appendAudit` ignores it (kept for source compatibility); it has no effect. | [build-scripts § Per-plugin override](./build-scripts#per-plugin-override) | | **Minor 11.** Fork-completion UX has 8 interactions | **Accepted in V1.** Batch by publisher: one consent for all `@papercupai` scripts in fork with full inline summary; “approve all” first-class flow. | [index § Vision](./index#vision-forking-a-complex-snapshot) | | **Minor 12.** Aliases will bit-rot — version pinning to the rescue | **Accepted in V1, architectural simplification.** `versionPin: { mode: "exact" }` is the reproducible default (legacy `pluginVersionPinned: true` maps to it); alias-walk only on explicit “fork against latest” opt-in. | [share-semantics § Plugin version pinning](./share-semantics#plugin-version-pinning-default-on) | | **Minor 13.** `shareable: false` accepts any string format | **Accepted.** JSON-Schema `pattern` field by convention. | [share-semantics § Format validation](./share-semantics#format-validation-via-pattern) | | **Minor 14.** compute:exec ↔ provision UX confusion | **Accepted in V1.** Single “host activity” tile on plugin settings showing both surfaces. | [build-scripts § Plugin host activity tile](./build-scripts#plugin-host-activity-settings-tile-v1) | | **Nit (LOC math).** 1,500 LOC budget doesn’t add up | **Accepted.** V1 honest total raised to \~2,000–2,100 LOC; arctic adoption (subject to audit) trims \~150. | [open-questions](./open-questions) | | **Nit (tarball format).** `.shape.json` IS a format change, even if additive | **Accepted.** Doc explicitly acknowledges as additive format change with backward-compat. | [index § Snapshot tarball format change](./index#snapshot-tarball-format-change) | ## Round 6 [Section titled “Round 6”](#round-6) Round-6 reviewer surfaced eight follow-ups to round-5 + a process observation. All accepted with concrete specs. | Review item | Resolution | Section | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **1.** macOS dev path needs a clearly-named escape | **Accepted in V1.** `papercusp plugin install --dev /path/to/local` locally signs with per-machine ad-hoc key + sets `dev: true` trust flag + consent UI text “Dev install — local machine only.” | [build-scripts § Dev install flow](./build-scripts#dev-install-flow-for-plugin-authors) | | **2.** Cloud preset maintenance + region templating concrete | **Accepted in V1.** Substrate bundles preset + monthly fetch from `presets.papercusp.io` signed with infrastructure key; `${cfg.region}` substitution at runtime. Updates are additive-only; opt-out for offline installs. | [build-scripts § Preset maintenance](./build-scripts#preset-maintenance) | | **3.** Teardown dispatcher contract: Path 1 explicit | **Accepted in V1.** Plugin’s `teardown.sh` IS the dispatcher; receives `state.json` via stdin or `$PAPERCUSP_PLUGIN_STATE`; switch on `kind`. Substrate does NOT interpret resource kinds. | [build-scripts § Teardown contract](./build-scripts#teardown-contract-plugins-teardownsh-is-the-dispatcher) | | **4.** Key rotation phishing surface | **Accepted in V1.** Rotation events must be countersigned by marketplace’s pinned infrastructure key; substrate refuses unsigned rotation events. | [build-scripts § Key rotation](./build-scripts#key-rotation) | | **5.** OAuth state wording inconsistency | **Wording bug fix.** State is URL parameter end-to-end, no cookies anywhere; doc clarifies in dedicated section. | [oauth-integration § State design](./oauth-integration#state-design-url-parameter-not-cookie) | | **6.** Queue overflow silent failure | **Accepted in V1.** Persistent badge on plugin settings tile lists dropped events + count; persists until user acknowledges. | [build-scripts § Queue overflow surfacing](./build-scripts#queue-overflow-surfacing) | | **7.** Shared-host detection false-positives | **Accepted in V1.** Primary check: `who \| sort -u \| wc -l > 1`. Secondary: passwd filter on UID **in `[1000, 60000]`** (the upper bound excludes the `nobody`/systemd high-UID range, so it is not merely `≥ 1000`) + a `/home/<name>/` home prefix + a valid login shell from a fixed allowlist. | [build-scripts § Single-user host detection](./build-scripts#single-user-host-detection) | | **8.** pluginVersionPinned + security advisories | **Accepted in V1.** Marketplace catalog adds `securityAdvisories` per-version; fork-time substrate prompts loudly with read/upgrade/pin choices when pinned version has open advisory ≥ moderate. | [share-semantics § Security advisories](./share-semantics#security-advisories-at-fork-time) | | **Process: arctic supply-chain audit** | **Accepted.** Adopting arctic is gated on audit (dep graph, maintainer count, signing posture, Atlassian 3LO coverage, lockfile pinning). Roll-our-own is the fallback if arctic fails audit. | [oauth-integration § Library decision](./oauth-integration#library-decision-arctic-vs-roll-our-own) | ## Pattern observations across rounds [Section titled “Pattern observations across rounds”](#pattern-observations-across-rounds) Every round added 3–6 substantive items that were genuine gaps. The gaps got smaller as rounds progressed: * **Round 1**: structural issues (idempotency contract, sandbox model, schema evolution, secret-shareable case) * **Round 2**: substantive refinements (sandbox/signing conflation, cost theater, audit retention) * **Round 3**: implementation-level holes (macOS asymmetry, IMDS/RFC1918, scriptHash comparison, marketplace moderation overconfidence, trust granularity) * **Round 4**: targeted gaps (smoke test, dev escape, ownership transfer, PG lock) * **Round 5**: surgical refinements of round 4 (Tauri sidecar, region templating, recordResource helper, key rotation, queue overflow) * **Round 6**: refinements of round 5 (named dev path, preset maintenance, teardown dispatcher, key-rotation attestation) Convergence is happening. Round 7 should be sign-off-only. If it surfaces substantive new issues, scope is re-evaluated. ## Outstanding for round 7 [Section titled “Outstanding for round 7”](#outstanding-for-round-7) Round-7 reviewers should focus on: * Are the V1 → V1.1 → V2 cuts in [Open Questions](./open-questions) honest? * Is the V1 LOC target (\~2,000–2,100) realistic, or understated? * Has anything been missed in the V1 set that would block vetted-publisher alpha? * Are the [sign-off checklist](./open-questions#sign-off-checklist) items actually all answered in the spec? The planned condition was: if round 7 returned “no substantive concerns,” implementation would begin in the order below. (This is the historical plan-of-record. Much of the build-script / OAuth substrate was subsequently implemented under `packages/operator-core/lib/provision/` and `/oauth/`, with the divergences flagged inline above; the snapshot-export subsystem was later retired.) The intended order was: 1. **PR 1** (\~600 LOC): Snapshot share-semantics + OAuth + GitHub provider + paste-PAT scope check + version pinning (`versionPin`) + securityAdvisories 2. **PR 2** (\~1,400–1,500 LOC): Build-script lifecycle (manifest, runner, sandbox with smoke test, audit, recovery via PG, consent flow, cloudProvider presets, network floor, trust per-(publisher, plugin) with rotation/transfer, hook queue-and-replay, single-user detection, helper library) + dogfood 3. **PR 3** (V1.1 onward): github-repo build-script refactor + `runAt` scheduling + `budgetCap` + AWS-Budgets helper + skip-teardown banner + marketplace moderation layer (separate spec)

# Per-field share semantics

> Plugins flag each configSchema field as secret (credential, stripped on snapshot by default), shareable:false (publisher-specific identifier, stripped), or default (config that travels with the snapshot). Schema evolution covered via aliases for renames + removals.

Retired — the harness-snapshot system is gone (2026-06-09) The entire harness-snapshot system was **retired on 2026-06-09** (plan `retire-snapshots-instance-spec-2026-06-09`, Phase B). Its three jobs were re-homed: **distribution → blueprints** (the Cupboard now distributes recipes), **backup → git + PG** (code + state are already durable), and the one remaining **reproducible-clone** job became the lightweight `InstanceSpec` at `packages/operator-core/lib/instance-spec/` (`capture` / `boot` / `vary`). This page documents the now-retired snapshot share-semantics *design*. None of the live code paths it cites still exist at the locations shown — they were moved to `_retired/snapshot-system/` (`lint:no-retired` guards re-imports). What **did** land and remains valid: the share-semantics flags on plugin `configSchema`s (`secret` / `shareable` / `oauth` / `aliases` / `pattern`) shipped on the reference plugins. The advisory-check helper (`security-advisories.ts`) also survives as live code — see the note in [Security advisories at fork time](#security-advisories-at-fork-time). ## The problem [Section titled “The problem”](#the-problem) When today’s snapshot system captures a harness, it copies `~/.papercusp/harnesses/<slug>/plugin-configs/<plugin>.json` verbatim into the tarball. That works for any field that’s pure configuration, but it fails two ways: 1. **Credentials leak**: a plugin config containing `github_token: ghp_...` ends up in the snapshot tarball. Anyone with the tarball gets the publisher’s GitHub access. 2. **Identifiers force-share**: a plugin config containing `accountId: f896...` (the publisher’s Cloudflare account) lands in the forker’s plugin-config. The fork is configured to deploy to the publisher’s CF account, which the forker doesn’t have access to. Today’s baseline mitigation is the `uiSchema`-driven redactor in the snapshot exporter (`redactPluginConfig`, since retired to `_retired/snapshot-system/operator-core/snapshot-config-redact.ts`) that replaces every field whose plugin `uiSchema` marks `{"ui:widget":"password"}` with `[REDACTED]`. This is fragile: * Misses any sensitive field the plugin author didn’t tag as a password widget. * Only handles credentials — has no notion of “publisher’s identifier”. * Can’t distinguish “publisher’s identifier” from “config that should travel”. (The key-pattern matching described below — `/token|secret|api[_-]?key/i` — is the *defense-in-depth fallback* that this proposal adds in `extractShape`, not the baseline redactor.) ## Proposal [Section titled “Proposal”](#proposal) Plugins declare per-field share semantics directly in `configSchema`: 
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["github_token"],
  "properties": {
    "github_token": {
      "type": "string",
      "secret": true,
      "oauth": { "provider": "github", "scopes": ["repo"] },
      "description": "GitHub PAT or OAuth token. Stripped from snapshots; users re-authorize on fork."
    },
    "owner": {
      "type": "string",
      "shareable": false,
      "description": "GitHub user or org. Different per forker — stripped from snapshots."
    },
    "repo": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Repo name. Defaults to harness slug. Travels with the snapshot."
    },
    "visibility": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["private", "public"],
      "default": "private"
    },
    "defaultBranch": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "main"
    }
  }
}
```
 ### Three semantics [Section titled “Three semantics”](#three-semantics) | Flag | Meaning | Snapshot behavior | Fork behavior | | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------- | ------------------------------------ | | `secret: true` (default `snapshotPolicy: "strip"`) | Credential — stripped from snapshot | Stripped | User re-authorizes (OAuth) or pastes | | `shareable: false` | Environment-specific identifier (account ID, owner name, project slug, region) | Stripped | User must supply their own value | | (neither flag) | Pure config (default branch, retry count, output dir, format choice) | Included verbatim | Inherited as-is | ### Secret policy: when secrets *should* travel [Section titled “Secret policy: when secrets should travel”](#secret-policy-when-secrets-should-travel) There are real cases where a publisher wants a credential to travel with the snapshot: * A demo Slack webhook for a fictional workspace the publisher controls. * A read-only public-bucket access key. * A test-mode Stripe key (`sk_test_...`). Today, publishers work around this by hardcoding such credentials into project files — which then leak via git history. Better: surface this as a first-class capability with safety rails. 
```json
{
  "demo_webhook": {
    "type": "string",
    "secret": true,
    "snapshotPolicy": "include",
    "description": "Test-mode Slack webhook. Travels with snapshot for demos."
  }
}
```
 Three policies for `secret: true` fields: | `snapshotPolicy` | Snapshot behavior | | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `"strip"` (default) | Field stripped from snapshot. Forker must supply their own. | | `"include"` | Field included in snapshot. **Publish CLI requires `--include-secrets` flag and a per-secret confirmation prompt naming each included secret.** | | `"warn-and-prompt"` | Publish CLI prompts the publisher per-snapshot: include this credential or strip it? | Without the explicit `--include-secrets` flag and per-secret confirmation, no secret is ever embedded in a snapshot tarball — even when the plugin’s manifest declares `snapshotPolicy: "include"`. The manifest expresses intent; the publish CLI enforces consent at the moment of publication. ### Defaults [Section titled “Defaults”](#defaults) * `secret`: defaults to `false`. A field is considered secret only if explicitly flagged. * `shareable`: defaults to `true`. A field is considered shareable unless explicitly flagged otherwise. * `snapshotPolicy`: defaults to `"strip"` for `secret: true` fields. Has no meaning for non-secret fields (they always travel). ### Format validation via `pattern` [Section titled “Format validation via pattern”](#format-validation-via-pattern) `shareable: false` fields prompt the forker for a value with no inherent format constraint. Plugin authors should leverage JSON-Schema’s existing `pattern` field to validate format at fork-time: 
```json
{
  "accountId": {
    "type": "string",
    "shareable": false,
    "pattern": "^[a-f0-9]{32}$",
    "description": "Cloudflare account ID (32 hex chars)."
  }
}
```
 The fork-completion UI shows the pattern’s hint, validates input client-side, refuses save until the value matches. This is convention rather than a substrate addition — `ajv` (already in operator deps) handles `pattern` automatically. Plugin docs should call out the recommended pattern for common identifiers (account IDs, region names, tokens with known formats, etc.). The spec encourages **explicit**, but doesn’t force it. Existing plugins that don’t update their configSchema continue to work — the pattern-based redactor stays in place as a fallback safety net for any field a plugin author hasn’t declared. ### Pattern-based fallback [Section titled “Pattern-based fallback”](#pattern-based-fallback) Even with explicit flags, the snapshot exporter applies the pattern-based redactor as a defense-in-depth check: * If a field is *not flagged* but matches a known secret pattern (`/token|secret|api[_-]?key|password|pat\b/i`), the exporter logs a **warning** in the snapshot manifest and strips it anyway. * If a field *is flagged* `secret: false` but matches a secret pattern, the exporter prompts the publisher: “Field `<name>` is flagged shareable but matches a credential pattern. Continue?” — defaulting to “no, strip anyway”. This catches plugin authors who forget to flag a field while still letting declared-shareable fields override the pattern when the author knows what they’re doing. ## Snapshot tarball structure [Section titled “Snapshot tarball structure”](#snapshot-tarball-structure) A snapshot’s tarball stages project files under `source/` and per-harness PG state under `state/`. Per-plugin redacted config and its share-shape are **not** written as sibling files in the tarball — they ride inside `manifest.json` as per-plugin string fields (`plugins[].configJson` holds the redacted config, `plugins[].shapeJson` holds the shape). The shape route reads them back from the manifest, not from tarball files. 
```text
snapshot.tar.gz
├── manifest.json            ← plugins[].configJson (redacted) + plugins[].shapeJson
├── source/
│   └── ... (project files)
└── state/
    ├── shared-<table>.csv    (one CSV per captured shared PG table)
    └── harness/             (subset copy of the harness's .papercusp/ dir)
```
 The `shapeJson` payload (the `SnapshotShape` produced by `extractShape()`) describes every field the original config carried but the snapshot stripped, with the configSchema metadata the fork-time UI needs to render the right input (“Connect with GitHub” button vs plain text input). Its shape is a `fields` map keyed by field name plus a top-level `warnings` array — each entry carries a `reason` (one of `secret-strip`, `secret-include`, `secret-warn`, `shareable-false`, `pattern-fallback`) and optional `oauth` / `pattern` / `description`. Fields that travelled in plaintext are simply absent from the map. 
```json
// plugins[].shapeJson for github-repo (parsed)
{
  "fields": {
    "github_token": {
      "reason": "secret-strip",
      "oauth": { "provider": "github", "scopes": ["repo"] },
      "description": "GitHub PAT or OAuth token. Stripped from snapshots..."
    },
    "owner": {
      "reason": "shareable-false",
      "pattern": "...",
      "description": "GitHub user or org..."
    }
  },
  "warnings": []
}
```
 ## Fork-time UX [Section titled “Fork-time UX”](#fork-time-ux) When a snapshot is forked, the operator scans every plugin’s `.shape.json`, groups missing-fields by plugin, and shows them in the fork-completion UI: 
```text
Snapshot fork: my-store ← from ecommerce-stripe-aws
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────


The following plugins need additional configuration before they can run:


  @papercupai/github-repo
    github_token  [ Connect with GitHub ]      ← oauth-flagged, button instead of paste
    owner         [____________________]       ← shareable:false, plain input


  @papercupai/cloudflare-pages
    api_token     [ Paste token… ]              ← secret-flagged but no oauth, paste field
    accountId     [____________________]       ← shareable:false, plain input
    projectName   [my-store_____________]      ← shareable:false but defaulted to harness slug


  [ Save and continue ]   [ Skip — I'll configure manually later ]
```
 The “Connect with GitHub” buttons go through the OAuth flow (see [OAuth integration](./oauth-integration)). Plain inputs save through the same `PUT /api/plugins/config` we already have. ## Implementation [Section titled “Implementation”](#implementation) | Surface | Change | LOC | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | | `@papercusp/plugin-sdk` | Document field-level extensions (`secret`, `snapshotPolicy`, `shareable`, `oauth`, `aliases`) on the manifest’s `configSchema`. | \~15 | | `_retired/snapshot-system/operator-core/snapshot-shape.ts` | `extractShape()` — walk configSchema and apply the share-semantics filter, returning redacted config + shape contents. | \~80 | | `_retired/snapshot-system/operator-core/endpoint-route-routes-snapshots/instantiate.ts` | Apply `resolveAliases()` and return list of missing-fields per plugin in the fork response. | \~30 | | `_retired/snapshot-system/operator-app-ui/snapshots/[id]/fork/ForkClient.tsx` | The fork-completion UI shown above. Reuses `/settings/plugins`’s field renderer. | \~120 | Total: **\~265 lines.** Smaller than the build-script work; closer to the OAuth scope. Retired (was: Implemented) This section once landed: `extractShape` + `resolveAliases`, the exporter that called it, the shape route, and the fork-completion UI all shipped. They were **retired on 2026-06-09** with the rest of the snapshot system and now live under `_retired/snapshot-system/` — `snapshot-shape.ts`, `endpoint-route-routes-snapshots/{create,shape,instantiate}.ts`, and `operator-app-ui/snapshots/[id]/fork/ForkClient.tsx`. The paths in the table above point at their retired locations; do not expect to find them live under `packages/operator-core/` or `apps/operator/`. ## Migration story [Section titled “Migration story”](#migration-story) Existing plugins (cloudflare-pages, github-repo, jira-sync, linear-sync, etc.) keep working without changes — fields without flags fall through the pattern-based redactor as today. Plugin authors *opt in* to explicit flags when they update their schemas. For papercusp’s reference plugins, we’d update their schemas in the same PR that introduces share-semantics: | Plugin | Field | Current behavior | New flag | | ---------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | github-repo | `github_token` | redacted (matches `/token/`) | `secret: true, oauth: {provider: github, scopes: [repo]}` | | github-repo | `owner` | leaks | `shareable: false` | | github-repo | `repo` | leaks (becomes harness slug for forker) | (default — shareable) | | cloudflare-pages | `accountId` | leaks | `shareable: false` | | cloudflare-pages | `projectName` | leaks | `shareable: false` | | cloudflare-pages | `branch` | leaks | (default — shareable) | | linear-sync | `LINEAR_API_KEY` | redacted (matches `/key/`) | `secret: true, oauth: {provider: linear, scopes: [...]}` (when OAuth ships) | | linear-sync | `defaultTeamKey` | leaks | `shareable: false` | | jira-sync | `JIRA_API_TOKEN` | redacted | `secret: true` | | jira-sync | `JIRA_BASE_URL` | leaks | `shareable: false` (the publisher’s atlassian.net is theirs) | | slack-notifier | `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` | leaks | `secret: true` (webhook URL contains the secret token) | ## Schema evolution [Section titled “Schema evolution”](#schema-evolution) The `.shape.json` baked into a snapshot is frozen at publish time. If the plugin’s `configSchema` changes between publish and fork, the substrate needs a deterministic way to translate old field names to new. The `aliases` field (already used in the spec for capability renames) extends to config-field renames *and* removals. It’s a **per-property array** of prior names (with `null` marking removal), declared on the property that supersedes them — `resolveAliases()` walks the *current* schema’s properties and remaps the forked config accordingly. ### Renames [Section titled “Renames”](#renames) 
```json
{
  "configSchema": {
    "properties": {
      "account": {
        "type": "string",
        "shareable": false,
        "description": "GitHub user or org.",
        "aliases": ["owner"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```
 The plugin author renamed `owner` → `account` in v0.2.0. A snapshot published with `github-repo@0.1.0` ships `.shape.json` referencing `owner`. On fork into a `github-repo@0.2.0` install: 1. Substrate reads the snapshot’s `.shape.json`, finds an entry for `owner`. 2. Substrate consults the *current installed plugin’s* `configSchema` properties. 3. Sees the `account` property declaring `aliases: ["owner"]` — translates `owner` references to `account`. 4. Fork-completion UI prompts for `account` (the current name), with the snapshot’s metadata about it (description, validation, etc.) sourced from the new schema, not the frozen one. ### Removals [Section titled “Removals”](#removals) A plugin may drop a field entirely (e.g., the auth flow changed and `legacyApiKey` is no longer used). The `.shape.json` from older snapshots still references it; without a removal hint, the fork-time UI would prompt for a field the new plugin doesn’t read. 
```json
{
  "configSchema": {
    "properties": {
      "newApiKey": { "type": "string", "secret": true },
      "legacyApiKey": { "type": "string", "secret": true, "aliases": [null] }
    }
  }
}
```
 A `null` entry in a property’s `aliases` array declares “this field was removed” — `resolveAliases()` drops `legacyApiKey` from the forked config, the user is not prompted, and the plugin’s runtime never sees the field. This is intentionally distinct from carrying the value forward under a new name via a rename alias (e.g. `newApiKey` declaring `aliases: ["legacyApiKey"]`). ### Combined [Section titled “Combined”](#combined) Renames and removals coexist by declaring `aliases` arrays across the schema’s properties: 
```json
{
  "properties": {
    "account":   { "type": "string", "aliases": ["owner"] },
    "legacyApiKey": { "type": "string", "aliases": [null] },
    "awsRegion": { "type": "string", "aliases": ["region"] }
  }
}
```
 ### When aliases are walked [Section titled “When aliases are walked”](#when-aliases-are-walked) Aliases are walked from the **current installed plugin’s** manifest, not the snapshot’s. This means: * A snapshot is forward-compatible automatically: as long as the new plugin version declares its aliases, old snapshots fork cleanly. * Plugin authors are responsible for keeping the per-property `aliases` arrays populated for every config-field rename or removal in their plugin’s lifetime. * The substrate never auto-infers aliases — explicit declarations only. If an old snapshot references a field that has neither a current counterpart nor an alias entry, the fork-time UI surfaces it as “unknown — this field is no longer recognized by the current plugin version” and the user can choose to drop it or abort the fork. ## Plugin version pinning (default-on) [Section titled “Plugin version pinning (default-on)”](#plugin-version-pinning-default-on) A plugin declares its restore pin policy on its manifest via `versionPin`: 
```json
// plugin manifest
{
  "name": "@papercupai/github-repo",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "versionPin": { "mode": "exact" }   // 'semver' | 'exact' | 'hash'
}
```
 `versionPin.mode` controls how a fork resolves the plugin version: `'exact'` restores the exact version captured (the reproducible default this section argues for), `'semver'` accepts any version satisfying the captured range, `'hash'` pins by content hash. (The legacy boolean `pluginVersionPinned: true` is still read for back-compat — it maps to `mode: 'exact'` — but `versionPin` is the current field and wins when both are set.) When the fork uses the exact captured version, the substrate doesn’t walk `aliases` because the schema is exactly the one the snapshot expects. The user can opt into the latest available version per-plugin during fork (“fork against latest” toggle), in which case the substrate walks the alias chain from pinned-version → latest. Most users want “fork-and-it-just-works”; pinning is the right default. This radically reduces the alias-map maintenance burden: plugin authors only need to maintain aliases when a user explicitly opts into forward compatibility, not every time the schema evolves. ### Security advisories at fork time [Section titled “Security advisories at fork time”](#security-advisories-at-fork-time) Pinning a vulnerable version is a vulnerability vector if the user has no signal about the vuln. The marketplace catalog adds a per-version field: 
```json
{
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "securityAdvisories": [
    {
      "cve": "CVE-2026-12345",
      "severity": "moderate",
      "fixedIn": "0.1.1",
      "summary": "OAuth state nonce reuse on rapid concurrent flows",
      "advisoryUrl": "https://github.com/papercupai/github-repo/security/advisories/GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz"
    }
  ]
}
```
 At fork time, substrate consults the catalog for the pinned version’s advisories. If any advisories exist with severity ≥ moderate, the fork-completion UI surfaces a loud prompt: 
```text
Security advisory
─────────────────
The pinned version of @papercupai/github-repo (0.1.0) has a known issue:


  CVE-2026-12345 (moderate)
  OAuth state nonce reuse on rapid concurrent flows.
  Fixed in 0.1.1.


Continue with pinned version, upgrade to latest, or read advisory?
  [ Pin (vulnerable)  ]   [ Upgrade to 0.1.1  ]   [ Read advisory ]
```
 No silent auto-upgrade — the user might have legitimate reasons to pin (reproducibility for a known-good environment). But the warning is loud, persistent (returns on next operator boot until acknowledged), and uncircumventable.
