If `papercup-coding` wants “one-click publish to Cloudflare Pages”, that integration is either baked into the template (forcing every coding harness in the world to know about Cloudflare) or has to be implemented separately by every template author. Same for vscode-server, Slack notifications, Postgres schema management, etc. This is why every mature plugin ecosystem has a **plugin marketplace** distinct from a **theme/template marketplace**: WordPress separates plugins from themes; VS Code separates extensions from project templates; Backstage separates plugins from app shells. Papercusp needs the same split. Templates are recipes; plugins are horizontal capabilities that any template can pull in. ## 14.1 Templates vs plugins — the ontological split [Section titled “14.1 Templates vs plugins — the ontological split”](#141-templates-vs-plugins--the-ontological-split) | | **Harness template** | **Plugin** | | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | | What it is | Recipe for spinning up a harness | Horizontal capability any harness can use | | Cardinality | 1 template → N harness instances | 1 plugin install → mounted into N harness instances | | Install scope | Per-instance (each `papercusp run` produces a fresh instance) | Per-machine (installed globally; enabled per harness instance) | | Examples | papercup-coding, papercup-org, “research-org”, “habit-tracker” | cloudflare-pages, vscode-server, slack-notifier, gemini-narrator | | Composition | One template per harness | Multiple plugins per harness instance | | Manifest field | `kind: 'template'` | `kind: 'plugin'` (the default) | | Closest analog | WordPress *themes*; npm-create-\* | WordPress *plugins*; VS Code *extensions* | | Lifecycle hook | `papercusp run` — instantiates a harness from the template | Substrate boot — discovers + mounts global-plugins for active harnesses | Both share the marketplace pipeline (catalog, signing, retraction, namespaces, reviews, SBOMs, authors, webhooks). They diverge only in the runtime model: templates produce instances; plugins extend instances. ## 14.2 Research summary — 8 plugin systems studied [Section titled “14.2 Research summary — 8 plugin systems studied”](#142-research-summary--8-plugin-systems-studied) | System | Sandbox | Capability model | Distribution | Hook system | Composition | | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | **VS Code** | Out-of-process extension host + iframe webviews | Manifest `activationEvents` + `contributes`; \~30 surfaces | Bespoke marketplace, \~50k extensions | Typed event API (`vscode.workspace.onDidChange*`) | `extensionDependencies` | | **WordPress** | None | None (full host privileges) | Bespoke + npm-style; 60k+ plugins | `add_action` / `add_filter` priority numbers | Hook-priority composition | | **Backstage** | None | DI container `ApiRef` typed services | npm packages, build-time | React context + DI | Plugins ship npm packages with peer-deps | | **Figma** | iframe + UI iframe + manifest network allowlist | Strongest of survey: manifest declares network domains; iframe enforces | Bespoke marketplace | postMessage RPC | Limited | | **Obsidian** | None (full Node + DOM) | All-or-nothing at install (cautionary tale) | Bespoke “community plugins” | Vault events + Plugin API | Plugins commonly conflict | | **Slack apps** | Hosted webhook | OAuth scopes (coarse) | App directory | Event subscriptions | None | | **Astro / Vite** | None (build-time) | None | npm | Build hooks | Linear pipeline | | **Probot / Hubot** | Hosted GitHub App / chat bot | Coarse permissions | npm scaffolding | Webhook events | Each app independent | ### The two failure modes to avoid [Section titled “The two failure modes to avoid”](#the-two-failure-modes-to-avoid) 1. **Obsidian / WordPress’s “no sandbox”** — host trivially exploitable by malicious or buggy plugin. Both retroactively bolted on capability prompts. 2. **Backstage’s “build-time only”** — installs require rebuild + redeploy. Backstage 2.0 is rebuilding the plugin model around runtime loading. Papercusp’s spec already commits to: iframe sandboxing for v2 UI plugins (Figma’s model), runtime install with capability consent (Chrome Web Store style), capability strings at the DI boundary (VS Code × Cap’n Proto). This proposal builds on that foundation. ## 14.3 The four design pillars [Section titled “14.3 The four design pillars”](#143-the-four-design-pillars) ### 14.3.1 Reuse the marketplace pipeline; add a `kind` discriminator [Section titled “14.3.1 Reuse the marketplace pipeline; add a kind discriminator”](#1431-reuse-the-marketplace-pipeline-add-a-kind-discriminator) `papercusp.json` adds: 
```json
{ "kind": "plugin", "name": "@papercupai/cloudflare-pages", "version": "0.1.0", ... }
```
 `papercusp publish` is kind-agnostic. The catalog stores `kind` in the package row. The marketplace site filters at `/marketplace/?kind=template|plugin` (default both). Search and authors all work without code changes. `papercusp install` checks the `kind`: * `template` → registers in `~/.papercusp/registry.json` (already implemented) * `plugin` → unpacks to `~/.papercusp/global-plugins/<slug>/` (already implemented in plugin-loader); the substrate’s plugin-runtime mounts on next `papercusp run` Both flows go through the same publish + signing + retraction infrastructure. Operators get the same ops dashboard counts. Authors see “5 templates and 12 plugins published” on their profile. **Shipped `kind` enum (a third category landed).** The proposal frames the world as templates vs plugins, but the manifest `kind` enum that shipped is `plugin | pack | template | snapshot | service | theme | harness`, and the default is **`plugin`** (not `template` as this proposal originally said). `'pack'` is a real third distribution category: a **runtime-less code-tool pack** — tools only, no `ui`/`roles`/`routines`/`actions`, and the runtime must stay `js`. The loader specially constrains it, rejecting any of those contributions on a pack (`tool-distribution-granularity-2026-06-05` D-001/D-004). `'snapshot'`, `'service'`, `'theme'`, and `'harness'` are reserved/dormant — the loader treats every non-`'pack'` value as a default plugin. The Cupboard’s `tool-pack` listing kind is how these packs surface in the storefront (and `learning-pack` is its sibling install kind for curated hive learnings). **Plugins ship in one of three runtimes.** Orthogonal to the action handler model, a plugin declares a `runtime` descriptor in `papercusp.json`. It defaults to `{ kind: 'js' }`; the other two are `wasm` (a `wasm32-wasip2` component artifact, loaded via `@papercusp/plugin-loader/wasm`, with a hard linear-memory budget) and `daemon` (a long-running stdio JSON-RPC peer, loaded via `@papercusp/plugin-loader/daemon`, with a restart policy). Action-invocation `concurrency` is `serial` or `parallel` — WASM defaults to serial (mpsc actor), daemon to parallel. JS plugins keep the in-process model the rest of this page describes. ### 14.3.2 Plugin lifecycle: install-time consent, harness-time mount [Section titled “14.3.2 Plugin lifecycle: install-time consent, harness-time mount”](#1432-plugin-lifecycle-install-time-consent-harness-time-mount) A plugin is **installed once globally** — capability-consent prompt at that point. Then **mounted at runtime** into every harness instance whose template `requires` it (or that the user enables via `papercusp plugin enable cloudflare-pages --harness sheets-clone`). This matches WordPress’s “active plugins per site” + Backstage’s “plugins mounted into the app”. ### 14.3.3 New primitive: `actions` (button-shaped, server runtime) [Section titled “14.3.3 New primitive: actions (button-shaped, server runtime)”](#1433-new-primitive-actions-button-shaped-server-runtime) The current SDK has hooks, routes, UI, routines, schema. Missing: a user-triggered action that the harness UI can surface as a button. 
```typescript
export interface ActionDefinition {
  /** Action name. Must match a key registered via ctx.actions.register(). */
  name: string;
  /** Human-readable button label for harness-toolbar etc. */
  label?: string;
  /** Where this action surfaces in the host UI / lifecycle. */
  surfaces?: ('mission-done' | 'harness-toolbar' | 'feature-row' | 'plugin-detail' | string)[];
  /** Capabilities this action additionally requires beyond the plugin's own. */
  capabilities?: Capability[];
  /** JSON-Schema for the params object the handler receives (see §14.3.5). */
  paramsSchema?: Record<string, unknown>;


  /**
   * Server-side handler hints. The actual handler is registered imperatively
   * from the plugin's `init()` via `ctx.actions.register(name, handler)`. The
   * manifest carries no function references — they don't survive serialization.
   */
  serverHandler?: {
    /** Per-invocation timeout in seconds (host enforces via AbortSignal). */
    timeoutSec?: number;
  };


  // Note: actions are strictly USER-CLICKED. There is no `autoOn` field.
  // To auto-fire an action on a substrate event (e.g. `mission.done`), the
  // plugin ships a routine that internally invokes the same handler the
  // action button calls. One trigger registry (routines), one event
  // capability namespace (`events:listen:*`), one audit trail.
}
```
 **Actions are server-runtime only.** The proposal originally sketched a presence-determined dispatch (`serverHandler` → server, `clientHandler` → iframe, both → hybrid, with a load-time rejection of hybrid manifests). The shipped `ActionDefinition` has **no `clientHandler` field** — there is no client or hybrid runtime, no presence-determined dispatch, and no hybrid-rejection code in the loader or SDK. Every action handler runs in the server runtime (Node, full DI, capability-checked), registered imperatively from `init()` and dispatched by the host on a surface event. The forwards-compatibility hook for an iframe sandbox (§14.9.5) is the `serverHandler` declaration itself — when a client runtime lands, the manifest gains a sibling declaration without rewriting the existing server actions. The `surfaces` enum that shipped is `'mission-done' | 'harness-toolbar' | 'feature-row' | 'plugin-detail'` (plus an open string for forward-compat) — note `harness-sidebar` from the original sketch is not a defined surface, and `mission-done`/`plugin-detail` are live additions. There is no `icon` field and no `defaultTimeoutSec` field on the action; the per-action timeout is set via `serverHandler.timeoutSec`. This pattern mirrors VS Code’s `contributes.commands` (declarative) + `commands.registerCommand` (imperative). It avoids the “function in JSON manifest” trap and keeps a clean migration path to iframe sandboxing. Three properties make actions worth their own primitive vs reusing routines/hooks: 1. **They’re user-discoverable.** A button in the dashboard. Routines and hooks are invisible to the end user. 2. **They have parameters.** A “Publish” button needs to know the target. JSON-schema → auto-form. 3. **They have execution status.** Async with a progress indicator. Routines fire-and-forget; hooks are passive. WordPress has admin actions, VS Code has commands, Slack has slash commands, Backstage has Actions Catalog. We need our equivalent. ### 14.3.4 Capability consent UI at install time [Section titled “14.3.4 Capability consent UI at install time”](#1434-capability-consent-ui-at-install-time) 
```plaintext
Install @papercupai/cloudflare-pages 0.1.0?


You are installing a plugin — it will be enabled into your harness instances
and run alongside the template's logic.


This plugin will be granted:
  ▸ HIGH   secrets:read:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
           — read your Cloudflare API token at deploy time
  ▸ MEDIUM http:fetch:api.cloudflare.com
           — make HTTPS requests to Cloudflare's API
  ▸ LOW    ui:harness-action:publish
           — register a "Publish" button in your harness dashboard
  ▸ LOW    ui:harness-sidebar:cloudflare-publish
           — claim the "cloudflare-publish" sidebar slot
  ▸ LOW    storage:plugin-private
           — store deploy history in plugin-private filesystem


Tier summary (per §10.6.1): 1 high · 1 medium · 3 low


Signed by: @papercupai (verified)
SBOM: no known CVEs (scanned 2026-04-27)


[Install]  [Cancel]
```
 Adapted from Chrome Web Store / iOS App Store consent screens, using the capability tiers we already have (§10.6.1). The first line names what kind of artifact is being installed (plugin vs template) so users understand the runtime implications. ### 14.3.5 Capability granularity — per-id everywhere [Section titled “14.3.5 Capability granularity — per-id everywhere”](#1435-capability-granularity--per-id-everywhere) All UI capabilities are **per-id**, matching the per-id collision-resolution rule from §10.5. A plugin claiming `ui:dashboard-tab:foo` can mount one tab named `foo`; mounting `bar` requires a separate `ui:dashboard-tab:bar` capability. This makes the consent prompt name what’s actually being claimed: | Capability | What it grants | | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | | `ui:dashboard-tab:<id>` | One tab in the dashboard tab strip | | `ui:sidebar-item:<id>` | One sidebar entry in the harness chrome | | `ui:harness-action:<id>` | One action surface (button, menu item) | | `ui:harness-route:<slug>` | One full-route mount under `/harness/<slug>` | | `ui:plugin-config-panel` | Override the auto-generated config form (see §14.3.7) | The previous coarse `ui:dashboard-tab` (no id) was *proposed* for removal here. In the shipped SDK, the coarse no-id forms (`ui:dashboard-tab`, `ui:sidebar-item`, `ui:harness-route`, `ui:tui-pane`) are what landed — the per-id capability granularity in this section is design intent, not the current `Capability` type. The shipped UI-surface set is therefore **`react` / `iframe` / `tui-pane`**, and `ui:tui-pane` is a live capability in addition to the dashboard-tab / sidebar-item / harness-route forms above. A `tui-pane` surface contributes a terminal pane hosted by the pui (`apps/tui`): the pui allocates a managed pane and runs the surface’s declared `command` argv in it (gated by `compute:exec:<command[0]>`, the same exec-gate as `ctx.spawn`), and the plugin renders its own content (ratatui or any TUI). The desktop targets (dashboard-tab / harness-route) are deferred with desktop; the terminal target is what shipped first (`revive-plugin-system-2026-06-04` D-002). ### 14.3.6 Server-runtime resource isolation [Section titled “14.3.6 Server-runtime resource isolation”](#1436-server-runtime-resource-isolation) Server-runtime action handlers run as Node code inside the substrate process. The iframe sandbox (§10.4) does not apply. To prevent one plugin from degrading the whole harness: * **Per-action timeout** — `serverHandler.timeoutSec` on the action (default 60s); substrate cancels via `AbortSignal` threaded through `ctx.signal`. * **Per-binary subprocess gate** — `compute:exec:<binary>`; see §14.3.6.1 below. * **Soft heap budget** — substrate polls `process.memoryUsage()` per harness; if a plugin’s RSS jumps >256 MB above its baseline during a handler call, the action is cancelled and the harness logs a budget violation. * **Postgres connection cap** — plugin’s `ctx.db` proxy holds at most one connection per concurrent action invocation; long-running queries get the same `AbortSignal` as the action. #### 14.3.6.1 Per-binary subprocess: `compute:exec:<binary>` [Section titled “14.3.6.1 Per-binary subprocess: compute:exec:\<binary>”](#14361-per-binary-subprocess-computeexecbinary) The original proposal argued for *no* `process:spawn` capability at all, on the grounds that common binaries have config flags that spawn other binaries (`git -c core.fsmonitor=<attacker-binary>` is the canonical example; the same trick works for `ssh`, `docker`, `npm`, `node`), so a generic spawn gate is unsafe and a per-(binary, args-pattern) gate would re-implement sudoers. What shipped is a **per-binary** subprocess capability rather than no spawn at all: `compute:exec:<binary>` (e.g. `compute:exec:ffmpeg`, with basename wildcards like `compute:exec:py-*`). A plugin invokes it via `ctx.spawn(bin, args, { cwd, env, stdin })` and receives `{ stdout, stderr, code }` after the process exits. The host enforces `compute:exec:<binary-basename>` against the plugin’s declared capabilities before invoking; `bin` is resolved via PATH and absolute paths are rejected (use the binary name plus the capability). The named typed wrappers the proposal sketched (`GitService`, `DockerService`, `execTrustedCommand`, a `TrustedBinary` enum) do **not** exist in the SDK — the capability gate is the binary-basename match, and the foot-cannon flags the proposal worried about are an authoring concern for the plugin, not a substrate-curated allowlist. The same `compute:exec:<command[0]>` gate is what a `tui-pane` UI surface’s `command` argv runs under (§14.3.5). ### 14.3.7 paramsSchema / configSchema dialect commitment [Section titled “14.3.7 paramsSchema / configSchema dialect commitment”](#1437-paramsschema--configschema-dialect-commitment) Every place this proposal says “UI auto-generates a form” needs a precise contract or it silently degrades to “we ship a generic form, every serious plugin overrides it” (the WordPress experience). **Commitments:** 1. **Dialect**: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, **strict subset**: * Allowed: `object`, `array`, `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `enum`, `oneOf` for tagged unions * Allowed: `format` for `email`, `uri`, `hostname`, `date-time`, `uuid` * Disallowed: `$ref` to external URIs (security + offline use); `if/then/else`; `not`; `additionalProperties: <schema>` * Disallowed: regex `pattern` containing backreferences (ReDoS class) 2. **Companion `uiSchema`** sibling using RJSF’s vocabulary (widgets, hints, ordering). Optional. Plugin author writes: 
   ```json
   {
     "paramsSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "domain": { "type": "string", "format": "hostname" } } },
     "uiSchema":     { "domain": { "ui:placeholder": "myapp.example.com", "ui:autofocus": true } }
   }
   ```
 3. **Escape hatch — `ui:plugin-config-panel` capability**: plugins that need full control register their own React component for the config UI. The substrate calls into it via the iframe-bridge (or directly in v1 trusted server-runtime case). This is what Backstage and VS Code arrived at after years of “auto-form” debt. Spec it now. ## 14.4 Worked example: `@papercupai/cloudflare-pages` [Section titled “14.4 Worked example: @papercupai/cloudflare-pages”](#144-worked-example-papercupaicloudflare-pages) papercusp.json 
```json
{
  "kind": "plugin",
  "name": "@papercupai/cloudflare-pages",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "One-click publish your harness's project output to Cloudflare Pages.",
  "papercusp": "^0.1.0",
  "license": "MIT",


  "capabilities": [
    "secrets:read:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN",
    "secrets:read:CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID",
    "http:fetch:api.cloudflare.com",
    "ui:harness-action:publish",
    "ui:harness-sidebar:cloudflare-publish",
    "events:listen:mission.done",
    "storage:plugin-private"
  ],


  "configSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "pages_project":         { "type": "string", "title": "Pages project name", "minLength": 1 },
      "build_dir":             { "type": "string", "title": "Build output dir", "default": "dist" },
      "custom_domain":         { "type": "string", "format": "hostname", "title": "Custom domain (optional)" },
      "auto_publish_on_done":  { "type": "boolean", "title": "Auto-publish on mission complete", "default": false }
    },
    "required": ["pages_project"]
  },
  "uiSchema": {
    "pages_project": { "ui:placeholder": "myapp" },
    "custom_domain": { "ui:placeholder": "myapp.example.com" }
  },


  "actions": [
    {
      "name": "publish",
      "label": "Publish to Cloudflare Pages",
      "surfaces": ["harness-toolbar", "mission-done"],
      "capabilities": ["secrets:read:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "http:fetch:api.cloudflare.com"],
      "serverHandler": { "timeoutSec": 120 }
    }
  ],


  "routines": [
    {
      "name": "auto-publish-on-done",
      "trigger": { "kind": "event", "event": "mission.done" },
      "targetAction": "publish",
      "enabledIfConfig": "auto_publish_on_done"
    }
  ]
}
```
 index.ts 
```typescript
import type { Plugin, PapercuspContext } from '@papercusp/plugin-sdk';


async function publishHandler(ctx: PapercuspContext, params: unknown) {
  const token = await ctx.api.secrets.read('CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN');
  const accountId = await ctx.api.secrets.read('CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID');
  const projectName = ctx.config.pages_project;
  const buildDir = join(ctx.projectDir, ctx.config.build_dir ?? 'dist');


  // Honour the AbortSignal from the substrate (timeout / user-cancel)
  const r = await ctx.api.fetch(`https://api.cloudflare.com/...`, {
    signal: ctx.signal,
    /* ... */
  });


  // Write to the per-action audit log via context
  await ctx.audit('publish.success', { url: `https://${projectName}.pages.dev` });


  return { ok: true, result: { url: `https://${projectName}.pages.dev` } };
}


export default {
  name: '@papercupai/cloudflare-pages',
  version: '0.1.0',
  papercusp: '^0.1.0',
  capabilities: [...],
  configSchema: {...},
  actions: [{ name: 'publish', /* ... */ serverHandler: { timeoutSec: 120 } }],


  init(ctx) {
    // Imperative registration — no function in the manifest.
    ctx.actions.register('publish', publishHandler);
  },
} satisfies Plugin;
```
 User flow: 1. `papercusp install @papercupai/cloudflare-pages` → consent screen → installed globally 2. `papercusp plugin enable cloudflare-pages --harness sheets-clone` → form for `pages_project`, etc. 3. User goes to `/harness/sheets-clone` → “Publish to Cloudflare Pages” button on the harness toolbar 4. Click → progress modal → success URL For auto-publish on mission complete: the routine declared in the manifest fires when the substrate emits `mission.done`. The routine handler invokes the same `publishHandler` function the action button does — single code path, single audit trail. `papercup-coding`’s template manifest just adds: 
```json
{ "recommends": ["@papercupai/cloudflare-pages@^0.1"] }
```
 The install flow then suggests “papercup-coding works well with cloudflare-pages — install it too?” but doesn’t force. ## 14.5 Existing tab classification — what should be plugin vs core? [Section titled “14.5 Existing tab classification — what should be plugin vs core?”](#145-existing-tab-classification--what-should-be-plugin-vs-core) The current papercusp dashboard has **8 tabs**: proposals, dashboard, summary, docs, vscode, pi, insights, config. Each needs a classification: keep in core, or extract to a plugin? The principle: **a tab is core if every harness — coding, research-org, content-pipeline, marketing-bot, anything — would benefit from it**. A tab is a plugin if it’s specific to one template family or external integration. | Tab | Today’s content | Recommended | Rationale | | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **dashboard** | Feature queue, agents, logs, issues — the main canvas | **CORE** | This IS the harness UI. Every harness has features+agents+logs. Plugins contribute INTO it via `dashboardTabs`/`sidebarItems`. If this were a plugin, harnesses with no plugins would have nothing to show. | | **summary** | High-level changelog of what’s been built | **CORE** | Generic across all templates. A research-org harness wants “what got researched”; a content-pipeline wants “what got published”; coding wants “what features shipped”. Same primitive. | | **insights** | Features count, cost, tokens, iterations | **CORE** | Universal harness metrics. Every harness pays for tokens; every harness has iterations. | | **config** | Per-instance configuration | **CORE** | Every harness needs config. Plugins contribute their own config sections via `configSchema`. | | **proposals** | AI-generated scope expansion suggestions for the SPEC.md | **CORE for v1**, defer extraction | See §14.6 — proposals isn’t a UI tab extraction, it’s an authorization-model question. | | **docs** | iframe of project docs (fumadocs on :4325) | **PLUGIN** (`@papercupai/fumadocs`) | Optional integration with an external docs server. Templates that don’t generate docs shouldn’t see this tab. | | **vscode** | iframe of code-server on the project dir | **PLUGIN** (`@papercupai/vscode-server`) | Code-server is heavyweight + only useful when there’s code to edit. Research, marketing, support harnesses don’t need it. | | **pi** | iframe of the pi (omp) interactive coding agent | **PLUGIN** (`@papercupai/pi-companion`) | Pi is one specific external tool. Would be like baking “ChatGPT side panel” into Slack. | ### Where this proposal disagrees with the maintainer’s initial take [Section titled “Where this proposal disagrees with the maintainer’s initial take”](#where-this-proposal-disagrees-with-the-maintainers-initial-take) The maintainer suggested: * Core: pi, insights, Config * Plugins: proposals, dashboard, summary, docs, vscode This proposal disagrees on three of them: 1. **`dashboard` should stay CORE, not become a plugin.** The dashboard is the composition surface — it’s where plugins’ actions and tabs render. Making it a plugin would mean “harness with no plugins = empty UI” which breaks the first-run experience and the “core works without plugins” guarantee. 2. **`summary` should stay CORE.** Every harness benefits from “what got done”; the implementation is template-agnostic (read features+goals from state, render a timeline). Pulling it into a plugin would force every template author to either reimplement it or depend on the same plugin (a tax on adoption). 3. **`pi` should be a PLUGIN, not core.** Pi/omp is one specific external tool; not all harnesses use it. Treating it as core would tie papercusp to one external tool. **The dashboard nuance**: the dashboard *chrome* (tab strip, panel layout, action surfaces) stays core. The dashboard’s *primary panel* (feature queue for coding ≠ briefing pipeline for research-org) is contributed by the active template via a `defaultDashboardPanel` UI contribution. Templates ship their own dashboard panel; the chrome stays core. ## 14.6 Migration plan — porting tabs to plugins [Section titled “14.6 Migration plan — porting tabs to plugins”](#146-migration-plan--porting-tabs-to-plugins) The migration is straightforward because each tab is already an isolated React component in `apps/papercusp/app/harness/`. Each plugin extraction is: 1. Move the component file into `libs/papercusp-marketplace/seeds/papercupai/<plugin-name>/src/` 2. Wrap it in a `Plugin` export with appropriate per-id capabilities 3. Replace the inline `activePanel === 'X'` render with a `dashboardTabs` contribution 4. Publish via the seed-publish pipeline (service token model) 5. Add to `papercup-coding`’s `recommends:` so existing users get it on install Per-tab effort estimate (post-Phase-P2): | Tab → Plugin | Lines | Capabilities | Est | Status | | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | -------------- | | `vscode` → `@papercupai/vscode-server` | \~10 (iframe) | `ui:harness-tab:vscode` + config `code_server_url` | 30 min | **Pilot — P5** | | `docs` → `@papercupai/fumadocs` | \~10 (iframe) | `ui:harness-tab:docs` + config `docs_url` | 30 min | P7 | | `pi` → `@papercupai/pi-companion` | \~150 (PiPanel) | `ui:harness-tab:pi` + typed-services for child-process needs | 1.5h | P7 | | `proposals` → `@papercupai/scope-proposals` | substrate-protocol change | New: plugin authorization to mutate harness-canonical state | DEFERRED to v1.5 | See note | **Why proposals is deferred to v1.5**: proposals isn’t a UI panel extraction. The blocker is **the write side** — today `apply_proposal_to_spec` is substrate code mutating substrate-canonical state (SPEC.md, the goals tree). For proposals to live in a plugin, the substrate has to authorize a plugin to mutate harness-canonical state, which is a real authorization-model question (not “let plugins call substrate functions” — those exist via the DI proxy — but “let plugins overwrite the harness contract”). Designing that authorization model is its own milestone; until then, proposals stays core. Total v1 migration effort (vscode + docs + pi): \~2.5h of straightforward refactoring once the action + tab plugin primitives are in place. The migration is **non-breaking** because: * Each tab keeps its component code, just relocates * The dashboard chrome already has a generic `dashboardTabs` slot * Plugins are loaded at substrate boot; existing harnesses see them on next `papercusp run` * Templates that haven’t been republished still work (they just don’t get the new tabs until users explicitly install the plugins) ## 14.7 Implementation roadmap [Section titled “14.7 Implementation roadmap”](#147-implementation-roadmap) Order matters; later items depend on earlier. **Status — 2026-04-27**: P1 → P8 shipped + operator dashboards for `audit.action_executions` (drill-down + webhooks) and plugin grants (`granted-capabilities.json` + `extended-grants.json` with revoke). **Seven** in-tree reference plugins (`@papercupai/{vscode-server, cloudflare-pages,pi-coding,fumadocs,slack-notifier,postgres-manager, notion-export}`) published to the local marketplace; full publish → catalog → install → enable → lockfile round-trip verified end-to-end with the service-token CI flow. Drill-down drawer has **Detail** + **History** tabs + a **Retry** button (re-invokes via the substrate CLI, mirrors the result back into `audit.action_executions`) + a **diagnose→remediate** affordance that surfaces a “revoke grants for this plugin” shortcut when an error message looks capability-related. Per-plugin audit page at `/papercusp-marketplace-ops/plugins/<slug>` aggregates every audit row across all action names with per-action filter chips. Top-of-page sticky nav links the four sections (Stats / Recent / Plugin grants / Action failures) with a red-pill count when there are recent failures. Webhook subscriptions are managed inline (operator-token-gated; create with event-type chips, disable/enable/delete per row, expandable per-row delivery log). `papercusp lock {check,upgrade-all,prune}` closes the lockfile-hygiene loop on the CLI; `lock prune` cascades transitive-orphan removal. Capability- aware install diff shows `+added` / `-removed` per cap before the consent prompt fires when there’s a prior grant. Per-harness audit page mirrors the per-plugin one — drill in from the harness column in the grants table to see every action invocation across all plugins on that harness. Both the per- harness and per-plugin pages show a cross-pivot grants table linking back to the other axis. History tab surfaces a per-row “vs prior” diff hint (same / +N / -M / \~K) so flaky-but-equivalent vs flaky-and-different is visible at a glance. Webhook deliveries sub-table is sortable by status / attempt / ts and gains a per-row replay button that resets a delivery to attempt 0. The drawer is deep-linkable via `?drawer=<auditId>`; back/forward syncs the open state naturally. Grants table supports multi-select + bulk-revoke and renders capability pills color-coded by tier (high=red, medium=amber, low=grey). Recent-action-failures table is now substring-filterable by harness, plugin, or error message. Persistent operator audit log (`audit.operator_actions`) records every operator-token-gated mutation and surfaces in a new dashboard panel with substring filtering. Grants table supports tier filter chips (high/medium/low) so operators can isolate the dangerous grants. Audit log + grants table both have CSV export for offline records. Webhook subscriptions can rotate their HMAC secret with a one-shot reveal modal. Marketplace Ed25519 signing key has an inspect + rotate surface that archives the old key (timestamped) and continues serving signatures already minted against archived keys. Test coverage: 27 plugin-loader action tests + 7 hot-reload + 12 lockfile + 7 lock-resolve + 15 consent + 7 plugin-cli + 9 grants = **84 passing**. Bonus operator surfaces: `papercusp plugin invoke <slug> <action>`, `papercusp plugin watch <slug>`, `papercusp upgrade-pin <slug>`, marketplace-ops Action-executions card + Recent-action-failures table + per-row drill-down drawer, a 30-second poller that emits `action.failed` / `action.timeout` webhook deliveries from `audit.action_executions`, and a **Plugin grants** card + per-harness table with revoke + sticky “extended to all” un-stick. Live state: `audit.action_executions` migration applied to the running `papercusp` Postgres DB (incl. `webhook_emitted_at` column for scanner idempotency); `/v1/admin/overview` includes `actionExecutions`, `/v1/admin/action-executions/:id` returns full row detail; the grants dashboard reads `~/.papercusp/{granted-capabilities,extended-grants}.json` server-side (no token needed; operator filesystem is the boundary). P9+ open (publishing the in-tree reference plugins, more reference plugins, action history view inside the drill-down drawer, retry-from-drawer). ### Phase P1 — Add `kind` to publishes (\~2h, completely additive) ✅ shipped [Section titled “Phase P1 — Add kind to publishes (\~2h, completely additive) ✅ shipped”](#phase-p1--add-kind-to-publishes-2h-completely-additive--shipped) * Schema: `ALTER TABLE packages ADD COLUMN kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'template'` * Server: read `manifest.kind` on publish, default to `'template'`, store in DB + Typesense * Marketplace site: `/marketplace/?kind=plugin` filter;
