Instead, start the operator under test with `PAPERCUSP_FAULT_INJECTION=1` and drive faults through the loopback-only control plane (inert without the env gate; rules are in-memory and vanish on restart): 
```sh
# fault the next profile save with a 500, then auto-expire
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/admin/fault-injection \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"pathPrefix":"/api/profile","method":"POST","status":500,"times":1}'
# delay-only rule (latency testing): {"pathPrefix":"/api/...","delayMs":3000}
# inspect / clear:  GET … | DELETE …?id=fault-1 | DELETE … (all)
```
 Implementation + tests: `apps/operator/bin/host-fault-injection.ts`. Trigger each by stopping the relevant backend / passing a bad parameter: | Surface | Trigger | Expected | | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/api/oracle/chat` | malformed body | 400 with `{error: "messages required"}`; dock shows `⚠ <message>` | | Add-plugin popover | `/api/plugins/global` returns non-200 | popover shows “Couldn’t load plugins” + Retry | | Plugin enable | server returns `{ok:false, error:"..."}` | `toast.error` with description \`(d.results?.\[0]?.log | | `/marketplace/<slug>` unknown slug | path doesn’t match registered template/plugin | 404 page “This page could not be found.” | | `/harness/<slug>` unknown slug | not in registry | `notFound()` triggers Next.js 404 | | `/pi` without `?harness=<slug>` | missing query param | inline message: “Missing `?harness=<slug>` query parameter.” | | Settings save | `/api/credentials` 500 | `toast.error("save failed: …")` | ## 13. Coverage checklist (paste into report) [Section titled “13. Coverage checklist (paste into report)”](#13-coverage-checklist-paste-into-report) The checklist mirrors the **live `/adv` shell** (the Vite SPA — `ADV_TABS` in `apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/AdvShell.tsx` is the source of truth for the tab strip). Rows are deliberately coarse for tabs whose internals churn; the per-panel detail lives in the panels themselves, not here. 
```plaintext
[ /adv]                 shell mounts, tab strip renders all tabs, pot selector works
[ /adv — Overview]      tab=overview mounts, workspace summary renders
[ /adv — Brainstorm]    tab=brainstorm mounts (per-pot)
[ /adv — Create]        tab=plans: plan list, plan editor, launch path
[ /adv — Calendar]      tab=calendar mounts (workspace-scoped scheduled/recurring plans)
[ /adv — Working]       tab=harnesses: dock mounts; Work-items grid (filter/search/row-select)
[ /adv — Health]        tab=health mounts (flag SYSTEM_HEALTH_TAB, default on; read-only system dashboard)
[ /adv — Working dock]  Add panel catalog (work-items/detail/overview/agents/logs/contributors/insights/chat), layout reset, per-slug layout persistence
[ /adv — Detail]        ?sel=WI-*/F-* drives Detail pane; Actions incl. Chat (wi-detail-chat)
[ /adv — Chat panel]    free slot picker (adv-chat-pick/adv-chat-start) → worker chat; repeat opens FOCUS the existing chat (no duplicate agent_chats row); archive frees the slot
[ /adv — Git]           tab=git: git-graph + PRs panels
[ /adv — Tests]         tab=testing: domains tree, per-file status, run affordances
[ /adv — Docs]          tab=docs (per-pot docs tree)
[ /adv — Insights]      tab=insights mounts
[ /adv — Evaluation]    tab=evals mounts (impartial-benchmark suite, workspace-scoped)
[ /adv — Conversations] tab=conversations: all 5 views (threads/deliberations/agentchats/messages/feed); threads reply/accept/promote; LIVE agent chat shows the interactive composer (advconv-live-chat), archived stays read-only
[ /adv — Learning]      tab=learning: papercusp-improvement backlog renders
[ /adv — Frames]        tab=frames mounts (workspace live view)
[ /adv — Settings]      tab=settings mounts, sections save
[ /adv — Sessions]      /adv/sessions: roster, session detail, launch controls
[ /admin]               /admin/{plans,git,features,tables,dbos,run}: each mounts; /admin/git pipeline view renders
[ /cupboard]            list + detail render; error state shows friendly copy + Retry
[ /coord]               coordination view mounts
[ Conversations chat]   Conversations tab → live agent-chat composer present and sends (replaces the old global "Operator chat" / "Reply to Papercup…" surface — see retired note)
[ Keyboard]             ⌘K palette, Esc closes modals/popovers, Mod+I → conversations
[ Header]               WorkspaceSwitcher present; the /adv header uses a text kicker ("Advanced orchestration"), NOT a mascot/wordmark brand pair (legacy — see retired note)
[ Empty states]         no work items, empty conversations views, empty Tests domains
[ Error states]         API 500 on a panel fetch → friendly error + retry (no crash); dead-origin recovery page
```
 ## 14. What “PASS” means [Section titled “14. What “PASS” means”](#14-what-pass-means) PASS only if **all of**: 1. The action was performed via verdict (clicks/fills, not curl). 2. The DOM after the action matches the documented expectation. 3. Backend state (where applicable) is corroborated via `curl` or the operator log. 4. No console errors with severity ≥ `error` were emitted by the action (run `verdict console error`). Anything else → `FAIL` or `INCONCLUSIVE`. Don’t report PASS without positive evidence — silence is not success. ### 14.1 Performance grading on the shared box (standing rule) [Section titled “14.1 Performance grading on the shared box (standing rule)”](#141-performance-grading-on-the-shared-box-standing-rule) Adopted by the owner 2026-06-11 from the load-sensitivity characterization (`papercup:e2e/perf-load-sensitivity-2026-06-11.md`, sampled over loadavg 9.5–48.6): 1. **Grade on medians (≥5 samples) at any load.** Medians proved load-insensitive (≤0.2ms shift quiet→heavy) — a median-based PASS/WARN/FAIL needs no loadavg gate. 2. **Never grade tails or single samples under load.** p90/max degrade up to \~25× under fleet load; any tail-based or single-sample FAIL taken at `load1 > ~24` must be re-sampled in a quiet window before filing. 3. **Record loadavg per sample** so grades are auditable. 4. Chat TTFT: grade the app-side split only (under 50ms); provider first-token inside the accepted 6.5–12.2s band is infra, not an app regression. ## 15. Common gotchas [Section titled “15. Common gotchas”](#15-common-gotchas) * **Verdict shares chromium with the human user.** Long click-and-wait sequences fail when the user is browsing. Run `verdict status` first. * **Sonner Toasts are lazy.** `[data-sonner-toaster]` only mounts when at least one toast is active. The empty `<section aria-label="Notifications alt+T">` is just the accessibility announcer. To assert a toast appeared, query `[data-sonner-toaster] li` *during* the action, not after the toast has timed out. * **Add-plugin enable is slow (3–9s).** No spinner. Wait for `curl /api/plugins/enabled` to reflect the change; don’t time out early. * **`/marketplace` URL behavior changed.** It now renders the Overview tab directly (4 tabs total: Overview, Templates, Plugins, Snapshots) — not a redirect to `/templates`. * **Stream parser unwrap.** Oracle stream events arrive as `{type:"stream_event", event:{type:"content_block_delta", delta:{...}}}` — parsing top-level `content_block_delta` silently drops every text token. (Already handled server-side; relevant if you’re writing a new SSE consumer.) * **Stale Vite parse cache.** If a JSX parse error references a line that doesn’t match the on-disk file, the cache is stale. `rm -rf apps/operator-vite/node_modules/.vite` and restart. (Next.js is retired — there is no `.next` cache anymore.) * **Harness tab nav uses `?panel=`.** `panel=plugin:<id>` selects a plugin-contributed tab. Test these the same way as built-in tabs. * **`tauri-agent-tools screenshot --selector` is flaky on tiny elements.** A short input (e.g. the operator composer at \~187×42 px) sometimes returns a 1×1 PNG. Workaround: `screenshot --title Papercusp -o full.png` then crop in ImageMagick using the rect from `eval "JSON.stringify($('input').getBoundingClientRect())"`. * **`ipc-monitor` is silent for the operator chat.** The composer sends via HTTP/SSE to `/api/agent-mcp/operator-converse`, not via Tauri IPC. Use `console-monitor`, `rust-logs`, or `curl /api/operator/conversations/<id>` to corroborate. `ipc-monitor` *is* the right tool for plugin/host wiring, workspace switching, and shell-sidecar calls. * **Bridge port is per-process.** `tauri-agent-tools probe` reports the live port (e.g. `34875`); restart the dev shell and the port changes. Always `probe` before scripting a sequence. * **Radix tabs (and other pointerdown-activated Radix widgets) ignore plain `click`.** A programmatic `el.click()` (or the bridge `click` verb) dispatches only a `click` event; Radix `Tabs` activate on *pointerdown*, so the tab looks clicked but selection and the nuqs `?tab=` param never change — and your test silently measures nothing. Dispatch the full sequence: `for (const t of ['pointerdown','mousedown','pointerup','mouseup','click']) el.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent(t,{bubbles:true,cancelable:true,view:window}))`. Plain anchors are fine with `click`. (Found 2026-06-10; cost a full battery round of invalid tab numbers.) * **Harness-panel tabs need a WARM single-pot context — and the PRs panel is NOT a standalone tab.** The per-pot tabs (`git`/`insights`/`docs`/ `testing`/`brainstorm`/`settings`, and the strip-hidden `prs`) render `AdvHarnessPanelPage` keyed on `?slug=<pot>` + `?scope=expanded` (NOT `all`). A COLD `location.href` straight to `?tab=git&slug=X` races the mount-time slug-restore and bounces you to `?tab=harnesses`. Two-step it: first load `?tab=harnesses&slug=X&scope=expanded` (warm projects + let the restore run), THEN switch to `?tab=git`. Critically, **`prs` is excluded from the visible tab strip** — there is no standalone PRs tab to deep-link or click. The live PR-review surface (PrsTab → recommendation chip, report panel, owner-gated auto-toggle) is auto-opened as a dock panel INSIDE the **Git tab** (`AdvGitDock` seeds git-graph + `adv:prs`). So to e2e the PR GUI, navigate to `tab=git` (a real strip tab), not `tab=prs`. (Found 2026-06-20 verifying PR-3; cost \~an hour targeting the vestigial `?tab=prs` route that the router never honors.) * **Close the Web Inspector before ANY memory or perf measurement.** All Tauri instances share one webview profile (`~/.local/share/com.papercusp.desktop`), and it restores the inspector OPEN from the last session. The inspector’s record buffers (its Network tab logs every SSE/API frame) grew \~1.9 GB across two nav batteries on 2026-06-10 and looked exactly like an app leak — closing it dropped RSS from 2.7 GB to 819 MB instantly. Latency numbers were unaffected; memory numbers with it open are garbage. * **Don’t measure under `tauri dev` on the shared dev box — launch the bare debug binary.** `tauri dev` watches `src-tauri/**`, and the fleet edits that tree continuously: a peer’s mid-flight Rust edit kills and rebuilds your app mid-test (and a peer’s compile error leaves you appless). Launch `./src-tauri/target/debug/papercusp-desktop` directly (the dev wrapper + bridge are compiled in) and pick the target via the build-switcher rail or a devUrl-restored URL. * **Wayland trap: a bare `DISPLAY=:9X` launch can land on the owner’s desktop.** GTK prefers Wayland when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set, so the isolated-Xvfb recipe silently opens the window on the live seat (focus-steal). Always launch with `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY GDK_BACKEND=x11 DISPLAY=:9X …`. * **`screenshot` verb may demand sway/grim** (it probes the host platform, not your X11 instance). Fallback that always works on an Xvfb display: `WID=$(DISPLAY=:9X xdotool search --name Papercusp | tail -1); DISPLAY=:9X import -window $WID shot.png`. * **`operator-converse` trigger enum.** When poking `/api/agent-mcp/operator-converse` directly, `trigger` must be one of `user_message | quiet_wait_resume | open_canvas | user_says_ready | user_welcomed | continue` — anything else streams a single `event: error` frame (`invalid_args`) and closes. ### 15.4 Xvfb / xdotool / OCR fallback cookbook [Section titled “15.4 Xvfb / xdotool / OCR fallback cookbook”](#154-xvfb--xdotool--ocr-fallback-cookbook) The bridge covers 99% of cases. Reach for this stack only when: * You’re on a **release build** (the bridge is `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`). * You’re on **macOS** and the bridge isn’t compiled in for that target yet. * You need to verify **visual** behavior the DOM can’t express (animation timing, font rendering, paint-order glitches). * The Tauri process **crashed** and you need forensics on the dead window (use `tauri-agent-tools diagnose` first; this is a deeper fallback). Bare `Xvfb` has no GPU/GL — WebKitGTK won’t paint → every screenshot is blank A plain `Xvfb` is a **software framebuffer with no DRI3/GL** (you’ll see `libEGL warning: DRI3 error: Could not get DRI3 device` in the app log). WebKitGTK’s accelerated compositor then **never paints the webview to that framebuffer, so every screenshot comes back uniformly blank white regardless of what the DOM actually contains** — a render-environment artifact that looks exactly like a broken/blank app. The DOM is fine; the pixels just never render. (This burned \~hours in the desktop-ipc Phase-4 smoke before it was spotted: the “blank window” was the GL-less Xvfb, not the app.) **Get real GPU GL one of two ways:** 1. **Run on `:0`** (the real GPU X server): `DISPLAY=:0 …`. Simplest, but puts a window on the operator’s actual screen (focus-steal — see §0). 2. **VirtualGL on an isolated Xvfb** (no focus-steal, real GPU) — *recommended.* `vglrun` routes GL to the GPU’s EGL render node while the app displays to the isolated Xvfb. **Always confirm real GL first** — it must report the GPU, not `llvmpipe`/`swrast`: 
   ```sh
   DISPLAY=:90 vglrun -d egl0 glxinfo | grep -i "OpenGL renderer"
   # → OpenGL renderer string: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090/...   (good)
   # → ...llvmpipe / swrast                                  (still software — wrong)
   ```
 VirtualGL isn’t in Ubuntu apt; install the GitHub release once: 
   ```sh
   curl -sSL -o /tmp/vgl.deb \
     https://github.com/VirtualGL/virtualgl/releases/download/3.1.4/virtualgl_3.1.4_amd64.deb
   sudo dpkg -i /tmp/vgl.deb
   ```
 Use `-d egl0` — the EGL **device index**. Do NOT pass the `/dev/dri/renderD128` path; VGL rejects it (“Invalid EGL device”). Recipe — isolated **GPU-accelerated** instance via VirtualGL (no focus-steal): 
```sh
Xvfb :90 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 -nolisten tcp &  echo $! > /tmp/xvfb90.pid
DISPLAY=:90 openbox &                            echo $! > /tmp/openbox90.pid
# Sanity — must be the real GPU, not llvmpipe:
DISPLAY=:90 vglrun -d egl0 glxinfo | grep -i "OpenGL renderer"
# Launch the app UNDER vglrun so WebKitGTK composites on the GPU:
( cd papercusp-desktop && env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY GDK_BACKEND=x11 DISPLAY=:90 \
    vglrun -d egl0 npm run dev ) > /tmp/tauri-xvfb.log 2>&1 &  echo $! > /tmp/tauri-xvfb.pid
# ⚠ Wayland trap: without `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY GDK_BACKEND=x11` GTK may pick
# the live Wayland seat and open the window on the OWNER'S desktop, ignoring :90.
# ⚠ On the shared dev box prefer the BARE binary over `npm run dev` — the tauri-dev
# watcher restarts/kills your app whenever the fleet edits src-tauri/** (see §15):
#   env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY GDK_BACKEND=x11 DISPLAY=:90 vglrun -d egl0 \
#     ./src-tauri/target/debug/papercusp-desktop > /tmp/tauri-xvfb.log 2>&1 &
# wait for window
until DISPLAY=:90 xdotool search --name Papercusp > /dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done
# The bridge binds an EPHEMERAL port (Server::http("127.0.0.1:0") in
# src-tauri/src/dev_bridge.rs) — there is NO PAPERCUSP_BRIDGE_PORT env var.
# Read the real port/token from /tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-<pid>.token, or just
# `tauri-agent-tools probe` (pass --pid to disambiguate this instance).
WID=$(DISPLAY=:90 xdotool search --name Papercusp | head -1)
DISPLAY=:90 xdotool type --window $WID "hello"; DISPLAY=:90 xdotool key --window $WID Return
DISPLAY=:90 import -window $WID /tmp/shot.png    # ← now shows REAL content, not blank
convert /tmp/shot.png -crop 1280x80+0+460 /tmp/band.png; tesseract /tmp/band.png - 2>/dev/null
```
 Cleanup: `kill $(cat /tmp/tauri-xvfb.pid /tmp/openbox90.pid /tmp/xvfb90.pid) 2>/dev/null`. For a **release build** (no dev bridge) screenshots are your *only* window introspection — so GPU GL via VirtualGL is **mandatory** there, or the screenshot tells you nothing. On a **debug** build the bridge is still up on the isolated instance — find it with `tauri-agent-tools probe --pid <pid>` or the `/tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-<pid>.token` file (the port is ephemeral; there is **no** `PAPERCUSP_BRIDGE_PORT` env var). Prefer the bridge for DOM/JS (it reads the DOM, not pixels, so it works even GL-less) and use this VirtualGL stack only for the pixels. ### 15.5 Driving React-controlled inputs via the bridge [Section titled “15.5 Driving React-controlled inputs via the bridge”](#155-driving-react-controlled-inputs-via-the-bridge) Setting a controlled `<select>`/`<input>` value through `eval` with the classic native-setter + `dispatchEvent(new Event('change'))` trick **silently fails** on this app (React 19: there is no `_valueTracker` on the node to reset, so React’s value tracking dedupes the event and the controlled value snaps back). No error, no state change — your “Start” button stays disabled and the test looks like an app bug. What works: call the component’s own handler through the React props expando on the DOM node (verified live, WI-125 verification 2026-06-11): 
```js
// the expando key carries a per-bundle hash — discover it, don't hardcode it
const el = document.querySelector('[data-testid="adv-chat-pick"]');
const propsKey = Object.keys(el).find((k) => k.startsWith('__reactProps$'));
el[propsKey].onChange({ target: { value: 'WI-62' } });   // updates React state
// then drive the dependent control the same way:
const btn = document.querySelector('[data-testid="adv-chat-start"]');
btn[Object.keys(btn).find((k) => k.startsWith('__reactProps$'))].onClick();
```
 Plain `.click()` on buttons works fine (React listens natively for clicks) — the expando path is only needed for **value-tracked** inputs. Also remember a value injected this way bypasses UI constraints: only pass values the real control could produce (e.g. an option that exists in the select), or you are testing a state the user can never reach. ## 16. Driving the zellij `pui` chat dock (the Sentinel / Queen TUIs) [Section titled “16. Driving the zellij pui chat dock (the Sentinel / Queen TUIs)”](#16-driving-the-zellij-pui-chat-dock-the-sentinel--queen-tuis) Everything above drives the **Tauri webview**. The desktop ALSO opens a *second* window: a **ghostty terminal running a zellij `pui` dock** — the live agent TUIs (owner directive 2026-06-11: “every agent chat is a LIVE TUI”). This is where the **Sentinel chat** and the **Queen** actually run for the user. `tauri-agent-tools` **cannot see it** (it’s not the webview) — drive it with `zellij action` + window screenshots instead. ### 16.1 What’s in the dock [Section titled “16.1 What’s in the dock”](#161-whats-in-the-dock) Launched by `ghostty … -e pui chat`, which starts a zellij session from `~/.papercusp/pui-chat-dock.kdl` (three tabs: `this hive` / `network` / `plans`). The `this hive` tab stacks: | Pane | Command it runs | What it is | | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 👁 overwatch | `pui brain-view --overwatch` | read-only live transcript | | ♛ queen | `pui brain-view --queen` | the Queen’s brain transcript (read-only) | | ♛✉ prompt / ⏸ wakes / ✉ mail / ☑ work | `pui {prompt,wake,mail,work}-pane --queen` | Queen control panes | | **🛡 sentinel** | **`psu --no-picker --agent=claude --role=operator`** | **the Sentinel chat — a Claude Code session acting as the operator, voiced via ElevenLabs** | | colony | `pui dock-driver` | reactively appends one `claude --resume` TUI per live bee | | ⏸ wakes | `pui wake-pane` | fleet-wide wake board | > ⚠ **The Sentinel chat is a `psu`/Claude-Code TUI — NOT the `apps/tui` (`pui`) ratatui converse client.** They are different surfaces; don’t conflate “the TUI chat” with `apps/tui`. (The `apps/tui` ratatui is a separate interactive converse client; it is not what this dock’s sentinel pane runs.) ### 16.2 Find the session + window [Section titled “16.2 Find the session + window”](#162-find-the-session--window) 
```sh
zellij ls                                    # → pui-dock-<pid> (the live one; ignore "EXITED")
DISPLAY=:0 wmctrl -l | grep pui-dock         # → ghostty window id (title "pui-dock-… | 🛡 sentinel")
```
 ### 16.3 Observe — read-only, always safe [Section titled “16.3 Observe — read-only, always safe”](#163-observe--read-only-always-safe) 
```sh
# text of the FOCUSED pane (strip ANSI for grepping):
zellij -s pui-dock-<pid> action dump-screen | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g'
# the whole dock (all panes) as the faithful "what the user sees":
DISPLAY=:0 import -window <window-id> /tmp/dock.png
```
 `dump-screen` captures only the **focused** pane (no path arg in this zellij — it writes to stdout). To read another pane, focus it (16.4) first, or use the window screenshot (which shows the whole stack). ### 16.4 Interact — ⚠ these are LIVE agents [Section titled “16.4 Interact — ⚠ these are LIVE agents”](#164-interact---these-are-live-agents) 
```sh
zellij -s pui-dock-<pid> action write-chars "your message"  # types into the FOCUSED pane's composer
zellij -s pui-dock-<pid> action write 13                    # Enter (submit)
zellij -s pui-dock-<pid> action write 127                   # Backspace
zellij -s pui-dock-<pid> action move-focus down             # move focus between panes
```
 * **Writes hit the FOCUSED pane** — confirm focus with `dump-screen` before typing (the 🛡 sentinel pane is `focus=true` in the layout, so it’s usually it). * **Render race:** a `write-chars` immediately followed by `dump-screen` often doesn’t show the text yet (the terminal hasn’t repainted). Re-dump, or space the `zellij action` calls out (each CLI call is a round-trip, which usually suffices). For a non-destructive smoke test, type a marker and delete it with `write 127` — **without** Enter — then confirm via `dump-screen`. * **Enter submits a real turn** to a real Claude-Code operator/Queen — it will act on it. Never drive the user’s live panes while they’re working without permission. * Dock keybinds differ from stock zellij (set in the layout): **Tab** = fullscreen the focused pane (not prompt-complete), **Alt+↑/↓** = scroll the agent stack, **↑/↓** = forwarded to the pane as cursor up/down. ### 16.5 What you can’t verify headlessly right now [Section titled “16.5 What you can’t verify headlessly right now”](#165-what-you-cant-verify-headlessly-right-now) * A **brain reply** (Sentinel/Queen) needs LLM capacity. If the account pool is rate-starved (every account in a 429 cooldown — surfaced as `[infra-liveness] all N LLM pool account(s) paused` escalations in the operator conversation), the panes render but won’t answer. Verify *rendering* now; defer *reply*-verification until capacity returns. * A pane only shows the Phase-2 `apps/tui` cards if it’s running the `apps/tui` ratatui (and a freshly-built `pui` binary) — **not** the `psu`/Claude-Code sentinel pane above. Check the running binary’s mtime vs the build, and the pane’s launch command, before concluding “cards work in the TUI.”

# Coordination system — adversarial test coverage matrix

Why this exists **EI-152** and **EI-153** — two real coordination bugs — shipped *past 27 green wake-executor tests*. Both escaped for the same reason: the existing suite was **single-agent unit tests with the real seams mocked**. They asserted the happy path but never **cross-agent isolation**, the **real socket / resume / config seams**, or **multi-session concurrency**. This matrix is the coverage map for the adversarial suite that closes those classes (plan `coordination-test-suite-2026-06-08`). It lists every failure-mode cell, whether it was covered before, and where it is covered now — **no silent gaps** (a silent gap is exactly what shipped EI-152). ## The four test classes that were missing [Section titled “The four test classes that were missing”](#the-four-test-classes-that-were-missing) | Class | What it asserts | Would have caught | | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | | **C1 — Cross-agent isolation (adversarial)** | For *every* channel (wake, `coord:send`, inbox, presence, locks, work-item claims): A’s traffic **cannot** reach or affect B. | EI-153 | | **C2 — Real-seam integration** | The **real** socket inject, the **real** resume (isolated config dir), the **real** PG — not mocked deps. | EI-152 + EI-153 | | **C3 — Multi-session concurrency** | N live isolated sessions; concurrent wakes / sends / claims / locks → no **lost / duplicated / misrouted** delivery. | both | | **C4 — Liveness/lifecycle matrix** | Every (alive / exited / stale / pid-reuse / no-pid / ended) × (handle? / live-socket?) → the **correct** outcome. | EI-152 | | **C5 — Identity invariants** | `PAPERCUSP_SID` / coord ownerId / config-dir correct across launch **and** resume; zero identity/conversation bleed. | EI-153 | | **C6 — Idempotency / coalescing / retry** | Re-arm idempotency; coalescing windows; retry/backoff; no duplicate deliveries; `once=false` standing semantics. | — | ## The keystone [Section titled “The keystone”](#the-keystone) `packages/operator-core/test/_multi-session-testbed.ts` — `MultiSessionTestbed` mints N genuinely-isolated sessions (own coord identity + own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` / `CODEX_HOME` + on-demand own live control socket in an **isolated discovery dir**) and drives every channel against them. Every C1/C3 cell reuses it. The isolated `psuPtyDir` both protects the live fleet’s `~/.papercusp/psu-pty` and is how a test proves `findLiveHost(A)` never returns B’s socket. ## Failure-mode matrix [Section titled “Failure-mode # P-079 runbook — live bidirectional federation acceptance

> **Webapp retired.** Every `localhost:3055`/`localhost:3070` URL here is only reachable while the **Tauri dev shell** is running (`cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev`). Drive the operator through the Tauri shell, not a browser (see [Agent E2E playbook](/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e)). This is the acceptance test for Phase-1b bidirectional federation: two **different** GitHub engineers join/share a harness and sync state **both ways** over the Model B Hyperswarm substrate. It is the gate that closes implementation **Open-Risk R-1** (see below) — the one thing that cannot be asserted offline. Design: `apps/operator/docs/plans/papercusp-phase1b-bidirectional-federation-2026-06-01.md` (now **superseded** — admission moved off the shared-repo contributor file). The deterministic offline proof (module + transport, gate stubbed) already exists at `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/__tests__/two-peer-swarm-bidi.test.ts`; this runbook covers what that test *can’t*: the real GitHub publish→verify loop with two real identities. R-1 — RESOLVED: channel-2(c) anchors on gist ownership, not a verified commit **Historical:** the original design required the contributor-file *commit* to be GitHub-**verified** (`commit.verification.verified === true`). A live probe found Contents-API commits come back **unverified** (`reason: unsigned`) in the real gh-token context, so that check was unsatisfiable and would have blocked **all** admission. **R-1 is resolved** by re-anchoring on **gist ownership**: the signed announce carries the `attestation_gist_id`, and `verifyAttestation` checks that gist is **owned by the claimed `github_user_id`** (GitHub reports `gist.owner.id`), attests the announced `device_pubkey`, and carries a valid device Ed25519 signature. No commit-verification is required anywhere. (The later write-free-join work removed the contributor-file commit path entirely, so this anchor is now the *only* gate.) The 2026-06-01 live run above confirms the gist-ownership anchor works with two real identities. ## Two modes [Section titled “Two modes”](#two-modes) * **Mode A — same laptop, two instances (Q-2 surrogate, do this FIRST).** Catches *code* bugs. Two operator instances with fully isolated state + two distinct GitHub accounts. Cheap, fast, repeatable. * **Mode B — two real machines.** Catches *network* bugs (NAT, firewall, DHT reachability). Run only after Mode A passes. The **decision rule** (from `papercusp-dogfood-phase11-multi-engineer-dogfood-2026-05-26`): **P-079 PASSES when ≥5 of the 7 walkthrough steps land within 30 s of the user action** — AND the two hard gates hold: (i) both peers’ attestation **gists** are owned by their claimed GitHub id (channel-2(c) holds), (ii) data flows **both** directions. ## Prerequisites (both modes) [Section titled “Prerequisites (both modes)”](#prerequisites-both-modes) * Two **distinct** GitHub accounts (call them **Alice** and **Bob**), each with access to a shared test repo (use a throwaway repo, not a production one). Any real GitHub identity is admissible — there is **no** repo-collaborator gate at the substrate; GitHub’s own write/branch-protection rules gate the actual PR merge. So Alice and Bob each just need to be real, `gh`-authenticated GitHub users — join is **write-free**, so neither needs push access to the repo (only read, to clone the harness). * Each side authenticated: `gh auth status` shows the intended account (Alice on her instance, Bob on his). The join/share flow resolves identity **server-side** from this — you do **not** type credentials into the UI. ### Mode A — isolating two instances on one laptop [Section titled “Mode A — isolating two instances on one laptop”](#mode-a--isolating-two-instances-on-one-laptop) Each instance needs its **own**: workspace root (→ its own per-harness corestore), Postgres database, `gh` identity, and Tauri bridge port. Run the second instance under its own Xvfb display so it never steals your focus (see [Agent E2E §15.4](/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e)): 
```sh
# Instance B (Bob) — isolated display and gh config (the dev bridge binds its
# own ephemeral port per instance — discover it with
# `tauri-agent-tools probe --pid <pid>` or /tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-<pid>.token)
Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 -nolisten tcp &
DISPLAY=:99 openbox &
DISPLAY=:99 \
  GH_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/gh-bob \
  PAPERCUSP_HOME=/tmp/papercusp-bob \
  bash -lc 'cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev'
# (gh auth login --hostname github.com  with GH_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/gh-bob, as Bob, beforehand)
```
 Instance A (Alice) is your normal `papercusp-desktop && npm run dev` on `:0`. Point each instance’s operator at a **separate** PG database (distinct `DATABASE_URL` / embedded-pg dir) so “Alice’s PG” and “Bob’s PG” are observably different — that is what makes “data crossed the wire” verifiable. ## The 7-step walkthrough [Section titled “The 7-step walkthrough”](#the-7-step-walkthrough) 1. **Alice shares the harness.** Sharing is now **hive-level**: in Alice’s Tauri shell, share the hive via the **Share-Hive** form (`PublishHiveCard` / `ShareHiveDialog` — the old per-harness `ShareWizard` and its share-finalize/binding-resolve/cupboard-publish routes were retired in `comb-retire-per-harness-sharing-2026-06-11`). This **publishes Alice’s attestation gist** (no shared-repo contributor file is written — the gist id rides Alice’s signed announce), boots Alice’s substrate (joins the swarm topic derived from the repo id) and announces. Note the **hive invite** (`papercusp://hive` link) to send to contributors. 2. **Confirm Alice’s binding: an owned attestation gist (the admission gate).** There is **no** `user/<id>` contributor branch under the write-free model — the binding is the attestation gist carried on Alice’s signed announce. Take the `attestation_gist_id` Alice announced (visible in her boot-history / substrate diagnostic) and confirm the gist exists and is **owned by Alice’s account** (the `verifyAttestation` anchor — `gist.owner.id === github_user_id`; no commit-verification is involved): 
   ```sh
   # confirm that gist's owner id === Alice's github user id
   gh api gists/<gist_id> --jq '.owner.id, .owner.login'
   # expect:  <alice_id>   <alice_login>
   ```
 **If the gist is missing or owned by a different id, `verifyAttestation` won’t admit** — see *Troubleshooting*. 3. **Bob joins via the link.** In Bob’s shell, paste Alice’s link to join. The create-harness picker has **no discrete “harness link” entry** — its entries are New local directory, Existing local repo, Search GitHub or enter URL, Start a work hive, Search the Comb (blueprint), Browse the Comb, and Hive invite (`papercusp://hive`). Harness-link join (`POST /api/harness/join-link`) is reached through the GitHub-search / Comb hive flow (`EntryGithubUrlForm`); a `papercusp://hive` invite goes through the Hive-invite card. Bob’s identity is resolved server-side from his `gh` auth (no creds typed). Watch the join progress through the 6 steps: `oauth_attest → clone_repo → publish_binding → boot_federate → await_admission_merge → route_insights`. `publish_binding` performs **no repo write** (write-free) — it just carries forward Bob’s attestation gist id, so there is no `user/<bob_id>` file to re-check; instead repeat the Step-2 gist-ownership check against the `attestation_gist_id` **Bob** announced. * If join returns **“GitHub authentication required”**, Bob’s `gh` isn’t authenticated in that instance’s `GH_CONFIG_DIR` — fix and retry. 4. **Bob admits Alice (publisher→joiner).** On Bob’s `/admin/dogfood-substrate` (or the boot-history), expect an `announce_admitted` for Alice’s device pubkey within \~30 s. `announce_pending` is fine transiently (GitHub propagation) — it self-heals via the retry; `announce_rejected` is a failure (inspect the reason). 5. **Alice admits Bob (joiner→publisher).** Symmetric: Alice’s boot-history shows `announce_admitted` for Bob within \~30 s. 6. **Alice → Bob data flow.** Alice creates/edits a feature in the shared harness. It appears in **Bob’s** queue (Bob’s PG / Bob’s harness UI) within \~30 s. 7. **Bob → Alice data flow.** Bob creates/edits a feature. It appears in **Alice’s** queue within \~30 s. (Bonus: have both claim the same feature to exercise the LWW advisory claim + clobber-toast.) ## Pass criteria [Section titled “Pass criteria”](#pass-criteria) * **Hard gate 1 — channel-2 anchor:** both contributors’ attestation **gists** (Steps 2 + 3) exist and are **owned by the claimed `github_user_id`** (so `verifyAttestation` returns valid). *Non-negotiable.* (This replaces the obsolete “verified commit” gate — see the R-1 Aside; no commit-verification is required.) * **Hard gate 2 — bidirectional:** Steps 6 **and** 7 both succeed (data crosses in *both* directions, into *separate* PGs). * **Soft gate:** ≥5 of the 7 steps land within 30 s of the triggering action. Record each failing step as a P-027-style observation on `F-DOGFOOD-001` (per the Phase-11 plan). ## Inspecting state [Section titled “Inspecting state”](#inspecting-state) * **Boot/admission events:** `/admin/dogfood-substrate` (substrate diagnostic), or `GET /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-boot-history`. Kinds: `peer_connected`, `announce_admitted`, `announce_pending`, `announce_rejected`, `announce_error`, `peer_revoked`, `merge_error`. * **Health:** `GET /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-health` (idle = `harnesses:[]`, `worstVerdict:'healthy'`). * **Replicated rows:** query each instance’s Postgres for the harness’s feature queue / contributor tables (the read-merge projects admitted peers’ ops there). ## Troubleshooting [Section titled “Troubleshooting”](#troubleshooting) * **`announce_rejected` with `binding_invalid`** → `verifyAttestation` couldn’t verify the peer’s binding. Most likely the peer’s **attestation gist is missing or owned by a different GitHub id** (`gist.owner.id !== github_user_id`), or the `device_pubkey` in the gist doesn’t match the announced key (e.g. a multi-device collision — same login on two machines). Note: a deleted gist surfaces at runtime as `gist_not_found`, which the adapter maps to `'fail'` and `reverifyAdmitted` treats as the **owner/self revocation signal** (the peer is dropped). (The `channel2_attestation_missing` identifier is only a leftover enum member from the removed `verifyBoth` runtime — it does not name the live signal.) * **Stuck `announce_pending`** → GitHub hasn’t propagated the just-pushed file yet; it self-heals within the 30-min grace. If it never clears, the file/branch is missing or the API read is failing. * **No `peer_connected` at all** → swarm/DHT reachability (Mode B: NAT/firewall on the DHT port). Confirm both booted with a non-null `swarm` and the **same** `topicHex`. * **Federation only one way** → the silent side’s binding isn’t verifiable by the other (re-check that side’s Step-2 gist-ownership, and that the announced `device_pubkey` matches the gist body). Attestation gists are **public**, so no repo-read access is needed to verify — but if the gist is unreachable the verify call throws and the binding sits `pending` rather than `fail`. ## Revocation [Section titled “Revocation”](#revocation) Two levers, both consistent with the write-free model (the old “delete the `user/<id>` branch” lever is a silent no-op now, and deleting another user’s gist is infeasible): * **Owner revocation** — `revokeContributorViaGithub` (gated on GitHub repo-**admin** authority) unions the target’s device pubkeys into the **owner’s own** contributor-row `revoked_pubkeys` and federates it. Read-admission unions `revoked_pubkeys` across all contributor rows, so every peer honors it. * **Self-revocation** — the contributor deletes its own attestation gist; the next verify returns `gist_not_found` → `'fail'` → `reverifyAdmitted` drops the peer. Either path records a `peer_revoked` entry in the boot-history. ## Escalation — channel-2 gist anchor (R-1 history) [Section titled “Escalation — channel-2 gist anchor (R-1 history)”](#escalation--channel-2-gist-anchor-r-1-history) R-1 was the worry that channel-2(c) required a GitHub-**verified commit**, which a live probe showed is unsatisfiable (Contents-API commits return `verified:false / reason:unsigned`). **That risk is closed:** channel-2(c) now anchors on **gist ownership** (`verifyAttestation`: `gist.owner.id === claimed github_user_id` + device-pubkey match + Ed25519 sig), which needs no commit verification and is confirmed live (2026-06-01, two real identities). If a future change reintroduced a commit-verification dependency, the same escalation ladder would apply (GitHub App commit signing → registered GPG/SSH key → documented relaxation) — but it does not apply today. A reliability gotcha the live run found: the attestation **gist filename** must use the URL/filename-safe base64 alphabet — a raw base64 pubkey prefix contains `/` (\~11% of keys), which GitHub rejects as a gist filename. Fixed in `attestationGistFilename` (`ae5e25be3`); the regression test pins it. After this passes, the longer **P-080 soak** (Alice + Bob each use Papercusp for ≥5 consecutive working days on the harness) is the next acceptance milestone.

# Production release checklist (v1)

This page is the operational **release gate checklist for v1** — what must be green before `:3070` is trusted as production-ready, and which lanes are knowingly excluded and why. It complements the design/strategy doc at [`testing/index`](./index); this page is the narrower “is v1 actually ready” verdict, produced by `production-test-readiness-2026-07-06` (P-007). v1 scope, not v2 Per owner decision D-001 (2026-07-06, `production-test-readiness-2026-07-06`): **v1 explicitly excludes p2p/shared-hive/federation** — that whole testing lane is deferred to v2. A green v1 gate verdict means “v1 is ready,” not “every test in the repo passes.” The excluded lanes are itemized below with their filed v2 de-quarantine follow-ups. ## 1. What must be green for a v1 release [Section titled “1. What must be green for a v1 release”](#1-what-must-be-green-for-a-v1-release) The **green-checkpoint gate** (`apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.ts`, driven on an hourly tick; manually fireable via `release:checkpoint-run`) is the single verdict. It runs the full affected/nightly test surface and applies the file-level quarantine filter (`quarantine.txt`) before deciding green/red. A v1 release requires: 1. **The gate’s own verdict is green** (`release:deploy { op: 'status' }` → `gate.green: true`, `consecutiveReds` resetting to 0). Never force-deploy past a red gate for a real release (`op: 'force'` is the audited, owner-gated escape hatch for the rare no-users-window case only — see the CLAUDE.md “gate is everyone’s job” section). 2. **The green pin has advanced past the release commit** — `deploy.greenPinSha` includes the commit you intend to ship; `dev:pipeline_position` confirms `committed → staging → main (gate green) → deployed`. 3. **`:3070` is actually running that pin** — `deploy.deployedSha === deploy.greenPinSha` (or trigger `release:deploy { op: 'trigger', confirm: true }` to promote a green-but-stalled pin). 4. **Core canonical-framework suites pass** (see §2) — Vitest unit + integration, Playwright E2E critical-journey specs, the Cargo/Rust native suite (desktop shell), and the LLM scenario suite’s *behavioral* findings (not its historical error-burst noise — see WI-3203). 5. **The artifact drill is current** — a `.deb` built from the release commit boots clean on a fresh VM and preserves data across an upgrade (see §4). Re-run this per release, not just once. 6. **No un-triaged flaky-test candidates** — `testing:flakiness` (14d window) returns an empty auto-quarantine candidate list, or any candidates are quarantined accountably with a de-quarantine follow-up filed (see §3). ## 2. Signal sources and what they cover [Section titled “2. Signal sources and what they cover”](#2-signal-sources-and-what-they-cover) | Source | What it proves | How to check | | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Vitest unit + integration | Per-package correctness; the bulk of the suite | `npm run test:affected[:integration]`, or the gate’s full nightly run | | Playwright (`apps/operator/e2e/*.spec.ts`) | Critical user journeys inside the Tauri shell: boot, pot/harness create, work-items flow, tests tab, deploy/admin-git, chat (WI-3204 audit) | Tests tab, or `npx playwright test` | | Cargo (`#[cfg(test)]`, desktop shell) | Rust/Tauri native suite — \~203 test fns across `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri` | Wired into `harness_shared.test_runs` (framework=`cargo`) since WI-3228/P-009; previously **zero** cargo signal existed | | LLM scenario suite | Operator/Sentinel behavioral regressions under judged conversation scenarios | `harness_shared.llm_test_runs` / `llm_test_findings` — triaged 2026-07-06 (WI-3203); see the two active findings below | | Artifact drill | The actual shipped `.deb` boots + upgrades correctly, not just “tests pass in-tree” | Manual VM drill, see §4 | | Backup/restore drill | A real restore recovers a populated workspace | Manual drill, see §4 | ### Known active (non-blocking) findings from the LLM scenario triage (WI-3203) [Section titled “Known active (non-blocking) findings from the LLM scenario triage (WI-3203)”](#known-active-non-blocking-findings-from-the-llm-scenario-triage-wi-3203) * **WI-3229** (major) — delta-merge staleness: the operator/Sentinel can show removed rows as still-current or stale pre-update titles after a list delta. Filed, not yet fixed as of this checklist’s writing — track before calling the chat/converse surface fully hardened. * **WI-3230** (minor) — a “banned pattern” scenario assert false-positives on quoted/discussed forbidden terms (assert-quality bug, not a SUT regression). ## 3. Excluded lanes (v1 scope cut) — `quarantine.txt` [Section titled “3. Excluded lanes (v1 scope cut) — quarantine.txt”](#3-excluded-lanes-v1-scope-cut--quarantinetxt) These file patterns are excluded from the v1 green-checkpoint **verdict** (failures still run and are logged, just don’t hold the gate red). Each has a filed, owned v2 follow-up — a quarantine here is never silent: | Pattern(s) | Lane | v2 de-quarantine follow-up | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `@papercusp/operator-core::lib/sync/hyperbee/**` | p2p sync/hyperbee | WI-3240 | | `@papercusp/operator-core::lib/shared-hive-loop/**` | shared-hive loop | WI-3241 | | `@papercusp/operator-core::lib/p2p/**`, `lib/deployment/p2p-perf-tier3/**`, `lib/**/*p2p*.test.ts`, `lib/**/*federation*.test.ts`, `lib/**/dogfood-substrate*.test.ts`, `lib/**/substrate*.test.ts` | p2p/substrate/federation (operator-core) | WI-3242 | | `@papercusp/p2p-voice::src/**`, `@papercusp/pubsub-substrate::src/**` | generic p2p-voice / pubsub-substrate libs | WI-3243 | | `@papercupai/operator::apps/operator/e2e/voice-mode.spec.ts` | Known-red harness limitation (NumField blur-commit + ipcFetch transport not reliably assertable headless); feature verified working via direct API | Not v2-scoped — pre-existing headless-assertion gap, see the test’s own comment | This is implemented as a **file-level** filter in `green-checkpoint.ts` (`applyTestQuarantine` / `parseTestQuarantine`), not a whole-workspace exclusion — `@papercusp/operator-core` still holds the gate for every non-matching file. Encoded + tested in WI-3210/P-012 (96/96 focused tests green). ## 4. Manual operational drills (per release, not just once) [Section titled “4. Manual operational drills (per release, not just once)”](#4-manual-operational-drills-per-release-not-just-once) These prove the *shipped artifact* behaves, not just the in-tree test suite: * **Artifact fresh-install + upgrade (WI-3208)**: build the `.deb`, install on a clean VM (hive auto-wire disabled — p2p is v2, don’t join production swarm topics from a test frame, cf WI-1423), verify cold first-boot green (embedded PG boots, all migrations apply from empty, sidecar + webview up, no STARTUP VALIDATION errors), then install over a populated data dir and verify migrations apply and data survives. Last run: `.deb` sha256 `1213d1ba0d2556b0bea70fc43107c2c55d0ad045c06c5d7f5b9ff93749c0f2ed`; 403 migrations through 525; sentinel row preserved across reinstall. * **Backup/restore round-trip (WI-3207)**: snapshot a populated workspace (kopia), restore into a clean environment, boot, verify plans/work-items/ settings intact. Last run: staging snapshot `53191` / kopia `57da08e7ced063167af3f591d6469455e...`; strict temp-DB restore/import checklist passed; fixes committed in `7ee61c4e5a62`. * **Perf/stability soak (P-010, WI-3209 — in progress as of this checklist)**: a bounded (>=2h) soak under agent load asserting on `loop_lag_p95_ms` / `rss_mb` ledger columns for RSS growth + event-loop-lag thresholds, plus a cold-boot-time assertion. **Not yet complete** — the perf-field producers are fixed and live-smoked, but the full >=2h window had not finished collecting as of this writing. Do not treat a release as fully soak-verified until WI-3209 passes. ## 5. Before you cut a release — the actual sequence [Section titled “5. Before you cut a release — the actual sequence”](#5-before-you-cut-a-release--the-actual-sequence) 1. `release:deploy { op: 'status' }` — read the gate + deploy state fresh. If red, fix the reds (even out of your lane) or quarantine accountably; never force past a red gate for a real release. 2. If gate is green but stalled, `release:deploy { op: 'trigger', confirm: true }` to promote it. 3. Confirm `deploy.deployedSha === deploy.greenPinSha` and that pin is at or after your release commit. 4. Re-run the artifact drill (§4) against the release commit if it’s been more than a few days since the last drill — a green gate doesn’t substitute for a fresh install/upgrade proof. 5. Check `testing:flakiness` for new auto-quarantine candidates since the last release; triage per §1.9 of [`testing/index`](./index). 6. Cut the release. Record the gate SHA, deploy SHA, and drill evidence on the release work-item/plan for the audit trail. ## 6. Most recent verified gate + deploy (2026-07-06, P-007) [Section titled “6. Most recent verified gate + deploy (2026-07-06, P-007)”](#6-most-recent-verified-gate--deploy-2026-07-06-p-007) * Fresh green-checkpoint run fired manually (`release:checkpoint-run`) after Phases 1-2 landed → **gate went green** (`consecutiveReds: 0`), green pin advanced to `8abf9cd2ab48686f8549136b4693af820efa112c`. * `release:deploy { op: 'trigger', confirm: true }` promoted the pin; deploy steps (swap/preflight/migrate/restart/health/verify-paths/ broadcast) all `ok: true`. * Confirmed `deploy.deployedSha === deploy.greenPinSha` and `:3070` serving live (`GET /api/harness/papercusp/status` responds 200 with current harness state). * State right after: `staging-buffered` (a few more staging commits awaiting the next tick) — expected, not an error.

# Visual regression — Storybook + Lost Pixel

This page is the operational guide to Phase 4 of the testing framework (see [`testing/index`](./index)). Stories are the test cases; a diff against the committed baseline is the assertion. ## TL;DR [Section titled “TL;DR”](#tldr) 
```bash
# Local — verify your branch hasn't drifted
npm run lostpixel --workspace libs/generic/ui-primitives


# Local — regenerate baselines (intentional change only)
npm run lostpixel:update --workspace libs/generic/ui-primitives


# CI — runs automatically on `run-visual` PR label or push to main
```
 ## What’s covered today [Section titled “What’s covered today”](#whats-covered-today) | Package | Stories | Baselines | Storybook port | | ---------------------------------- | ------------ | --------- | -------------- | | `libs/generic/ui-primitives` | 6 components | 33 PNGs | `:6006` | | `libs/marketplace-public-ui` | 3 components | 14 PNGs | `:6007` | | `libs/agent-chat` | 2 components | 7 PNGs | `:6008` | | `apps/operator` | 3 components | 10 PNGs | `:6009` | | `libs/generic/papergrid/grid-core` | 1 component | 5 PNGs | `:6009` ⚠ | `libs/generic/papergrid/grid-core` is fully wired **locally** (its own `.storybook/`, `lostpixel.config.ts` at threshold `0.05`, one `RichGrid.stories.tsx`, 5 committed baselines) but has **no step in the CI `visual` job** — its baselines are never checked on CI yet (open follow-up; see [CI behavior](#ci-behavior)). It also reuses port `6009`, colliding with `apps/operator`; reassign it to e.g. `:6010` to honor the unique-port rule below. ## Adding a story [Section titled “Adding a story”](#adding-a-story) 1. **Drop a `Foo.stories.tsx` next to `Foo.tsx`** in any `libs/*/src/` that has Storybook wired: 
   ```tsx
   import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
   import { Foo } from './Foo';


   const meta: Meta<typeof Foo> = { component: Foo };
   export default meta;


   export const Default: StoryObj<typeof Foo> = {};
   export const WithTone: StoryObj<typeof Foo> = { args: { tone: 'good' } };
   ```
 2. **Verify it renders** — `npm run storybook --workspace libs/<lib>` and visit the port shown above. 3. **Generate the baseline** — `npm run build-storybook --workspace libs/<lib>` then `npm run lostpixel:update --workspace libs/<lib>`. PNGs land in `lostpixel-baseline/`. **Commit them.** 4. **Verify clean** — `npm run lostpixel --workspace libs/<lib>`. Should exit 0 with all stories within threshold. ## Adding Storybook to a new lib [Section titled “Adding Storybook to a new lib”](#adding-storybook-to-a-new-lib) If you’re stand­ing up Storybook for the first time in a lib: 
```bash
npm install --save-dev --workspace libs/<lib> \
  storybook @storybook/react-vite @storybook/addon-docs lost-pixel \
  --legacy-peer-deps --ignore-scripts
```
 Then create the four required files (copy from `libs/generic/ui-primitives`): * `.storybook/main.ts` — story glob + framework * `.storybook/preview.ts` — backgrounds + global CSS imports * `lostpixel.config.ts` — paths + threshold * `.gitignore` additions: `storybook-static/`, `lostpixel-current/`, `lostpixel-diff/` Add four scripts to `package.json`: 
```json
"storybook": "storybook dev -p 6008",
"build-storybook": "storybook build -o storybook-static",
"lostpixel": "lost-pixel",
"lostpixel:update": "LOST_PIXEL_GENERATE_ONLY=1 lost-pixel"
```
 Pick a unique port per lib (`6006` ui-primitives, `6007` marketplace-public-ui, `6008` agent-chat, `6009` operator — and currently also `grid-core`, which is the one collision to fix; `6010+` for new ones). Wire the new lib into the `visual` job in `.github/workflows/test.yml` so CI covers it. Lost Pixel pins playwright-core\@1.47.2 The repo’s main Playwright is `1.59.1`, but Lost Pixel ships its own older copy. The CI workflow installs Chromium for that copy via `node node_modules/lost-pixel/node_modules/playwright-core/cli.js install chromium`. Locally the same command runs on first use. ## When a baseline diff is reported [Section titled “When a baseline diff is reported”](#when-a-baseline-diff-is-reported) Two cases: 1. **Intentional UI change** — eyeball the diff (`lostpixel-diff/`), confirm the new render is what you wanted, then `npm run lostpixel:update` and commit the new `lostpixel-baseline/` PNG. The CI run on your PR will then exit 0. 2. **Unintentional regression** — read the diff, fix the bug. Don’t regenerate the baseline. The threshold is `0.05` (5%); small antialiasing wobble below that won’t flag. If you find yourself wanting to bump the threshold, something is probably wrong — investigate the wobble first. ## What gets baselined vs ignored [Section titled “What gets baselined vs ignored”](#what-gets-baselined-vs-ignored) `.gitignore` per lib: * ✅ **`lostpixel-baseline/`** — committed (the test fixtures). * ❌ `lostpixel-current/` — per-run output, ignored. * ❌ `lostpixel-diff/` — per-run output, ignored. * ❌ `storybook-static/` — per-run build, ignored. Spec §1.11 mandates git-lfs for baseline blobs unconditionally. We currently direct-commit instead — simpler, and it avoids any LFS-bandwidth surprises in CI. The “\~50 images” cutover is a local heuristic from each `lostpixel.config.ts` docstring, not the spec; revisit LFS when the per-lib PNG count climbs toward it. ## CI behavior [Section titled “CI behavior”](#ci-behavior) The `visual` job in `.github/workflows/test.yml`: * Runs on PRs **only** when the `run-visual` label is applied (matches the spec §1.11 opt-in pattern), and on every push to `main`. * Builds Storybook + runs Lost Pixel in sequence for the four libs with explicit steps: `ui-primitives`, `marketplace-public-ui`, `agent-chat`, and `apps/operator`. **`grid-core` has no step yet** — its local wiring is not covered by CI (open follow-up). * Uploads `lost-pixel-diffs` artifact on failure (combined `current/` and `diff/` from those four libs). To auto-apply `run-visual` when story files touch, the labeler **config** already exists: `.github/labeler.yml` carries the rule `libs/**/*.stories.@(ts|tsx)`. The only missing piece is a runnable labeler **workflow** — one with `on: pull_request_target` and `uses: actions/labeler` — so the action never fires (open follow-up). Note the stray `.github/workflows/labeler.yml`, which duplicates the config but has no `on:`/`jobs:`/`uses:`, so it is not a runnable workflow either. ## Related [Section titled “Related”](#related) * [Testing framework spec v1.1](./index) * [Agent E2E reference](./agent-e2e)
